At 7:05 p.m., Lu Tianfeng hurried to the entrance of Tianshu Western Restaurant, only to find it closed. A man in waiter’s attire sat on the ground, looking bewildered.

“What’s going on?” Lu Tianfeng’s intuition as a policeman immediately made him alert.

He knew very well that at this time, the Tianshu Western Restaurant should not have its doors closed, and the waiters hired by this high-end restaurant should not be sitting on the ground in a state of complete disgrace.

Unless something major happened in the restaurant.

“I’m a policeman; stay calm. What happened?” Lu Tianfeng put his hand on the waiter’s shoulder and asked again in a deep voice.

“There are gangsters… and a bomb in the restaurant…” the waiter stammered.

“A bomb? Have you called the police?”

“Not yet…”

“Call the police immediately, and then notify the building’s security team to come for reinforcements.” Lu Tianfeng subconsciously touched his waist and then realized that he had not yet resumed his job, so where would he have his service gun?

After the waiter nervously called the police, Lu Tianfeng grabbed him again and asked, “How many hostages are there? How many criminals are there?”

“There should be thirty or forty hostages… criminals… I saw five in total…”

“All five of them are armed?” Lu Tianfeng couldn’t help but frown. What was the purpose of attacking a Western restaurant in the city center with such fanfare?

“They all had guns, and the leader even said he wanted to plant bombs and block all entrances and exits.”

“Besides the main entrance, does the restaurant have any other entrances and exits?”

“There are also employee passages and fire escapes…” As the waiter was speaking, the building’s security team finally hurried to the scene.

Lu Tianfeng calmed the chaotic scene and shouted, “Everyone, calm down and follow my instructions. Security Captain, please assign people to guard the remaining entrances and exits of the restaurant to prevent the criminals from escaping. Immediately evacuate the remaining floors of the building, but be sure to maintain order. Arrange for personnel to meet the police in the first-floor lobby.”

The security guards were stunned when they heard this. They nodded continuously but did not move. It was not until Lu Tianfeng roared that they woke up as if from a dream and dispersed.

“Is there any way to contact the restaurant?” Lu Tianfeng patted the waiter’s shoulder.

“Ah? Contact?”

“Of course, what do you think the criminals’ purpose was in coming here with guns and taking a group of hostages?”

The waiter hesitated and couldn’t answer for a moment.

“Hostage taking in a place like this will definitely make the city’s news. The criminals must be trying to negotiate with the police and force them to agree to certain conditions through public pressure.” Lu Tianfeng frowned, and the thought that Chen Nuolan might be trapped inside made him feel anxious. “I have to take the initiative and find out their details and motives.”

Lu Tianfeng called the restaurant’s reservation number, but the line kept ringing until it was disconnected and no one answered. When he called again, someone hung up rudely.

Lu Tianfeng was not discouraged and called for the third time.

“What’s the matter with you?” There was a roar from the other end of the phone.

“I’m a negotiation expert sent by the police. I want to see if there’s anything I can do to help,” Lu Tianfeng replied calmly.

The other party was obviously stunned. He didn’t expect the police to take the initiative to call. After a few seconds, he said viciously, “What a bullshit expert; get out! You called the wrong number!”

“I’m right in front of the Tianshu Western Restaurant. I can help you convey the message—”

“Beep, beep, beep—”

The call was hung up.

“Captain Lu?” At this time, a familiar voice sounded behind Lu Tianfeng. He turned around and saw it was Tong Yao.

Tong Yao was wearing a white T-shirt, blue jeans, and a casual ponytail today. At first glance, she looked very different from the serious policewoman she usually was.

“Tong Yao, why are you here?”

“I’m on my day off today and happened to be shopping nearby. I rushed over to help after receiving the message from headquarters,” Tong Yao answered concisely.

Lu Tianfeng nodded and asked, “Have the reinforcements arrived?”

“A colleague is already organizing the evacuation downstairs and maintaining order. The SWAT team is expected to arrive in about ten minutes.” Tong Yao paused before saying, “I just heard you calling the criminals…”

“Well, the criminals will definitely make some demands. I want to take advantage of their unstable position and take the initiative to attack and disrupt their deployment.”

Tong Yao didn’t say anything else. She knew very well how dangerous it was to communicate and contact directly with the criminals at the scene. If she said the wrong thing by mistake, it would cause irreversible consequences.

Lu Tianfeng had not yet officially resumed his post. If anything went wrong during the operation, his police career may very well end there.

Even so, Lu Tianfeng did not hesitate or evade at all. His eyes were extremely firm, and looking at them made people feel at ease.

“What are you thinking about?” Lu Tianfeng’s words brought Tong Yao back to reality.

“Ah, no. I was wondering why the criminals chose such a place to commit the crime.” Tong Yao calmed down and pointed out the key doubts in this hostage-taking case.

The restaurant was on the top floor of a skyscraper, a place where all entrances and exits can be easily blocked. If dozens of hostages were taken at once and they were surrounded by the police, it would be almost impossible for the criminals to escape unscathed.

“These people are probably crazy people who don’t care about their lives.” Lu Tianfeng became even more anxious. Chen Nuolan’s life was actually in the hands of such crazy criminals.

“Captain Lu, let’s wait for reinforcements to arrive.”

“No, we have to race against time.” As he spoke, Lu Tianfeng called Tianshu Western Restaurant again.

This time, the call was picked up quickly.

“What’s the matter? Tell me quickly!” The person who answered the phone seemed to be another person, and his voice was even deeper.

“I’m a police negotiator…”

“Can you meet our conditions?” The other party interrupted Lu Tianfeng abruptly before he could finish speaking.

“Please tell me; I will try my best to negotiate…”

“First of all, I only want to negotiate with specific people. Don’t just pick someone to piss me off.”

“Do you want to contact our director directly or other leaders?” Lu Tianfeng asked.

“No, I want you to send Lu Tianfeng from the Criminal Police Brigade to the scene to be in charge of the negotiations.”

“Lu Tianfeng?” Even though he had prepared himself mentally, Lu Tianfeng was still shocked to hear his own name at this moment.

“I’ll give you half an hour to find Lu Tianfeng. Otherwise, I’ll start killing people.” The other party paused for a moment, then said, “We really dare kill people.”

The call was hung up without any warning. Lu Tianfeng immediately looked at his watch. It was 7:15 in the evening.

“Captain Lu, this is very unusual,” Tong Yao said worriedly. “We must not agree to their request.”

“I have no other choice—”

Lu Tianfeng’s phone vibrated, and he saw a message from an unfamiliar number. The photo was clearly taken inside the Tianshu Western Restaurant. It showed a girl lying in a pool of blood, her eyes wide open, as if she had died.

Then came a text message: “We’re really going to do it.”

Tong Yao gasped: “Captain Lu, a hostage has died.”

“Did you notice? The bullet went through the hostage’s neck,” Lu Tianfeng said with a frown. “Most people only aim at the target’s body when shooting. Who would shoot at a person’s neck?”

“Someone who is very confident in his marksmanship… someone who kills people without mercy, such as a professional killer, or a mercenary who only cares about money and is not afraid of death.” Tong Yao also frowned.

Lu Tianfeng’s expression became increasingly serious. He said, “Tong Yao, can you find a way to confirm the identity of the deceased? Also, check the information on this phone number, though I don’t think there will be any clues.”

“Of course I can, but Captain Lu, the SWAT team will be here in three minutes at most…” Tong Yao’s meaning was self-evident. She hoped Lu Tianfeng would not act impulsively.

“The other party is coming for me; there is no way I can hide. Go and collect information quickly.” Lu Tianfeng patted Tong Yao’s shoulder, but he didn’t expect Tong Yao to suddenly make a move and grab Lu Tianfeng’s wrist.

Lu Tianfeng wanted to fight back, but Tong Yao hit his arms and knees smoothly and continuously, pinning him to the ground and handcuffing him to the railing next to him.

“Tong Yao, what are you doing!” Lu Tianfeng was so angry that he almost vomited blood.

“I’m sorry, Captain Lu. You haven’t officially been reinstated yet and still aren’t considered a police officer. I can’t let you take this risk alone.”

“Are you kidding? You know, Chen Nuolan is in the restaurant!”

“What?” Tong Yao was stunned.

“Let me go… please!”

Tong Yao never expected that Lu Tianfeng would speak to her in such a pleading tone. She saw an expression on his face that she had never seen before.

That was a concern for Chen Nuolan.

“Tong Yao, trust me again.”

“I trust you, but I also have responsibilities as a police officer.” Tong Yao squeezed out these words with difficulty, then turned around and said, “Sorry, I have to go meet the SWAT team first. Please wait here until I come back.”

“Tong Yao!”

Tong Yao floated away, and Lu Tianfeng stomped his feet fiercely. Then he noticed that the waiter from Tianshu Western Restaurant was still sitting next to him, his face pale and stunned.

The waiter wore an exquisite work badge on his chest, which was attached to his clothes with a pin.

Lu Tianfeng’s eyes suddenly lit up: “Quickly take off your work badge and give it to me.”

“W-why?”

“Hurry!” Lu Tianfeng shouted. The waiter didn’t dare ask any more questions. He quickly took off his work badge and threw it to Lu Tianfeng.

Lu Tianfeng looked at the pin on the work badge and smiled with satisfaction.

CONTENT END 65

chapters.title: Chapter 66
chapters.content:
At 7:20 p.m., Lu Tianfeng rubbed his red right wrist as he walked into the Tianshu Western Restaurant. A pair of handcuffs alone couldn’t hold a highly qualified criminal police officer, so he wasn’t sure whether Tong Yao had let him go on purpose or if it was a mistake. Regardless, he had finally entered this dangerous place.

As soon as he entered the door, a gun was pressed against Lu Tianfeng’s forehead.

Lu Tianfeng raised his hands above his head, palms open, indicating that he had no weapons. Although he seemed to have his head lowered and his expression tense, he was actually secretly scanning the interior of the restaurant with his eyes, analyzing the situation.

“Go in!” the man wearing a dog-head mask shouted sternly with a gun in hand.

Lu Tianfeng walked forward. It seemed as if all the hostages in the restaurant had been moved to a private room. For the moment, he could only see three gangsters—one of them was pointing a gun at his head, and not far away, the other two also had guns. The way they held their guns revealed them to be veterans. Lu Tianfeng suspected that the man in the pig mask might be their leader.

The restaurant had a large glass curtain wall, which was originally designed for customers to enjoy the night view. Now all the glass curtain walls were covered by thick curtains, and the situation inside could not be seen from the outside, which would bring difficulties to the possible surprise operations carried out by the special police team.

Moreover, the criminals installed bombs on several of the glass curtain walls. If the SWAT team chose to attack here, there would be heavy casualties.

Seeing that the criminals were more far-sighted than he had imagined, Lu Tianfeng’s already insufficient self-confidence was further shattered.

“Are you Lu Tianfeng?” said the man in the pig mask. Lu Tianfeng secretly gave him the code name “Pig-Head” in his heart.

“Yes.”

“Where’s your ID card?” Pig-Head did not easily believe Lu Tianfeng’s words.

Lu Tianfeng slowly put his right hand into his pocket, took out his ID card, and handed it to the gangster wearing a dog head mask next to him.

Unexpectedly, Pig-Head said, “No need to give it to him; throw it to me.”

Lu Tianfeng had no choice but to throw his ID card to Pig-Head. Pig-Head took the ID card, looked at it carefully, and said, “Very good, the ID card is real.”

“Of course it’s real; why would I lie to you?” Lu Tianfeng tried to take the initiative.

“Officer Lu, what do you think of my on-site command level for this operation?” Pig-Head completely ignored Lu Tianfeng and changed the subject.

Lu Tianfeng had no idea about the other party’s background and did not respond.

Pig-Head chuckled, “Officer Lu, there are only three entrances and exits here, all of which are rigged with bombs. If you were to command your men to storm, which one would you choose as the breakthrough point?”

“This is the top floor of the building. I will send someone to lower a rope from the rooftop to break the glass curtain wall—” At this point, Lu Tianfeng realized the terrifying nature of his opponent. The several glass curtain walls where bombs were installed happened to be the locations that the police would prefer to choose when launching an attack.

“Let’s pray that they don’t act rashly.” When Pig-Head laughed, his shoulders shook, which made people feel very awkward.

“Who are you?”

“Shh, don’t ask questions. Just answer my questions truthfully.” Pig-Head made a silencing gesture. “First question: are you a time perceiver?”

When Lu Tianfeng heard this, it was like a bolt from the blue. He never thought that his biggest secret would be casually revealed by such a stranger.

“What… are you talking about…” Lu Tianfeng’s tone lost its usual calmness.

“Officer Lu, we know your secret. Please cooperate with us,” Pig-Head said casually. “You know, finding a suitable Perceiver is not easy…”

Lu Tianfeng bit his lower lip and decided to remain silent.

Seeing that Lu Tianfeng was silent, Pig-Head spread his hands and continued, “We came here today hoping to reach a cooperation agreement with Officer Lu. As long as you do us a small favor, we will never bother you again in the future.”

“Favor?” Lu Tianfeng sneered in his heart. The other party came with such a fierce momentum; how could it be like he wanted help from him?

“Officer Lu, you know about the Wang Donglin prison van robbery that’s been making a lot of noise these past few days, right?”

“I’ve heard of it.” Lu Tianfeng nodded, secretly shocked. Was this a coincidence, or did someone deliberately arrange it? Before the appointment, he was still studying Wang Donglin’s case in the police station and almost missed the appointment. He didn’t expect that this group of criminals was also paying attention to the same case.

“I want you to take care of this for me.”

“The police are already doing their best to track down…”

“No, you completely misunderstood.” Pig-Head shook his head repeatedly and rudely interrupted Lu Tianfeng. “I’m not asking you to solve the case, but to prevent it from happening.”

“Prevent the case from happening?” Lu Tianfeng couldn’t understand the meaning of this sentence at all.

“I’m well aware that you’re a Time Perceiver and can sense single-day time loops, but I want to tell you that in the game of time travel, single-day loops are just small ripples. As long as you improve your abilities, you’ll be able to perceive time travel at a higher level.”

“I… still don’t understand…”

Pig-Head pulled a small test tube from his pocket and waved it in front of Lu Tianfeng. “This is the ability enhancer. It won’t have any effect on ordinary people, but after you drink it, your Time Perception will be temporarily enhanced. Then, we can reverse time and send you back to the early morning of May 31st.”

“The last day of last month?” Lu Tianfeng immediately thought that that was the day when Wang Donglin had the accident.

“Yes, it’s very interesting, isn’t it? You can experience the wonderful feeling of time flowing backwards, and you can also nip the evil in the bud and save Wang Donglin’s life. It’s a two-pronged approach. The terms of this deal seem very reasonable.”

Lu Tianfeng stared at the strange test tube without saying a word.

“Officer Lu is probably still skeptical! Caution is indeed your strength!” Pig-Head made a gesture to his men, and then a gangster wearing a dog-head mask brought Chen Nuolan out.

Lu Tianfeng wasn’t surprised. Since the other party had already investigated him thoroughly, how could they have missed the information about Chen Nuolan? He even suspected that the other party had chosen this time and place to take hostages because they knew in advance that they would meet there.

“If you have anything to say, come at me. She is innocent!” Lu Tianfeng said, gritting his teeth, his voice cold.

“Officer Lu, have you ever thought about why we planned this hostage taking? Even if we have hostages, there is no way to retreat here. Aren’t we walking into a trap and dying in vain?” What Pig-Head said was exactly what Lu Tianfeng was thinking.

“Is there any way for you to escape unscathed?”

“It’s simple. If I don’t have the ability to turn back time, we will definitely die.”

Lu Tianfeng’s heart skipped a beat. This seemed like a very reasonable explanation. Could it be that in this world, besides time loops, time could actually flow backwards?

“Why did you choose me?” Lu Tianfeng asked.

“Because you’re a police officer, you have the legitimate ability to prevent crime.” Pig-Head glanced at Chen Nuolan casually. “Another reason is that there aren’t many Perceivers, and the data we have on even fewer of them is even smaller.”

Lu Tianfeng pondered and said, “But I may not be able to prevent that case…”

“No, you must stop this crime from happening; otherwise, your precious girlfriend’s life may be in danger.”

“You dare!” Lu Tianfeng’s eyes widened with anger.

“What do you think?” Pig-Head asked instead of answering.

“Feng, don’t bother with me, and don’t listen to their nonsense!” Chen Nuolan suddenly shouted.

Pig-Head handed the test tube to Lu Tianfeng: “You have no choice. Don’t try to escape with Chen Nuolan after time goes back, and try to stay out of it. That way you will die a more miserable death. Complete your mission well, and I will ensure that you are safe.”

Lu Tianfeng subconsciously took the test tube, his hand still in mid-air. As he approached Pig-Head, he smelled an indescribable and strange fragrance on him, unlike the common spices in China.

“Officer Lu, what are you still hesitating about?”

Extreme anger made Lu Tianfeng’s vision blurred, and his hands trembled slightly.

“Drink it; everything will be fine.” Pig-Head smiled, his voice sharp and dry.

Lu Tianfeng forced himself to concentrate and take a closer look at the strange liquid in the test tube—it was almost transparent, with a faint pink tint. It also smelled a bit like alcohol.

“Feng! Don’t agree to him…” At this time, he heard Chen Nuolan’s pleading.

“Shh…”

“”Click”—that was the sound of the gun safety lock opening.

The man raised the gun and put the muzzle against Chen Nuolan’s temple.

“Don’t hurt her!” Lu Tianfeng shouted sternly.

“Drink it quickly!” the man urged Lu Tianfeng and moved his finger to the trigger.

“I’ll drink it. I’ll agree to all the conditions you propose, as long as you stop hurting other people.” Lu Tianfeng gritted his teeth, held his breath, closed his eyes, and poured all the liquid in the test tube into his throat in one breath.

Unexpectedly, this thing was not difficult to drink. The taste was similar to some kind of cocktail. Maybe it really contained alcohol.

“Very good. It will take about ten minutes for the drug to fully take effect. Before that, I want to prove something to you.”

“What’s the matter?” Lu Tianfeng finally swallowed the last drop and slowly opened his eyes.

“There’s no turning back.”

After the man said this coldly, he pulled the trigger without hesitation.

“Bang!”

“Nuolan—”

The world in front of Lu Tianfeng suddenly turned black and white, and the sound disappeared all of a sudden.

In addition to black and white, there was also a glaring red.

Then the red color gradually turned black, and Chen Nuolan fell into the darkness, like an innocent person swallowed by the darkness.

CONTENT END 66

chapters.title: Chapter 67
chapters.content:
“Why…” Lu Tianfeng clenched his right hand into a fist and squeezed out the word with difficulty.

“I want to tell you that we’re not only capable but also courageous.” The man’s voice was tinged with a sneer. “Anyway, time will flow back, and Chen Nuolan will be resurrected. I’m sure you’re already familiar with this routine, so there’s no need to be so angry. Oh, and if you don’t listen to me and run away with Chen Nuolan after time flows back… I advise you to give up this foolish idea as soon as possible, because no matter where you are, I can find you.”

Lu Tianfeng felt as if his internal organs were burning and there was a tearing pain. He didn’t know whether it was due to the effect of the potion he had just drunk or due to anger.

“I won’t let you go,” Lu Tianfeng said word by word.

“Oh?”

“I guess there aren’t any Perceivers here, right? So, when time goes back, you won’t remember what I said, but I will remember you clearly.”

Pig-Head was silent for a rare moment.

“I will find you and make you pay the price!”

Two gangsters wearing dog-head masks raised their guns and pointed them at Lu Tianfeng’s chest.

“Of course you don’t dare to hurt me, because you still have to rely on me to save Wang Donglin.” Lu Tianfeng sneered, “I don’t know what your real purpose is, but I can guarantee that your wishful thinking will be thwarted.”

“Lu Tianfeng, you’re oversimplifying things.” Pig-Head suddenly spoke, his tone lower than ever before, and he no longer politely addressed Lu Tianfeng as Officer Lu. “Please don’t underestimate us. We have the ability to turn back time.”

“But for some reason, you can only rely on me to deal with Wang Donglin’s affairs, right? Although I don’t know the specific situation yet, that should be my only advantage.”

Lu Tianfeng and Pig-Head looked at each other, neither of them willing to show weakness.

“Just do what we say and don’t act rashly.” After a long time, Pig-Head cast this warning.

“If I can really save Wang Donglin, what next?”

“We will take care of the rest; you don’t have to worry,” Pighead said in a tone that seemed unwilling to say more.

Lu Tianfeng gritted his teeth, looked at Chen Nuolan lying motionless in a pool of blood, and said in a resounding voice, “You will definitely pay the price for this.”

“Then we’ll see… it’s about time.”

Lu Tianfeng realized that the so-called miracle drug should have worked—but could time really flow back? Could he remember everything clearly?

If time couldn’t be turned back… Lu Tianfeng inexplicably thought of this, and his hands and feet suddenly became cold, and his breathing became difficult. Was Nuolan going to die in such an unclear way?

A black shadow flashed before Lu Tianfeng’s eyes. He looked closely and found that it was not the shadow of something, but everything within his sight was covered with a shadow.

“What’s going on…”

The shadows overlapped and swayed rapidly.

Lu Tianfeng felt that the floor, walls, and glass curtain wall were all cracking and shattering. He was a little unsteady and reached out to hold on to something, but his head was spinning, and his hands reached out to nothing.

His stomach felt queasy, his body felt like it was about to burst, and he had an urge to vomit. He couldn’t hear anything, only a high-pitched buzzing sound that pierced deep into his eardrums, making him even more uncomfortable.

Were time reversal and time looping completely different feelings?

The whole world was turned upside down. Lu Tianfeng seemed to have fallen into a whirlpool, being swept to the bottom of the sea by the undercurrent. He felt depressed, suffocated, and in pain…

“Ah!”

Lu Tianfeng screamed strangely and suddenly woke up. When he opened his eyes, he saw the ceiling of his bedroom.

“Feng, what’s wrong with you?” Chen Nuolan gently placed her hand on Lu Tianfeng’s waist. “Did you have a nightmare?”

“I…” Lu Tianfeng’s internal organs seemed to be still in a state of being torn apart, his whole body was in pain, and he couldn’t help but groan.

“Are you sick?” Chen Nuolan nervously got out of bed and reached out to touch Lu Tianfeng’s forehead. “Oh my god, why are you sweating all over? What’s wrong with you?”

“I’m… fine. I just need to rest for a while,” Lu Tianfeng gasped painfully. “Nuolan, quickly check the time…”

“It’s just past two in the morning. Is there any problem?” Chen Nuolan asked worriedly.

“What month… what day?”

“May 31st.” Chen Nuolan was a little confused.

“Nuolan…” Lu Tianfeng hugged Chen Nuolan tightly. This sudden enthusiasm left Chen Nuolan at a loss.

“What the hell is going on?”

“It’s great to have you here.” Lu Tianfeng gently kissed Chen Nuolan’s earlobe. “There’s something I need your help with.”

Chen Nuolan gently pounded Lu Tianfeng’s chest: “You can tell me anything, but can we wait until dawn to talk? I’m so sleepy now…”

“No, we don’t have much time.” Lu Tianfeng hugged Chen Nuolan again and whispered in her ear, “Time is running out; we must race against time.”

Chen Nuolan nodded, not quite understanding.

CONTENT END 67

chapters.title: Chapter 68
chapters.content:
May 31st, 4:30 a.m.

Chen Nuolan lay quietly in Lu Tianfeng’s arms, listening to him unravel the story of the time loop. It was a long story, taking Lu Tianfeng over two hours, but she listened intently, her eyes, initially a little sleepy, gradually brightening.

The same day repeating five times, a fate that could be altered, the secrets of Feng Teng Gene and Luo Tengfeng, the mysterious forces lurking behind the scenes that influenced the time loop… And then there was Lu Tianfeng’s most recent experience, being forced to travel back from June 2nd to May 31st—this shattered his previous understanding of the time loop, and he truly felt that there were many secrets behind it all that he had never known.

“Luo Tengfeng’s RAN-X technology might have involved the secrets of Time Perceivers, which is why he was silenced…”

“I finally understand why you insisted I feign amnesia and have nothing to do with the Feng Teng Gene case,” Chen Nuolan sighed. “But why didn’t you tell me earlier?”

Lu Tianfeng smiled bitterly: “I… I was worried you wouldn’t believe it.”

“If someone else had said it, I certainly wouldn’t have believed it, but you…” Chen Nuolan smiled but stopped talking. Instead, she gently kissed Lu Tianfeng’s chin. “You’ve been up all night, and you’ve even got stubble.”

“Nuolan, there must be others in this world studying the secrets of time. You’re a scientist, and you know English. Could you look up some information for me?” Lu Tianfeng gently stroked Chen Nuolan’s hair.

“No problem, we can start now,” Chen Nuolan said, looking energetic and ready to jump out of bed.

Lu Tianfeng quickly and firmly held her down, saying, “No, your priority right now is to get some rest and wait until daybreak before working.”

Chen Nuolan tried to protest, but Lu Tianfeng refused to let her get up. Finally, she compromised, resting her head on his chest and soon falling into a deep sleep. Lu Tianfeng waited until she was sound asleep before carefully laying her down, tucking her in the blanket, and tiptoeing out of bed.

Chen Nuolan’s support and trust filled him with energy. Although his body ached after the time-reversal experience, this minor difficulty was nothing.

Outside the window, the stars dimmed; it was the darkest hour before dawn.

.

May 31st, six in the morning.

Tong Yao, wearing a black T-shirt and aqua blue jeans and with her hair tied in a simple ponytail, was walking to a snack bar near her home. She spotted Lu Tianfeng sitting in the corner and hurried over.

“Captain Lu, good morning.” Tong Yao, though filled with confusion and puzzled as to why the suspended Lu Tianfeng had come to see her so early in the morning, maintained a composed expression.

“Tong Yao, I need a favor.” Lu Tianfeng skipped the small talk and got straight to the point, which gave Tong Yao a sense of trust.

“Tell me, is it business or personal?”

“Remember what I told you about the time loop?” Lu Tianfeng lowered his voice, leaning close to Tong Yao’s ear.

Tong Yao nodded. Of course she remembered it perfectly. Although she still had some doubts about the truth of his statement, her intuition told her that Lu Tianfeng was neither crazy nor joking.

“I… experienced something even more incredible.” Lu Tianfeng paused, a dull, inexplicable pain in his chest. “I came back; two days from today, on June 2nd.”

Tong Yao was stunned for a moment, then understood what Lu Tianfeng meant. “Captain Lu, what you experienced this time wasn’t a time loop but a time reversal?”

“Yes, and I’m back with a mission.” Lu Tianfeng rubbed the sore spot. “Someone threatened to kill Chen Nuolan and me if I couldn’t complete the mission.”

“So, what was the mission?”

“Do you know about Wang Donglin?”

“The guy who murdered four girls but was exonerated of criminal responsibility due to a psychiatric evaluation? That case shocked the whole city, so of course I know.”

Lu Tianfeng thought, This is easy now; we can skip a lot of the preparation.

“Today is the day Wang Donglin is transferred from the detention center to the psychiatric hospital, but a group has already prepared to hijack the prison van and kill him en route.”

“What?” Although Tong Yao was prepared, she was still shocked by the news.

“Until June 2nd, the police still had no clue about the attack on the prison van. This shows how sophisticated the perpetrators were,” Lu Tianfeng said with a wry smile.

Tong Yao lowered her head and subconsciously twirled her fingers. She certainly believed Lu Tianfeng, but what he was saying was too bizarre. She needed some time to digest it.

“So, your mission today is…”

Surprisingly, Lu Tianfeng didn’t answer directly. Instead, he gazed thoughtfully at the crowd outside the snack bar.

“Captain Lu? Are you okay?” Tong Yao asked, confused.

“I feel something is wrong.” Lu Tianfeng frowned and recounted to Tong Yao the hostage-taking incident on the night of June 2, omitting the minor conflict between them.

Tong Yao was even more confused after hearing this.

“So, a group of well-armed criminals forced you to return to today to rescue Wang Donglin, and another group planned today’s attack on the prison van and killed Wang Donglin… The question is, why do both groups attach so much importance to Wang Donglin?”

“That’s what really puzzles me,” Lu Tianfeng sighed. “It seems there are many unknown stories behind Wang Donglin, but no matter what, we have to rescue him first.”

“Then, should I lead my people to the crime scene in advance and set up an ambush? Captain Lu must know the exact location.” Tong Yao proposed the simplest, most direct, and most feasible plan.

Lu Tianfeng pondered for a moment, then slowly shook his head. “Have you ever considered that Wang Donglin’s transfer should have been classified information? How could the criminals have planned the attack so precisely?”

Tong Yao immediately understood: “Is there a traitor?”

“So we can’t rely solely on the police.” Lu Tianfeng paused, took a deep breath, and then said, “I’d like to ask Yu Yongsheng for help. What do you think?”

Tong Yao gave a forced smile. Yu Yongsheng had been loyal to Lu Tianfeng, even admiring him. However, the case a month ago changed everything—his partner Huang Xuanxuan died, and Lu Tianfeng was suspended for investigation. This left Yu Yongsheng disheartened, so he resigned and never had any contact with his colleagues at the police station again.

“I’m not sure how he’s doing now…” Tong Yao hesitated, unsure whether to voice her deepest concerns.

“I know. He went to work for Huaquan Security.”

Tong Yao was quite surprised. She had originally assumed that Lu Tianfeng and Yu Yongsheng held a grudge and would never speak to each other again, but she hadn’t expected them to actually still be in touch.

“Captain Lu, are you and him… okay?” Although Tong Yao’s questions were fragmented, they were enough for Lu Tianfeng to understand.

“Not really. We chat occasionally, and everyone’s very polite,” Lu Tianfeng said helplessly. “Maybe he still hates me?”

Tong Yao was speechless for a moment. Lu Tianfeng’s frankness made it difficult for her to respond.

“You’re probably wondering why I’m looking for Yongsheng. There are three reasons: first, I believe in his abilities; second, I know him; and third, he works for the security company and can get us a crucial prop.”

“What prop?” Tong Yao thought. Although Huaquan Security was considered a leader in the industry and well-equipped, it couldn’t possibly rival the police, could it?

“Car.” Lu Tianfeng seemed to have the plan in mind. “To conceal our presence and keep a low profile, the vehicle used to transfer Wang Donglin to the psychiatric hospital today won’t be an ordinary prison van, but an escort vehicle loaned from Huaquan Security.”

Tong Yao understood, uttered an “Oh,” and nodded, saying nothing more.

“I’ll go talk to him now. Please prepare these things for us in advance.” Lu Tianfeng handed Tong Yao a note, seemingly oblivious to the possibility of her refusing.

“I understand,” Tong Yao said, her tone calm as she took the note.

.

May 31st, 7:15 a.m.

Yu Yongsheng, dressed in the uniform of his security company, had just walked downstairs when he saw a familiar figure standing alone in the community’s central garden.

“Boss?” Yu Yongsheng couldn’t believe his eyes.

Lu Tianfeng looked up at Yu Yongsheng and smiled. “Sorry, I forgot your address.”

“Why are you here…” Yu Yongsheng suddenly ran out of words.

“Just for you calling me ‘Boss,’ my visit wasn’t in vain.” Lu Tianfeng patted Yu Yongsheng’s shoulder. “How have you been lately?”

“Fine.”

“There’s something I need your help with…”

“Okay,” Yu Yongsheng agreed without hesitation.

This surprised Lu Tianfeng. He said, “I haven’t told you what it is yet.”

“Anyway, I’ll agree.” Yu Yongsheng also laughed. This was the first time he had smiled with relief in the past month.

Lu Tianfeng patted Yu Yongsheng’s shoulder even harder. It seemed as if there was no need for further words between the two men.

CONTENT END 68

chapters.title: Chapter 69
chapters.content:
May 31st, 8:30 a.m.

The living room of Lu Tianfeng’s home became a makeshift command center. Lu Tianfeng was, of course, the commander, and Tong Yao, Yu Yongsheng, and a sleepy Chen Nuolan also participated in the discussion.

“Everyone, look here first.” Two maps were taped to the wall: one was a tourist map of D City, the other a zoomed-in close-up of a specific area on the map. “The criminals attacked at 11:10 a.m., inside the No. 2 Fuhe Road tunnel. Traffic here isn’t heavy on weekdays, and there’s no surveillance inside the tunnel, so the lighting is dim, making it an ideal location.”

“Wait, I have a question.” Tong Yao raised her hand. “This road is narrow, and it’s not the only way from the detention center to the psychiatric hospital. Why didn’t the prison van take the Inner Ring Road?”

“Because this section of the Inner Ring Road was severely congested around 10 a.m. this morning,” Lu Tianfeng marked a section of the road on the map with a red marker. “To avoid the traffic jam, the prison van took Xifeng Road, then turned onto Fuhe Road, passed through two tunnels on Fuhe Road, and then rejoined the Inner Ring Road.”

Everyone nodded in understanding.

“The criminals must have ambushed the prison van in the tunnel, then shot through its tires as it passed. A shootout ensued. Besides Wang Donglin, there were four other escorts in the van. The ultimate result was one death and three serious injuries, with the seriously injured remaining unconscious as of June 2nd.”

“These criminals are truly ruthless!” Yu Yongsheng said.

Chen Nuolan couldn’t help but chime in. “Wang Donglin’s case has been a hot topic online. Many netizens believe he deserves the death penalty, while others believe he must be feigning illness to escape punishment. If he were the only one killed, I think many would still believe the perpetrators were acting in the name of justice. But this brutal method is truly… sigh!”

“It’s ironic to think about it. We risked our lives to save a psychopathic murderer,” Yu Yongsheng said self-deprecatingly.

Lu Tianfeng didn’t respond directly but continued to explain the case: “According to the information I’ve read, there were at least four criminals, equipped with submachine guns and other heavy weapons, and at least two vehicles. They fled separately after committing the crime. Although we have four people on our side, Nuolan can’t handle the frontline mission…”

“We came prepared. Even if we’re missing one person, it won’t be a problem,” Tong Yao said confidently.

“Even so, we can’t be careless. There’s one thing I’ve never understood. Even if they were four heavily armed criminals, it’s unlikely they could easily defeat the officers escorting the prison van, right? As long as the van stops, the escorts will be on full alert. However, the on-site investigation revealed that the gunfight was largely one-sided. The escorts only fired two or three shots, while the criminals fired nearly a hundred rounds.”

Yu Yongsheng’s face paled. “What on earth is going on?”

Lu Tianfeng said sternly, “Earlier, Tong Yao had suggested that we could directly notify the police and have them set up an ambush at the crime scene, waiting for the criminals to appear and capture them immediately. This plan seems sound, but given that the criminals have precise information about the transport, I believe they have spies within the police force. If this theory is correct, any attempt to utilize police resources would likely alert the enemy.

Facing such a well-trained and ruthless group of criminals, attempting to resolve the situation without the assistance of police resources would be incredibly difficult. As Lu Tianfeng finished speaking, Tong Yao frowned, as if deep in thought. Yu Yongsheng also changed his usual demeanor and became more serious. Chen Nuolan, on the other hand, remained relaxed, as she had no immediate understanding of the mission’s difficulty.

“Although the enemy is powerful, we do have good news—to maintain secrecy for this escort and transfer, they’ve borrowed Huaquan Security Company’s escort vehicle, and Yongsheng happens to have a way to get us the same model…”

Tong Yao suddenly realized, “No wonder Captain Lu assigned me to urgently create a set of fake license plates.”

“Are there any problems with the fake plates? Is time a bit tight?”

“No problem, we’ll definitely have them before ten o’clock,” Tong Yao replied.

“Yongsheng’s job is to drive one of your company’s escort vehicles back before ten o’clock.”

“Leave it to me!” Yu Yongsheng said, patting his chest.

Lu Tianfeng gestured on a partially enlarged map and said, “According to the route, the prison van carrying Wang Donglin will first pass through Fuhe Road Tunnel No. 1 and then Tunnel No. 2. The criminals are lying in ambush in Tunnel No. 2. We must preemptively set up a roadblock inside Tunnel No. 1 and try to stop the prison van and delay it. Meanwhile, we’ll drive the escort van with a fake license plate into Tunnel No. 2 to serve as bait to lure the criminals. Do you understand this tactic of substituting a cat for a prince1?”

“I understand.” Surprisingly, only Chen Nuolan responded. Yu Yongsheng and Tong Yao exchanged bewildered glances, each pondering the same question.

“Captain Lu, who will drive the escort van into Tunnel No. 2?” Tong Yao finally asked. The driver, facing four ferocious gunmen alone, was walking into a dangerous trap.

“Yongsheng, intercept the prison van in Tunnel No. 1. The driver is from Huaquan Security. You’ll be more effective in communicating. Tong Yao can pretend to be a police officer passing by, ready to support Tunnel No. 2. I’ll be driving the disguised escort vehicle.”

“That’s too dangerous, Boss! I should be the one driving. I’m a Huaquan employee, and I’m still in uniform!” Yu Yongsheng quickly declared.

“No, let me drive. After all, I have a gun,” Tong Yao chimed in.

Chen Nuolan looked at Lu Tianfeng, silent, but her face was filled with worry.

“Listen, driving the disguised escort vehicle is extremely risky. We can’t afford to make any mistakes. I should be responsible.”

“Boss…”

“Captain Lu…”

“Nuolan, what do you think?” Lu Tianfeng turned to Chen Nuolan.

“Personally, I don’t want you to take any risks, but objectively speaking, this is indeed the best option,” Chen Nuolan said slowly.

Tong Yao and Yu Yongsheng were both a bit surprised by these words. But looking at Chen Nuolan’s expression, it didn’t sound like she was joking at all.

Tong Yao began to understand why these two people with such different personalities could become a couple.

Chen Nuolan continued, “But even if we face four brutal criminals alone, we’re not completely hopeless.”

“Do you have any suggestions?” Even Lu Tianfeng was surprised.

“Our biggest advantage is that no matter how the enemy tries, their target is Wang Donglin inside the car. This means they always need to open the back door of the escort vehicle, which lays a good opportunity for us to set a trap.” Although Chen Nuolan was a civilian, her words were so coherent that they couldn’t be ignored.

“Well… what kind of trap can we set?” Lu Tianfeng’s first thought was an explosive device, but it was obviously not suitable for them.

“Don’t forget what my specialty is,” Chen Nuolan said with a confident smile. “There are many interesting creatures in nature that can help, like bees.”

“Bees?”

“Under normal circumstances, bees won’t attack humans, but with the addition of a certain hormone, they become formidable killers. I won’t go into the details of how this works, but leave it to me. I can prepare the bees and the hormones within an hour.”

“Great! This gives us a better chance of success!” Lu Tianfeng was overjoyed.

Chen Nuolan took two steps forward, gently took Lu Tianfeng’s hand, and said, “I allow you to take this risk alone, but you must promise me you will return safely.”

Lu Tianfeng was speechless for a moment. He could only hold Chen Nuolan’s hand tightly and nod vigorously.

.

May 31st, 9:00 a.m., in a solitary cell at the D City Detention Center.

A thin, pale young man sat on a bed, his back against the wall, holding a slightly yellowed copy of “Selected Chess Endgames.” He stared intently at a single page, muttering to himself.

“Wang Donglin, get ready. You’ll be transferred shortly,” the guard shouted.

Wang Donglin didn’t even look up, continuing to read.

“Wang Donglin, did you hear that?” the guard said, his voice rising, a hint of vehemence in his voice.

“Sorry, I heard that. Thank you,” Wang Donglin said softly, with a scholarly air.

Looking at his gentle demeanor, it was hard to imagine he had brutally murdered four young women.

The guard snorted and turned away.

Wang Donglin remained in the same position, motionless, poring over his book until the sound of the guards’ footsteps faded completely. Only then did the corners of his mouth curl slightly, and his expression gradually relaxed.

“Abandoned pawns, these are all abandoned pawns,” he muttered to himself.

Wang Donglin took a deep breath, closed his book, and looked up. Sunlight filtered through the iron bars of the window, casting a shadow on his distinct features.

He smiled into the sunlight.

CONTENT END 69

chapters.title: Chapter 70
chapters.content:
May 31st, 10:00 a.m., downstairs of Lu Tianfeng’s house.

The agreed departure time had come, but Yu Yongsheng hadn’t arrived yet.

Lu Tianfeng checked his watch, and even the usually calm man couldn’t help but feel a little anxious.

He knew that only an hour to prepare for such a mission was too short, but he had no choice.

“Should I call and urge them?” Chen Nuolan, gloved hands on, carried two large boxes filled with bees she had begged from acquaintances.

“No rush, we’ll probably be here soon,” Lu Tianfeng said.

As soon as he finished speaking, a blue-and-gray escort vehicle appeared at the corner of the road. Lu Tianfeng couldn’t help but breathe a sigh of relief, but as the vehicle got closer, his expression darkened.

“Boss, sorry, there was so much traffic on the road, I almost got late,” Yu Yongsheng said as he jumped out of the vehicle. “I didn’t expect borrowing an escort vehicle would be so troublesome. Luckily, the vehicle manager said a vehicle originally scheduled for an outbound mission had its mission canceled, so I was able to save myself a lot of paperwork and get the vehicle out.”

Lu Tianfeng remained silent as he stared at the escort vehicle, but both Chen Nuolan and Yu Yongsheng noticed something was wrong with his expression.

“Boss… did I get the wrong model?” Yu Yongsheng asked nervously.

“No, you’re right, I was wrong.” Lu Tianfeng sighed and said self-reproachfully, “Why didn’t I think of that?”

Chen Nuolan and Yu Yongsheng looked at each other, confused as to what had gone wrong.

Lu Tianfeng picked up the fake license plate wrapped in newspaper at his feet and handed it to Yu Yongsheng, saying, “Look, this is the fake license plate Tong Yao urgently ordered based on the information I provided.”

“Not bad quality… Ouch!” Yu Yongsheng was suddenly stunned.

The numbers on both the front and back fake license plates were “1M465.”

The license plate number on the escort vehicle parked in front of them was also “1M465.”

“You said you borrowed this vehicle because the mission was canceled. So its original mission was to escort Wang Donglin.”

“What exactly… is going on?” Chen Nuolan asked.

“Besides me, there are others who can sense the flow of time, and they clearly know our target is Wang Donglin,” Lu Tianfeng said with a forced smile. “So, someone has managed to change the escort process, completely thwarting our previous plan.”

Yu Yongsheng was stunned and said, “What should we do? We’re out of time.”

“No, we still have over an hour.” Lu Tianfeng knew he couldn’t show any sign of discouragement. If he lost his fighting spirit, the entire team would collapse.

But what could he do in just over an hour?

A strong sense of powerlessness washed over him, and his body seemed to ache again.

.

May 31st, 10:15 a.m., D City Detention Center, playground.

A white commercial vehicle, seemingly ordinary on the outside but actually modified internally, parked outside the main entrance of the detention center office building.

Wang Donglin, dressed in casual clothes, emerged from the building. The strong sunlight made him squint, and he was momentarily overwhelmed.

“What a beautiful day!” he sighed to himself.

Although still cuffed and shackled, Wang Donglin had the illusion of being free.

“Hurry up and get in the car!” the escorting officer urged.

Wang Donglin squinted at the man—he was in his early twenties, his uniform brand new, likely a rookie cop who had just graduated. His expression couldn’t conceal his dislike for Wang Donglin.

Haha, what a childish fellow.

Because of the shackles, Wang Donglin struggled to get into the car, and the young officer didn’t even bother to offer a hand.

Also sitting in the car was another escorting officer, his expression serious. He was probably around forty years old. He held a rifle in his right hand, his left hand resting on his knee. He must have been a veteran who had seen a lot. He looked at Wang Donglin with a look similarly filled with anger and indifference.

Wang Donglin didn’t seem to mind. He casually plopped down in the seat next to the middle-aged officer and greeted him, “Comrade, thank you for your hard work today!”

“Just a job,” the middle-aged officer replied coldly, clearly not wanting to engage in conversation.

The young officer carefully checked Wang Donglin’s handcuffs and shackles, then conducted a thorough body search. After confirming there were no issues, he nodded to the middle-aged officer and said, “Brother Long, we’re ready to go.”

“Let me take another look.” Brother Long, presumably the escort, carefully checked Wang Donglin’s entire body. Then he gestured to the driver, who immediately understood and started the car.

Wang Donglin cast his gaze out the car window, like a child longing for nectar. Unexpectedly, as soon as the car left the detention center, Brother Long had drawn all the curtains in the back seat, completely covering the windows.

“We should keep a low profile. There are a lot of people out there who would love to skin you alive,” Brother Long observed, noticing Wang Donglin’s annoyance and remarking dismissively.

“It’s okay. This is fine. The sun’s glaring.” Wang Donglin shrugged, seemingly unfazed.

The young officer stared at Wang Donglin the moment he got in the car, his lips tightly pursed, as if he wanted to say something but didn’t know where to begin. Wang Donglin understood and pleasantly asked, “Young man, what’s your name?”

“Me?” The young officer paused, glancing at Brother Long as if seeking his opinion.

Brother Long curled his lips but remained silent.

“Just call me Xiao Su.”

“Brother Long, Xiao Su, we’re quite connected!” Wang Donglin said with a smile. “I’m sure you’re both hoping this trip leads to my execution, not to a psychiatric hospital, right?”

Brother Long and Xiao Su exchanged awkward glances.

“Actually, I feel the same way as you—” Wang Donglin’s voice suddenly took on a chilling tone. “People like Wang Donglin deserve to die!”

Brother Long’s face darkened, and his hand on his gun tensed. Xiao Su instinctively reached for the pistol at his waist.

“How ironic! The law actually protects murderers! Hahahaha—” Wang Donglin’s laughter echoed throughout the small vehicle. Although still an unarmed prisoner, his aura completely overwhelmed the two armed police officers.

“What do you mean by that?” Brother Long, once again, remained composed and demanded.

Just then, the driver, who had been driving quietly, suddenly said, “Brother Long, look at that red car behind us. It seems to have been following us.”

Brother Long glanced through the rear window and frowned, “How long has it been following us?”

“I noticed it since I left the detention center. It’s been following us for at least five minutes.”

“Slow down, turn on your hazard lights, and pull over,” Brother Long ordered.

The driver did as he was told. The red car finally slowly changed lanes, overtook the other car, and sped away. Brother Long gazed in the car’s direction, lost in thought.

Xiao Su breathed a sigh of relief. “Thank goodness it was just a false alarm.”

Brother Long’s expression remained unrelenting: “Better safe than sorry.”

At that moment, Wang Donglin had actually closed his eyes, ignoring the brief incident, but it was clear he couldn’t have fallen asleep so quickly.

A sleeping demon was still a demon.

Brother Long couldn’t help but shudder, then pulled a pack of cigarettes from his pocket. Xiao Su pretended not to notice. Although smoking was forbidden during a mission, no one bothered to stop him.

.

May 31st, 10:30 a.m., D City Highway Network, Ring Road.

Yu Yongsheng was driving the Huaquan Security escort vehicle, while Lu Tianfeng sat in the passenger seat, answering a phone call.

“Feng, I think I’ve been spotted. Their car suddenly pulled over, and I can’t follow.” It was Chen Nuolan on the other end.

“It’s okay. The car’s route shouldn’t change. I just wanted to give them a sense of panic.”

“Where am I going next?” Chen Nuolan asked.

Lu Tianfeng hesitated, not answering immediately. Chen Nuolan keenly noticed the unnecessary pause.

“Don’t worry too much; just speak frankly.”

Lu Tianfeng smiled bitterly. “Nuolan, you really understand me. I can’t think of a better solution right now. The only solution is the simplest and most drastic one—rob the prison van before the enemy does.”

“What? Feng, are you kidding?” Chen Nuolan exclaimed in surprise.

Not only Chen Nuolan but also Yu Yongsheng, who was driving, was taken aback. They had originally planned to simply delay the prison van’s journey, but how had it suddenly become a robbery?

“It’s still not too late to back out of this plan. I’ll keep it a secret from Tong Yao for now,” Lu Tianfeng said, his eyes fixed on Yu Yongsheng.

Chen Nuolan almost immediately replied, “Don’t be silly! How could I possibly quit?”

“Then go home and wait for me,” Lu Tianfeng instructed briefly before hanging up the phone. He then addressed Yu Yongsheng sternly, “Yongsheng, this is a very risky matter. If you back out, I won’t blame you.”

“Boss, I’m committed to you.” Yu Yongsheng slammed the steering wheel. “I just don’t understand. Isn’t it a bit unfair for you not to discuss this with Tong Yao?”

“No, I don’t want to leave any clues. If we kidnap Wang Donglin, we’ll definitely be wanted by the police. Tong Yao will be our insider.”

“Have you made an appointment with her?”

“No, but she’ll definitely understand what I mean,” Lu Tianfeng said, glancing in the rearview mirror. “Yongsheng, this is your last chance to get out of the car.”

Yu Yongsheng also glanced in the rearview mirror and clearly saw the prison van carrying Wang Donglin following behind them.

“Boss, I won’t get out of the car, but there are only two of us and no weapons, while the other side has four and guns…” Yu Yongsheng wasn’t afraid of being outnumbered, but the disparity in strength was too great.

“Someone will help us.”

“Who? Didn’t you say you didn’t notify Tong Yao?”

“An enemy spy.” Lu Tianfeng tapped the window lightly. “I just figured out why the on-site forensics I saw on June 2nd showed the criminals firing wildly, while the escort only fired three shots.”

Yu Yongsheng suddenly realized, “Did the spy tamper with the situation?”

“Yes, the criminals’ spy must be in the escort car, using drugs or something to neutralize the escort. And I can guess who it is.” Lu Tianfeng recalled the information he had seen in the “future.” “The criminals not only shot Wang Donglin but also wanted to silence the spy. So the escort who died in the shootout must be the spy.”

“So, who is it…”

“It’s the person in charge of this escort mission, Long Zhixun, known as Brother Long—take the exit ahead and then go down Xifeng Road,” Lu Tianfeng reminded him.

“They took the exit, too.” Yu Yongsheng kept glancing in the rearview mirror.

“Speed ​​up, get away from them,” Lu Tianfeng said calmly. “We’ll get there first and attack inside the first tunnel on Fuhe Road.”

CONTENT END 70

chapters.title: Chapter 71
chapters.content:
May 31st, 11:00 a.m., Fuhe Road was lightly trafficked.

The prison van carrying Wang Donglin entered the tunnel, its speed steadily decreasing.

“Drive carefully; don’t fall asleep!” Brother Long suddenly patted the driver’s shoulder.

“Oh, sorry!” The driver seemed startled, coming to his senses.

“Didn’t you get a good night’s rest last night?”

“No, probably spring fatigue,” the driver said with a self-deprecating chuckle.

Brother Long knew full well that this wasn’t spring fatigue but rather the tranquilizer he’d hidden in his cigarettes.

“Everyone, cheer up… Eh? What’s on the road?”

Brother Long saw a security company escort vehicle parked diagonally in the middle of the road not far away, its hazard lights on, completely blocking the two-lane tunnel. A man in a Huaquan security uniform crouched on the side of the road, his head buried between his knees. He wondered if he was injured.

“What’s going on?” Xiao Su rubbed his eyes and yawned.

“It looks like a car accident. You guys go down and take a look. I’ll guard the prisoner here.” Brother Long felt his heartbeat quicken. Hadn’t they agreed to strike in the second tunnel? Why did they do it earlier?

“Okay.” Xiao Su and the other two escorts got out of the vehicle. Even though the man appeared to be injured, they remained vigilant, their hands on their guns.

“Hey, big brother, are you all right?” Xiao Su asked, raising his voice.

The uniformed man was naturally Yu Yongsheng. Without even looking up, he feigned pain as he said, “I’m fine… Is the cargo in my car… all right?”

Xiao Su and the driver exchanged glances. They both raised their guns, aiming at the rear door of the escort vehicle, while the other pointed a gun at Yu Yongsheng.

“Who are you?”

“I… am just an errand boy…”

Xiao Su shouted, “How could you be the only one carrying out a security company mission?”

“My colleagues… may have stolen the cargo…” Yu Yongsheng finished, feigning exhaustion and collapsing to the ground.

The three of them exchanged glances, and finally Xiao Su said, “Let’s take a look inside the car. If everything’s alright, we’ll move it out of the way. Once we’re out of the tunnel, we can call the traffic police. After all, we can’t afford to let that guy in our car down.”

The other two nodded in agreement. Of course, they were a little puzzled by the fact that Brother Long, who was in charge of directing the operation, had remained seated in the car the entire time, giving no instructions.

At this moment, Brother Long, who remained in the car, was even more restless. He had a vague feeling that the situation was getting out of control, but he didn’t know what to do.

“Are you nervous?” Each word was harsh. The speaker was Wang Donglin.

The frail scholar from before had transformed into a terrifying man emanating a chill.

“Shut up! Stop talking nonsense!”

“Brother Long, your fingers are twitching unconsciously, and your heartbeat is much faster than before.” Wang Donglin glanced at the escort vehicle not far away. “And you’re staring at the car in front, as if you knew that if the door opened, something bad would happen.”

Brother Long felt as if all his strength had been drained. Although he had taken the antidote beforehand, so the tranquilizer shouldn’t work on him, he felt inexplicably dizzy.

“What did you put in that cigarette you just smoked?” Wang Donglin sneered.

Beads of sweat formed on Brother Long’s forehead. He only just realized that the tranquilizer seemed to have no effect on Wang Donglin at all.

But he didn’t have time to dwell on it. A few meters away, Xiao Su and the others had already carefully opened the back door of the escort van.

Though they were on full alert, their guns trained on the van, they never imagined that the contents inside were beyond the reach of bullets.

As the door swung open, a continuous buzzing sound filled their ears, accompanied by a whirlwind of black air, followed by stinging and numbness.

“It’s bees!”

“Get down, cover your face—Ouch!”

“Ahhh—what’s going on!”

The hormone-induced bees attacked their targets frantically. Even though the three men ducked immediately, they couldn’t avoid the stings. Xiao Su struggled to crawl toward the prison van, hoping to call for help from Brother Long, but after only a few meters, his vision went black and he passed out. The bee toxins and the tranquilizer they had inhaled produced a remarkable chemical reaction, and all three men quickly fell silent.

Brother Long finally lost his patience and leaped from the car, gun in hand. However, before his feet even touched the ground, he was struck hard on the back of the head, collapsing to the ground.

“Don’t hurt my son… You asked… I did…” Brother Long’s head was splitting with pain, his eyes shimmering with stars. He couldn’t see the attacker clearly and could only mutter a plea for mercy.

“You were so foolish!” Lu Tianfeng lamented, feeling overwhelmed. Brother Long’s fleeting thought nearly sent everyone in the car to their doom. He sighed deeply, punched Brother Long again, knocking him to the ground, and then jumped into the driver’s seat.

Lu Tianfeng looked back and saw a pair of bright eyes staring back at him from the dark car.

“Wang Donglin, I’m here to help you.”

Wang Donglin snorted, remaining noncommittal.

Lu Tianfeng didn’t have time to waste chatting with Wang Donglin. He simply stepped on the accelerator, turned the steering wheel, and used the tunnel’s emergency exit to force a U-turn.

At this moment, Yu Yongsheng rushed forward and tried to open the car door to get in but found it locked. Bewildered, he shouted, “Boss, open the door!”

“Yongsheng, it’s harder to conceal our whereabouts with more people. Let me bear the blame for kidnapping a serious criminal.”

“How can you…”

“Let’s split up. You buy me some time.”

Yu Yongsheng reluctantly stepped aside. He knew full well that Lu Tianfeng’s choice was rational. If everyone acted together, it would be nearly impossible to escape the police’s tight net.

“Take care, Boss.”

“You too.” Lu Tianfeng stepped on the accelerator, and the prison van sped away.

.

May 31st, 11:10 a.m., on the highway beside the railway.

Lu Tianfeng finally stopped the van and jumped out.

Inside the vehicle, Wang Donglin, who had been sitting silently in the shadows, suddenly laughed. “You’re all alone, and you think you can take me away like this? Do you really think the police are idiots?”

“If you don’t want to die, you’d better obey,” Lu Tianfeng retorted harshly. “Did you know that the electronic anklet you’re wearing has a tracker? If you don’t have the password to unlock it, it’s useless to escape to the ends of the earth.”

Wang Donglin’s mouth twitched. He truly didn’t know that.

“And I happen to know the password.” Lu Tianfeng had a photographic memory; he’d seen this information in the files, but naturally, he wouldn’t tell Wang Donglin the truth.

“How could it be…” Wang Donglin was stunned.

“Ding—” Lu Tianfeng swiftly removed the anklet and refastened it, the whole process taking only seconds.

“That way, the pursuers will think the shackles are still on you.”

Wang Donglin stared at the shackles dangling in Lu Tianfeng’s hand without saying a word.

“Many freight trains pass through this area, and we can just throw the shackles onto one of them…” As he spoke, they could already hear the roar of the train approaching.

“Clack, clack, clack—”

With the increasing popularity of high-speed rail, fewer and fewer people remember this sound of the past.

“Then we can mislead the police.” Wang Donglin grinned, laughing unrestrainedly.

“Woo—”

A locomotive, belching black smoke, came into view.

Lu Tianfeng sighed, “Is humanity’s increasing reliance on high technology a good thing or a bad thing?”

No one could answer that question.

As the freight train passed them, Lu Tianfeng accurately tossed the shackles into one of the cars, and Wang Donglin breathed a sigh of relief.

“Don’t be too happy. This little trick will only delay the police pursuit by an hour or two at most. We must not let our guard down from now on. The train can’t move anymore. Let’s go.”

Lu Tianfeng stepped forward, but Wang Donglin stood there motionless, his eyes glazed over, his mind dazed, and his expression strange.

“Who are you? Why should I go with you?” Wang Donglin’s eyes were filled with suspicion and wariness.

“It’s a long story. Let’s talk somewhere else. Your only choice is to trust me and come with me.”

Wang Donglin remained skeptical and didn’t move.

“My name is Lu Tianfeng. I’m a police officer. I’m now responsible for protecting you.” Lu Tianfeng had no choice but to produce his ID.

“Police? I don’t understand…” Wang Donglin remained bewildered. “In short, someone was trying to kill you in the Fuhe Road Tunnel, and I saved you. But if you keep wasting time, you’ll have to bear the consequences.”

“Someone wanted to kill me?”

“Isn’t that strange? Don’t you know what crime you’ve committed? Don’t you know that over ten million people have signed a petition online demanding your death?”

Wang Donglin’s face suddenly turned pale, his lips trembling, but no sound came out.

“Let’s go. Let me remind you, the person who wanted to kill you has a spy planted within the police, so for now we’ll have to rely on ourselves.”

Wang Donglin no longer objected. He obediently followed Lu Tianfeng across the railway and into an unknown alley.

CONTENT END 71

chapters.title: Chapter 72
chapters.content:
May 31st, 11:30 a.m., in a small, neatly decorated apartment less than 20 square meters.

“Take a seat.” Lu Tianfeng entered and locked the door behind him.

Wang Donglin didn’t sit down immediately but instead surveyed his surroundings. This place didn’t resemble Lu Tianfeng’s home. The furniture and decor were so simple they barely conveyed a sense of life. However, the tables, chairs, and floor were all clean; it couldn’t possibly have been vacant for years.

“What is this place?” Wang Donglin couldn’t help but ask.

“A place no one knows about.” Lu Tianfeng handed Wang Donglin a bottle of mineral water. “To avoid the police, you need to remember two things: first, don’t let anyone know your whereabouts; second, minimize contact with others. These two points may seem simple, but they’re incredibly difficult to achieve in modern society. Technology is so advanced that it’s difficult to remain completely invisible.”

“So… is this place safe?” Wang Donglin sat down nervously.

“At least for a short while.”

Lu Tianfeng had secretly rented this small apartment under a false name after the Feng Teng Gene case came to an end. He had initially intended to leave a fallback for himself and Chen Nuolan so they could use the apartment as a refuge in case of an emergency. Since he was suspended from work, he had plenty of time, so he came here every two or three days to clean up, then quietly read for a while, a way to relax.

But today, the tranquility of this small space seemed to be shattered forever.

Wang Donglin had only sat for a moment when he couldn’t contain his excitement. He stood up and paced back and forth, occasionally nervously lifting the curtains to observe the movements outside.

“What should we do next?”

“Wait.” Lu Tianfeng turned on the TV. Earlier, he had deliberately abandoned his phone at the Fuhe Road scene to prevent tracking. Currently, TV news was their only source of information from the outside world.

“Just sit there and wait?” Wang Donglin frowned. “Based on the driving and walking time just now, we’re only three or four kilometers from the crime scene! Staying that close is too dangerous.”

Lu Tianfeng glanced at Wang Donglin and said expressionlessly, “I didn’t expect you to have such a solid knowledge of counter-reconnaissance.”

“I’m just showing off my skills,” Wang Donglin said awkwardly.

“Don’t worry. The electronic anklet will draw the police’s attention to the extensive railway system. We have every chance of escaping. Why stay so close to the crime scene? It doesn’t make sense.”

“Yes, it’s suicidal.”

“Because it’s irrational, no one will think of it. So we’re safe for now,” Lu Tianfeng sighed. “We have at least four to six hours of buffer time.”

Wang Donglin lowered his head in thought. He seemed to understand Lu Tianfeng’s strategy. “Besides, we’re not just waiting here. We need to use this time to resolve two crucial issues—” Lu Tianfeng’s eyes flashed sharply. “Who is hunting you, and who is saving you?”

“I… I don’t know who’s trying to kill me. Besides, wasn’t it you who saved me?” Wang Donglin shook his head repeatedly, his eyes blank. It didn’t look like he was acting.

Lu Tianfeng’s heart sank. He vaguely remembered Pig-Head’s words, “We’ll handle the rest.” Could it be that Wang Donglin didn’t know Pig-Head’s gang at all?

Unfortunately, given the current situation, if he wanted to turn the tide, he had to evade this police pursuit first and then find a way to uncover the truth.

“But you should be well aware of what you’ve done.” Lu Tianfeng, determined to keep pressuring Wang Donglin, stared at him intently and spoke in an aggressive tone. “In the past year, you’ve killed four women. Behind each of them lies her family, classmates, friends, and lover. These people naturally hate you to the core.”

Wang Donglin’s head gradually dropped, his fingers nervously intertwined.

“Tell me all about your crimes, and we’ll analyze who would go to such great lengths to eliminate you.”

At this, Wang Donglin suddenly looked up and gazed at Lu Tianfeng with a complex expression. Then, he grinned uncontrollably.

“I finally understand. This is your true purpose, isn’t it?”

“What did you say?” Lu Tianfeng was lost in thought.

“You self-righteous policemen are hell-bent on killing me, so you orchestrated this grand prison van hijacking in hopes of tricking me into revealing the so-called truth.” Wang Donglin’s expression darkened, his eyes gleaming with a murderous glare. “I’ve already said everything I needed to say. I did kill the man, but I know nothing else.”

Lu Tianfeng finally understood; Wang Donglin had completely misinterpreted his intentions.

“You’re such a jerk…” Lu Tianfeng was about to curse him harshly, but he froze mid-sentence, a terrifying thought flashing through his mind.

Why was Wang Donglin so wary?

Could there really be some unspoken secret behind the four murders he was responsible for?

Lu Tianfeng tried to recall the day before time had flown back, when he had spent the entire afternoon researching the prison van hijacking. Although the files from that time contained information related to Wang Donglin’s serial killings, he had only skimmed through them. What impressed him most was Wang Donglin’s method of killing: he would knock his victims unconscious and then drown them in the bathtub; he never sexually assaulted them. Another noteworthy detail was that Wang Donglin would remove a piece of jewelry from his victims, using it as a “souvenir” and burying it somewhere in the city.

The first victim’s hairpin, the second victim’s ring, the third victim’s necklace, and the fourth victim’s keychain—of these four “souvenirs,” the police ultimately only found the hairpin and necklace, buried in two different locations. The other two “souvenirs” were never found, and Wang Donglin remained completely secretive about their whereabouts.

Lu Tianfeng vaguely felt that the two missing “souvenirs” might be a crucial clue, directly or indirectly connected to why Wang Donglin was being hunted.

At this moment, Wang Donglin exuded a wild and dangerous aura.

“I won’t be fooled.”

After saying these words, Wang Donglin’s features instantly relaxed. Within seconds, he looked at Lu Tianfeng in bewilderment, like a completely different person.

Witnessing Wang Donglin’s complete transformation, Lu Tianfeng felt a chill run down his spine.

Was releasing this beast from its cage truly the right decision?

Lu Tianfeng’s internal organs began to ache again.

.

May 31st, 11:40 a.m., D City Police Department Building.

Starting at 11:15 a.m., the phone in Director Luo’s office rang incessantly, without a single pause. Exasperated, he simply hung up the landline and set his cellphone to silent mode, ignoring all calls in an effort to find a moment of peace and quiet.

In just half an hour, Wang Donglin’s escape became the focus of the entire city’s attention. Even Director Luo, accustomed to the turmoil of events, found the situation a distressing one. At this moment, Tong Yao’s name appeared on the silent phone screen.

Director Luo’s brow furrowed. He had a good impression of Tong Yao: young, energetic, and capable. However, they were several levels apart and rarely interacted. He couldn’t understand why she had come directly to him.

Director Luo answered the call.

“Director Luo, this is Tong Yao from the First Detachment of the Criminal Investigation Brigade.” The signal on the other end was poor, and the voice was very distorted.

“I know. What’s the matter?”

“Director Luo, I’m at the scene on Fuhe Road. To cut to the chase: I know it was Lu Tianfeng who took Wang Donglin away, but I’m asking you to temporarily suspend the public arrest warrant for him.”

Director Luo’s brows knitted even deeper. The Wang Donglin incident alone was already a source of anxiety, so how could Lu Tianfeng, currently under suspension for investigation, be implicated? Moreover, he heard a subtext in Tong Yao’s words: this rising star seemed to be implicated in the incident as well.

“Explain to me exactly what’s going on?”

“Director Luo, Captain Lu received reliable intelligence from an informant claiming someone was planning to hijack the prison van and kill Wang Donglin. That’s why he took the initiative and protected Wang Donglin before the criminals could act.”

“Ridiculous! Why didn’t he report the intelligence through proper procedures and arrange for police reinforcements?” Director Luo’s rage was almost unbearable. “What could he accomplish on his own? Do you think you’re filming a Hollywood movie?”

“Captain Lu said there’s a mole planted within the force by the criminals, and he’s afraid of alerting them…” “A traitor?” Director Luo was stunned. “Do you have any evidence?”

“Not yet.”

Director Luo sighed. “Isn’t this just Lu Tianfeng messing around? Contact him immediately and tell him to bring Wang Donglin back! I’ll find a way to deal with the aftermath and minimize the impact.”

“Sorry, Director Luo, I can’t contact Captain Lu either.”

Director Luo’s voice trembled with rage. “What are you doing? Tong Yao, you have half an hour to come back and explain yourself to me!”

Director Luo hung up without waiting for Tong Yao’s reply. Unexpectedly, within ten seconds, another call came in.

“It never ends…”

.

May 31st, 12:00 p.m., in the small shelter apartment.

Lu Tianfeng and Wang Donglin sat in silence in front of the TV, watching the midday news.

Internet summit, new subway line opening, falling vegetable market prices, and sunny weather for the next few days… Until the news ended half an hour later and the host smiled and said goodbye to the audience, Lu Tianfeng’s expression grew even uglier.

Wang Donglin sneered, “Officer Lu, such a major news event, and the TV station didn’t even report it verbally. What do you think is going on?”

“I don’t know. This isn’t normal.”

“Stop playing dumb. I’ve always guessed this was just a police ploy. This robbery never happened. Your trap-laying skills are terrible!” Wang Donglin stood up and stretched. “Alright, take me back to where I belong. I hear the D City Psychiatric Hospital is nestled in the mountains and by the water, with nice views.”

Lu Tianfeng didn’t bother to respond. His mind replayed today’s operation over and over again, wondering how he would arrange the pursuit if he were the police commander. Checking the surrounding surveillance, identifying the suspect, tracing their escape route, and tracking them electronically…

“Oh no!” Lu Tianfeng suddenly cried out, lost in thought. He had finally discovered a potentially fatal error—the electronic anklet with a tracking device.

With surveillance cameras everywhere, it would only take the police fifteen minutes to identify Lu Tianfeng as the key suspect, so the capture strategy would inevitably target him personally.

For example, if he had indeed taken Wang Donglin aboard the train, he would have been well aware of the tracking device in the anklet and would have quickly found a way to disable it or block the signal. It was impossible for him to ignore it.

However, the anklet’s tracking signal remained uninterrupted. This alone suggested that the current signal was likely a sham—either they hadn’t boarded the train at all, or they had removed the shackles and escaped.

If the police commander was clever enough or familiar with Lu Tianfeng, they could easily deduce their hiding place based on the location where they abandoned the train. Lu Tianfeng immediately tensed at this thought.

“We have to leave now.”

“What’s the matter? Isn’t everything calm now?” Wang Donglin remained nonchalant, as if convinced Lu Tianfeng was playing tricks on him.

“The police may have already located our area. If we don’t leave now, it’ll be too late.”

Before he finished speaking, there was a rapid knock on the door.

.

May 31st, 12:10 p.m., Tiedao New Village, a busy intersection.

A black commercial vehicle was parked on the side of the road. Lu Tianfeng’s superior, Cheng Tuo, captain of the Seventh Detachment of the Criminal Police Brigade, was inside, remotely directing hundreds of plainclothes officers and auxiliary police officers to quietly cordon off the entire block and conduct a blanket search.

“Captain Cheng, the personnel are assembled and ready to begin the search at any time,” a young officer in the uniform of a gas company safety inspector reported.

“Very good, act immediately, and be careful not to alert the enemy.” Cheng Tuo thought for a moment, then asked, “How long do you estimate it will take?”

“Tiedao New Village is large, with a large population, plus a large number of migrant workers and rental housing. The search may take quite a while…”

“Just state your conclusion,” Cheng Tuo interrupted his subordinate impatiently.

“Based on the current manpower allocation, a preliminary search will take at least six hours.”

“No, that’s too slow. We must find them within two hours, or we’ll have no more time to search here,” Cheng Tuo said firmly. “You guys start the search; I’ll request reinforcements.”

“Understood.” The young police officer took his orders and left.

Cheng Tuo looked out the window at the bustling traffic and couldn’t help but sigh. He was well aware of the state of Tiedao New Village. The once-prosperous large residential complex that had opened twenty years ago now looked out of step with the times. Poor road planning, a lack of supporting facilities, and severe noise pollution due to its proximity to the railway had led many locals to avoid living here, renting their homes to migrant workers instead. Consequently, public security in this area was notoriously chaotic.

The gray buildings not far away resembled a forest of steel and concrete, yet no one knew how many dangers lurked within this forest.

CONTENT END 72

chapters.title: Chapter 73
chapters.content:
May 31st, 12:30 p.m., inside the small apartment.

Lu Tianfeng gestured to Wang Donglin, signaling him to hide in the bathroom. Then he approached the door and put his eyes to the peephole. He saw a tall, thin man standing outside. He wore a baseball cap and a tracksuit, holding a small stack of flyers. He looked like a college student working part-time, though a bit older.

“Who is this?” Lu Tianfeng asked through the door.

“Zhicheng Housekeeping Service, could you spare some time?”

“No, thank you.” Lu Tianfeng didn’t even open the door, observing through the peephole. Rejected, the man stood there for a moment, helpless, before turning and leaving.

Wang Donglin emerged from the bathroom upon hearing the noise and said casually, “It’s just a salesman. Officer Lu, there’s no need to get so alarmed.”

To his surprise, Lu Tianfeng simply said, “Let’s leave immediately.”

“What’s going on?” Wang Donglin noticed that Lu Tianfeng was definitely not joking.

“The man who knocked on the door just now wasn’t a salesman. First, he had too few flyers. This building has over a hundred households, and he only had a dozen or so.
