Second, after being turned away, he left without even leaving a single flyer. Third, he didn’t go door-to-door next door to continue selling but went straight down the stairs. These three points combined make it almost certain he’s an imposter.”

Wang Donglin’s expression grew nervous. “So he’s a plainclothes police officer?”

“His behavior doesn’t seem like a police officer. Of course, it could be that he’s an exceptionally skilled actor, but a plainclothes agent with such skill wouldn’t reveal so many flaws.” Lu Tianfeng took a deep breath. “It’s more likely that this man is one of the assassins who wants to kill you.”

“How… could they possibly have found their way here?” Wang Donglin’s face turned red and pale, his face skeptical.

“We can think about that later. Right now, we need to figure out how to get out.” Lu Tianfeng pulled a waist bag from under the coffee table and strapped it to his waist. “Hurry!”

Lu Tianfeng didn’t hesitate. He knew he was facing at least four enemies—probably professional assassins or mercenaries. They were not only strong individually but also had excellent teamwork. Unarmed, he and Wang Donglin would be no match for them. Their only chance was to escape before they formed a circle.

“Let’s head to the rooftop.”

Since Lu Tianfeng had rented this apartment for emergencies, he had naturally considered an emergency escape route. The building had nine floors, and they were on the seventh. The stairs could reach the rooftop in half a minute. Furthermore, the building was connected to three other buildings of the same structure, so reaching the rooftop would provide three additional escape routes.

Although Wang Donglin didn’t understand the situation, he knew he had no choice but to follow Lu Tianfeng. The two hurriedly left the apartment and ascended the stairs to the ninth floor. Although a sign warning “Rooftop Dangerous, No Trespassing” adorned the rooftop’s iron gate, the lock had long since rusted and fallen off. Pushing the gate open, they were greeted by clotheslines and drying racks strewn with clothes. There were also patches of self-designated “green belts,” some filled with bonsai, others planted with vegetables, and even vineyards growing on trellises. It felt more vibrant and alive than the cold, concrete jungle below.

“This way.”

Lu Tianfeng, not bothering to avoid the tangled mess of clothes, dove under a quilt. After walking a short distance, a middle-aged man with a shaggy haircut suddenly appeared before them. He, likewise, roughly pushed aside the clothes blocking his path and approached.

Lu Tianfeng and the man made eye contact, and they both instinctively dodged to the side. When the man noticed Wang Donglin following Lu Tianfeng, his eyes glared, and his right hand quickly reached for his waist.

Lu Tianfeng reacted quickly, grabbing a nearby white shirt and removing the metal hanger. He realized that the rooftop was deserted at noon, and this seemingly random man might very well be one of the assassins out to flank him!

Sure enough, the next second, Lu Tianfeng saw the cold gleam of a dagger.

“Back off!” Lu Tianfeng shouted at Wang Donglin, simultaneously using the hanger in his hand to meet the opponent’s dagger.

Although the hanger didn’t pose much of a threat, its unusual shape made it a powerful weapon. After a few exchanges of blows, Lu Tianfeng surprisingly held his own.

The assassin took a small step back, dagger raised, and assumed a defensive stance, seemingly abandoning his attack. Lu Tianfeng immediately understood that he was waiting for reinforcements and that the opponent would likely arrive on the rooftop soon.

“Wang Donglin, run!” Lu Tianfeng acted decisively, shouting.

“Run? Where to?”

“Anywhere, as long as you don’t look back.”

Wang Donglin wasn’t stupid. He immediately understood that Lu Tianfeng was simply trying to break the stalemate, so he took off running.

Lu Tianfeng was actually quite nervous. He wasn’t sure if Wang Donglin would still obey his orders once he ran far away. But he knew better than to try to remain calm and force the other party to become even more anxious than he was.

However, the killer’s move was beyond Lu Tianfeng’s expectations—he threw the dagger like a flying knife, aiming it at Wang Donglin’s back!

“Get down!” Lu Tianfeng shouted.

The dagger’s impact was powerful and deadly, leaving Wang Donglin unable to react. He stumbled over something, nearly falling, and narrowly avoided the fatal blow.

The blade whistled past Wang Donglin’s ear. For the first time, he felt so close to death. His legs gave way, and he sat dumbfounded on the ground.

In a flash, the killer had drawn his pistol and aimed it at Wang Donglin. He couldn’t care less now; his only thought was to complete the mission.

Lu Tianfeng reacted quickly, picking up a sheet drying nearby and throwing it at the killer.

“Bang!”

The killer’s vision was obscured by the bed sheet, and the bullet only shattered the flowerpot at Wang Donglin’s feet.

Before the killer could fire a second shot, Lu Tianfeng rushed forward, holding a clothesline, and thrust it straight at the killer’s throat. In close combat, the pistol was useless, and the killer had to grab the clothesline with his bare hands, forcing Lu Tianfeng into close combat.

Lu Tianfeng launched a punch straight into the killer’s chest, but the killer easily blocked it with his elbow. Even this single round of fighting made Lu Tianfeng groan inwardly. The two were evenly matched in strength. If he couldn’t defeat the other quickly, it meant the enemy could stall until reinforcements arrived. Furthermore, he had to keep an eye on the other’s gun, unable to let his guard down even for a moment.

This was a nearly hopeless situation.

Instantly, the killer’s fists struck again and again. His goal was clear: whether to buy time for his companions to arrive or to repel Lu Tianfeng so he could fire, he was willing to accept it.

Lu Tianfeng dodged left and right, momentarily forced to defend himself. The killer, gaining the upper hand, launched an unstoppable attack. Taking advantage of Lu Tianfeng’s delay, he launched a sweeping kick, knocking him to the ground.

Lu Tianfeng quickly rolled awkwardly out of the way.

The killer let out a strange cry and was about to launch another flying kick at Lu Tianfeng when he suddenly stopped.

A dagger lodged in the killer’s waist.

Wang Donglin, with a cold expression, half-crouched on the ground and, with a rather awkward gesture, thrust the blade into his enemy’s body.

The killer’s lips twitched as he stared at the dagger in disbelief. His right hand grasped the hilt, as if trying to pull it out, but he dared not force it. He spat blood and collapsed to the ground.

Lu Tianfeng finally caught his breath and smiled bitterly, “Although your move was embarrassing, it was quite effective.”

Wang Donglin’s voice was chillingly cold: “This man’s still breathing. Do you want to give him another blow?”

Lu Tianfeng was stunned for a moment, then simply said, “Let’s go!”

Wang Donglin chuckled and said, “Officer Lu, you’re a good man. I bet you’ve killed even more people than I have.”

Lu Tianfeng didn’t answer.

The two of them ran silently across the rooftop and down the stairs of another building. When they reached the second floor, Lu Tianfeng waved and signaled for them not to continue down. Instead, they reached the end of the second-floor corridor, climbed over the railing, and leaped onto the wall. After walking a short distance along the wall, they jumped into another alley.

This was one of Lu Tianfeng’s initial considerations in choosing Tiedao New Village as the emergency shelter. The old building plan resulted in insufficient spacing between buildings, which in turn provided more escape routes.

In the alley, a courier had just finished delivering a full load of packages that morning and was about to return to his office when he saw two men scaling a wall in broad daylight. The righteous courier was about to yell, “Catch the thieves!” but Lu Tianfeng got there first, flashing his officer ID.

“The police are on a special mission and need to requisition your car.” Lu Tianfeng immediately took a liking to the electric delivery vehicle. Although the cabin was small, it was more than enough for Wang Donglin to hide.

The courier had only seen this kind of situation in movies before and was speechless, at a loss for words. Lu Tianfeng jumped into the driver’s seat, and Wang Donglin quickly climbed in.

“Go to Qingfeng Street to retrieve your car in half an hour.”

After saying this, Lu Tianfeng stepped firmly on the accelerator and slowly sped away.

Soon, the electric car arrived at Qingfeng Street. When Wang Donglin emerged, he was stunned and asked, “Why are we actually here?”

“Because there’s a bus stop here,” Lu Tianfeng pointed to the bus stop ahead.

“Aren’t there surveillance cameras on buses?”

“Yes, that’s why we’re taking one of those illegal taxis.”

Qingfeng Street was one of Tiedao New Village’s main thoroughfares. Many illegally operated minibuses specifically come here to solicit passengers. It had been cracked down on several times before, but Tiedao New Village had a large influx of migrants, and as long as there was market demand, these illegal taxi drivers would still find ways to slip in.

“Come on, come on, going to Moyun Town! Get on board! Hurry!” the conductor shouted.

Lu Tianfeng and Wang Donglin hopped onto the minibus, which was filthy on the outside and not much cleaner on the inside, and sat down in the empty seats in the last row. However, before Wang Donglin could settle down, Lu Tianfeng’s hands began to expertly explore his body. “What the hell is going on…”

“You must have a tracking device on you; otherwise, how could they find us?” Lu Tianfeng said in a low voice.

Wang Donglin finally came to his senses and immediately remembered what happened when he got on the van at the detention center.

“That Brother Long is the mole, right? He searched me…”

“Found it.” Lu Tianfeng plucked a tracking device, smaller than a button, from under Wang Donglin’s collar.

“Damn, high technology is terrifying!” Wang Donglin cursed.

Lu Tianfeng tossed the tracking device out the window. As the car drove out of Tiedao New Village, they finally had a chance to breathe.

“You must tell me your story in detail. Otherwise, the enemy is in the dark, and we’re in the light. We might not be so lucky next time.”

Wang Donglin twitched his lips but said nothing.

But Lu Tianfeng could see that the man before him was wavering.

.

May 31st, 1:10 p.m., Tiedao New Village, intersection, police command vehicle.

“Captain Cheng, a male body was found on the rooftop of Yuelong Building. The cause of death was excessive blood loss from a dagger wound to the abdomen. A fingerprint strongly matching Wang Donglin’s was found on the dagger handle, pending further confirmation.”

“Captain Cheng, we discovered a wooden door in Unit 707 of Meihao Apartments, Block C, Yuelong Building, that had been violently damaged. There were also signs of rummaging inside the room, and a clear fingerprint on the door handle belonged to Wang Donglin.”

As reports from his subordinates continued to pour in, Cheng Tuo’s expression grew increasingly grim.

“Captain Cheng, do we need to seal off the entire building?” the subordinate asked again.

“It’s too late! Immediately retrieve the surveillance footage from all bus stops and major intersections within Tiedao New Village and assign personnel to analyze and investigate. Also, the team conducting the door-to-door search can withdraw…”

“Withdraw? Captain Cheng, do you need to ask your superiors first?”

Wang Donglin was, after all, a high-ranking fugitive. Hundreds of officers were deployed with nothing to show for it. Withdrawing in disgrace was a bit embarrassing.

“Withdraw! That’s an order! I’m going back to the bureau to report on my work.” Cheng Tuo gritted his teeth. The situation had finally gotten out of control.

Lu Tianfeng, you’re really quick to slip away.

CONTENT END 73

chapters.title: Chapter 74
chapters.content:
Memories of Wang Donglin (I)

The first time I was called “other people’s kid1” was when I was less than five years old.

It must have been the Spring Festival. My father took me to visit his colleague, Uncle Li, at his home. When we arrived, Uncle Li was teaching his six-year-old son how to play chess. I was captivated by the intricately shaped, black and white chess pieces, clutching them tightly in my hands like toys, unwilling to let go. So Uncle Li burst into laughter and said, “Let’s learn chess together.”

Two hours later, having just learned the basic rules, I had completely defeated Uncle Li’s son.

Uncle Li smiled, patted my head, and said, “Look at how fast Wang Donglin understands! He’s a true genius! I think in three to five years, he’ll be able to beat Uncle Li!”

Looking back now, Uncle Li’s smile was a bit awkward.

Uncle Li was half right. I was indeed a chess genius. On this battlefield of black and white, I always found winning strategies that my peers couldn’t grasp. But he was also half wrong. Seven months after I officially started learning chess, I defeated him.

It was then that I realized Uncle Li was just an amateur at the entry level. With my father’s support, I was fortunate to study under a provincial chess champion, receiving private lessons three times a week. With unwavering commitment, my chess skills naturally improved dramatically. In first grade, at the age of seven, I won my first tournament—the City Children’s Palace Challenge Tournament. I easily won the first through third grade division with a perfect record.

I have become the “other people’s kid” in the eyes of more and more people, and I was proud of it.

Of course, I also had a happy family that others envied. My father was a surgeon, known for his exceptional skills as one of the hospital’s “Four Masters.” His daily workload was incredibly stressful, and major surgeries often required him to work in the operating room for over ten hours straight. Even so, he dedicated every bit of his free time to playing chess with me, chatting with me, and listening to my childish stories. He never used being busy or tired as an excuse to be perfunctory.

My mother was a piano teacher at a music conservatory. She was incredibly beautiful and looked much younger than her age. I was grateful to have inherited her looks. In my memory, my mother was always gentle and graceful. She quietly took care of all the household chores, kept the house tidy, and cooked delicious meals every day. Because my mother had two winter and summer vacations, while my father rarely had a long vacation, every long trip I took during my childhood was taken with my mother alone.

From elementary school through middle school and high school, I attended the best schools in the country, and my grades consistently ranked in the top ten in my grade. Over time, a rumor arose among my friends, almost like an urban legend, that if I fell out of the top ten in my class, our school would lose a student.

Teenagers were so naive and ignorant. It was ridiculous. How could I not be in the top ten in my class? The knowledge in the textbooks was simply too simple for me, not challenging at all.

What truly excited me was the ever-changing dynamics of chess. I didn’t aspire to be a professional chess player, but I deeply enjoyed the feeling of winning, so I constantly signed up for tournaments of all levels, hoping to one day become a national champion.

At eleven, I won the citywide youth tournament and qualified to represent D City at the national competition. At the national competition held the following year, I fought my way through the competition, defeating several older players and reaching the semifinals. At that time, I envisioned winning two more games, clinching the championship, and making it to the top of the heap. However, I was utterly humiliated in the semifinals of a three-game match. My opponent seemingly effortlessly defeated me in straight sets.

Our chess skills were on a different level.

Then, I witnessed the player who had eliminated me suffer a crushing defeat in the five-game final, losing 0-3, barely holding his own. The champion was a fifteen-year-old boy who appeared to be completely relaxed throughout the match, seemingly playing chess with us as if he were just playing house.

Later, I learned that the winning player had been eliminated from a professional chess tryout. No wonder amateur competitions seemed so easy. But I also saw the huge gap between me and a true professional.

That was the first time I started to doubt that I was a naturally gifted child.

Afterward, I gave up on challenging professional players and became addicted to “beating” weaker opponents on online gaming platforms. I realized it wasn’t chess itself that I loved, but simply the feeling of victory.

Of course, at school, I still found it easy to find my own sense of superiority. In high school, I redirected all the time I’d previously allocated to chess practice to study, and my grades became more consistent. I consistently ranked in the top three in my class on most exams, and my teachers said I had the talent to get into any key university in China.

But when it came time to apply for college in my senior year, I backed out. I chose to stay in D City and accept the recommended admission offer from D City University. Because I was afraid, afraid of failure, afraid that after going to a top prestigious school, I would once again experience the feeling that there was always someone better than me.

I could only accept victory, not failure.

My undergraduate years were uneventful. Although D City University also had many outstanding students, I managed to maintain my top ranking.

In my sophomore year, I fell in love. I had always thought love was a waste of time. Having been adept at rejecting advances from girls since fifth grade, I felt the thrill of young love for the first time. Moli, a junior who was a year younger than me, became my first girlfriend.

With excellent grades, a harmonious family, and a gentle and beautiful girlfriend, and having already secured a spot in graduate school by my senior year, I was still that “other people’s kid.”

Everything collapsed during my first year of graduate school.

I still remember it was a Saturday, my parents’ 30th wedding anniversary. My father sent me a text message in advance, telling me to stay home that weekend so he could spend some time with my mother.

Every year on this day, they would “abandon” me. I had long since grown accustomed to it.

Around 10:00 p.m. that evening, I had just finished studying at the library when I received a call from an unfamiliar number. The line was clamorous, and a loud-voiced man, rasping, told me there had been a serious fire at my house, with casualties, and asked me to return immediately.

At first, I thought it was a scam, but when I called my parents’ cellphones, no one answered. I panicked and quickly took a taxi home. Outside the gate of the residential complex, I could hear the sirens of police cars and ambulances and see thick smoke rising into the sky. In that moment, I knew the call was real.

In the chaos, I couldn’t remember where I went, who I met, or what I said. I felt like a soulless puppet, a puppet on a string, and the hand pulling the strings was fate.

“There were two people in the bedroom… a man and a woman…”

“They seemed to have drunk red wine and were fast asleep, unable to escape…”

“You can go check on them…”

I stumbled through the crowd and reached the ambulance. With trembling hands, I lifted the white sheet from one of the stretchers.

It was my father, his expression serene, seemingly unharmed.

Tears welled up in my eyes, and I wept silently.

I didn’t even have the courage to lift the sheet from the other stretcher.

“Donglin!” Someone suddenly called my name.

I froze. It was my mother’s voice.

“Mom… Mom?”

My mother leaned against the ambulance door, gasping for breath. Her hair was ruffled by the wind, and she looked like she had rushed in a hurry.

“Donglin, calm down. Let me explain.”

What was going on?

I quickly lifted another piece of white cloth and saw the face of a young woman, probably around my age.

Who was the person who died in the same bed as my father?

I collapsed to the ground, almost exhausted.

“Impossible… what happened…”

My mother supported me and said, “Donglin, you’ve grown up. I don’t want to hide this from you anymore.”

I stared at her blankly. She looked so unfamiliar.

“Your father and I broke off our relationship a long time ago,” my mother said with difficulty, taking a deep breath. “But in order for you to grow up healthy and happy, this family must not break up. We had to keep it a secret from you.”

“When did that happen…?” I realized my voice was dry and low, almost unrecognizable to myself.

“A long time ago, I don’t know how to put it…” Mother sighed and was silent for a moment, as if trying to find the right words. “Your father has some health issues…”

At that moment, I noticed a gray-haired man standing in the crowd. He looked at my mother and me with concern. I had never seen this man before, but his features felt familiar.

My parents had been married for thirty years. People of their generation generally had children right after getting married, but I was only twenty-three.

So they tried for over six years to conceive me. My mother said that my father had health issues and that their relationship had long since broken down.

The strange man before me didn’t look like anyone I knew, but like me.

In that instant, I understood everything. I’m a very smart person.

No wonder my father and mother rarely traveled together.

No wonder they always seemed to spend time with me in their own ways.

I felt sick to my stomach. How happy this family had felt before, and how disgusting it felt now.

“No!” I roared. “Shut up! Stop talking nonsense!”

“Donglin, Mom’s sorry…”

“No, it’s impossible! Get out of here!” I screamed like crazy.

This can’t be true. It can’t be like this.

How could I, Wang Donglin, be such a person?

I don’t remember what else I said. I just remember violently pushing my mother aside, shoving aside everyone in my way, and running desperately. I seemed to run to the bus stop and instinctively jumped on a bus that had just arrived. I sat for a long time before I realized I had caught the bus back to school.

I suddenly longed to see Moli. She had moved out of the dormitory to prepare for the postgraduate entrance exam and rented a small house near the school. I had only been there twice.

At this moment, I needed her comfort, her embrace, and her body.

In my backpack, I had the spare key she had left for me. So, numbly, I got out of the bus and, relying on my vague memory, spent quite some time finally finding Moli’s residence.

For some reason, I didn’t knock but instead used my key to open the door and enter. The small living room was dark and unlit, while the only room was closed, with light leaking through the crack.

In the dim light, I spotted a pair of men’s sneakers on the shoe cabinet that didn’t belong to me.

What was going on? My head spun, and my stomach twisted.

Inside the room, through the thin door, I could faintly hear heavy breathing.

I mechanically walked to the door and pressed my ear to it.

“Ah… so amazing…” It was Moli.

“Much better than your nerdy one, right?” a man said triumphantly.

“Of course. Ah… you’re so bad… you scoundrel! Ah…”

I had no idea the innocent and lovely Moli could make such a wanton noise.

Fury filled me with rage, and I slammed the door open, startling the couple making out in bed. But when they saw it was me, they both smiled.

“You’ve come just in time. You saved me a lot of explaining. Let’s break up,” Moli sneered. Was this still the girl I love so deeply?

The man smiled scornfully: “Are you Wang Donglin? You’re not worthy of Moli; forget it.”

“You two are having an affair, and you think you’re justified?” I raged, not caring that he was a muscular man, and raised my fist to attack him.

The man raised his knee and slammed it hard into my groin.

The pain was so intense that tears streamed down my face. My vision went dark, and I couldn’t catch my breath. I almost fainted.

All the anger and hatred suddenly turned to fear and humiliation. I doubled over, clutching my groin, unable to stand for a long time.

“You’re such a jerk; you want to compete with me for a woman? Get out of here! If you don’t leave, I’ll kill you!”

Moli also agreed, “Yes, go quickly. Let’s part ways amicably and owe nothing to each other.”

No one owes anyone anything? This is my first love, and I gave it my all.

But I dared not utter a single word. I could only silently hold onto the wall, enduring the excruciating pain as I walked out, step by step, haltingly.

My other world had collapsed, and the entire world was reduced to ashes and debris.

That night, I walked aimlessly for a long, long time on the cold, deserted streets.

Overnight, I went from being the envied “other people’s kid” to a subject of conversation and ridicule.

23-year-old Wang Donglin was dead.

CONTENT END 74

chapters.title: Chapter 75
chapters.content:
May 31st, 3:00 p.m., Moyun Town.

This small town at the foot of Moyun Mountain was a renowned gathering place for internet celebrities and hipsters and a flagship of D City’s tourism industry. Every night, as night fell, the town’s cafes were illuminated with lights and music, where those whose daily lives were less fulfilled found a place to indulge in the glitz and glamor, never wanting to leave.

During the day, the town was less bustling than at night, offering a touch of tranquility. Therefore, many tourists chose to spend entire afternoons sitting in the corners of cafes, whispering in the lazy sunshine.

Lu Tianfeng and Wang Donglin were discussing hidden past events in a cafe called “Cat’s Nest.”

“Officer Lu, is this information helpful?” Wang Donglin, feeling dry from his long speech, took a long sip of his coffee.

“I’m not sure yet, but I do want to learn more about your past.”

Maybe it was because he forgot to put sugar in his coffee, but Wang Donglin’s expression was bitter. “I didn’t go into detail about this kind of thing during the interrogation.”

“Why?”

“Because they don’t care. The officers interrogating me only care about whether I killed the person. They repeatedly asked me about the process and details of the murder.” Wang Donglin’s eyes suddenly turned cold again.

“That’s their job responsibility,” Lu Tianfeng sighed. He was well aware of the pressure police officers face. Often, it wasn’t that they didn’t care about the story behind the case, but that they didn’t have the time to do so.

Catch the murderer, find evidence to convict him quickly, close the case as quickly as possible, and then focus on the next case—this seemed to be the fateful cycle of their police careers.

“I really don’t understand. This case should have nothing to do with you. Why do you insist on getting involved?”

“Because I received a reliable tip that someone wants to kill you.” Lu Tianfeng naturally didn’t want to say more.

“Then why are you protecting me? I’m just a murderer who’s escaped justice.” Wang Donglin trailed off. “A murderer deserves death. It’s a matter of course.”

“I’m a police officer. I know no one can take another’s life without a legal trial.”

“Interesting,” Wang Donglin said, his voice tinged with sarcasm. “Even I think I deserve death, yet you’re risking your life to protect me.”

“Because it’s my duty.”

Wang Donglin tapped his empty coffee cup and said, “So, should we continue hiding in this cafe, or should we move?”

Lu Tianfeng glanced at his watch. They had left Tiedao New Village about two hours ago, escaping the police cordon. According to police practice, they would first check security surveillance and public transportation. Tracking illegal taxis would take even longer.

But Lu Tianfeng absolutely didn’t underestimate the police’s ability. Two hours was plenty of time for them to trace their escape route.

So now, it was Lu Tianfeng’s turn to make the next move.

“Do you know how most fugitives are discovered by the police?” Lu Tianfeng asked.

Wang Donglin tilted his head, thought for a moment, and replied, “They were accidentally caught on surveillance cameras.”

“That’s wrong. They were tracked and targeted by the police while contacting family or friends.” Lu Tianfeng pulled a cheap phone from his waist bag. “So I’m going to do the same.”

Wang Donglin frowned. He certainly didn’t believe Lu Tianfeng would fall into his trap, but he felt a vague sense of unease. It was a feeling of helplessness, a sense of having one’s fate controlled by others.

.

May 31st, 3:10 p.m., D City Police Department Office Building.

The atmosphere in the meeting room was tense.

The senior police officers participating in the meeting were locked in a stalemate over whether to issue a public wanted notice for Wang Donglin. Those in favor of a public wanted notice argued that Wang Donglin’s case had a significant social impact. The court’s decision to transfer him to a psychiatric hospital based on the results of a psychiatric evaluation had already sparked a public outcry. Now that Wang Donglin’s whereabouts were unknown, if the news wasn’t disclosed and the media broke the news first, the consequences would be unimaginable.

Those opposed to a public wanted notice argued that the police had already issued a top-level wanted notice and deployed sufficient personnel to pursue him. Publicizing Wang Donglin’s escape would likely cause public panic, and they feared extremists would exploit the situation to incite public sentiment. This would not only be unhelpful in the pursuit of the fugitive but could even further complicate the situation.

As the frontline commander of the first roundup operation, Cheng Tuo was forced to attend the hearing. He felt deeply resentful. The Tiedao New Village operation had failed largely because his superiors were reluctant to act publicly and hadn’t imposed a full curfew in the area, allowing Lu Tianfeng to quickly escape. If he continued to be so timid, the next task would be truly difficult.

Interestingly, despite severely reprimanding Cheng Tuo for his ineffective work, the superiors didn’t assign anyone else to lead the operation. Clearly, no one within the police force wanted to take on this difficult task, so Cheng Tuo had to remain in charge.

In this meeting room, Cheng Tuo held the lowest position, his influence was minimal, and he hadn’t been given a chance to speak. The longer he sat, the more suffocated he became. Just then, a young officer knocked on the door and entered. He approached Cheng Tuo and whispered something in his ear. Cheng Tuo’s eyes suddenly lit up.

“Excuse me, leaders. We just received the latest information on the fugitive.”

The moment Cheng Tuo spoke, the meeting room fell silent.

“Go ahead,” Director Luo, who was presiding over the meeting, nodded.

“Two minutes ago, we intercepted a text message on Chen Nuolan’s phone from an unknown number. We suspect it was a code from Lu Tianfeng to Chen Nuolan, and we’re actively working to decipher it.”

“Can you track the location of the phone that sent the message?”

“The phone’s location is in a small village over a thousand kilometers away, a place with no connection to Chen Nuolan. We suspect Lu Tianfeng is using some kind of virtual gateway software to disguise himself and evade our tracking.”

“What’s the content of the message?”

“It’s a string of numbers.”

Cheng Tuo skillfully operated the projector, displaying the contents of the mysterious text message on the snow-white wall:

203.13.14

102.6.9

2.4.8

88.16.19

492.3.3

103.7.14

35.6.10

“What is this?”

“It’s probably an index table. We need to find the corresponding password table to decrypt it,” someone in the room said.

Cheng Tuo nodded and said, “Yes, our current priority is to find this password table. Also, I want to personally monitor Chen Nuolan, as she could contact Lu Tianfeng at any time.”

The crowd, who had just been arguing over whether to issue a wanted order, suddenly fell silent. The real solution to the problem was to quickly locate Lu Tianfeng and Wang Donglin.

“Cheng Tuo, go follow up on the situation there first,” Director Luo finally spoke. This statement was like a pardon to Cheng Tuo. He quickly bowed to the leaders and took his leave before quickly departing.

In fact, he already had some ideas about how to crack this code. The next step was to confront Chen Nuolan head-on.

CONTENT END 75

chapters.title: Chapter 76
chapters.content:
May 31st, 3:30 p.m., Lu Tianfeng’s house.

Less than ten seconds after Cheng Tuo knocked on the door, Chen Nuolan opened it. She was dressed in a tracksuit, her expression calm, as if unsurprised by Cheng Tuo’s visit.

“Hello, Nuolan.”

“Captain Cheng, thank you for your hard work.” The two had met several times at police gatherings, so they were acquaintances after all, but Chen Nuolan didn’t show any particular enthusiasm.

“Busy today, huh? My colleagues must have been here several times.”

“Not bad,” Chen Nuolan said coldly.

Cheng Tuo was certainly aware that he wasn’t welcome, but he sat casually on the sofa and asked directly, “Did Afeng just send you a text?”

“No,” Chen Nuolan denied immediately.

“Let me rephrase that. Did you just receive a strange, unfamiliar text message?”

Chen Nuolan was forthright, placing her phone in front of Cheng Tuo and unlocking the screen.

“You’ve already seen it, right?” She was well-versed in police procedures, and the police were surely monitoring the messages on her phone 24/7.

Cheng Tuo wasn’t shy. He took the phone, looked at the string of numbers, and asked, “What does this message mean?”

“I don’t know. Maybe it’s an underground Mark Six lottery advertisement,” Chen Nuolan said, still indifferent.

“No, I think this is an encrypted message from Lu Tianfeng.” Cheng Tuo gently put down the phone and strolled over to the bookshelf in the corner of the living room, seemingly casually browsing the books. “If I were him, I’d agree with you to use a book as the password table.”

Chen Nuolan said nothing, but she bit her lip lightly, unable to hide her nervousness.

“Each line of numbers is divided into three sections, and the numbers in the second and third sections don’t exceed 20. I think the first section represents the page number, the second the line number, and the third the word number, right?”

Chen Nuolan’s expression grew even more strange, her eyes shifting.

Cheng Tuo grew more confident. He ran his finger over the spines of the books one by one and said, “There’s a crucial flaw in the password: 492.3.3 on the fifth line. If the password table is a book, then it must have at least 492 pages.”

Chen Nuolan gave a wry smile, a look of self-abandonment.

“On this shelf, I think there are less than ten books over 492 pages thick,” Cheng Tuo said, picking up one of the books. “Even if I were to go through all of them, it wouldn’t take long, but if I had to gamble, I’d pick this one.”

In his hand was a local travel guide to D City.

“Why?” Chen Nuolan couldn’t help but ask.

“Because information usually requires time and place, and this book contains plenty of local place names, so I’ll definitely find the words I need.”

Chen Nuolan sat woodenly by the side while Cheng Tuo flipped through the guidebook to a specific page, trying to decipher the coded information.

203.13.14, corresponding to the word “today,” and 102.6.9, corresponding to the word “evening.” After deciphering the first two words, Cheng Tuo was 100% certain that this book was the cipher agreed upon by Lu Tianfeng and Chen Nuolan.

So he quickly spelled out the remaining words—

2.4.8, “seven”; 88.16.19, “point”; 492.3.3, “Mo”; 103.7.14, “Yun”; 35.6.10, “Town.”

Tonight at 7 o’clock in Moyun Town.

“Lu Tianfeng is in Moyun Town?” It was a question, but Cheng Tuo didn’t need an answer. His phone rang at that moment.

“Captain Cheng, we’ve pinpointed the location where that mysterious text message was sent.” It was a report from a colleague from the technical team.

“Where is it?”

“Moyun Town, at the foot of Moyun Mountain.”

“Got it.”

Cheng Tuo left the stunned Chen Nuolan behind and hurried away. This time, he couldn’t afford to make any mistakes.

Chen Nuolan sighed, closed the door, and a smile of victory crept into her lips.

Lu Tianfeng had anticipated all of this, so he and Chen Nuolan had agreed in advance that when using coded communication, if the message had an odd number of characters, it was a false message; if it had an even number of characters, it was the truth.

Although Chen Nuolan didn’t know Lu Tianfeng’s exact location, she knew he was definitely not in Moyun Town.

.

May 31st, 3:45 PM, D City Police Station, Director’s Office.

The thick curtains were drawn, and the dim light added to the solemn atmosphere.

Director Luo sat at his desk, frowning, poring over the file in his hands. Tong Yao stood slightly stiffly at the desk, looking preoccupied. In another chair sat a burly, unremarkable middle-aged man. He was Yan Jin, captain of the Fourth Detachment of the Criminal Police Brigade, who had been responsible for following up on the Wang Donglin serial murder case and had personally arrested the perpetrator.

Yan Jin’s low-key style and quiet demeanor made him a minor presence within the police department, making it easy for people to mistake him for someone with little talent. However, the number of difficult cases he solved rivaled even the force’s top detectives.

“This isn’t a formal meeting. Everyone is welcome to speak freely and discuss whether there are any unsolved issues in this case,” Director Luo stated directly.

Yan Jin’s expression remained calm as he replied, “All information regarding the Wang Donglin case has been recorded. I have nothing special to add.”

“Captain Yan, what do you think of Wang Donglin?” Tong Yao asked.

“Very cold-blooded,” Yan Jin said without hesitation. “I’ve seen many murderers, but none as cold-blooded as him.”

Director Luo’s interest was piqued: “Tell me more!”

“Wang Donglin’s killing methods are very ‘gentle.’ After selecting his victims, he would lure them home, drug them, strip them, and drown them in the bathtub. After the murder, he would wash and dress the bodies before dumping them in a nearby lake. He never sexually assaulted the victims in any way.”

Director Luo and Tong Yao shuddered at this. Only those who dealt with death and crime daily could understand the terrifying coldness hidden behind Wang Donglin’s ritualistic “gentleness.”

Extreme non-violence was even more terrifying than extreme violence.

Yan Jin continued, “Wang Donglin killed four people in a row, one of whom was his ex-girlfriend. If he hadn’t chosen to commit the fourth crime in a hotel room instead of his own home, we might not have caught him yet.”

Director Luo tapped the table. “Isn’t that a bit strange? Any suspicious points in this case can be discussed. Remember, this is an informal discussion.”

Director Luo emphasized “informal” again, hoping Yan Jin would speak frankly.

Yan Jin thought for a moment before saying, “I truly don’t understand why Wang Donglin broke his pattern by choosing an unfamiliar location, one riddled with surveillance cameras, to commit his crimes, leaving behind crucial evidence.”

“There’s another point that concerns me,” Tong Yao interjected cautiously. “After killing someone, Wang Donglin would take certain items from the victim, place them in an elegant box, and bury them in an unknown location. He called them ‘souvenirs.’ But in the end, we only found items belonging to two of the victims. The whereabouts of the other two ‘souvenirs’ are unknown, and Wang Donglin wouldn’t reveal their burial locations.”

“While these details are strange, the fact that Wang Donglin is the murderer is unshakable. Furthermore, his uncooperative attitude ultimately meant we were unable to investigate further.” Yan Jin’s tone was filled with indignation.

Director Luo glanced at Tong Yao, then at Yan Jin, and sighed deeply. “I called you two here just to have a good chat. According to Tong Yao’s confidential report, Lu Tianfeng’s real motive for suddenly hijacking the prison van and taking Wang Donglin away this morning was to uncover the truth behind this case.”

Even Yan Jin, known for his composure, was startled by this shocking news. His eyes widened as he looked at Tong Yao in disbelief.

“This… is too reckless! Why aren’t they following procedures?”

“Lu Tianfeng suspected a mole within the police force, so he acted on his own. Now, I just want you to speak your mind. Is there really any need to investigate Wang Donglin’s case further? Is he hiding any crucial information?”

Yan Jin fell silent. He knew his next words could change Lu Tianfeng’s fate.

If he said there was no need to pursue the matter further, Lu Tianfeng would surely be wanted, perhaps even convicted. If he revealed the suspicious aspects of the case, Director Luo might try to legitimize Lu Tianfeng’s actions.

But as a police officer, he couldn’t speak against his will simply to protect a colleague.

Tong Yao looked at Yan Jin, her eyes filled with both anticipation and unease. Yan Jin suddenly realized that Tong Yao’s access to such confidential information meant she was likely involved in Lu Tianfeng’s carjacking plan, and that her police hat might even be in jeopardy.

He really couldn’t say this lightly!

Just as Yan Jin was hesitating, the intercom on the desk rang. Director Luo picked up the receiver, and within seconds, his expression darkened.

Tong Yao and Yan Jin exchanged a knowing glance; they knew something major must have happened.

Director Luo put down the phone, sighed heavily, and said, “The news of Wang Donglin’s escape has been leaked online!”

.

On May 31st, at 4:00 p.m., on an illegally operated bus from Moyun Town to D City, Lu Tianfeng and Wang Donglin unexpectedly returned to D City using the same method again.

“Isn’t this dangerous?” Wang Donglin once questioned.

But Lu Tianfeng replied, “We don’t have any truly safe options. We can only choose a plan that’s as elusive as possible.”

So, after leaving the Cat’s Nest Cafe, the two of them took a deliberate walk around Moyun Town, buying some dry food, drinking water, a tent, a picnic stove, and other camping equipment, creating the illusion that they were planning to hide in Moyun Mountain.

Lu Tianfeng was well aware of the power of Skynet surveillance. Even if the two of them wore sunglasses and sun hats and applied some simple makeup, the police could still track them down through facial recognition technology.

Currently, only a small area of ​​Moyun Mountain had been developed as a tourist attraction. There were still hundreds of square kilometers of pristine forest, attracting many extreme sports enthusiasts. If they truly infiltrated the mountains, even with ample manpower and advanced equipment, it would be difficult for the police to capture them. Therefore, escaping from Moyun Town to Moyun Mountain was a very reasonable option.

Precisely because it was reasonable, Lu Tianfeng rejected it.

“Conventional tactics will definitely be discovered. We need to take a risky tactic.”

“Interesting! I also like this when playing chess,” Wang Donglin smiled.

So, the two of them hailed a black bus and climbed into the last row of seats. Although the bus was filthy and worn, the seatbacks glistening with grease, as if they hadn’t been washed in years, they didn’t mind at all. They even chatted about everyday matters like good friends who hadn’t seen each other for years.

The relaxed and cheerful atmosphere between the two continued until the radio news broadcast began to fill the bus.

“Dear listeners, our reporter just received a message—” The radio, originally listened to by only the driver, suddenly became a bus-wide announcement. It seemed that some major news had occurred, prompting the driver to turn up the volume deliberately.

Lu Tianfeng and Wang Donglin exchanged glances subconsciously. The big news they were most worried about was themselves.

“The Wang Donglin serial murder case is currently attracting widespread public attention. Although Wang Donglin confessed to killing four innocent women, he was ultimately ruled to have severe schizophrenia and was not criminally responsible. He was transferred to a mental hospital for treatment. However, around 11:00 this morning, Wang Donglin absconded while being transferred to the mental hospital, injuring several security guards. The police have issued a public wanted notice, offering a reward of up to 100,000 yuan for anyone who can provide information on Wang Donglin’s whereabouts…”

“What a boast! It sounds like I single-handedly took down a whole bunch of security guards,” Wang Donglin muttered in dissatisfaction.

“Shh, don’t talk.”

“…According to the police, Wang Donglin is likely fleeing towards Moyun Mountain. Citizens, please be vigilant. If you spot any suspicious individuals, call the police immediately. Please be mindful of your own safety when you go out, and be wary of strangers following you. Wang Donglin is a highly dangerous fugitive with strong offensive and criminal tendencies…” The radio news anchor continued his description, his voice growing increasingly animated.

“Damn, this is so annoying!” Wang Donglin clenched his fists. Lu Tianfeng glanced at him with concern but noticed that the emotion in his eyes wasn’t anger or uneasiness but contempt.

“Keep calm,” Lu Tianfeng warned again.

The radio began playing other news, and the passengers on the bus couldn’t help but chatter. Some said a pervert like Wang Donglin should be shot outright; some said he was faking mental illness to avoid imprisonment; others said he might be a wealthy second-generation kid who had paid off everything and was now bribing the guards to avoid punishment…

This case had become a hot topic in the city lately, with passengers who hadn’t previously met before engaging in a lively debate. Fortunately, Lu Tianfeng and Wang Donglin were sitting in the last row; the two rows ahead were empty, and no one approached them.

Wang Donglin’s face was sullen; he remained silent, his expression of disdain still etched in his face.

As the bus approached the D City area, Lu Tianfeng nudged Wang Donglin with his elbow and said, “We’re getting ready to get off. There’s less surveillance around here.”

Wang Donglin nodded.

“Sir, stop at the intersection ahead,” Lu Tianfeng said loudly, standing up.

These illegally operated buses stopped at random. The driver didn’t even glance at Lu Tianfeng, just spun the steering wheel and pulled over.

Lu Tianfeng thought that the indifference between people was also a key factor in their escape.

After getting out of the bus, the two blended into the crowd without looking back.

CONTENT END 76

chapters.title: Chapter 77
chapters.content:
May 31st, 4:10 PM, D City Police Station, parking lot.

Tong Yao finally received special permission from Director Luo to attempt contact with Lu Tianfeng, under the condition that she not help him escape or disclose any information about the police operation. The only thing she could do was to assist Lu Tianfeng in uncovering the details of Wang Donglin’s case, bringing Wang Donglin back to the police station as soon as possible, and bringing this incident to a close.

To ensure the secrecy of the operation and to avoid any conflict between Tong Yao and the other colleagues in charge of the arrest, Director Luo publicly announced that Tong Yao would be temporarily transferred.

Privately, he also earnestly told Tong Yao that if the incident wasn’t properly resolved, not only would her reinstatement be difficult, but Director Luo himself might even have to retire early.

“Director Luo, if the risk is so great, why allow me to carry out this mission?” Tong Yao was puzzled.

“After netizens broke the news, the situation quickly spiraled out of control. We’ll also have to deal with pressure from the media and higher-ups, so our work will undoubtedly be stretched thin. Therefore, I hope that if you’re unfettered, you’ll become our ultimate weapon.”

Tong Yao nodded, half understanding.

“Besides, I think Lu Tianfeng is a rare talent; we can’t give up on him easily.” Director Luo, realizing his stance was a bit off, waved his hand and told Tong Yao to quickly find Lu Tianfeng.

So, without saying hello to anyone or even taking the elevator, Tong Yao quietly walked down the fire escape to the parking lot. Only after getting into her car did she pull out a small note from her pocket. On it was the scribbled code that Lu Tianfeng had sent to Chen Nuolan. This was likely the last piece of information she had obtained from official police channels regarding the case.

203.13.14

102.6.9

2.4.8

88.16.19

492.3.3

103.7.14

35.6.10

Actually, this password held a little secret only Tong Yao knew.

Lu Tianfeng had told her that morning that he had prepared some brand-new anonymous phone cards for emergency contact. The phone number used to send the message to Chen Nuolan would be discarded after one use to prevent tracking. And hidden within this message was another number—Lu Tianfeng had said that all his phone cards were virtual numbers starting with “1770,” and the following seven digits were the first digits of each line in the password message: 17702128413.

This was Lu Tianfeng’s current contact information.

Tong Yao pulled out her phone, debating whether to call someone immediately, when another figure suddenly appeared in the parking lot. She quickly pocketed the note with the password and her phone.

Looking closely, she saw it was her boss and mentor, Wu Guoqing, deputy captain of the First Detachment.

“Boss?” Tong Yao was a little stunned.

“Why did you leave without a word?” Wu Guoqing asked casually, standing outside the car, one hand resting on the window.

“I… have something to ask.” Tong Yao was torn. She naturally trusted Wu Guoqing completely, but the mission she shouldered demanded she keep it secret.

“It’s okay. I understand. When Lao Luo was still on the front lines of criminal investigation, he also didn’t like to follow the rules when solving cases.” Wu Guoqing smiled. “I just want to remind you of one thing.”

“Boss, please speak.”

“Did you know that the colleagues responsible for tracking down Wang Donglin earlier discovered a male corpse on the rooftop of Yuelong Building? I was responsible for tracing the deceased’s identity and origins, and I discovered something very strange.” Wu Guoqing tapped gently on the car window, paused, and then said, “The deceased was between thirty and thirty-five years old, in good health. His muscles are sturdy, and judging by the calluses on his hands, he must be a professional who regularly handles firearms and knives. He bears numerous scars, some of them quite severe, likely from fights. However, there are no criminal or medical records for this individual, nor is he a registered police officer or soldier. I suspect he’s a mercenary who smuggled himself into the country, specifically targeting Wang Donglin.

“Mercenary?” Tong Yao frowned. Lu Tianfeng had also said that the group that hijacked the prison van had ample firepower and brutal methods; they were definitely not a ragtag group.

“To hire mercenaries, you need not only financial resources but also connections in the underworld. Why mobilize such a large force to deal with Wang Donglin, a womanizer?” Wu Guoqing posed the question to his apprentice.

Tong Yao pondered for a moment, then suddenly realized, “Could it be that the woman Wang Donglin murdered was connected to a criminal organization?”

“I haven’t found any relevant information from the files, but my intuition tells me there must be something deeper behind the Wang Donglin case. You must be careful.”

Tong Yao felt a chill in her heart, and she was filled with admiration for her master. Lu Tianfeng, because of his ability to travel through time, and Yan Jin, because of his intimate knowledge of the case, were suspicious of Wang Donglin’s case and sought to uncover the truth. It’s understandable, but Wu Guoqing, relying solely on the information in the files and his own reasoning, saw the mystery behind the case. He truly possessed a keen eye.

“Actually, I have one more thing to say…” Wu Guoqing hesitated for some reason.

“Boss?” Tong Yao could see the unusual look on her master’s face.

“You must be wary of Lu Tianfeng.”

“Why?” Tong Yao was stunned.

“A plan to send mercenaries against Wang Donglin must have been meticulously detailed, but Lu Tianfeng clearly foiled their plan, and a fierce conflict erupted between the two sides. The question that puzzles me is how Lu Tianfeng saw through his plan.”

Tong Yao was speechless. This time, she couldn’t use the “informant” cover-up.

“I… don’t know…”

“Well, be careful. I hope Lu Tianfeng is a good person.” Wu Guoqing sighed, his worry evident.

“I understand. I will definitely not let my guard down.”

Although Tong Yao felt a little guilty toward her master, she ultimately kept Lu Tianfeng’s secret. Once revealed, this secret would trigger unforeseen chain reactions.

“Then go.” Wu Guoqing patted the car, gave Tong Yao a meaningful look, and then turned and left.

Tong Yao always had the illusion that her master could see through everything in her heart, just not reveal it.

But she also suddenly realized that she couldn’t use her own phone to contact Lu Tianfeng.

.

May 31st, 4:30 p.m., Huangjia Village, on the outskirts of D City.

Huangjia Village was no longer a village. It was still home to tall buildings, bustling traffic, and a newly opened subway station and light rail station. Although housing prices were significantly lower than in the city proper, the comprehensive amenities have attracted many outsiders to D City.

Or rather, Huangjia Village was an “upgraded version” of the Tiedao New Village, with a larger area, a larger influx of immigrants, and a more complex security situation.

Therefore, there were many small hotels around Huangjia Village, offering overnight stays for just a few dozen yuan. Special requests could even be made for an additional twenty yuan, waiving ID registration. These places were hotbeds of crime, closing down during crackdowns only to revive again after a while, changing locations and rebranding, causing headaches for management.

Lu Tianfeng and Wang Donglin were currently in a room at one of these small hotels. It was called the “Happiness Hostel,” but looking at the moldy walls, leaking ceiling, and filthy bedding, it was hard to say where their happiness stemmed from.

“How long can we stay here?” Wang Donglin plopped down on the bed, which immediately creaked unpleasantly.

“Two or three hours should be fine. We’ll move on after dark.” Lu Tianfeng wasn’t making this claim. He believed that by seven o’clock, police surveillance would be focused on Moyun Town, and as long as they left before then, they would be safe.

“But running away like this isn’t a solution!” Wang Donglin stretched. “I’m exhausted. I might as well stay in the psychiatric hospital.”

“I’m just worried you won’t make it to the hospital alive.” Lu Tianfeng checked the doors and windows of the room, confirming nothing was wrong, then pulled a stool over and sat down beside the bed. “Hurry up and continue your story. We need to find the mastermind behind your murder as soon as possible.”

“No problem, as we were talking about—”

Lu Tianfeng’s phone suddenly rang, startling Wang Donglin.

“Your phone’s still on?”

“Don’t worry, this is a new number no one else knows.” Lu Tianfeng glanced and knew it was Tong Yao on the other end.

“Who’s calling?”

“My friend,” Lu Tianfeng answered. “Hello?”

“It’s me.” As expected, it was Tong Yao’s voice on the other end.

At this moment, Wang Donglin gestured to Lu Tianfeng, indicating that he needed to go to the bathroom. Lu Tianfeng nodded in agreement without giving it much thought.

Lu Tianfeng had already checked the bathroom upon entering—the window was rusty and could only be opened a tiny crack, so there was no fear that Wang Donglin would escape.

Lu Tianfeng lowered his voice and asked Tong Yao, “How’s the situation?”

“It’s hard to explain, but I’m able to move freely. Can we meet?”

“Okay,” Lu Tianfeng thought for a moment and said, “Let’s meet in the evening. You can prepare a place for me to stay overnight.”

“Have you found any new leads with Wang Donglin?”

“Not yet, but he’s gradually beginning to trust me… I believe that with patience, I can get everything we need to know within a day.”

“That’s great! Captain Lu, you decide the time and place for the meeting, right?”

“Tonight at 7:30, New Era Plaza.” Lu Tianfeng chose a place with a high flow of people, making it easier to respond.

“Okay, see you then.” The two of them tacitly agreed to keep their conversation short, minimizing the possibility of being tracked.

After Lu Tianfeng hung up the phone, he pulled out the D City travel brochure and map he’d brought with him and researched his route plan for tonight’s meeting with Tong Yao.

A long moment passed before Lu Tianfeng felt a sudden sense of alarm—Wang Donglin was being far too quiet in the restroom.

“Wang Donglin, are you okay?” Lu Tianfeng pounded on the bathroom door, but there was no response.

“Wang Donglin!” Desperate, Lu Tianfeng abandoned his attempts to pick the lock. Instead, he slumped his shoulders and rammed the door open.

In the narrow space, there was no sign of Wang Donglin. The window, which couldn’t be opened, had been forcibly removed due to severe rust on the hinges.

Lu Tianfeng poked his head out the window. Although it was only the third floor, he could easily climb down through the sewer pipes and reach the ground level in less than half a minute. Therefore, Wang Donglin had already vanished without a trace.

Lu Tianfeng’s head felt hot, and he had the urge to jump down and run for hundreds of meters through the alley. However, a rational voice inside him warned that he had no way of judging which direction Wang Donglin had fled, and blindly chasing him would be futile.

Now he had to stay calm, calm down, and come up with a solution—

Lu Tianfeng’s stomach twisted, and an inexplicable, excruciating pain surged over him. His eyes went black, his hands and feet went limp, and he slumped over the toilet, retching.

Could this really be a side effect of the medication?

Lu Tianfeng slumped on the cold floor, and it took about five minutes before he regained his breath. He struggled to stand, washed his face with cold water, and slapped himself twice.

It hurt, but he was awake and calm. Lu Tianfeng glanced at his watch. It was 4:42 p.m., meaning Wang Donglin had already escaped for over ten minutes.

He had no choice but to call Tong Yao.

“It’s me.” A bitter taste lingered in Lu Tianfeng’s mouth.

“What’s wrong?” Tong Yao, like the last time they spoke, didn’t call out Lu Tianfeng’s name.

“The big fish has broken free and escaped.”

There was silence on the other end of the line for a long time. Lu Tianfeng could almost hear Tong Yao gasp.

“Where are you?” she said, trying to be as calm as possible.

“Huangjia Village Shopping Center.”

“I’ll be there in half an hour—no, twenty minutes.”

“Okay.” Lu Tianfeng hung up the phone and only then noticed that his right hand was trembling slightly.

No, I can’t give up.

Lu Tianfeng gripped his right wrist tightly with his left hand, and the trembling stopped.

I won’t lose.

He repeated this in his mind again.

CONTENT END 77

chapters.title: Chapter 78
chapters.content:
Wang Donglin’s Memories (II)

That heartbreaking night took everything from me.

I became silent and unwilling to interact with people. I felt like everyone was talking behind my back, mocking and laughing at my weakness and incompetence.

Yes, incompetence.

After that man’s vicious kick, my lower body ached for nearly half a month; even urinating was painful.

After a month, the pain finally subsided. But I realized I’d lost my ability to function as a man. The mere sight of revealing pictures of beautiful women or the thought of sexual intercourse filled me with nausea and vomiting. I remembered Moli’s disdainful expression that night and my mother’s sympathetic gaze when she confessed.

These two shameless women gave me a physical aversion to the word “woman.”

I tried several methods and finally confirmed that I had absolutely no way of getting an erection.

Having given up on life, I spent every day holed up in my dorm, sleeping and playing games. Only when I was starving did I order takeout. Day and night, I spent my time online, playing chess with others.

I kept applying for new alt accounts, trying to keep my level points at the novice level, then mercilessly crushing the newbies. Only with one overwhelming victory after another could I find some solace.

It seemed like the only thing I could do.

My mother must have heard about my situation through hearsay. She called me repeatedly, supposedly to apologize and ask for forgiveness, but in reality, she was constantly hinting that if I continued like this, I’d lose my master’s degree and my life would be completely ruined.

It was so ironic. Did she think my life wasn’t already completely ruined?

It turned out she had no idea what she had done.

My mother still contacted me regularly. I found her not only disgusting but also annoying. I really wanted to find a way to make her shut up and stop bothering me.

When she suggested taking me on a trip like we used to when we were kids, I hesitated for a moment before finally agreeing. I said I wanted to go abroad, maybe to Malaysia or Thailand, but we wouldn’t go to popular tourist destinations. We’d find a quiet island resort for a few days to enjoy some peace and quiet.

My mother agreed, as I felt she would agree no matter where I suggested. She handed me the task of booking the hotel and itinerary, saying money wasn’t a problem, as long as I was comfortable.

Finally, I chose Sabah, Malaysia, and booked an island resort that was expensive and relatively rarely visited but offered first-class ambiance and privacy.

After reading the resort’s description, my mother was delighted and thought I had chosen a fantastic destination. I forced a smile; she would never understand why I chose this place.

During this trip to Sabah, I tried my best to play the role of a “good son,” reassuring my mother that the rift between us was rapidly healing.

So, I made a somewhat impulsive request: I asked my mother to wear a swimsuit and swim with me, go kayaking out to sea, snorkel, and observe corals in the clear waters. My mother wasn’t particularly active, wasn’t familiar with water, and her swimming skills were pretty average, but to accommodate me, she never refused a single one of my invitations.

On the third night at the resort, the starry sky was exceptionally beautiful. Sitting on the beach, I could clearly see the stars. I suggested we go swimming in the sea and gaze at the stars. After a moment’s hesitation, my mother agreed. She changed into a black swimsuit and slowly walked into the water with me.

The water was a little chilly at night, but my mother didn’t want to spoil my fun, so she said nothing. After swimming with me for a short while, she stopped and stood chest-deep in the water. I snuggled up to her, pointing to the sky and teaching her to identify the constellations. She asked questions like a curious child.

“Mom, do you ever regret it?” I suddenly asked.

“Regret?”

“Regret marrying a man who can’t have children. Regret pretending to love this family for over twenty years.”

“No, Donglin, Mom really loves you,” my mother said weakly.

“But I don’t love you.”

Earlier on the beach, I had made a sandbag out of an old sock and always carried it with me. Hitting someone on the back of the head with the sandbag could knock them unconscious, leaving almost no mark.

My mother hadn’t anticipated my sudden attack. The blow hit her hard, her eyes rolled back, and she fainted.

I gently supported her and lowered her head under the water.

The silvery starlight was beautiful.

My unconscious mother struggled futilely for a few moments before she was no longer moving. Of course, I was patient. I waited for her to remain in the water for a full ten minutes, leaving no chance of survival, before I pulled her out of the water.

Her pupils were dilated, her mouth was agape, and her face was filled with agony.

Seeing that pained, twisted expression, I felt an unprecedented sense of joy and relief.

The rest was easy. I untied my socks and dumped sand into the sea, making the murder weapon vanish without a trace. Then I began to scream and shout. As I did so, I slowly pulled my mother’s body back to shore.

It wasn’t until I reached shore that someone noticed my cries for help and came to my aid. I silently thanked them for their delayed arrival while I wept bitterly over my mother’s body, perfectly imitating the role of a son grieving the loss of his mother in a foreign country.

The Sabah police seemed to suspect no foul play and quickly closed the case as an accident. The resort insisted that the beach where we went into the sea wasn’t designated as a swimming spot and therefore rejected my substantial compensation claim. In reality, I didn’t need any compensation at all. To avoid suspicion, I spent several days arguing, threatening to hire a lawyer, and then approaching the embassy for help. Finally, I extorted 50,000 Malaysian ringgit in compensation and tearfully brought my mother’s ashes back home.

It wasn’t until I set foot on my homeland that my heart truly settled.

My problem with my mother was completely resolved.

When good fortune struck, it was truly unstoppable. When the news of my disappearance had slowly spread through my friend circle, a junior schoolmate named Wang Xiaomian suddenly came up to me and confessed her love for me, saying she’d had a crush on me for years.

In the past, I would have laughed off such a confession and politely declined, but things were different now. I needed love to help me regain my confidence.

To be precise, whether it was love or not didn’t matter. I needed a woman, someone who would obey me and to whom I could show off my power.

And Xiaomian, as her name suggested, was as soft and adorable as cotton. She had no romantic experience and always looked at me with admiration. She was exactly the kind of woman I needed.

I accepted her confession, but I also wanted to test whether my “ability” had recovered. So, a few days after we established our relationship, I took her to a small hotel outside the school gates.

She truly didn’t know how to do anything, especially not how to say no. She was quickly captivated by my coaxing. Stripped naked, she closed her eyes, lay flat on the bed, and surrendered like a lamb to my will. Fortunately, she didn’t notice my penis had remained limp.

I panicked, but luck smiled on me once again. For some reason, when I noticed Xiao Mian shyly opening her eyes a fraction before hastily closing them again, my mind suddenly flashed back to the expression on my mother’s face as she drowned.

Xiaomian’s and my mother’s faces shifted, intertwined, and finally overlapped.

So, as a man, I rekindled my virility in Xiaomian, loudly declaring my ownership of her body and soul.

After our passionate lovemaking, Xiaomian drifted off to sleep with a contented smile, but I remained utterly aroused and awake the entire time.

Because I knew that Wang Donglin had finally been reborn.

I had found love, won back my studies, and upon graduation, successfully joined the faculty. Although I wasn’t teaching, I had become Teacher Wang, deeply respected and beloved by my students.

Teacher Wang, I liked that name.

CONTENT END 78

chapters.title: Chapter 79
chapters.content:
May 31st, 5:05 p.m., Huangjia Village Shopping Center.

Lu Tianfeng sat in a coffee shop near the entrance of the shopping center, absentmindedly stirring his cup of coffee. Although he hadn’t agreed on a specific meeting place with Tong Yao, he was confident that Tong Yao would be able to guess his location within a minute once she arrived.

Because this coffee shop was both the best observation point in the area and the most versatile escape route.

“I’m here.” As expected, Tong Yao sat down in the seat across from Lu Tianfeng. She wore plain glasses and had her hair simply curled; her entire appearance and demeanor were transformed.

“I’m sorry; this was a serious lapse on my part,” Lu Tianfeng apologized sincerely.

Tong Yao shook her head.

“How’s the situation over there?” Lu Tianfeng asked again.

Tong Yao briefly explained the internal police investigation and the special mission Director Luo had assigned her. Her original plan had been to meet with Lu Tianfeng and jointly interrogate Wang Donglin, but now everything was about to be rewritten.

“We must find Wang Donglin as soon as possible,” Tong Yao said.

The unspoken part of her words was that if Wang Donglin escaped, the fate of many people would be disastrous, including her own.

“Have you notified Director Luo?” Lu Tianfeng’s heart ached. So many people trusted him, yet he had messed things up. The feeling was too agonizing.

“I texted him, but he hasn’t replied yet.”

The lack of a reply was a sign of trust in them. Otherwise, Director Luo would have ordered Tong Yao to bring Lu Tianfeng back to the police station.

Lu Tianfeng took a sip of coffee and said slowly, “We have to find Wang Donglin before the police do; otherwise, all our efforts today will be in vain.”

“I suddenly remembered someone,” Tong Yao said. “He used to be our bureau’s top suspect hunter, but later, due to a conflict with his superiors, he resigned and left to open his own detective agency…”

“I know who you’re talking about,” Lu Tianfeng said with a helpless smile. “‘Hound,’ Zhang Zhiqi. It’s said there’s no one he can’t find, no information he can’t dig up, but he seems to hate the police, doesn’t he?”

“He just hates the police, not the money.” Tong Yao pointed out the window. The large screen in front of the Huangjia Village Shopping Plaza was broadcasting a special news report from the local TV station.

At the bottom of the screen, large red letters read: Wang Donglin Prison Escape Case: Police Increase Reward to 300,000 Yuan.

“Do you know where his detective agency is?” Lu Tianfeng asked.

“A cheap, mixed place, Qunxian Building.” Tong Yao checked the navigation app on her phone. “It’s a fifteen-minute walk.”

“What are we waiting for? Let’s go!”

.

May 31st, 5:25 p.m., Qunxian Building, Zhang Zhiqi Detective Agency.

This so-called detective agency was actually just a 12-13 square meter glass cubicle. The faded words “Zhang Zhiqi Detective Agency” were plastered on the glass door. Inside, there was only a desk, an old computer, and a mountain of newspapers and magazines.

Zhang Zhiqi didn’t even have an assistant, not because he was poor, but because no one could stand the work environment here. Besides, he didn’t like working with anyone less intelligent than himself.

But in Zhang Zhiqi’s eyes, there were far too few people as smart as him.

So he became known as the “Lone Wolf” among his peers, though he preferred the nickname he earned during his time in the police force—Hound.

A hound that never missed its prey.

Zhang Zhiqi’s fees were more than double those of other large firms, and his unassuming appearance, like an ordinary, unrecognizable man thrown into a crowd, caused many clients to back out early.

Zhang Zhiqi didn’t mind this situation at all. He even thought it was a good thing, as it helped him filter out less intelligent clients. Idiots were always troublesome, so he might as well focus on making money from the smart ones.

The office hours here were quite flexible. When he wasn’t conducting investigations, Zhang Zhiqi would rush over every morning after waking up. He would spend his time in the small office surfing the internet, chatting, and playing games. When he felt tired or sleepy, he would close the office and go home to sleep.

“Let’s go home for dinner…” Zhang Zhiqi stretched lazily. Just as he was about to shut down his computer and leave, a man and a woman, rather impolitely, pushed open the glass door and barged into his space.

“Sorry, we just closed,” Zhang Zhiqi frowned slightly, his tone remaining calm.

“Hello, Senior. I’ve met you once before…” Tong Yao said hurriedly.

“I remember you, Tong Yao, right?” Zhang Zhiqi interrupted, standing up without greeting either of them. “Then you should also remember what I said last time: I have no interest in interfering in any police investigation.”

“This time is different.” Tong Yao placed her phone directly in front of Zhang Zhiqi. The screen displayed the latest police reward announcement. “This time, there’s a huge reward of 300,000 yuan.”

Zhang Zhiqi glanced at it and scoffed. “How could I not understand the police’s tactics? It says the maximum reward is 300,000 yuan, but it doesn’t guarantee it.”

“Help us capture Wang Donglin, and I guarantee the reward will be the full 300,000 yuan.” Lu Tianfeng, who had been silent since entering, finally spoke.

Zhang Zhiqi looked Lu Tianfeng up and down and chuckled. “Excuse me, who are you?”

“Lu Tianfeng…”

“Deputy Captain of the Seventh Detachment of the D City Criminal Police Brigade, currently suspended under investigation.” Unexpectedly, Zhang Zhiqi finished the rest of his sentence for him.

Lu Tianfeng was stunned.

“Do you know me?”

Tong Yao nudged Lu Tianfeng’s elbow and whispered in his ear, “His hacking skills are impressive. He should be able to access our internal database.”

“So exaggerated?” Lu Tianfeng gasped.

“Isn’t this just basic stuff?” Zhang Zhiqi waved his hand dismissively. “Lu Tianfeng, I’ve followed the cases you’ve handled, and I have to admit, I have no idea how you obtained such top-secret intelligence, which is almost impossible to leak, during the course of your work.”

Lu Tianfeng naturally avoided answering this question.

Zhang Zhiqi carefully reviewed the news and announcements related to Wang Donglin’s escape on his computer and finally fell into deep thought.

After a long pause, Zhang Zhiqi finally asked, “The police have already issued a city-wide wanted order. Why would they send you two to look for a low-ranking detective like me? Does the chief think we’re more powerful than all the police officers in the city combined?”

“I’m here in my personal capacity.” Lu Tianfeng recounted briefly what happened today, omitting only the part about going through the time reversal.

Zhang Zhiqi listened quietly, never interrupting Lu Tianfeng. Even more remarkable, his expression remained perfectly composed, as if nothing at all surprised him.

“Has it never occurred to you that Wang Donglin might escape on his own?”

“At first, I was wary of him, but then…” Lu Tianfeng sighed. It turned out that just when he thought he was beginning to gain Wang Donglin’s trust, he had actually fallen into a trap set by Wang Donglin.

“This man actually managed to trick you? Interesting, very interesting.” While listening to Lu Tianfeng, Zhang Zhiqi had already opened the internal police file on the Wang Donglin serial murder case and was slowly reading through it.

Tong Yao’s suspicions were completely correct. This man had somehow managed to easily access the police database.

Lu Tianfeng glanced at his watch. It had been a full hour since Wang Donglin’s escape.

“Without further delay, if you’re willing to help, we’ll begin our operation immediately. If we can finally capture Wang Donglin, the entire reward will be yours. If you’re not interested, we’ll take our leave and not bother you again.”

Zhang Zhiqi said calmly, “What nonsense! I’m already studying Wang Donglin’s file, aren’t I? But I must state in advance that even if we don’t receive the reward offered by the police, you’ll still have to pay my retainer.”

“No problem,” Lu Tianfeng agreed immediately.

“You’d better check my prices first.” Zhang Zhiqi tossed over a laminated A4 sheet of paper, which turned out to be the firm’s price list. Lu Tianfeng glanced at it casually and said, “That’s a very reasonable price.”

“Oh?”

“You have an amazing memory. You were able to remember Tong Yao, whom you’d only met once, and even memorize my personal information from the vast sea of ​​police records. You possess extraordinary hacking skills, allowing you to navigate the police database with ease. You’re mentally stable, showing almost no emotion when you spoke to us. Furthermore, you have a very ordinary appearance, so ordinary that you could appear anywhere without looking out of place. You’re a natural investigator, and this fee is quite favorable.”

“Captain Lu, thank you for your compliment.” Zhang Zhiqi maintained his unfazed demeanor, but his tone was noticeably more polite.

“I hope we can enjoy our cooperation.” Lu Tianfeng extended his hand and shook Zhang Zhiqi’s hand quickly.

Tong Yao, standing nearby, chuckled quietly. Remembering the last time she’d been turned down by Zhang Zhiqi, her admiration for Lu Tianfeng grew even stronger.

“So, where should we go next?” Lu Tianfeng asked.

“We’ll stay here.” Zhang Zhiqi gestured to the computer screen. “We need to thoroughly understand Wang Donglin before we can predict his behavior. And the internet is the best tool for uncovering a person’s details.”

“Okay, I’ll listen.”

“But there’s a piece of news about you that just popped up online. Let’s take a look!”

Lu Tianfeng took a closer look. It was a trending article on a social media site titled “Wang Donglin’s Prison Escape: Was There Secret Assistance from a Police Insider? Can We Still Trust the Police in D City?”

Clicking on the article, he found not only pictures of the Fuhe Road crime scene but also a profile picture of Lu Tianfeng. The article specifically stated that Wang Donglin’s escape was closely related to Lu Tianfeng, who was currently under investigation.

Below the article, a flood of netizens, unaware of the truth, left angry comments, demanding that senior police officials come forward to clarify the incident and apprehend the murderer as soon as possible. Some even suggested that if Lu Tianfeng had nothing to do with the case, he should immediately reveal his identity to allay everyone’s concerns.

“That’s a cruel move.” Lu Tianfeng shook his head bitterly.

“Do you know who did it?” Zhang Zhiqi asked.

“It must be the group that wanted to kill Wang Donglin…”

“I remember now. The news of Wang Donglin’s escape was also leaked by an anonymous netizen.” Tong Yao patted her head, suddenly realizing. “So the enemy has been shooting secretly all along. How despicable.”

Zhang Zhiqi tapped away on his keyboard, saying nonchalantly, “Don’t worry. I’m here to track them down. By the way, there’s a fee for this.”

CONTENT END 79

chapters.title: Chapter 80
chapters.content:
May 31st, 5:35 p.m., Lu Tianfeng’s house

Chen Nuolan had a satisfying afternoon nap and walked out of the house refreshed. She prepared to drive to Moyun Town. Although she knew Lu Tianfeng wasn’t there, the police would surely become suspicious if she didn’t show up for her “appointment” at seven o’clock.

However, she didn’t expect that as soon as she got downstairs, a man wearing glasses and holding a microphone rushed over and rudely shoved the phone in her direction.
