“Ms. Chen, is Mr. Lu Tianfeng home?”

What was going on? Chen Nuolan glared at the man in confusion, then turned and walked away.

But then a short, well-mannered woman blocked her path.

“Ms. Chen, I’d like to ask, have you seen your boyfriend, Lu Tianfeng, today?”

Chen Nuolan frowned. She could see at least ten people rushing towards her from all directions, each holding a microphone, cell phone, or DV camera. Suddenly, she was surrounded.

“Are the rumors online true?”

“Why was Lu Tianfeng suspended for investigation?”

“It’s said that Lu Tianfeng deliberately let Wang Donglin go because he was dissatisfied with his suspension as a way to get back at society?”

“Ms. Chen, what do you know? Please respond directly!”

The cacophony of chatter made Chen Nuolan’s head spin. She hadn’t seen the news circulating online, and she had no idea why the reporters were hounding her. But from the scattered snippets of information, she had a rough idea of ​​what was going on.

“I’m sorry, I don’t know anything,” Chen Nuolan said, trying to break free. But it wasn’t that easy. Someone even reached out and grabbed her upper arm, preventing her from leaving.

“Ms. Chen, where are you going now?”

“Are you under police investigation?”

“Do you have anything to say to the netizens?”

Chen Nuolan shook her head repeatedly, but the group still swarmed around her like locusts, and for a moment, she couldn’t escape.

Just then, someone suddenly shouted, “What are you doing? Do you want to come back to the police station and talk it over?”

Everyone was startled and turned back to see a man charging towards them with a fierce look.

Chen Nuolan finally relaxed when she saw it was Yu Yongsheng.

“Disperse, disperse! I’m taking Chen Nuolan back for questioning.” Yu Yongsheng played his part flawlessly.

“Officer, you can’t interfere with our right to report…” a bold reporter protested, but Yu Yongsheng glared at him fiercely, and he swallowed the rest of his words.

“Who among you has a proper press card? If you do, show it. If not, please disperse. Don’t force me to do anything serious, okay?” Yu Yongsheng said firmly, his gaze sweeping across everyone’s faces.

He had determined that these so-called reporters who had rushed in to dig up information were basically unqualified online media outlets, so how could they possibly have press cards?

As expected, the moment these words were spoken, the crowd’s arrogance immediately subsided. Yu Yongsheng seized the opportunity to part the crowd and help Chen Nuolan escape.

“What’s going on?” Chen Nuolan asked quietly.

“We’ll talk as we walk,” Yu Yongsheng continued, not stopping. “On the way here, I checked the news on my phone and saw someone was smearing the boss online.”

“Could they be forcing a connection between him and Wang Donglin?” Chen Nuolan, incredibly intelligent, understood immediately.

“Yes, I’m afraid this will force the police to list the boss as a wanted criminal as well,” Yu Yongsheng sighed.

“Are you okay?” Chen Nuolan knew Yu Yongsheng’s mission and knew the police would definitely question him after the incident. She hadn’t expected him to escape so unscathed so quickly.

“I’m the bait.” Yu Yongsheng gave a wry smile and pointed at his feet. “They couldn’t get anything out of me, so they just let me out, hoping I’d go meet up with the boss. Now there’s a tracker on the sole of my shoe.”

“You knew there was a tracker, so why didn’t you remove it?”

“I deliberately stayed put, so they’d think I was just a reckless person.” Yu Yongsheng shrugged. “Sister Nuolan, where do you think I’d run to?”

Chen Nuolan’s eyes rolled, and she smiled. “What a coincidence! You can come with me to Moyun Town.”

.

May 31st, 6:00 p.m., Moyun Town, Cat’s Nest Cafe.

Cheng Tuo sat in the booth where Lu Tianfeng and Wang Donglin had sat a few hours earlier, gazing absentmindedly out the window. The sun was setting, night was approaching, and the streets of Moyun Town were slowly becoming bustling.

But the bustle before him couldn’t dispel the chill in Cheng Tuo’s heart.

He felt he might have been tricked.

The owner of the Cat’s Nest immediately recognized the two men from the photos and wanted posters who had been drinking coffee and chatting privately for over an hour there. She remarked that they seemed to have a good relationship, like old friends who had known each other for years.

Colleagues dispatched to investigate nearby also made some discoveries. The owner of an outdoor gear store said Lu Tianfeng had come to buy a tent. A waiter at a bakery had seen Wang Donglin and said he’d bought a large batch of bread. A bookstore clerk reported that someone resembling Wang Donglin had purchased a detailed off-road map of Moyun Mountain.

All signs indicated that Lu Tianfeng and Wang Donglin were planning to sneak into the Moyun Mountain area. Once they entered the undeveloped area of ​​the mountain range, locating them would be like finding a needle in a haystack.

“Captain Cheng, Chen Nuolan is driving to Moyun Town. We also spotted Yu Yongsheng in her car,” a young subordinate hurried over to report the latest situation.

“Why are they both here together?” Cheng Tuo’s brow furrowed even more.

“I guess they’re meeting up with Lu Tianfeng? We could just catch them all in one fell swoop.”

“Chen Nuolan knew we were following her, yet she brazenly went to meet him? Besides, Yu Yongsheng’s no fool. Wouldn’t he understand why we let him go at this critical juncture?” Cheng Tuo sighed. “This place is getting increasingly suspicious. We might have come all this way in vain.”

“Captain Cheng…” The young man seemed to want to say something but hesitated.

“Continue the search. I’ll contact headquarters. Other departments shouldn’t stop either. Don’t just rely on us closing the net and arresting them.”

Cheng Tuo’s phone rang. He saw it was Director Luo and quickly answered.

“Director Luo, please give instructions.”

“The latest news is that Lu Tianfeng and Wang Donglin are no longer operating together. Wang Donglin is likely not in Moyun Town but in D City.”

“Director Luo, is your source reliable?” Cheng Tuo broke out in a cold sweat. Even commanding from the front lines, he still felt a lingering fog. How could the director, sitting in his office, have such precise intelligence?

“Absolutely reliable. Adjust personnel arrangements immediately.”

“Understood!”

Cheng Tuo hung up the phone and shook his head helplessly. The operation in Moyun Town was already scheduled, and it had to be launched. How could he adjust the arrangements?

This matter was truly complex.

.

May 31st, 6:10 p.m., Qunxian Building, Zhang Zhiqi Detective Agency.

Zhang Zhiqi was typing away on his keyboard, switching between four different program windows open simultaneously on his screen. He absolutely did not want to be disturbed at this moment.

Therefore, Lu Tianfeng and Tong Yao sat silently to the side, each holding an old magazine and aimlessly flipping through it.

The keyboard tapping suddenly stopped, and Lu Tianfeng subconsciously raised his head, just in time to meet Zhang Zhiqi’s gaze.

“How is it?” Lu Tianfeng asked.

“Some progress,” Zhang Zhiqi’s tone remained calm.

“Tell me about it!” Lu Tianfeng was a little excited.

He was well aware of the difficulty of tracking down Wang Donglin, and Zhang Zhiqi had only spent the better part of an hour, so for him to calmly say “some progress” was already quite remarkable.

“Actually, as long as we find the right breakthrough, it’s not that difficult.” Zhang Zhiqi finally smiled. “Where do you think the breakthrough is?”

Lu Tianfeng was stunned, not expecting Zhang Zhiqi to keep him in suspense. He glanced at Tong Yao, who also looked helpless.

Zhang Zhiqi continued, “The breakthrough actually lies with Captain Lu.”

“With me?”

“That’s right. Captain Lu’s actions were well-prepared, but Wang Donglin wasn’t. How could someone so unprepared suddenly abandon their well-prepared companions and flee alone? He didn’t even have a penny on him, so where could he go?”

Lu Tianfeng suddenly understood why he hadn’t been wary of Wang Donglin. He had assumed Wang Donglin would need to rely on him to escape.

But Wang Donglin’s actions proved Lu Tianfeng wrong.

“So my conclusions are twofold: first, there must be someone Wang Donglin trusts completely, someone he can turn to without worry; second, Wang Donglin must have found a way to get around, or at least some money for an emergency.”

“By comparison, money is a bit easier to solve,” Tong Yao said.

Zhang Zhiqi nodded. “I thought so too. Captain Lu, if you were faced with a similar situation, how would you handle it?”

“I’d probably try to steal some money,” Lu Tianfeng said sheepishly.

“Wang Donglin might use a similar method, but judging by his criminal record, he’s more accustomed to leveraging his personal charm to achieve his goals. If I were Wang Donglin, I’d try to trick a child into taking his transit card.”

Lu Tianfeng couldn’t help but marvel at this method. Not only was it safer, but it also had a high success rate—it truly suited Wang Donglin’s style.

“Wang Donglin’s escape coincided with the end of school at two nearby elementary schools and a middle school. So, I searched the city transit card database and compiled a list of all the students from those three schools who had applied for student discount cards. There were 835 of them in total.”

Ordinary transit cards were anonymous, but student cards, which offer a 50% discount on rides, required real-name registration to ensure the user was a student. Zhang Zhiqi’s idea immediately clarified the scope of the investigation.

“After 4:30 p.m., there were a total of 173 student cards with recorded usage. I extracted the cardholders’ home addresses and historical usage records, and I can basically confirm that none of the 170 cards are out of the ordinary. Only these three are suspicious.”

Zhang Zhiqi made it sound casual, but in reality, he had to search through several databases and employ clever methods to perform comparisons and screening to pinpoint his target so quickly. He accomplished this effortlessly, truly worthy of the name “Hunter.”

Lu Tianfeng took a look and saw that one of the cards had been used on the subway, entering from Huangjia Village and exiting at D City University. The other two cards had been used on the bus, and the two people were not on their usual routes.

“Did these two people seem to be riding the same bus?” Tong Yao asked.

Zhang Zhiqi took a closer look. “Yes, Bus No. 238, the same one.”

“Check the transit card registration information.”

“Yang Jian and Pang Feifei, both third-year students at Huangjia Village Middle School, are classmates.”

“A boy and a girl? Could they be a couple sneaking out to play together?” Tong Yao said with a smile.

Lu Tianfeng pointed to the subway record and said, “This one is the most suspicious. Don’t forget, Wang Donglin has a close connection to D City University.”

Tong Yao hesitated and said, “But he should know that where he works and lives is under strict surveillance. Running back to the university—wouldn’t that be too dangerous, right?”

“It’s a risky move. We first need to confirm whether the person using this transit card is Wang Donglin.”

Lu Tianfeng glanced at Zhang Zhiqi, who shrugged and made a helpless gesture.

“Don’t rush me. I’m trying to check the subway surveillance. Give me five more minutes…”

Before he could finish his words, the lights in the room suddenly went out, and everything was pitch black.

The power went out.

“Do you often have power outages here?” Lu Tianfeng asked warily.

“No, this is the first time.” Zhang Zhiqi opened a drawer, pulled out something, and handed it to Lu Tianfeng. “I know what you’re worried about. Here, the stun gun.”

“Be careful,” Lu Tianfeng urged Tong Yao, who then unsheathed her service pistol.

The interior of the Qunxian Building lacked almost all natural lighting. After the power outage, everything was pitch black. The hallways lacked even the most basic emergency lighting. Although it was past six o’clock, many employees were still working overtime, leading to complaints and some even quarreling for unknown reasons.

“Where is the emergency exit?” Lu Tianfeng asked in a low voice.

“There are two. You can turn left or right when you get out; just keep going. But it seems a bit chaotic outside right now, so I suggest you hold off for now,” Zhang Zhiqi said calmly.

“No, let’s go next door,” Lu Tianfeng said decisively, leading the two outside.

Next door was an e-commerce company, three times the size of Zhang Zhiqi’s office. Zhang Zhiqi knew their receptionist, and after a quick hello, he walked straight in, not caring if she cared or not.

“Brother Qi, what’s going on? The power went out all of a sudden?” the young receptionist asked.

“I don’t know, but I need to borrow your office temporarily,” Zhang Zhiqi said mysteriously. “My two customers are both important people, and my place is too small. It’s really stuffy without the power and air conditioning.”

As Zhang Zhiqi spoke, he slipped something to the receptionist. The girl smiled and pretended not to notice.

The corridor was bustling with noise and clamor, and someone could faintly hear someone cursing.

“Are you blind? How are you walking?”

“Hey, do you have any manners?”

However, the scolded person said nothing.

“Be careful; they might be enemies,” Lu Tianfeng warned.

Three flashlights beamed down the corridor, followed by the sound of shattering glass. The intruders kicked open the office’s glass door.

“The glass door will be charged separately!” Zhang Zhiqi muttered softly.

Faced with the deserted office, the intruders remained silent. After a moment’s silence, they quickly retreated.

Lu Tianfeng wasn’t willing to let them go easily. After a gesture to Tong Yao, he quietly returned to the corridor, taking advantage of the darkness and chaos to follow.

“Perfect timing,” Zhang Zhiqi murmured, praising him softly, and then followed them on tiptoe. Tong Yao couldn’t stay here alone, so she had to join them.

In the pitch-black corridor, three menacing figures parted the crowd, sprinting towards the emergency exit.

Without warning, one of the figures stopped moving.

Lu Tianfeng knew the enemy a few meters away had probably sensed he was being followed, but he didn’t hesitate. He continued walking at his usual pace, saying, “Excuse me, please make way. Thank you.”

The man, about the same height as Lu Tianfeng, almost instinctively moved aside to allow him to pass.

Just as Lu Tianfeng brushed past the man, he suddenly struck out, aiming for his throat.

In the dim light, in a split second, the man didn’t fall but instead used his sturdy arms to block Lu Tianfeng’s attack.

With his top-notch skills and professional techniques, Lu Tianfeng could almost be sure this was the same mercenary group that had attacked him and Wang Donglin in Tiedao New Village that afternoon.

In a flash, the others were already watching the excitement. Zhang Zhiqi reacted the fastest, sliding forward and delivering a sweeping kick, hitting the opponent’s most vulnerable spot. Tong Yao and the other two mercenaries simultaneously assumed firing positions.

Lu Tianfeng, fearing he would accidentally injure the others, quickly shouted, “Get out of the way!”

Tong Yao certainly wouldn’t fire carelessly, but the other party didn’t care—”Bang!”

In this narrow, enclosed corridor, the sound of the bullets exploding was deafening.

At the same moment, Zhang Zhiqi had just knocked the enemy to the ground. Without giving him a chance to struggle, Lu Tianfeng delivered a relentless kick to the back of the head, knocking him unconscious.

“Get out of the way!”

“Bang! Bang! Bang!”

Three more shots were fired, and Lu Tianfeng and Zhang Zhiqi tumbled to the sides in panic, trying to protect themselves.

Tong Yao fired back. Her advantage was that the enemy was closer to the emergency exit, providing more light, which facilitated her aim.

But the sound of another submachine gun disrupted the seemingly balanced situation.

“Bang, bang, bang—”

Screams, wails, shattering glass, and the sound of objects crashing—as if countless sounds rang out simultaneously, filling the entire room.

Lu Tianfeng pressed himself against the wall, waiting for the gap between rounds of ammunition to finish. Then, gathering all his strength, he swung the electric baton.

“Bam!” The electric baton slammed heavily against the iron door of the emergency exit.

Although it missed the enemy, he had temporarily abandoned his most advantageous attack position to evade them.

As the enemy’s attack slowed, Lu Tianfeng and Zhang Zhiqi instantly connected, reaching out to grab the unconscious man’s ankles and forcefully pulling him back.

As long as they could capture him alive and interrogate him thoroughly, they would surely uncover his background.

“Tong Yao, cover us.”

“Roger!”

Tong Yao no longer spared her ammunition, firing repeatedly and suppressing the enemy’s fire, allowing Lu Tianfeng and Zhang Zhiqi to safely escort the suspect.

The enemy, knowing full well they couldn’t remain here for long, returned fire with all their might. After a hail of bullets, the two mercenaries fled through the emergency exit. Lu Tianfeng didn’t dare pursue them and quickly turned on his flashlight to survey his surroundings.

Glass shattered everywhere, and many people fell to the ground, their faces, hands, and feet stained with blood. Fortunately, the injured appeared to have only been scratched by the broken glass; no one had been shot.

The only person shot was the man they had accidentally caught. He had two dark bullet holes in his chest and a bullet wound in his thigh. He was covered in blood and looked beyond saving.

“What a ruthless attack!” Lu Tianfeng realized that the other two mercenaries, as they retreated, had fired all their bullets into their companion, silencing him.

Zhang Zhiqi checked the man’s breath, felt his pulse, and shook his head, “Dead.”

“Call the police, call an ambulance, and then we’ll leave.” Lu Tianfeng’s chest suddenly tightened, the unpleasant pain lingering like a shadow.

“Where to go next?” Tong Yao asked.

“D City University,” Lu Tianfeng thought. Every second counted.

CONTENT END 80

chapters.title: Chapter 81
chapters.content:
Wang Donglin’s Memories (III)

Perhaps I was a cursed person, destined to be utterly unreachable by happiness.

In the eyes of others, I had completely emerged from the shadow of my parents’ death a few years ago. I had a stable and respected job, school-assigned housing, and a girlfriend who was completely obedient and ready to marry me. Outside of work, I used my ample free time to pick up chess again, having abandoned it for years, and even won championships in some low-level amateur tournaments.

They said this kind of life was truly enviable.

But only I knew best that the real shadow had never dissipated.

Every time I was with Xiaomian, I had to recall the scene of my mother’s drowning in order to become a real man. But as time went by, the memory of that scene gradually faded.

Xiaomian also noticed that my “interest” in her seemed to be gradually waning, but she thought I was just a little bored, so she did everything she could to rekindle my passion for her.

But what would she think if she found out the problem was me?

Moli’s harsh words from back then still echoed in my ears.

I absolutely couldn’t destroy the perfect image I held in Xiaomian’s eyes, but what could I do?

I could only watch helplessly as the rift between us widened. If this continued, I would lose her.

Even more terrifying was the fear that if she learned my secret, she would tell everyone about it, like a joke. Then, the whole world would know I was a cowardly, incompetent man.

I began to numb myself with alcohol. Xiaomian would go back to her parents’ house in a neighboring city every weekend or two, and whenever she wasn’t home, I would drive alone, far from school, to drink.

Drinking and driving was certainly dangerous, but I always limited myself to one or two drinks to avoid losing consciousness. The thrill of breaking the rules gave me an inexplicable thrill.

I needed excitement, more intense excitement.

Fate finally gave me a chance.

That day, Xiaomian wasn’t home, so I went to a newly opened nightclub in the southern suburbs to try it out. It was crowded with young people, and the music was a bit loud. I only ordered a mojito and slowly drank it all night.

As I left, I noticed a light rain falling from the sky, and the parking lot had become muddy. I couldn’t help but curse myself. There were so many bars and nightclubs in the city; why did I have to come here tonight?

Then, I got my answer.

From a distance, I saw a woman in a red shirt and a denim skirt. She held an umbrella in one hand and the other on my car’s rearview mirror. She stood awkwardly on tiptoe, as if she was about to lean over the hood. I guessed she was quite drunk; the umbrella didn’t cover her at all, and her upper body was almost soaked.

“Excuse me…” I still greeted her politely.

“Ah, teacher, it’s you!” The girl turned around. It was a familiar face, but I couldn’t remember her name.

“Hello…” I said hesitantly.

Even in the dim light, the girl’s face was flushed. She smiled and said, “I just remember the teacher’s car was this color, and then I saw that… our school pass…”

I followed her finger and saw it was an internal parking pass for D City University.

“You’re from our school too, right? I think I’ve seen you before!”

“Yes, I’m Jiang Suyu, a junior in the philosophy department. I worked part-time in the student affairs office last year.” As she spoke, she shuddered.

I quickly unlocked the car and invited her in. “It’s late. If you want to go back to school, I’d give you a ride.”

Jiang Suyu didn’t hesitate, nodded, and got in. To my surprise, as soon as she settled into the passenger seat, tears began to fall.

“Wuwuwu—” she sobbed non-stop. I tried to soothe her while driving, but to no avail.

I had no choice but to find a secluded spot to stop the car and comfort her. Ten minutes later, she finally calmed down a bit and spoke in fragments about why she was there tonight.

Jiang Suyu had been suddenly dumped by her boyfriend of many years. After a heart-wrenching scolding, she ran out of the school gate, hopped on a random bus, and rode all the way to the terminal. She happened to see this brightly lit nightclub and walked into it for the first time in her life. She counted her cash, ordered every cocktail on the menu, and drank away her living expenses for the month.

Half-drunk, she realized the bus had stopped running long ago, and she didn’t have enough money to take a taxi back to school. To make matters worse, she had broken her phone during a quarrel with her boyfriend earlier and couldn’t even turn it on. Perhaps emboldened by the alcohol, she braved the rain and ran into the parking lot, intending to strike up a conversation with a random driver and beg them to take her back to school. It was then that she recognized my car and my school pass.

“Suyu, you’re so lucky!”

“Wuwuwu… I’m so lucky… I won’t… meet a scumbag… Wuwuwu…” Her voice gradually faded, probably tired from crying, and the alcohol taking its toll.

“Stop crying. Get some rest. It’ll take over half an hour to get back to school.”

“Hmm… Wuwuwu…”

“Are you cold?” I saw her shivering and casually threw my coat over her.

Jiang Suyu didn’t answer. She had already fallen asleep, her head tilted to one side, leaning back against the seat.

Suddenly, another voice echoed in my ears. It belonged to a man, a calm, ruthless, demonic man.

“Take her home,” the man said.

“No, I’m not interested in her,” I argued. “You don’t, but I do.”

Then, I became a bystander, watching helplessly as the man drove the unconscious Jiang Suyu to his home.

I was completely powerless to stop him.

I had complained about the house the school had assigned me, located in the far corner of the dormitory area, on the dampest first floor, and about the previous owner’s extravagant bathtub in the tiny bathroom.

Unexpectedly, all this only served to further the man’s evil plan.

He parked his car under the shed at the door so he could bring Jiang Suyu inside without being seen.

Another man might have carried the unconscious girl to bed, but he rushed to the bathroom without hesitation, grasped her under the arms, and laboriously lowered her into the bathtub.

Jiang Suyu hummed a few words in a dreamlike manner but did not wake up.

The man began to remove her clothes, folding them neatly aside. She, limp and powerless, subconsciously cooperated with his movements.

The girl quickly returned to her naked state at birth. The bathtub was still running, the water neither too hot nor too cold, perfect for a bath. Even in her sleep, she probably felt the comfort and warmth, her face flushed and a happy smile spread.

The man also smiled brightly.

“No, no!”

I screamed with all my might, but no sound came out.

The water in the bathtub rose higher and higher, and the man grew more and more excited.

He gently caressed the girl’s body, then brought out the body wash and carefully rubbed every inch of her skin. His movements were very gentle, afraid to wake her from her deep sleep and ruin the beautiful atmosphere.

Finally, the bathtub was full, and the girl was clean, spotless.

He kissed her forehead, then grasped her shoulders and pushed her completely under the water.

The moment the water rushed into her airway, the girl woke up with a start. She opened her eyes in fear, unable to believe what was happening. She kicked her legs wildly, trying to struggle, but before she could truly exert any strength, her helpless struggle was over.

The girl’s eyes widened, soaking quietly in the water.

She seemed to be asking me—why didn’t I save her?

“I couldn’t help it!”

Because I was that man, and that man was me!

I finally breathed a sigh of relief. Killing Jiang Suyu was a hundred times more thrilling than killing my mother.

I hoped this powerful dose would be enough for Xiaomian and me to live a good life together.

So I sat down on the edge of the bathtub, took the girl’s still-warm hand, and whispered, “Thank you, Jiang Suyu. I will be forever grateful to you.”

CONTENT END 81

chapters.title: Chapter 82
chapters.content:
May 31st, 6:20 p.m., Moyun Town, in the police command vehicle.

Cheng Tuo’s brow furrowed as he pondered Director Luo’s instructions. The more he thought about it, the more he felt something was amiss. Director Luo’s words, “Immediately adjust staffing arrangements,” could be interpreted in many different ways. Could it be that his superiors were planning to cancel the operation in Moyun Town?

“Captain Cheng, Chen Nuolan’s car has arrived in Moyun Town.” A subordinate’s report brought Cheng Tuo back to his senses.

“Exact location!”

“She dropped Yu Yongsheng off near Bar Street and then… headed towards the old district.”

The new district of Moyun Town was a bustling tourist destination, while the old district was mostly residential. Cheng Tuo hadn’t expected Chen Nuolan and Yu Yongsheng to split up, let alone Chen Nuolan to head straight for the old district.

“Does she have any relatives or friends living in the old district? Check!” Cheng Tuo groaned inwardly.

“Chen Nuolan has two aunts living in Moyun Town…”

“Oh no!” Cheng Tuo slapped his thigh fiercely. “Send someone to her aunt’s house immediately and keep them under close surveillance.”

Elsewhere, colleagues tracking Yu Yongsheng reported that he had seemingly chosen a bar at random, sat down, ordered a beer, and was drinking it leisurely, not at all looking like he was waiting for anyone.

“Captain Cheng, Chen Nuolan has arrived at her aunt’s house. We can see clearly with the telescope. There are four people in the house: Chen Nuolan, her aunt and uncle, and a little boy, presumably her cousin. There’s no sign of Lu Tianfeng or Wang Donglin.”

Reports came pouring in, but none of them were good news.

Completely fooled. Just then, Cheng Tuo’s phone vibrated.

“This is Cheng Tuo; go ahead.”

“Captain Cheng, something’s happened. A gunfight just broke out at the Qunxian Building in Huangjia Village.” It was Wu Guoqing on the other end.

“A gunfight?” Cheng Tuo still didn’t understand what this had to do with him.

Wu Guoqing quickly said, “Yes, there’s surveillance video confirming Lu Tianfeng was at the scene of the gunfight.”

Cheng Tuo chuckled self-deprecatingly. The dragnet he’d laid in Moyun Town had ultimately come to nothing.

That cunning fish had slipped away long ago.

.

May 31st, 6:45 p.m., D City University, faculty dormitory area.

“Wang Donglin’s home is over there,” Tong Yao said, pointing to a building not far away. “It’s in the corner unit on the first floor, out of sight from the main road.”

Lu Tianfeng surveyed the surroundings, his gaze finally settling on a white van on the side of the road. “That doesn’t leave many surveillance locations to choose from,” he said.

Zhang Zhiqi also stared at the van. For experienced police officers like them, a quick glance at the scene would reveal where the police had deployed their surveillance. In other words, they could formulate targeted tactical plans.

“So, should we try to get in?” Tong Yao asked.

“Wang Donglin’s wife, Wang Xiaomian, should still be living here. Could Wang Donglin have come here to look for her?” Zhang Zhiqi speculated.

Lu Tianfeng shook his head. “Wang Donglin should be well aware that his wife is under close surveillance. Going to see her would be like walking into a trap.”

“Or perhaps they have some special method of communication?”

Lu Tianfeng and Tong Yao exchanged a glance. Indeed, Wang Donglin might be clever enough to have already prepared a secret communication method with his wife.

At this moment, Zhang Zhiqi remarked, “Wang Xiaomian is no ordinary woman. Wang Donglin caused such a big incident, and not only did she not become his ex-wife, but she even dared to continue living at the murder scene. She’s truly bold!”

Lu Tianfeng felt a strange feeling in his heart. Zhang Zhiqi’s words had hit the nail on the head. What Wang Xiaomian did was indeed not something an ordinary girl could do. If she would risk her life to protect Wang Donglin, that was also logical.

It seemed they had to find a way to meet Wang Xiaomian.

A few minutes later, Tong Yao knocked on the window of the white van.

The two young police officers inside the van grew nervous upon seeing a strange face. “Criminal Police Brigade, First Detachment, Tong Yao.” Tong Yao flashed her officer ID. “Has Wang Donglin’s wife been out of the house?”

This directness, without any prelude or explanation, actually put the two young men at ease. One of them answered honestly, “She’s been staying home the whole time. She hasn’t gone out, and no suspicious individuals have approached.”

“That’s good…”

Tong Yao had barely finished her words when a bicycle suddenly hurtled toward her, nearly hitting her. She screamed and jumped aside, causing the cyclist to lose balance and fall to the ground. The bicycle then slammed into a parked van.

“What the hell are you doing!” Tong Yao shouted angrily.

The cyclist bowed submissively to Tong Yao, repeatedly apologizing. The impetuous man was none other than Zhang Zhiqi.

The series of unexpected incidents distracted the two young police officers. Although they quickly resumed their surveillance, Lu Tianfeng had already seized the opportunity and slipped into the dormitory building.

Lu Tianfeng knocked gently on the door, and soon a haggard, petite woman opened it.

“Who is it?”

“Police, I’m here to see Mrs. Wang about something,” Lu Tianfeng said, flashing his ID.

Wang Xiaomian didn’t even bother to examine him. She lowered her head and replied, “Oh,” before letting Lu Tianfeng in. Perhaps she’d been interrogated so many times by the police that she’d become numb to it.

“How’s Mrs. Wang doing lately?”

Wang Xiaomian was stunned, not expecting the officer to start with such a question.

“Not bad,” she replied hesitantly.

“You must have been under a lot of pressure today, right?”

Wang Xiaomian, unable to discern the officer’s intentions, grew even more cautious, biting her lip in silence.

Lu Tianfeng threw out another false bait: “After Wang Donglin escaped today, the information the police currently have indicates that he was last seen at D City University.”

Surprisingly, Wang Xiaomian’s face flickered with fear at this.

“Why did he come back?”

“Maybe he wanted to contact you. He’s broke and can’t get far.”

Wang Xiaomian shrank back, shaking her head.

“No, he won’t come to me… Even if he does, I won’t help him!” she cried hysterically.

“Why? He’s still your husband—”

“I hate him!” Wang Xiaomian interrupted Lu Tianfeng with gritted teeth. “Don’t you understand? He doesn’t love me at all. He just wants a woman who’s completely devoted to him. ‘Getting married and having children’ is what he considers his life’s fulfillment, and I’ve unfortunately become a victim.”

“Then why don’t you leave—”

“Leave? Where could I go?” Wang Xiaomian laughed sadly. “When that guy was arrested, we’d only been married for less than six months. My parents were against the marriage to begin with, and after the scandal broke, they disowned me. Relatives and friends treat me like a plague, avoiding me like a demon. I can’t even find a stable job. I want to rent a place away from the media spotlight, but I simply can’t afford it. Do you think I like living here? The souls of three innocent women are lingering in the bathroom…”

Wang Xiaomian grew increasingly emotional as she spoke, her face flushed, her chest heaving. It was as if she had finally let out what she had been suppressing for a long time.

Lu Tianfeng believed in his heart that what she said was true, and Wang Donglin should not have come back.

But why had he gone all the way to the D City University subway station?

Suddenly, a tightness in his chest seized Lu Tianfeng, and a more terrifying possibility occurred to him—Wang Donglin was imitating his tactics. In just a few hours, he had mastered all the essentials of escaping police pursuit.

The only reason he appeared nearby was to lure Lu Tianfeng away.

“If that’s true, this man is truly terrifying…” Lu Tianfeng muttered to himself.

“No, I don’t think he’s human at all,” Wang Xiaomian said coldly, tears streaming down her face.

.

May 31st, 7:00 p.m., northern suburbs of D City.

On a secluded riverbank, a red sedan sat crookedly under a highway bridge. No one was around, and the car swayed slightly.

Finally, the shaking stopped.

The disheveled woman slumped in the back seat, panting, her face flushed. “You rascal! You just lied to me, saying you wanted to go to the bar to relax, and now—” the woman said coquettishly.

“It’s not bad to relax here,” Wang Donglin smiled, slipping his hand under the woman’s blouse.

“Well… but I still want to go to Moyun Town to see some more.”

“Okay, I promise. I’ll take you there later,” Wang Donglin said, lowering his head to kiss the woman in his arms.

He had long known that his physical charm was one of his greatest weapons, and he must never waste it.

After a passionate kiss, the woman felt weak all over and whispered tenderly, “That’s enough… Let’s get going…”

“Is that really enough?” Wang Donglin stared at her mischievously.

The woman shyly turned away: “Well, that’s enough. How about you drive?”

“Okay, let me take you on your way.”

The woman nodded happily.

Wang Donglin sighed inwardly. Why were there so many stupid women in this world?

Taking advantage of the opportunity when the woman lowered her head to button her clothes, Wang Donglin raised his right hand and hit the back of the woman’s neck with the edge of his palm.

“Ah!” the woman cried out, falling forward, her head banging against the back of the front seat.

She felt dizzy, and before she could comprehend what had happened, she was hit again on the back of her head. Then, her vision went black, and she lost consciousness.

Wang Donglin helped the unconscious woman out of the car, slowly leading her to the river.

The river looked black at night, even darker than the night itself.

“Don’t trust men so easily in your next life.” Wang Donglin crouched down, leaning close to the woman’s ear, and spoke in the gentlest of words.

The woman seemed to realize something, and her right hand struggled to grab a corner of Wang Donglin’s clothes. She stirred, but she didn’t wake up.

And there was no chance of waking up again.

Wang Donglin pressed her head firmly into the river and began to hum a nursery rhyme:

“Twinkle, twinkle, little star, how I wonder what you are… Wait, there are no stars tonight.”

There were no stars, no moonlight. The sky above, like Wang Donglin’s heart, was filled with darkness.

Soon, the woman’s hand loosened, drooping limply into the river.

The surrounding silence made Wang Donglin’s breathing sound especially heavy.

CONTENT END 82

chapters.title: Chapter 83
chapters.content:
May 31st, 7:30 p.m., D City University, Faculty and Staff Dormitory.

Retired Professor Yuan Chengren had just returned home from a walk downstairs. Less than two minutes later, before his pot of hot tea was even brewed, the doorbell rang.

“Who’s there?” Yuan Chengren asked, slowly pacing to open the door.

“Teacher Yuan, it’s me, Zhang Zhiqi.”

Yuan Chengren opened the door and looked at Zhang Zhiqi standing there. He was stunned for a moment, then burst into laughter.

“Oh my, I haven’t seen you in a few years. How come you’ve matured so much!”

Zhang Zhiqi smiled awkwardly and said, “Teacher, I’m not mature; I’m old.”

“Nonsense! Do you have the right to say ‘old’ in my presence?” Yuan Chengren patted Zhang Zhiqi’s shoulder, and the master and apprentice walked into the house, chatting and laughing.

Yuan Chengren was a renowned criminal psychologist in China. When Zhang Zhiqi was a student in the Department of Psychology at D City University, Yuan Chengren was the department head and also taught the undergraduate criminal psychology course.

At that time, Zhang Zhiqi’s grades in other subjects were mediocre, but he was particularly enthusiastic about criminal psychology. During class discussions and research papers, he always came up with insightful ideas.

One day during a break, Zhang Zhiqi approached Yuan Chengren with an American case to discuss. After Yuan Chengren shared his thoughts, he casually asked, “Zhang Zhiqi, are you particularly interested in this course?”

“Yes, my dream is to be a criminal profiler.”

“Haha, but there aren’t any professional criminal profilers in China yet!”

“Then let me be the first!” Zhang Zhiqi’s answer was filled with the confidence and passion typical of youth, and it made Yuan Chengren remember this student.

Thus, even after so many years, the two men still felt very cordial when they met. Without many pleasantries or small talk, they got straight to the point.

“Zhiqi, you came all the way here today. You didn’t just want to catch up with an old man like me, did you?”

“To be honest, I make a living as a private investigator, and the commission I received today is to track down this guy.” Zhang Zhiqi held up Wang Donglin’s photo. “The police reward has reached 300,000 yuan. That’s a lot of money!”

“Wang Donglin?” Yuan Chengren frowned. He had also seen the news about Wang Donglin’s escape on TV, but he hadn’t expected his student to join the pursuit.

“Teacher Yuan, I’ve reviewed Wang Donglin’s file. He’s been diagnosed with severe schizophrenia, split personality disorder, and paranoia by three professional institutions in China. One of these institutions is our school’s Criminal Psychology Laboratory—”

“I know what you’re asking. I did participate in the evaluation, and as long as it doesn’t involve confidential information, I can answer some of your questions.” Yuan Chengren brewed two cups of tea and said with a smile, “Of course, that depends on your questioning skills.”

Zhang Zhiqi couldn’t help but think of the teacher who used to challenge his students with tricky questions in class.

“You used to ask questions, but today it’s finally my turn!” Zhang Zhiqi thought for a moment before saying, “I only have one question: if you were the commander of the manhunt, what would you do?”

Yuan Chengren was stunned for a moment, then burst into laughter, proud of his student’s cunning. This was just a scenario-based question; there was no way he could directly leak secrets. However, to answer it properly, he would need to consciously or unconsciously use the inside information he possessed. It was a surefire question.

Zhang Zhiqi had precisely observed Yuan Chengren’s reverence for criminal psychology and his witty personality and knew he wouldn’t be vague in his response.

“How can I, with my old bones, be a commander?” Yuan Chengren sighed, finishing his tea in one gulp.

Zhang Zhiqi naturally heard the hidden meaning in his teacher’s words, but he remained silent, only smiling.

Yuan Chengren set down his teacup, his eyes flashing with a fierce, imposing light. Someone like him must devote himself to work and reflection to truly realize his true self-worth.

“I believe that in this emergency, Wang Donglin will act according to his usual thinking patterns and may even commit another crime. Therefore, I will be tracking him based on the following keywords—the first is ‘water.’ Wang Donglin only kills by drowning, and he has an unwavering obsession with ‘water.'”

“That means a river or lake, but escaping along a river is more likely. After all, it allows for greater distances and makes it harder to detect.” Zhang Zhiqi’s mind was already conjuring up a map of the entire city. According to Yuan Chengren’s deduction, Wang Donglin’s most likely route was along the Baiyun River, which runs through D City.

“The second key word is ‘people.’ Wang Donglin is extremely charismatic and eloquent. Choosing densely populated areas would not only make it easier to conceal his whereabouts, but he could also use the surrounding population to provide cover.”

Yuan Chengren closed his eyes as he spoke, and in his mind, like Zhang Zhiqi, a map appeared. On this imaginary map, densely populated areas along the Baiyun River were marked.

“What do you think the third keyword is?” Yuan Chengren deliberately kept it a secret.

Zhang Zhiqi had a photographic memory and remembered Wang Donglin’s file details perfectly. Three of the four victims were taken by Wang Donglin while intoxicated, and the remaining victim had drunk a cocktail laced with sleeping pills.

“It’s ‘alcohol.’ Wang Donglin liked to scout his victims in bars.” Zhang Zhiqi snapped his fingers. The three clues—the banks of the Baiyun River, a busy area, and a bar cluster—all pointed to the same location.

Moyun Town.

Zhang Zhiqi’s expression suddenly dawned on him, and Yuan Chengren nodded approvingly. Although neither master nor apprentice spoke, they both knew the other had grasped the point.

“Teacher, I have another question. Why do you think Wang Donglin will continue his pattern of crime instead of retreating into hiding?” This was the main premise of Yuan Chengren’s analysis, but Zhang Zhiqi wasn’t completely convinced.

Yuan Chengren gave a thumbs-up. “I came to this conclusion because I spoke with Wang Donglin several times during the evaluation process, and it’s clear to me that he’s a very strange case.”

“Strange?”

Yuan Chengren remained silent for a moment, seemingly weighing his words. After a long pause, he spoke again: “Do you remember the textbook description of split personality?”

“Dissociative intermittent personality dissociation: Patients with more than one personality possess multiple traits, often manifesting with bizarre beliefs and behaviors, unusual habits, bizarre speech, paranormal perceptions, apathy, lack of emotional experience, and aloofness.”

“Yes, you remember that personalities can perceive and communicate with each other?”

“In most cases, each personality will interact with the other.” A dominant personality holds authority and control for a period of time, during which time the other personalities effectively disappear. The original primary, or primary, personality is likely unaware of the existence of the other secondary personalities, but the secondary personalities are usually aware of the primary personality. Communication between the secondary personalities is common, but communication between the primary and secondary personalities is rare.

Yuan Chengren nodded. “But Wang Donglin’s case is different. He has two personalities. The primary personality lacks confidence, is cowardly, and is friendly—I call it the ‘angel’; the secondary personality is extremely manic, violent, and destructive—I call it the ‘devil.’ He can simultaneously awaken both of his personalities, so every crime seems like a conspiracy between the ‘angel’ and the ‘devil.’ This is a key reason he’s able to deceive women.”

Zhang Zhiqi was astonished and asked, “Has there been a case like this before?”

“There was a similar case in the United States, but it was ultimately unconfirmed. That’s why I’m very interested in Wang Donglin’s case.”

“So… could he simply be faking his multiple personalities to evade legal punishment?” Zhang Zhiqi’s question echoed a theory circulating online. While a bit sensationalist, it did seem plausible at first glance.

“Impossible. Wang Donglin’s ‘angel’ personality even demanded the death penalty, steadfastly denying the existence of his other personality. Yet, he can actually communicate with his ‘devil’ personality… This chaotic split has led to his extremely unstable mental state. But judging by his appearance, he’s more polite and refined than most people, making him quite deceptive.”

“So, his current state is completely out of control?” Even though Zhang Zhiqi had seen a lot, the thought still made him shudder.

“Yes, I think he’ll continue killing until he’s caught by the police or killed by someone else.” Yuan Chengren sighed heavily, perhaps out of helplessness.

Zhang Zhiqi stood up abruptly and said firmly, “Teacher, rest assured. I will definitely bring Wang Donglin to justice.”

Yuan Chengren laughed and patted Zhang Zhiqi’s shoulder firmly. “Keep going; I believe in you. I believe that good will prevail over evil in this world.”

Zhang Zhiqi nodded, but there was an inexplicable sadness in his smile.

.

May 31st, 7:40 p.m., Moyun Town, Bar Street.

Yu Yongsheng finished his third beer of the night. As he put it down, he realized there was someone sitting across from him.

Cheng Tuo’s face was gloomy, and he stared coldly at the empty glass on the table.

“You shouldn’t drink while on a mission.”

Yu Yongsheng laughed dumbly. “Captain Cheng, how come you’re drunk when you’re not drinking? I’m neither a police officer nor on a mission right now.”

“What about the mission Lu Tianfeng assigned you?”

Yu Yongsheng gestured to the bartender for another drink, then said, “Captain Cheng, you misunderstood. I came here tonight purely to drink and relax. I don’t have any mission at all.”

“Then why were you traveling with Chen Nuolan?”

“She was going to Moyun Town, and I gave her a ride.”

“About an hour ago, there was a fierce gunfight at the Qunxian Building in Huangjia Village. Intelligence indicates Lu Tianfeng may have been there as well.”

Yu Yongsheng’s expression remained unchanged. “Oh, really?”

Cheng Tuo, knowing he couldn’t extract any information from him, sighed and said, “Yongsheng, there’s no need to be so hostile towards me. You can tell me whatever you think…”

“Captain Cheng, I really just came here for a drink.” Yu Yongsheng tapped the glass in front of him.

“I advise you to stop before things get out of hand.” Cheng Tuo stood up, but Yu Yongsheng remained seated, motionless.

Cheng Tuo walked out of the bar door, and a young police officer waiting nearby immediately stepped forward and whispered, “Captain Cheng, do we need to continue the surveillance?”

“Leave two people here on standby, and the rest of you pack up and follow me.”

“Where are we going?”

“Back to D City immediately,” Cheng Tuo said through gritted teeth.

CONTENT END 83

chapters.title: Chapter 84
chapters.content:
May 31st, 7:45 p.m., outside the back gate of D City University.

Lu Tianfeng and his two companions sat in a quiet milk tea shop, each with a cup of pearl milk tea in front of them, barely touched.

Tong Yao listened to the news from Lu Tianfeng and Zhang Zhiqi while stirring her milk tea with a straw.

“So, Mr. Yuan believes Wang Donglin is likely fleeing toward Moyun Town and committing another crime. This possibility also perfectly aligns with Captain Lu’s analysis—he’s imitating Captain Lu’s escape tactics.”

The two men nodded in unison.

“Then the question arises: why don’t we leave for Moyun Town immediately?” Tong Yao asked anxiously.

“There are two reasons. First, I want to wait until Cheng Tuo’s men have withdrawn before heading there. They’ll mistakenly believe I’ve arranged to meet Nuolan in Moyun Town at 7 o’clock, and Nuolan will undoubtedly play along. And once Cheng Tuo realizes he’s been tricked, he’ll likely lead the main force back to D City, leaving a few men in Moyun Town to continue surveillance.”

“That makes sense,” Zhang Zhiqi agreed.

“Secondly, from this moment on, I hope you’ll view our battle with Wang Donglin as a game of chess. In a chess match, we must not only discern our opponent’s moves but also understand their purpose. Now, besides deducing Wang Donglin’s ‘where he is,’ we also need to diligently consider ‘what he’s trying to do.'”

“Where? What?” Tong Yao repeated softly, a thoughtful expression on her face.

Zhang Zhiqi snorted and said, “I think it’s very simple. He just wants to kill people. He knows he has the mental health test results as a golden ticket to avoid death. Even if he kills a few more people, he won’t be sentenced if caught by the police.”

“So his purpose in escaping is simply to commit more crimes?” Lu Tianfeng shook his head, disagreeing. “I don’t think Wang Donglin’s actions are that simple.”

“Does Captain Lu think he has other motives?” Zhang Zhiqi asked.

“I’ve always been concerned about the two missing ‘souvenirs’ from the previous case. Wang Donglin refused to reveal where he buried them, proving they held special meaning for him. Could his risky escape this time be related to the whereabouts of those ‘souvenirs’?”

Tong Yao interjected, “Could he have buried them in Moyun Mountain?”

“Wang Donglin’s previous burials of ‘souvenirs’ were all near the lake…” Zhang Zhiqi said thoughtfully, apparently recalling something.

“At the foot of Moyun Mountain lies the source of the Baiyun River and the Baiyun Lake Reservoir,” Lu Tianfeng said confidently. “I suspect Wang Donglin’s destination might be there.”

Tong Yao looked hesitant. “But Baiyun Lake Reservoir covers hundreds of square kilometers, and the lakeshore terrain is complex. How could the three of us possibly find Wang Donglin?”

“No matter where he wants to go, he’ll have to wait until tomorrow morning to act.” Zhang Zhiqi snapped his fingers. “Baiyun Lake Reservoir is a major water source protection area. It’s cleared at night, so it’s rarely visited. Therefore, it would be extremely easy to spot anyone approaching by car or on foot. I think, given Wang Donglin’s cautious nature, he’ll definitely wait until tomorrow daytime before entering the lake area as a tourist.”

Lu Tianfeng nodded repeatedly. “That makes sense. So, Wang Donglin will need to find a place to stay tonight, but he probably doesn’t have any ID or cash on him.”

“So the most convenient way is to pick up a girl on Moyun Town’s bar street.”

Tong Yao frowned, a look of disgust on her face. But she had to admit that Zhang Zhiqi’s method was the best fit for Wang Donglin’s personality. Lu Tianfeng sighed and smiled bitterly, “Now I wish Cheng Tuo had left more men in Moyun Town.”

In reality, he still had a small, unspoken worry. He knew Chen Nuolan was also in Moyun Town, and he’d originally wanted to keep her away from the center of the vortex, but unexpectedly, a series of twists and turns had put her in the most dangerous situation.

The air outside the window was oppressively hot and humid; a real storm was about to arrive.

May 31st, 8 p.m.

On the intercity highway, several police cars were speeding towards D City.

Cheng Tuo rested his chin on the window, his elbows resting on the side, staring intently at the countless raindrops hitting the glass. He said nothing, and his subordinates dared not speak either. The atmosphere in the car was freezing cold.

Just then, Cheng Tuo’s phone rang. The corners of his mouth twitched. It was Director Luo calling.

“Director Luo, please give me your instructions.”

“Where are you? How far is it from Small Stone Bridge?” Director Luo asked bluntly. Small Stone Bride wasn’t a bridge but a place in the northern suburbs of D City. Cheng Tuo glanced at the car’s GPS, quickly estimated the time, and replied.

“We can arrive in eight minutes.”

“Very good. Go there in person, and I’ll send you the exact location.”

“Director Luo, what’s going on?” Cheng Tuo couldn’t help but ask. Director Luo’s speech was incoherent, which was completely unlike his usual style.

“The body of a young woman was found near Small Stone Bridge. She died within an hour. The cause of death is preliminarily determined to be drowning, and there are no signs of violence. After investigating the scene, the local police recalled the Wang Donglin case and immediately reported the case to the municipal bureau.”

Cheng Tuo’s mouth twitched. “Wang Donglin actually dared to kill someone?”

“Go to the scene first and report back.”

“Roger that!” Cheng Tuo hung up the phone and shouted to the driver, “Get off the highway and head to Small Stone Bridge immediately!”

A long streak of lightning streaked across the distant sky, and the rain gradually intensified.

.

May 31st, 8:10 p.m., Small Stone Bridge, northern suburbs of D City.

Cheng Tuo rushed to the crime scene and saw a sea of ​​red and blue police lights flashing non-stop. He couldn’t help but curse under his breath.

“Can’t you be more discreet?”

Despite his complaints, Cheng Tuo didn’t hesitate. He grabbed a disposable raincoat and threw it on, then hurriedly jumped out of the car, not caring about the muddy ground.

The local police guarding the cordon recognized Cheng Tuo as a member of the Criminal Police Brigade and hurriedly and politely stepped forward to greet him.

“What’s going on?” Cheng Tuo got straight to the point.

“A young woman’s body, discovered by a passerby…”

Cheng Tuo took in the surroundings: the quiet road, the deserted bridge culvert, and the pitch-black river. At night, the body should be difficult to discover.

“The body was only dead about an hour ago, so it’s quite a coincidence that these passersby arrived.”

The police officer scratched his head awkwardly. “They’re a young couple from a nearby town. They had planned to spend some time in this secluded place, but they didn’t expect…”

“Alright. What did the medical examiner say?” Cheng Tuo continued to walk. By then, he could see several figures in black police raincoats busy on the riverbank.

“The forensic doctor just arrived. I’m not entirely sure…”

“Alright, I’ll ask myself.” Cheng Tuo left the officer and stepped forward, speaking loudly. “I’m Cheng Tuo from the Municipal Criminal Police Brigade. Could anyone please report the situation here?”

A middle-aged man turned and nodded to Cheng Tuo. “I’m Xiao Ran from the Small Stone Bridge Police Station. We received a call at 7:42 p.m. from a young couple claiming to have found a female body by the river in a culvert under a bridge. We arrived at the scene at 7:49 p.m. and cordoned off the area. Evidence preservation is in good condition. The deceased’s clothing is intact, there are no obvious signs of violence, and no identifying information is available. The preliminary forensic examination indicates the deceased died around 7:00 p.m., and the cause of death was mechanical asphyxiation due to drowning. There are signs of impact on the back of the head, which is not fatal, but could have caused coma. Our current assessment is that the murderer knocked her unconscious and then forced her into the river to drown.”

Cheng Tuo listened, bending down to closely examine the details of the body.

Neat clothing, no obvious injuries, drowning as the murder method, and… Cheng Tuo’s gaze locked on the woman’s left wrist. There was a lighter mark on the skin there. Judging from its shape, the deceased must have worn a watch regularly.

“Have you found her watch nearby?”

“We’ve searched thoroughly but haven’t found anything.”

Souvenirs. Three words swirled in Cheng Tuo’s mind like a curse.

“Do you think Wang Donglin did it?”

Xiao Ran was stunned for a moment but didn’t answer. He knew he was just a police officer and shouldn’t comment on the case.

Cheng Tuo gave a wry smile and asked, “Are there any other clues at the scene pointing to Wang Donglin?”

“Not yet. We need to await further forensic results.”

Cheng Tuo patted Xiao Ran’s shoulder in gratitude, knowing the heavy responsibility of the next task fell on him. However, he still couldn’t believe that Wang Donglin would kill someone during his hasty escape.

Unless there was a reason he had to kill.

If so, what was it?

Cheng Tuo stood silently by the river, lost in thought. The night wind, wrapped in cold rain, lashed his face, but he remained unmoved.

.

May 31st, 8:15 p.m., Intercity Highway, D City heading towards Moyun Town.

Lu Tianfeng was driving intently. Zhang Zhiqi was in the passenger seat, looking down at his phone. Tong Yao, sitting in the back seat, had turned on the night light and was diligently reading the relevant documents on the Wang Donglin case.

Everyone looked preoccupied. Besides the roar of the car engines, the only sound in the car was the clatter of raindrops hitting the roof.

Suddenly, Zhang Zhiqi let out a “Huh?” but when Lu Tianfeng cast a questioning look at him, he remained silent.

“What’s wrong?” Lu Tianfeng asked.

“I’m trying to form my words. How about you get off the highway at the next exit?” Zhang Zhiqi replied, pointing to the highway exit sign.

Lu Tianfeng knew Zhang Zhiqi wasn’t the type to hesitate or be mysterious, so he kept quiet. He flipped the steering wheel, and the car smoothly entered the ramp, exiting the intercity highway.

It wasn’t until the car turned into a gas station on the highway and stopped at the rest area that Zhang Zhiqi turned his phone screen towards Lu Tianfeng and said slowly, “The latest announcement just released on the police internal system: the Wang Donglin escape incident has escalated, and a suspected victim has appeared.”

Lu Tianfeng and Tong Yao didn’t have time to investigate how Zhang Zhiqi had accessed the police intranet. They both asked in unison, “Victim?”

“Yes, it seems Wang Donglin killed someone before even reaching Moyun Town.”

Lu Tianfeng’s heart tightened. He asked, “Where was the crime scene?”

“Small Stone Bridge, not far from here.” Zhang Zhiqi knocked on the car window. “The question now is, should we go there?”

“Even if we go to the scene, we won’t be able to conduct the investigation, right?” Tong Yao asked, puzzled.

Zhang Zhiqi smiled mysteriously. “Don’t worry. A murder occurred at Small Stone Bridge. The local police station chief will likely respond personally. Coincidentally, Xiao Ran, the chief of the Small Stone Bridge Police Station, is a good friend of mine.”

Lu Tianfeng’s eyes lit up, and he remained silent, his hands gripping the steering wheel.

“Captain Lu?” Tong Yao looked at Lu Tianfeng with concern.

Lu Tianfeng said gravely, “Generally speaking, the more frequently a murderer commits crimes, the easier it is to catch them, because they leave more clues. But I’m worried that Wang Donglin is exploiting this to delay the police’s pursuit.”

“What do you mean?”

“After the murder, he could deliberately leave clues at the crime scene to mislead the police and buy himself more time and space.”

“Is this… even possible?” Tong Yao found it unbelievable. How much courage must Wang Donglin have to dare disrupt the police’s pursuit by killing someone?

But seeing Lu Tianfeng’s serious expression and then Zhang Zhiqi’s equally apprehensive face, Tong Yao couldn’t help but waver.

“So, should we continue on to Moyun Town or go to Small Stone Bridge?” Zhang Zhiqi asked calmly.

“Split into two groups,” Lu Tianfeng finally decided. “Tong Yao and I will continue on to Moyun Town, while you investigate the situation at Small Stone Bridge.”

“But we only have one car,” Zhang Zhiqi said with a frown, gazing at the rain outside the window.

As he spoke, two police cars, sirens blaring, sped past them, one in front and one behind.

“The police will conduct a thorough search of the area around Small Stone Bridge. I can’t go near there,” Lu Tianfeng said.

Zhang Zhiqi shrugged and forced a smile. “I hope you’ll keep your word and leave the reward money to me.”

After saying this, Zhang Zhiqi pulled a worn black umbrella from the glove compartment, opened the car door, and rushed into the rain without looking back.

“Can he get any information?” Tong Yao asked worriedly.

“Of course he can; otherwise, how could he live up to the title of ‘Hound’?” Lu Tianfeng suddenly sighed. “I’m a little worried about the situation in Moyun Town. Perhaps I should remind Nuolan to be careful.”

Tong Yao was a little slow to react, but she quickly understood what Lu Tianfeng meant. “But they must still be monitoring Sister Nuolan’s phone communications.”

“So we have to think of a way…” Lu Tianfeng mused.

In the distant gray sky, a rumble of thunder echoed.

CONTENT END 84

chapters.title: Chapter 85
chapters.content:
May 31st, 8:30 p.m., Moyun Town, Bar Street

Even the torrential downpour couldn’t dampen the bustling atmosphere of this street.

The once-popular outdoor seating was unavailable, forcing customers to crowd indoors. Instead, many businesses seemed busier than usual.

However, popularity was rather elusive. Even in the renowned Moyun Town, some businesses struggled with mediocre business.

For example, around the corner was a bar called “Black & White.” Its exterior featured a pattern of alternating black and white piano keys, suggesting a musical theme. But once you pushed the door open, you discovered a paved interior with black and white bricks arranged in a pattern of plum blossoms and bamboo. Medieval European armor and weapons hung on the walls, and the waiters were dressed as chariots, horses, and pawns. The true theme was chess.

Perhaps due to the unassuming sign outside, the bar wasn’t crowded, and even at this hour, there were still quite a few empty seats. The bartender, a bit restless, frantically wiped the always spotless glasses on the counter.

A man pushed open the door, clutching a large red umbrella that didn’t quite suit him. He glanced around and finally settled for a corner seat facing a wall-mounted LCD TV, which was broadcasting the day’s hottest news: the Wang Donglin escape case.

This new customer was none other than Wang Donglin.

“Sir, what would you like to drink?” a waiter dressed as a chess piece, a knight, approached Wang Donglin.

“A glass of soda water.”

“Okay.” The waiter’s tone was inevitably a bit cold, which always felt awkward for customers drinking in a bar.

But just as the waiter turned to get the soda, Wang Donglin suddenly asked, “Where’s your beautiful bartender?”

“Judy? She starts work at nine tonight, so she should be here soon.”

“Okay, thank you,” Wang Donglin said nothing more. The waiter scratched his head and walked away.

Wang Donglin took a look at the lady’s watch from his pocket. It was just past 8:30, so the wait would only be half an hour at most. Since there weren’t many customers here and the lighting was rather dim, it seemed like a good place to hide. The only problem was whether there were any other entrances or exits besides the main door.

He decided to sit for a while, then take a restroom break to survey the surroundings.

Wang Donglin glanced up at the archival photo of himself at the time of his arrest on the large screen and couldn’t help but laugh.

The photo showed him with a glazed look and a goofy expression, a stark contrast to his real self.

“…A special reminder: fugitive Wang Donglin is a highly dangerous individual, responsible for multiple deaths and extremely unstable mentally. Citizens are advised to call the police immediately if they spot him and stay away from him to ensure their own safety. Do not attempt to follow or confront him…”

“Sir, your soda,” the waiter returned.

“Thank you,” he said politely, accepting the glass.

At that moment, a beam of light hit Wang Donglin’s face. Though it was only for a brief second, Wang Donglin felt as if the waiter’s movements paused.

“Enjoy your meal,” the waiter said, his steps seeming a bit stiff as he turned and left.

Wang Donglin stared at the waiter’s back and suddenly snorted coldly.

“I’m not even afraid of the police, so why would I be afraid of you?”

As Wang Donglin thought about the layers of mystery he had set up, a sense of accomplishment welled up in his mind. The dumbest police officer was probably still scrambling around near D City University. A more perceptive officer might have noticed that the female corpse at Small Stone Bridge was connected to him and was conducting a thorough search of the area. Furthermore, someone smart enough and knowledgeable about so-called criminal psychology might be able to track him down as far as Moyun Town.

The pursuer’s attention would likely be focused on the “souvenir,” and there was no way they could guess his true purpose: to meet a female bartender at this bar.

Like the complexity of a chess game, there were obvious intentions, hidden backhands, and even true trump cards that the opponent could hardly anticipate.

Only those who can fully see through the chess game could be considered among the ultimate masters.

Wang Donglin felt that no one in this game was worthy of being his opponent.

Perhaps Lu Tianfeng had the potential to be a challenger, but he had already been defeated. The head-on confrontation in the Huangjia Village inn must have been a profound psychological blow to him.

“I will definitely be the winner,” thought Wang Donglin, downing half a glass of soda in one gulp.

As he put down his glass, he happened to see a man push open the door and enter Black & White. A man he had met that morning.

Wang Donglin’s blood froze.

.

May 31st, 8:40 p.m., Moyun Town, Bar Street.

Yu Yongsheng pushed open the door and entered the Black & White bar.

Twenty minutes ago, Chen Nuolan suddenly ran to Bar Street to find him, saying she needed to discuss an emergency, completely oblivious to the men watching them closely.

“What happened?” Yu Yongsheng had never seen such a serious expression on Chen Nuolan’s face.

“I received this text message.”

Yu Yongsheng glanced at the screen and saw a string of numbers:

29.11.6

98.3.5

“Is this the code you agreed on with the boss?”

“Yes, it translates to just two words,” Chen Nuolan said softly. “Go home.”

“Go home?” The words were so simple that Yu Yongsheng was momentarily lost. “Does the Boss mean you should go back to D City?”

“I think so.”

“Then let’s go now,” Yu Yongsheng said, hastily standing up.

“My first reaction after seeing the text was to leave immediately, but on second thought, why would he ask me to do that? He sent me to Moyun Town to confuse the police and buy time. But if we immediately return to D City, wouldn’t all our efforts be wasted?”

Yu Yongsheng remained silent. This was the first time he truly witnessed Chen Nuolan’s intelligence, and he understood even more clearly why Lu Tianfeng was so deeply infatuated with the woman before him.

“Sister Nuolan, what do you suggest?”

“I think the most likely possibility is that he thinks it would be dangerous for me to stay in Moyun Town.”

“Dangerous? We’re under police surveillance, much safer than ordinary people, unless…” Yu Yongsheng stopped mid-sentence, having already considered the most terrifying possibility.

“That demon has come to Moyun Town,” Chen Nuolan stated her speculation in a deep voice.

“How would the Boss know… Well, never mind. If Wang Donglin is really here, the Boss will definitely come over. We should stay and help.”

“I have a bold idea.” Chen Nuolan glanced at the plainclothes police officer who was following her from a distance. “Where do you think Wang Donglin might be hiding?”

“Somewhere crowded and with lots of eyes, like… this bar street would be nice.”

“Is there any way we can trick him? For example, disguise ourselves as plainclothes police officers and conduct a search.”

Yu Yongsheng frowned. “Sister Nuolan, isn’t that too dangerous?”

“How could he kill someone in public? If Wang Donglin discovers the police, he’ll just flee in disgrace, and that’ll give him away.”

Although Yu Yongsheng still felt a little uneasy, he couldn’t argue with Chen Nuolan. Besides, he wasn’t afraid of a head-on confrontation with Wang Donglin. What kind of man was a man who only bullied women?

So, Yu Yongsheng followed Chen Nuolan’s advice and specifically targeted bars with average business. Posing as a “plainclothes police officer,” he would show Wang Donglin’s photo and ask the staff if they had seen him. Chen Nuolan would lie in wait outside, watching for anyone sneaking out.

If anything went wrong, they had real police officers following them, and they could even ask for help.

Black & White was the fourth bar Yu Yongsheng had visited.

The bar was sparsely populated, and Yu Yongsheng knew at a glance that Wang Donglin wasn’t there. But as usual, he still picked up the photo and asked a waiter dressed as a chess piece.

“I’m a police officer. Have you seen this man?”

The waiter looked at the photo, a slightly uneasy expression on his face.

Yu Yongsheng’s question was initially casual, but the other person’s reaction told him something was amiss, and he quickly pressed, “Have you seen him? This guy is extremely dangerous. If you have any leads, don’t hide them.”

“There was a customer just now… who looked a bit like him…” the waiter said timidly.

“Where is he?” Yu Yongsheng suddenly became alert.

“In that corner over there… Huh? Where’s he?”

The waiter pointed to an empty table with a half-empty glass of soda on it and a red umbrella next to a chair.

“Strange! He was here just a minute ago,” the waiter muttered to himself.

“Does your bar have a back door?”

“That corridor over there leads to the restroom, and further back is the employee passage and the employee-only entrance…”

Before the waiter could finish, Yu Yongsheng had already taken off in a flash.

“Did anyone just come over here?” Yu Yongsheng rushed to the restroom door and asked a cleaning lady.

“There was a strange guy who forced his way into the employee passage. Young people these days are so uneducated…”

Yu Yongsheng had no patience to listen to the lady’s complaints. He strode towards the employee passage. Just as he saw the iron gate of the employee-only entrance from a distance, a dark figure flashed out and closed it.

“Don’t run!” Yu Yongsheng shouted, rushing forward at the speed of a 100-meter sprint and flinging the gate open.

Outside, a fierce storm raged. The figure in front, without an umbrella, had already turned into an alley.

Yu Yongsheng didn’t have time to think; he took off. The ground was cratered with potholes and stagnant water, but that didn’t slow him down at all.

“Ah! Help!”

A girl’s cry for help faintly emanated from the box.

Yu Yongsheng gritted his teeth. “Wang Donglin, you pervert! How dare you hurt innocent women at this hour?”

He followed the sound into the dimly lit alleyway and saw a petite figure crouched in a corner, trembling.

“Are you okay?” Yu Yongsheng couldn’t see where Wang Donglin had fled, so he had to help the girl up.

“A man just knocked me down. My knee hurts. Wuwuwu…” The girl was nearly in tears, her delicate face looking pitiful.

“Don’t be afraid. Did you see where he ran?”

“I don’t know. Wuwuwu, it hurts…”

“Come, hold my arm—”

To Yu Yongsheng’s surprise, the girl threw herself into his arms and hugged him tightly. He could feel the young woman’s warm body, the delicate fragrance of her hair, and her nearly soaked clothing. This sudden action left him somewhat bewildered.

Yu Yongsheng instinctively wanted to push her away, but he felt that would be too rude. As he hesitated, a sudden, icy pain pierced his chest.

“Ah!” Yu Yongsheng cried out in shock. He was about to struggle free from her embrace, but she suddenly used both her hands and feet, pressing herself forward, wrapping herself around him like a venomous snake, her bright red lips sealing his mouth with a passionate kiss.

Even if a passerby noticed the couple under the eaves, they would simply think they were making out in the rain.

Yu Yongsheng’s mind spun, and his eyes darkened. He felt as if a hole had been torn in his chest. All the strength in his body was drained, and soon he could no longer stand.

Using his last bit of strength, he bit down hard on her wet tongue. The girl screamed in pain and recoiled, and the venomous kiss finally ended.

“Oh, handsome boy, you’re really not giving me face.” The girl wiped the blood from the corner of her mouth and giggled.

Yu Yongsheng tried to open his mouth, but no words came out. He spat out a large mouthful of blood and collapsed forward.

“Really? You’re still trying to take advantage of me at this moment!” She smiled and supported Yu Yongsheng, letting his head rest against her chest, then ruffled his messy hair.

The scene before him was like a considerate girl comforting her drunken boyfriend, quite warm and romantic.

Only Yu Yongsheng felt the despair and helplessness of that moment.

His vision was blurry, but he noticed the name on the girl’s badge: Judy.

He also recognized the Black & White Bar logo printed on her clothes.

Black and white—these were the last two colors Yu Yongsheng would see in his life.

Translator’s note:  I was not ready for that. This isn’t a time loop like in Book 1. There’s no do-over. Yongsheng T-T

CONTENT END 85

chapters.title: Chapter 86
chapters.content:
May 31st, 9 p.m., Moyun Town, Bar Street.

Several police cars were parked at the entrance of a back alley, their rooftop lights flashing frantically, exuding a murderous aura that forced passersby to take a detour.

A hundred meters away, Lu Tianfeng stopped his car.

“Are we still a step too late?” Lu Tianfeng slammed the steering wheel.

Tong Yao, however, said thoughtfully, “Logically, Wang Donglin shouldn’t be killing so often, right? If he were to commit a crime here, the Small Stone Bridge case would immediately lose its impact!”

“Are we mistaken?”

“Don’t worry, maybe it’s just another case he happened to stumble upon. I’ll go check it out,” Tong Yao suggested. Lu Tianfeng was now a fugitive and couldn’t appear before the police without permission.

Lu Tianfeng nodded, a sense of foreboding growing stronger.

He was usually a very patient man, but Tong Yao had only been gone for about five minutes, and he felt as if he’d been waiting in the car for hours, every second a torture. The sadness on Tong Yao’s face upon her return only heightened Lu Tianfeng’s anxiety.

“What happened?” he asked impatiently.

Tong Yao didn’t answer but instead gently covered her face with her hands and lowered her head.

“I’m sorry, Boss.”

Lu Tianfeng’s heart seemed to be gripped by something, because Tong Yao had never addressed him as “Boss” before, always politely calling him “Captain Lu.”

“What happened?”

“Yongsheng’s in trouble.” Tong Yao took a deep breath. “He was stabbed in the chest. He can’t be saved.”

Lu Tianfeng was stunned. He thought there must be something wrong with his ears.

Why was Yu Yongsheng in Moyun Town? And why had he gotten into trouble? With his skills, he should have been no match for Wang Donglin, let alone those brutal mercenaries from the day before. How could he have been stabbed so easily?

The most difficult thing to accept was why Yu Yongsheng was the one who died.

Lu Tianfeng spoke with difficulty, his voice becoming unusually dry. “The person who should have died today was Wang Donglin.”

Tong Yao remained silent.

“But I saved Wang Donglin, causing one innocent person after another to sacrifice themselves.”

Tong Yao whispered, “It’s not certain yet whether Wang Donglin is responsible for Yongsheng’s death…”

“Don’t lie to me, and don’t lie to yourself,” Lu Tianfeng interrupted Tong Yao sharply. “Wang Donglin is definitely involved in Yongsheng’s death.”

“But could Wang Donglin alone kill Yongsheng in a head-on fight?” Tong Yao raised her voice, meeting Lu Tianfeng’s gaze.

Lu Tianfeng’s mouth twitched, and he sighed, “Yongsheng sacrificed his life to convey a crucial message to us—there’s someone behind Wang Donglin.”

“Who could it be?”

“No matter who it is, we must find him.” Lu Tianfeng’s hands trembled as he gripped the steering wheel. “We must…”

“Boss…” Tong Yao wanted to reach out and pat Lu Tianfeng’s shoulder, but she felt awkward. Her hand hung awkwardly in mid-air, unsure how to comfort him.

“I’m fine, it’s just—”

At that precise moment, someone suddenly knocked on the car window.

Standing in the rain was Chen Nuolan, without even an umbrella.

.

May 31st, 9:05 p.m., Moyun Town, near Bar Street.

In the back seat of the car, soaking wet, Chen Nuolan huddled, head bowed, silent. And Lu Tianfeng, always so attentive to his girlfriend, didn’t even offer the most basic greeting. Finally, Tong Yao couldn’t bear it any longer and turned to hand her coat to Chen Nuolan.

“Sister Nuolan, are you cold? Put it on.”

Chen Nuolan shook her head and didn’t take the coat, only mumbling a thank you.

The car fell silent again.

“Boss, what’s next…”

Tong Yao had originally wanted to ask, “Where are we going?” But before she could finish her sentence, Lu Tianfeng spoke without warning. His voice was cold and hard.

“Did you get my text?” Lu Tianfeng stared straight ahead, but the question was clearly directed at Chen Nuolan.

“Yes,” she replied in a low, clear voice.

“According to the code we agreed on, what did the text say?”

“Go home.”

“Yes, you should go home,” Lu Tianfeng simply sighed.

Chen Nuolan bit her lip, her fingers clasped together tightly, her shoulders trembling slightly, but she managed to hold back her tears. Tong Yao felt incredibly burdened as she watched the two of them. If they hadn’t been so restrained, whether they’d burst into tears, cursed, or even expressed their inner anger through body language, it would have been easier.

However, Lu Tianfeng didn’t blame Chen Nuolan or press the issue further. Instead, he abruptly changed the subject, saying to Tong Yao, “Drive back and pick up Zhang Zhiqi.”

“But Wang Donglin might not have gotten far…” Tong Yao said in astonishment.

“We’ve suffered heavy losses this round, and we still don’t know what Wang Donglin’s side has up their sleeves. If we rush forward, we’ll likely be wiped out.” Lu Tianfeng took deep breaths, trying to calm himself. “Next, no matter how reluctant we are, we have no choice but to retreat. We’ll reunite with Zhang Zhiqi and make plans later.”

“Okay, I understand.”
