“One more thing… Tong Yao, you drive.” After Lu Tianfeng finished speaking, his vision went dark and he fainted.

.

May 31st, 9:15 p.m., Small Stone Bridge Police Station.

Xiao Ran returned to his office, sank into his chair, and breathed a sigh of relief.

Tonight’s case had been completely transferred to the Municipal Criminal Police Brigade for follow-up. He was actually happy to have some free time, but even with this sense of relief, he felt a tinge of resentment.

If he hadn’t been so perceptive, connecting the clues at the crime scene to Wang Donglin, would the investigation have progressed so quickly? Yet, throughout, no one had even praised his professionalism, which left him rather frustrated.

“Brother Xiao, you’re finally back?”

Xiao Ran was startled, sitting up straight. He took a closer look and saw that the man who had dared to barge in was Zhang Zhiqi.

“Zhang Zhiqi? What brings you here?”

“I’m here to help Brother Xiao with his problems.”

Although Zhang Zhiqi boasted to Lu Tianfeng that Xiao Ran was his buddy, the two had only collaborated on a case before and weren’t close friends. However, Zhang Zhiqi had made a contribution that time, helping Xiao Ran find the fugitive murder suspect. Therefore, he felt confident that Xiao Ran wouldn’t reject him this time.

“I’ve been doing fine lately. I don’t have anything to worry about,” Xiao Ran said, his words a bit uncertain.

Zhang Zhiqi pointedly said, “Didn’t a murder just happen tonight?”

“Haha, you really are worthy of being called ‘Hound,’ your speed is terrifying, isn’t it? But the case has been transferred to the Municipal Criminal Police Brigade, so it has nothing to do with me anymore.”

“How come you’re so efficient? Normally, a case like this would take half a day to be reported to the city, right?”

Xiao Ran was eagerly awaiting Zhang Zhiqi’s question. He coughed dryly, cleared his throat, and then said, “Because the scene is a bit strange, it looks like it might be the work of the ‘Souvenir Killer,’ Wang Donglin…”

“Who has such a sharp eye? I think it must be you, Brother Xiao, haha!”

“Don’t flatter me,” Xiao Ran said this, but a smile still appeared on his face.

Zhang Zhiqi observed Xiao Ran’s expression and immediately followed up on the topic: “This case is clearly within Brother Xiao’s jurisdiction. Why let the City Bureau take all the credit?”

Xiao Ran narrowed his eyes, studying Zhang Zhiqi, somewhat unsure of his intentions.

“Besides being good at finding people, I also have some skills in deducing the deceased’s identity. If Brother Xiao can do it before the City Bureau…”

Zhang Zhiqi knew that this was enough.

Sure enough, Xiao Ran raised his eyebrows and said hesitantly, “Let’s not even talk about whether it’s legal for you to participate in the investigation. Now that the body and the evidence from the scene have been sent to the City Bureau, even if you had superpowers, you wouldn’t be able to investigate.”

“Brother Xiao, you’re joking. I don’t have any special abilities. I can only rely on this.” Zhang Zhiqi pointed to his eyes. “You must have a copy of the visual evidence from the scene, right?”

“Just looking at the pictures will do the trick?” Xiao Ran asked doubtfully.

“Give it a try. You won’t lose anything, right?” Zhang Zhiqi said with a smile.

“You can’t take it with you. You can only view it on my computer.” Xiao Ran finally relented.

“No problem!”

Zhang Zhiqi sat down carelessly, fingers darting across the keyboard. Although Xiao Ran was still a little worried, he stopped worrying when he thought this might be a chance to show off.

“Wow, this girl comes from a well-off family,” Zhang Zhiqi said, pointing at the screen. “Look, the top she’s wearing is a high-end fashion brand, the skirt is custom-made, and the underwear is… Brother Xiao, you don’t know these brands, right?”

“Yes,” Xiao Ran admitted honestly.

“It doesn’t matter. Clothing brands big and small now have membership systems. The victim was wearing clothing from five different brands, so I can compare the customer databases of all five…” Zhang Zhiqi spoke as he quickly operated the computer. Several different windows opened on the screen, and countless lines of code scrolled across the screen.

“Wait, what are you operating? Is there even software like this on my computer?” Xiao Ran wasn’t particularly computer literate, but he could still identify what software was installed on his own machine.

“Don’t panic; this is my specialized database extraction software. It’s entirely cloud-based and won’t affect the data on your computer… Look, I got it!” Zhang Zhiqi shouted excitedly. “There are twenty-nine phone numbers with membership cards for all five brands.”

“Not many. It won’t take long to check them one by one.” Xiao Ran couldn’t help but get excited.

“Don’t worry, I’m here.” Zhang Zhiqi’s confidence grew. “First, eliminate those over thirty. Then, look at the victim’s shoe size—it’s a 38—so we can eliminate those… Then, we can continue to eliminate them based on clothing size… Okay, great, there are only two candidates left.”

“Two?” Xiao Ran glanced at the time. Zhang Zhiqi had spent less than ten minutes turning a needle-in-a-haystack situation into a two-way search. He truly lived up to his reputation.

“Wait a moment. One of these two people doesn’t own a car and doesn’t have a driver’s license. Clues at the crime scene indicate the victim and the murderer arrived together in a car. Since Wang Donglin couldn’t have a car, the car must belong to the victim. Therefore, the victim is very likely this person—”

On the computer screen, a graduation photo of a woman in a bachelor’s gown appeared. The girl in the photo was smiling brightly. Although the photo was taken several years ago, her features were vaguely recognizable; she bore a striking resemblance to the girl brutally murdered tonight.

“Yang Yazi, 27 years old, graduated from D City University. Two years ago, she married the son of a real estate developer. She’s now a freelancer, occasionally doing livestreams and also registering as a part-time ride-sharing driver. So far, she seems to fit the profile of the victim perfectly.”

“I’ll contact the City Bureau immediately.” Xiao Ran turned and rushed out of the office. Then, as if remembering something, he returned and said seriously, “Zhang Zhiqi, isn’t it time for you to leave?”

“Of course, my mission has been successfully completed.” Zhang Zhiqi smiled, stood up, and stretched. His phone was vibrating in his hand.

CONTENT END 86

chapters.title: Chapter 87
chapters.content:
Wang Donglin’s Memories (IV)

Was there really a goddess of luck in this world?

If there was, I’d like to ask her why she gave me so much false happiness in the first twenty-plus years of my life and then so much pain and suffering after that.

I thought Jiang Suyu was the magic bullet that would completely change my fate. Fortunately, my murder and body disposal went surprisingly smoothly, and no one connected her disappearance or death to me. The police seemed to have been investigating in the wrong direction, and I had never come into their sight.

After a period of anxiety, my heart finally settled, convinced that my crime would never be exposed.

But unfortunately, it turned out that this “miracle drug” had a time limit.

Three months later, my spirits began to decline, and my interest in Xiaomian plummeted. I had to plead stomach discomfort as a temporary excuse, but I knew excuses would only delay the issue for a short while. If I truly wanted to solve the problem, I had to find a way to take “medicine.”

I was a patient; how could I get better without medicine?

However, “medicine” wasn’t easy to find. I needed to act with absolute safety in mind, and I couldn’t make any mistakes due to impatience.

The right time, right place, and right people were all essential.

So I was patient, lurking amidst the vibrant lights and nightlife, searching for the next “miracle cure.”

On another rainy weekend, in the early hours of the morning, I ran into Song Yue outside the back door of a bar.

Song Yue, a charming singer, was the bar’s resident singer and occasionally helped sell beer to earn some extra cash. In the process, she was inevitably forced to drink by customers with ulterior motives. She wasn’t much of a drinker, but the more she did so, the more difficult it became for customers.

That day, she was drunk and stood outside the back door under the awning, leaning against the wall and vomiting all over the floor.

“Are you okay?” I noticed no one was around, so I dared to approach her.

She glanced at me, probably thinking I meant no harm, and simply smiled politely before shaking her head.

“Here, wipe your mouth.” I handed her a clean white handkerchief.

“Thank you.” This time, she spoke, her voice clear and melodious, just as beautiful as when she sang.

“The person who just tried to get you drunk is actually my friend. I’m sorry I couldn’t stop him…” I told a harmless lie, taking the blame, knowing women are naturally vulnerable to apologies.

“It’s okay. It’s not your fault.” She took the bait, and her expression softened considerably.

“How about I give you a ride? Don’t worry, I’m a teacher at D City University. I’m definitely not a bad person.” I simply showed her my work ID. Song Yue glanced at it casually and waved her hand. “The ID might be fake, but I think you’re quite genuine. Let’s go!”

“Well, you could take a picture and post it on WeChat Moments or something. That would help keep you safe.” I knew girls well enough. If you said that, she definitely wouldn’t do it. Otherwise, it would be too embarrassing.

“Hmph, stop dithering. Where’s your car?” Song Yue burped and staggered forward.

“Over there… Can you still walk?”

“Of course… I can…” Song Yue said defiantly, but her body kept leaning towards me. So I simply put my arm around her waist and supported her forward.

“Be careful; there’s water on the ground.”

“I’m fine… I hang around bars… How could I not handle a few beers… Haha…”

I didn’t say anything else but surveyed my surroundings warily. I’d tried this several times before, only to have my prey get into the car and be spotted by passersby. Whenever that happened, I’d obediently send them home without touching them.

However, today, my luck finally turned. No one saw us get in the car together.

Song Yue sat in the passenger seat, her face flushed. She looked groggy but not completely drunk.

But I was prepared and handed her a bottle of mineral water.

“Clear your throat with some water. It’ll help.”

Song Yue, a frequent bartender, wasn’t stupid. She carefully checked the bottle cap, making sure it wasn’t opened before unscrewing it and gulping down a large gulp of water.

“How do you feel?”

“Yeah, much better…”

What she hadn’t anticipated was that I’d already used the tiniest syringe to inject a generous amount of sleeping pills into the water through the bottle.

As I drove, I chatted with her idly. At first, she was articulate, but after a few minutes, she became dazed, her speech incoherent, her head swaying from side to side.

“I… feel a little dizzy…” she said with difficulty, pressing her temple.

“You’re still drunk, right? How about a couple of sips of water?”

“Hmm… okay…” She raised the bottle to her lips, and just as she was about to take another sip, her hand suddenly gave way, and the bottle fell, spilling the icy mineral water all over her.

She only groaned softly before falling into a drenching sleep.

“Go to sleep, my dear.” I stroked her hair lovingly.

An hour later, as I gently carried the sleeping Song Yue out of the bathtub, I noticed a heartbreakingly beautiful smile still on her face.

I took another dose of my precious “miracle medicine” and felt instantly refreshed. With my previous experience, I handled Song Yue’s body even more flawlessly this time. It wasn’t until a week later that I saw a small news report in the corner of a newspaper about the discovery of an unidentified female body in a lake west of the city.

The police still didn’t suspect me, and I acted as if nothing had happened. I went to work every day as normal, and after work, I went home to spend time with Xiaomian, discussing matters big and small, such as getting a marriage certificate, getting married, holding a wedding banquet, and going on a honeymoon.

My life seemed blissful and peaceful, but only I knew the greatest crisis was rapidly approaching. I noticed that the “effects” of Song Yue’s medicine were fading rapidly. Within a month, they had almost completely disappeared, whereas Jiang Suyu’s effects had lasted nearly three months.

This meant I had to increase my hunting frequency, which also exposed me to greater risks. My biggest concern was that if the “effects” continued to decrease, the consequences would be disastrous. I couldn’t possibly go hunting every other day, could I?

Was there a permanent cure for this disease?

While bored and scrolling through my social media, I learned from a junior fellow student I didn’t know well that Moli was getting married. At that moment, a saying suddenly struck me: “Only the one who tied the bell can untie it; a heart’s medicine for a heart’s disease.”

I knew exactly where my problem lay. To cure it, perhaps I needed not a “miracle drug” but a true “heart’s medicine.”

So I began planning a true redemption operation, targeting my unfaithful ex-girlfriend, Moli.

I was well aware that if Moli were killed, I would likely become the subject of a police investigation. Therefore, this operation was far more dangerous than the previous two, and I couldn’t afford to make any mistakes.

I suppressed my urge to act, calmed myself, and carefully planned every step of the operation. I wanted to create a chance encounter at the right time and place, so that Moli would be caught off guard and follow me. Finally, I decided to enlist the help of Xiaomian to make my plan even more seamless.

The night of the operation, a drizzling rain fell. I knew Moli was reminiscing with classmates at a karaoke bar near D City University, so I pretended to run into her there and cleverly steered the conversation towards wedding preparations. I highlighted the studio where Xiaomian and I had taken our wedding photos. I boasted so eloquently that she was thrilled and offered to go home with me to see the photos.

I feigned displeasure, but she laughed and asked if I was henpecked and didn’t dare bring my ex-girlfriend home. This was exactly what I wanted. I deliberately asked her if she dared to sneak out and meet her ex-boyfriend without telling anyone. Sure enough, she fell for the provocation, grabbed my hand, and walked out.

I carefully chose a side road away from security cameras and brought Moli home. Before leaving, I poured sleeping pills into the teapot. Xiaomian had a nightly tea habit, so when I got home, she was already asleep, completely unaware I’d brought someone else home.

Moli, likewise, drank the spiked tea without much suspicion. Soon, she fell asleep on the sofa, clutching the beautiful wedding photo album. I carried Moli to the bathroom, but instead of rushing in, I went back to the bedroom and forcibly woke Xiaomian. Taking advantage of her drowsiness, I had sex with her, making sure to mention it was 9:30 p.m. After our passionate lovemaking, Xiaomian fell asleep again, under the effects of the drug. It was then that I returned to the bathroom, placed Moli in the tub, and pressed her head under the water. The instant the warm water rushed into her airways, she jerked awake and struggled desperately, but I held her thrashing body firmly in place.

Soon, Moli fell silent.

Her eyes were opened wide, an expression of both astonishment and fear.

It was over.

I leaned, exhausted, against the wall, gasping for breath. After a short rest, I returned to the bedroom and woke the soundly sleeping Xiaomian.

“I’m so sleepy…don’t wake me…” Xiaomian muttered in her sleep, not even opening her eyes.

“Honey, it’s 10:30 p.m.”

“Yeah, I know…”

“Come on, make out with your husband.”

“No, no…” Xiaomian tried to refuse, but she couldn’t resist my extreme excitement, so she finally gave in.

This time, I felt like I had given it my all.

Perhaps the curse that had plagued me for years had finally been lifted.

Xiaomian fell into another exhausted sleep, but I didn’t let my guard down. I quickly ran to the bathroom and continued to clean up as quickly as possible.

Two hours later, after finishing disposing of the body, I rushed home breathless and immediately woke Xiaomian up again. She was clearly exhausted from the multiple interruptions I had made that night, but I didn’t care. I just wanted her to remember that I had tormented her all night; that was my alibi.

The next day was the first day of my complete rebirth.

CONTENT END 87

chapters.title: Chapter 88
chapters.content:
May 31st, 9:30 p.m., Moyun Town, inside a low-rent apartment.

Wang Donglin sat on a hard folding chair, his hands resting nervously near his knees, rubbing them vigorously from time to time, looking restless.

The sound of running water reached his ears; someone was showering in the bathroom.

Bathroom, shower.

At the thought of these two words, Wang Donglin felt a surge of heat all over his body, something stirring within him. He closed his eyes and forced himself to take a deep breath.

The running water finally stopped, and after a rustling sound of fabric rubbing against itself, Judy, dressed in a sports T-shirt and jeans, emerged from the bathroom, muttering to herself as she wiped her hair with a towel.

“Finally, it’s clean. What a hassle!” Judy shook her head, picked up the cup on the table, and chugged down a large gulp of cold water.

Wang Donglin stared intently at her wet hair and slender figure, swallowing hard. But he also knew that this woman was no pushover, and he couldn’t afford to offend her.

Judy seemed accustomed to this kind of gaze from men. She smiled, put down her cup, and sat nonchalantly on the edge of the bed. She pulled a duffel bag from under the cabinet and began packing.

“Where are you taking me?” Wang Donglin couldn’t help but ask.

“What?” Judy asked, her eyes wide. “Where am I taking you?”

“Aren’t you… the contact person arranged by the ‘Organization’?”

Judy’s face turned cold, and she said in a deep voice, “If you still want to live, don’t mention the word ‘Organization’ so casually.”

“Why…” Wang Donglin was halfway through his sentence when, with a change of heart, he swallowed the question back.

He had already sensed the unusual atmosphere; saying the wrong thing at this moment could very well cost him his life.

Seeing Wang Donglin stop talking, Judy ignored him, bending down and continuing to pack her luggage.

Wang Donglin lowered his head, but his mind was racing frantically. “That person” had clearly agreed with him: he only needed to come to this bar, find this person, and give her the code, and she would take him to a safe place. But why did she seem completely unaware of this?

Had he been deceived by “that person”?

But if it was just a simple scam, why make it so complicated? Couldn’t they just trick him into looking for someone who didn’t even exist?

“If you still want to live, don’t say the word ‘Organization’ so casually.” Judy’s words echoed in Wang Donglin’s ears.

What had gone wrong?

“Okay, I’m leaving now. You should leave too.” Judy slung her bag over her shoulder and strode out the door.

Wang Donglin remained seated, motionless, his eyes fixed on Judy, observing her every movement.

Just then, Judy’s phone rang with a message. She glanced down, put the phone away, and muttered, “An annoying ad.”

Wang Donglin’s heart tightened. He noticed that while Judy’s facial expression remained unchanged as she looked at her phone, her pupils dilated considerably. He had studied micro-expression analysis to learn how to read his opponent’s thoughts during chess games, and he knew this was Judy’s reaction to important information; it definitely couldn’t be an ad.

That cover-up only served to reinforce Wang Donglin’s suspicions.

“That person” had arranged for him to come here not to help him escape but to control his escape route.

The true goal of the ‘Organization’ was to take his life.

Wang Donglin suddenly understood everything. This morning’s attacker was likely sent by the ‘Organization.’

Kill to silence him.

Because he had lost his usefulness to the ‘Organization.’

Wang Donglin raised his head, his gaze locked on Judy, who had already reached the door and could leave at any moment. She still stood hesitantly at the door, probably debating how to safely and securely eliminate him.

“Aren’t you leaving?” he asked.

“After careful consideration, it’s safer to take you with me. If you fall into the hands of the police, I’ll be in trouble,” Judy said with a casual air. “Come on, follow me.”

“Okay, where are we going?” Wang Donglin said without hesitation.

“Just follow me.” Judy didn’t explain anything, pushing the door open and leaving.

Wang Donglin followed closely behind, seemingly unsuspecting.

This low-rent apartment building didn’t have an elevator, and the stairway lights flickered on and off, casting an eerie glow. Judy led the way, walking briskly without a glance back, completely unconcerned about whether Wang Donglin could keep up.

“Hey, can you slow down a bit?” Wang Donglin called out, panting.

Judy snorted coldly, ignoring him. Instead, she quickened her pace and turned into a dark alley.

Wang Donglin had no choice but to run, panting.

However, as he turned into the alley, he saw Judy standing by the wall at the corner, waiting for him to appear and pounce. Without forewarning, few men could avoid the sudden, passionate embrace of this beautiful woman, let alone the sharp dagger hidden in her hand.

Wang Donglin didn’t shy away either. “Bang!” Judy clearly felt the dagger, aimed straight for Wang Donglin’s chest, not penetrate him, but instead lodge itself against something hard. The shock numbed her wrist, and the dagger immediately slipped from her hand.

Judy reacted incredibly quickly, leaping back without caring what was happening, avoiding Wang Donglin’s uppercut aimed at her chin.

“Very skilled!” Wang Donglin sneered, picking up the dagger from the ground.

Judy wasn’t in a hurry. She said slowly, “You actually have a piece of iron plate hidden on you? That’s outrageous!”

“While you were showering, I was bored and made some preparations.” Wang Donglin pulled the lid of a cookie jar from under his clothes and tossed it aside. “After all, your ruthless killing methods scared me.”

“You think I can’t defeat you just because you have a dagger?” Judy said aggressively. “Wang Donglin, you think you can go against us? You’re so naive!”

“Who wants to go against you? But if you don’t give me a way out, I won’t let you off either,” Wang Donglin said through gritted teeth. “You want to trick me? It won’t be that easy.”

“Then give it a try.” Judy raised her hands, ready for battle. “I’ll make sure you die clearly today.”

“Take me to see someone from the ‘Organization,’ and I’ll consider letting you go,” Wang Donglin said coldly.

“What a joke!” Judy snarled. Just as she was about to rush forward and snatch the dagger back with her bare hands, she stumbled and nearly fell.

She awkwardly clung to the wall, surprised to find her body losing control. Her head felt dizzy, her limbs weak.

“What… is going on…”

“Know yourself and your enemy, and you can fight a hundred battles without defeat.” Wang Donglin grinned. “You know who I am, so you should know how I killed people before.”

Judy was stunned for a moment, then a look of horror crossed her face.

“Do you remember? The glass of water you drank after you came out of the bathroom contained sleeping pills.”

“No… Impossible…”

“You can’t understand. I probably needed you back then, so why would I have drugged your water? That doesn’t make sense, does it?” Wang Donglin reached out and cupped Judy’s chin. “Because I’ll never trust a woman again in my life.”

Judy took two steps back, avoiding Wang Donglin’s hand, but she could no longer stand. She leaned against the wall and slowly sat down.

“You… can’t escape…”

“I’ll give you one last chance. Tell me about the ‘Organization,’ and I’ll spare your life. Otherwise—do you remember how the other women died?”

Judy shuddered.

Wang Donglin placed the dagger against Judy’s neck and asked, “Have you thought it through?”

“Wang Donglin… you’ll regret this.”

Judy lunged forward, her snow-white neck meeting the sharp dagger. Wang Donglin quickly retracted his hand but was still a step too late. The dagger slit Judy’s throat, leaving a dark red streak. Seconds later, blood gushed out, and she collapsed to the ground.

Judy soon perished, and Wang Donglin stared blankly at her body, feeling as if he, too, was half dead.

He finally felt the terrifying nature of the ‘Organization’ behind Judy and realized the extent of his earlier mistakes.

His biggest mistake was betraying the only person who genuinely wanted to help him, Lu Tianfeng.

.

May 31st, 10 p.m., a motel at the outskirts of D City.

Lu Tianfeng slowly opened his eyes, looking at the unfamiliar room, a sense of bewilderment as he recalled the last scene before he lost consciousness.

His mouth felt dry, and he managed to say, “Where is this?”

“A motel. Very safe.”

Lu Tianfeng hadn’t expected an immediate answer to his question, and even more astonishing, the person sitting next to his bed was Zhang Zhiqi.

“You?”

“It’s me,” Zhang Zhiqi replied crisply.

“Where are they?”

“In the next room. Your girlfriend has calmed down and just fell asleep.”

Lu Tianfeng struggled to sit up, rubbed his aching temple, and said, “How are you doing now?”

“Why don’t you tell me about yourself first?” Zhang Zhiqi patted Lu Tianfeng’s shoulder. “Why did you suddenly faint?”

“Maybe I was too tired…” Lu Tianfeng had always suspected the mysterious potion he’d drunk was to blame, but he couldn’t find any concrete evidence.

“Don’t put too much pressure on yourself. Many times, fate doesn’t give us the chance to choose. Don’t blame yourself.”

Lu Tianfeng’s face fell. Zhang Zhiqi’s words, meant to comfort him, had unexpectedly stabbed him in the heart.

Zhang Zhiqi, perceptive enough to notice the change in Lu Tianfeng’s expression, asked in astonishment, “Did I say something wrong?”

“No, I’m the one at fault, not you.” Lu Tianfeng sighed and closed his eyes.

Zhang Zhiqi could tell that Lu Tianfeng was hiding something, but he also knew he couldn’t force his way to know it.

“I’ve always felt like you’re different from everyone else.”

Lu Tianfeng opened his eyes in surprise and looked at Zhang Zhiqi. “What’s different?”

“You have a strong sense of responsibility, a sense that transcends ordinary people’s understanding. Sometimes I feel like you’re Spider-Man himself.”

“Spider-Man?” Lu Tianfeng frowned, not understanding the gag.

“With great power comes great responsibility, haha!” Zhang Zhiqi laughed easily, and perhaps influenced by it, Lu Tianfeng’s expression softened a bit.

“Let’s get down to business. What happened to the Small Stone Bridge case?”

“It’s very likely Wang Donglin’s doing. I’ve checked the victim’s information, and there’s no connection to Wang Donglin. I guess Wang Donglin just randomly hooked up with this girl.”

Lu Tianfeng felt a tightness in his chest, and his mouth twitched. “Alas, another innocent person I’ve killed…”

“Who knew things would turn out like this?”

“I know,” Lu Tianfeng said, emphasizing each word, then added, “To be precise, I know things shouldn’t have turned out this way.”

“Can you tell fortunes?”

“No, I’ve witnessed the future with my own eyes. I’ve experienced today, tomorrow, and the day after tomorrow… Forget it, just treat it as nonsense.” Lu Tianfeng smiled bitterly and shook his head. He didn’t expect Zhang Zhiqi to understand these things; he just blurted them out in the heat of the moment.

Unexpectedly, Zhang Zhiqi’s expression grew graver than ever before. He even reached out and placed his hands firmly on Lu Tianfeng’s shoulders.

“What did you just say?”

“Just treat me as nonsense…”

“Not this one, the one before that.”

“…I’ve witnessed the future with my own eyes.”

Cold sweat instantly broke out on Zhang Zhiqi’s forehead. “Are you saying you can travel through time?”

“The details are a bit complicated, but you can understand it this way.”

Zhang Zhiqi’s expression grew increasingly grim. He swallowed hard, a rare expression of nervousness on his face, as if he was about to say something but hesitated.

Lu Tianfeng’s curiosity was piqued. This was Zhang Zhiqi, the “Hound” who could face earthquakes without batting an eyelid. Why did he seem so transfixed by such seemingly fantastical words?

“I want to share a story with you, a sad one.” Zhang Zhiqi took a long moment to regain his composure, then uttered something bizarre.

“Thank you,” Lu Tianfeng replied, also bizarre.

Then, the two of them exchanged a gentle smile, like old friends who had known each other for years.

CONTENT END 88

chapters.title: Chapter 89
chapters.content:
Zhang Zhiqi’s Story

I was born into an ordinary family. My father was a criminal police officer, and my mother was frail and often ill. After giving birth to me, she relied on traditional Chinese medicine year-round. Eventually, she gave up her job and became a full-time housewife.

When I was ten, my mother finally succumbed to her illness and passed away. To spend more time caring for me, my father voluntarily requested a transfer to a less busy clerical position, giving up his formidable criminal police work.

My father and I depended on each other for survival. During one casual after-dinner chat, he expressed his hope that when I grew up, I would enroll in the police academy and inherit his legacy. But at the time, I had absolutely no interest in the police profession. My father’s suggestion repelled me, and I even declared that I would never become one.

In my first year of high school, I became fascinated by micro-expressions through films and television. I later began poring over thick psychology books, determined to become a psychiatrist.

However, in the second semester of my senior year, a few months before the college entrance exam, a tragedy struck my family. My father was attacked by an unidentified assailant while walking in the park. He suffered a severe head injury and fell into a coma, becoming a vegetative state. The police investigated and apprehended the assailant, but after interrogation, they concluded that he was driven by hatred for society and randomly attacked passersby. Although I couldn’t accept this explanation, I was helpless.

Soon after, the assailant died inexplicably in custody, and my father was declared brain dead by doctors. I had no choice but to abandon treatment, and the case was hastily closed.

That was the first time in my life that I felt the real importance of the truth behind a crime. The dead could not be brought back to life, but if the truth of a case could ultimately be revealed, it would be the greatest comfort to the victim’s family.

I changed my ambitions and decided to specialize in criminal psychology, hoping to become the nation’s top criminal profiler. I successfully enrolled in the Department of Psychology at D City University. From my first day, I studied like crazy. Within two years, I had self-taught all the basic undergraduate courses. Then I turned to more advanced academic fields, even using a dictionary to read the latest foreign research that had not yet been translated into Chinese.

My goal at the time was to enroll as a graduate student under Yuan Chengren, the foremost figure in domestic criminal psychology and the founder of the “criminal modeling” theory. Unexpectedly, in my senior year, Professor Yuan applied for early retirement due to health reasons and would no longer supervise graduate students. Disappointed, I also noticed a civil service job posting for an information analyst position at the police station, a relevant field for psychology.

So I decided to enter the real world of combat and successfully joined the police force, achieving top marks in both the written exam and the interview, thus fulfilling both my own and my father’s wish.

I won’t go into detail about my daily work over the next few years; let me explain why I ultimately chose to leave the force.

A strange incident shook my faith.

I had a very close cousin, my aunt’s daughter, four years my junior. She was a bright, talented singer and dancer and a standout student from a young age. After graduating from university, she successfully landed a job at a large local company. While her initial position wasn’t high-ranking, her career prospects were limitless.

One day, however, my cousin suddenly called me in tears, saying she didn’t want to live. Her voice cracked, and I knew something was amiss. While trying to comfort her, I rushed to her house, phone in hand.

“Don’t cry! Your brother’s a police officer. Don’t worry!” She kept calling me brother, not cousin, which made our relationship seem particularly close.

“Wuwuwu… Brother, this time… even the police won’t help… Wuwuwu…”

“I’ll be there right away; don’t hang up!”

“Wuwuwu… Brother… I want to die…” She was sobbing on the other end of the line.

I sprinted like a madman, rushing to my cousin’s house as fast as I could. The moment I saw her, I was completely stunned.

Was this still my lively, lovely, intelligent, and charming cousin?

Her face was covered in tear marks, her eyes were red and puffy, and her once pretty face looked thinner, pale, and bloodless.

“Brother…” She threw herself into my arms, her tears soaking my shirt. But seconds later, she suddenly pushed me away and retreated in fear.

“No! Don’t come over here!”

At that moment, I hated my psychology studies, because I almost immediately guessed that my cousin had been assaulted by a man.

“Be good, it’s okay, I’m here, be good…”

“Wuwuwu!” She burst into tears, and no amount of persuasion could stop her.

I don’t know how long it took until she was tired of crying. She drooped her head weakly and said in a barely audible voice, “Brother, I was assaulted… but I don’t have any evidence…”

I held her, gently patting her back to calm her down. “It’s okay. You’re brave enough to speak up. No one can hurt you anymore.”

“No, brother, do you understand? I have no evidence… Because, because that man assaulted me in another time and space…”

I froze, subconsciously scanning her face to gauge her consciousness.

Although her face was expressionless, she didn’t seem to have lost her ability to think logically. However, I couldn’t understand a word she said. “That man, he’s my boss… Time repeats itself multiple times within the same day, so he insults and hurts me over and over again… But on the final loop, he’ll be dressed up again, playing the good guy… I can’t stand this life anymore…”

“Sister, calm down. Speak slowly, one sentence at a time.”

“Brother, you don’t believe me, do you? I knew no one would.” She couldn’t calm down. Instead, she grew increasingly agitated, shouting at the top of her lungs, her hollow eyes bloodshot.

“I believe you, but I really don’t understand…”

“That guy has superpowers. He brought me to a nonexistent time and space and repeatedly abused me, but in the real world, I wasn’t harmed at all,” she said seriously.

“So, if you call the police and have the medical examiner examine the injuries…”

“Brother, in this time and space, I’m still a virgin. That’s why I said I don’t have any evidence.”

I was silent. My cousin’s words were typical of paranoia, but she seemed more lucid than the average delusional patient, and her words were even stranger. I didn’t know what had happened to her to cause her to be like this.

All I knew was that this problem was a thorny one, one that couldn’t be solved in a few words. I had to persuade her to seek treatment from a qualified psychologist.

“Sister, how about this? I’ll take you to see a doctor this weekend…”

“No, I don’t need a doctor. I need your protection.” She clutched my hand tightly. “Brother, I want to quit. I don’t want to see him anymore.”

“No problem. If you want to quit, then quit. It’s okay to rest at home for a while.” Even though I said this, I was still very puzzled. I had never heard her mention anything particularly unpleasant about her work, so it shouldn’t be causing her so much psychological pressure.

“Brother… what should I do… I can’t sleep at night right now, and I can’t even tell my parents about this…”

“Let’s see a doctor! I can prescribe some sleeping pills to help you sleep.”

“No!” she reacted angrily. “The doctor will think I’m crazy and put me in a psychiatric hospital. I’m absolutely not going to see a doctor!”

I smiled bitterly. She was right. If I were a psychiatrist, I’d probably make the same diagnosis, because her condition was no longer suitable for home treatment.

I spent several hours chatting with her to calm her down. Then I coaxed her into taking some sedatives so she could get some sleep and relax. While she was asleep, I contacted several experienced psychiatrists and briefly explained the situation. Each of them agreed that my cousin needed immediate treatment and told me to schedule a visit as soon as possible.

Unexpectedly, even after waking up, my cousin still refused to go. I was at my wit’s end and worried that using overly forceful tactics would backfire, so I gave up for now and prepared to continue persuading her the next day.

This might be the biggest mistake I’ve ever made in my life.

Early the next morning, my cousin called again. Her voice was remarkably calm.

“Brother, I’m stuck in a time loop again. This is the fifth time I’ve experienced this day, and the fifth time I’ve called you.”

“Really? I’m sorry, I don’t remember…”

“Brother, thank you,” she said, then hung up. When I called back, her phone was off.

I was distraught and rushed to my cousin’s house. Waiting for me there was a body, already cold, dangling in midair.

She, always a beauty-conscious woman, had chosen such an unsightly death as hanging herself.

On the desk, there was a short suicide note from my cousin: “Actually, death isn’t painful, because I’ve already tried it. Brother, please believe me; everything I say is true.”

Tears blurred my eyes. Perhaps I should have believed her, because I was the only person she could trust in this world. But what could I do?

After my cousin’s accident, I locked myself in my room, pondering for two days and two nights, and finally decided to resign from my work. After leaving, I devoted all my time and energy to investigating my cousin’s boss.

It was a difficult task most people can’t imagine. I followed him every day, observing his every move, investigating everyone he came into contact with, analyzing his resume item by item, and even bribing those around him to obtain personal information about him. To better conduct my investigation, I diligently studied the most advanced hacking techniques. During those years, I even fortuitously became a “senior expert” in China’s largest hacker community.

My investigation lasted three full years, over a thousand days and nights, enough to unearth the darkest secrets of a person’s heart. I uncovered the man’s three mistresses and fourteen other women with whom he had had affairs. I dug up the hidden ledgers of three of his companies, revealing evidence of tax evasion totaling over 100 million yuan over the years. Insider trading, bribery, labor law violations, and other issues, large and small, were also numerous.

But even after thoroughly investigating his public and private affairs, I couldn’t find a single clue to support my cousin’s accusations. Although he was a womanizer, he never used violence to coerce women into submission. Perhaps it was because he simply didn’t need to.

I laughed at myself. How could such things as superpowers and time loops exist in this world? My cousin’s stories were just fantasies.

Three years had finally made me accept this reality. Although I still felt reluctant, I ended my investigation, publicly released all the information anonymously, and watched with indifference as the mad power of online public opinion consumed him. Unfortunately, his disgrace couldn’t save my cousin’s life.

I opened my own firm, and after solving several complex cases, my reputation within the industry grew. Everyone called me “Hound,” praising my investigative skills as if they were divine. To better portray myself, I readily accepted all the praise.

But I knew full well that my cousin’s death was a knot I would never be able to untie.

CONTENT END 89

chapters.title: Chapter 90
chapters.content:
May 31st, 10:30 p.m., Suburban Motel.

Lu Tianfeng listened quietly to Zhang Zhiqi’s narration, neither interrupting nor asking questions. He remained silent until Zhang Zhiqi concluded his melancholy story with a long sigh.

In the room, only the breathing of the two men remained.

After a long pause, Zhang Zhiqi was the first to break the silence: “Can you really travel through time?”

“I can help you unravel your mystery,” Lu Tianfeng said slowly. “Your cousin isn’t delusional, and she’s not lying to you. Everything she said must be true.”

“Really?” Zhang Zhiqi asked softly.

“There are indeed a very few people in this world who can perceive time loops. Whenever a time loop occurs, the same day repeats itself five times…”

Lu Tianfeng had great confidence in Zhang Zhiqi’s understanding, so without further pause, he unpacked the secrets of time loops, including how he had previously solved cases using this ability, how he had met Luo Tengfeng, who also possessed this ability, and the intense head-on battle between the two. Of course, he also briefly recounted his first experience with time travel.

Zhang Zhiqi’s eyes widened at this, unsure how to react to all this. While Lu Tianfeng’s description was bizarre and defied scientific common sense, it perfectly matched the details his cousin had recounted, and it clearly explained all the confusion and annoyance he had felt over the years surrounding her death.

Finally, Zhang Zhiqi could only sigh again and lament, “If only I had met you sooner.”

“So your cousin’s boss exploited the special abilities of a Perceiver to assault women in those time-looping spaces that leave no trace, to satisfy his perverted desires.”

“But… if there’s no trace left, why does my cousin… remember the assault?”

“I don’t know… I suspect your cousin may have become a Perceiver during this process, and she couldn’t handle the change. The ability to perceive time loops ultimately led to her own demise.”

“How did this strange ability arise?” Zhang Zhiqi spoke more and more slowly, his mind filled with unimaginable and terrifying answers.

Lu Tianfeng paused, then said, “I want to know, too.”

Zhang Zhiqi was silent for a long time, then sighed again, saying, “If only I had met you sooner.”

“You wouldn’t have believed me then.”

“No, I would have. Actually, when I stumbled across your profile while browsing the police database, my first reaction was, ‘Could this guy have superpowers?’ Your name has stayed with me ever since, but I just haven’t actively sought you out.”

“No wonder you accepted our commission without hesitation,” Lu Tianfeng suddenly realized. “Besides the money, there must be another reason.”

“Honestly, I don’t care much about the money. The only reason is that I want to meet you.”

Lu Tianfeng extended his right hand: “Nice to meet you!”

“Me too.” Zhang Zhiqi shook his hand firmly. “By the way, if today could happen again, I hope you’d come see me again.”

“But today isn’t the day of the time loop… Huh?” Lu Tianfeng froze, as if remembering something.

“What’s wrong?”

“Let me gather my thoughts—” Lu Tianfeng raised his right hand, pausing, then closed his eyes. Countless thoughts flashed through his mind.

He was certain that today, May 31st, wouldn’t be a time loop.

But he had “traveled back” from June 2nd.

The mysterious group that appeared on the night of June 2nd, whose origins were unknown, possessed a potion that could grant one the ability to sense the passage of time.

But simply sensing the passage of time wasn’t enough; time had to actually flow backwards. And the thug who threatened him had sworn they could trigger the time reversal.

So, what if they could find those people and force them to trigger the passage of time again? Could Yu Yongsheng and the other innocent people who died today have escaped their fate?

Lu Tianfeng’s eyes snapped open, his gaze blazing.

“Have you figured anything out?” Zhang Zhiqi asked.

“To make a long story short, I need you to help me find someone.”

“Wang Donglin?”

“No, someone else, someone even I don’t know.”

Zhang Zhiqi was stunned for a moment, then smiled. “That’s sure to be interesting.”

“Yes, the real key figure isn’t Wang Donglin.” Lu Tianfeng suddenly regained his confidence and strength. He jumped out of bed and paced excitedly around the room. “But we still have to find Wang Donglin first, because he’s the most useful bait.”

“No problem, but there’s something more important that needs your help now; that’s rest.” Zhang Zhiqi put his arm around Lu Tianfeng’s shoulder and said, “Tong Yao told me you haven’t been feeling well all day.”

“That’s a side effect of the potion…”

“It’s already late at night. Wang Donglin must be hiding somewhere for the night. We need to recharge our batteries for the next challenge. You can’t go without sleep for days on end, can you?”

Lu Tianfeng remembered how he’d managed to get through every time loop he’d encountered before without sleep, because at the end of each “day,” his energy and strength seemed to be fully replenished.

However, he had to admit that Zhang Zhiqi was right this time. He, like everyone else, needed rest.

“Rest is a luxury for me.”

“Then let’s indulge ourselves tonight. What time do you wake up tomorrow morning?”

“I’m used to getting up at 6:30.”

“What a workaholic! I’m used to sleeping until I wake up naturally. That’s the most physiologically sound schedule,” Zhang Zhiqi said with a smile.

“You’re kidding! Set the alarm for 7 o’clock.”

“No problem.”

Lu Tianfeng sank back into bed. His head suddenly felt heavy, his body light. It seemed he had indeed severely overdrawn his energy.

His consciousness gradually faded, and as he fell into sleep, he thought he heard a knock on the door.

But he was too exhausted, too exhausted to open his eyes to look.

The whole world fell silent.

.

May 31st, 11:00 p.m., D City Police Station, Conference Room.

Cheng Tuo stared blankly at the three crime scene photos on the big screen, feeling a wave of unspoken depression.

The first picture is a female corpse found at Small Stone Bridge. The identity of the deceased had been confirmed earlier. She was Yang Yazi, a wealthy young lady who had no worries about food and clothing. The second picture was Yu Yongsheng, Cheng Tuo’s former subordinate, and also the “bait” with a police tracker on him. The deceased in the third picture was a female bartender named Judy, who worked at the Black & White Bar. However, preliminary investigations found that all of Judy’s identity documents were fake, and the woman’s true origins were not clear at the moment.

Any one of these three cases would have been enough to ignite the current public outcry surrounding Wang Donglin’s escape, let alone the fact that three people died within a matter of hours.

“What suggestions do you have for the next step in the investigation?” Director Luo’s question brought Cheng Tuo back to his senses. He glanced around and saw that every colleague in the conference room was as preoccupied and silent as he was.

“Cheng Tuo, please speak.” Director Luo, seeing no one speaking, called on someone.

“There’s currently no evidence linking the last two cases to Wang Donglin. We need to carefully consider whether to investigate them together.” Cheng Tuo smiled wryly. Whether it was a blessing or a curse, the inevitable was inevitable.

“I support the combined investigation,” said Yan Jin, who had apprehended Wang Donglin once and was eager to do so a second time. “The latest news is that a waiter at the Black & White confirmed that Yu Yongsheng had been inside the bar to inquire about Wang Donglin before his death, and Wang Donglin happened to be there at the time! The waiter also said that Yu Yongsheng, realizing Wang Donglin might have just left, hurried out the back door and was attacked and killed in the alley a few minutes later.”

“What about that female bartender?” Director Luo asked again.

Yan Jin confidently replied, “When Wang Donglin first entered the bar, he asked the waiter about Judy. It seems he came to the Black & White specifically to find Judy.”

Director Luo frowned; the situation was spiraling out of control.

“Cheng Tuo, you will be primarily responsible for following up on the Small Stone Bridge case. Have Xiao Ran from the local police station cooperate with you. You should know that the deceased’s identity was quickly identified thanks to the clues he provided. Yan Jin, you will dispatch personnel to Moyun Town to conduct an in-depth investigation into the two cases on Bar Street. Maintain communication and share all leads promptly. Our primary goal remains to find Wang Donglin.”

“Yes, sir!” Cheng Tuo and Yan Jin said in unison.

Cheng Tuo knew this order effectively handed the position of frontline commander to Yan Jin, but he wasn’t displeased at all. Instead, he felt relieved.

Looking at Yan Jin again, although his expression remained calm, a fire seemed to blaze in his eyes.

“Can you find Wang Donglin within 24 hours?”

Director Luo didn’t address the question to anyone in particular, but Yan Jin answered with a resounding voice: “I guarantee with my badge that Wang Donglin will be apprehended within 12 hours.”

Everyone erupted in laughter. With Yan Jin’s bold words, the morale in the conference room seemed to soar. Cheng Tuo groaned inwardly. Even the usually steady Yan Jin had lost his composure. Using such extreme measures to motivate the team showed just how dire the situation was.

“Lu Tianfeng, you’ve really screwed us!”

At that moment, Cheng Tuo’s phone vibrated softly. He looked down and saw a Mark Six lottery advertisement from an unfamiliar number. The message began with a seemingly jumbled mess of four English letters: T, I, M, and E, which instantly terrified him.

It had been a long time since he had received a text from the ‘Organization.’

.

May 31st, 11:10 p.m., at the rest area of ​​the Hongfeng gas station on the suburban highway.

Wang Donglin sat in the shared car he had just rented, looking down at Judy’s bag. It wasn’t much, but it contained five different identities—five purses, five ID cards, credit cards, a cell phone, and other related items. It turns out that “Bartender Judy” was just one of the woman’s identities, and the shared car was unlocked using a credit card from Judy’s other wallet.

Wang Donglin figured the police wouldn’t be able to track him down for a while, but the crucial question now was, where would he go next?

Judy’s phone was incredibly sparse, unnaturally clean. The only text message he could see read, “Get rid of the trash.” The contact name was blank, and even the sending number was a long, dummy string of numbers. Wang Donglin knew this meant he had been ruthlessly abandoned by the ‘Organization.’

No, this wasn’t just a separation but a termination. The ‘Organization’ wanted to silence him, completely silencing him.

“Could it be that the information I possessed was so important to them?” Wang Donglin stared silently out the car window, recalling every detail of his dealings with the ‘Organization.’ Unfortunately, he couldn’t recall what crucial information he might have.

If one didn’t know what cards and chips one held, one couldn’t engage in a game of chance with them.

Wang Donglin felt a surge of frustration, akin to the feeling he’d had when facing a top-tier chess master, completely unable to fathom their intentions.

“But I have the cards!” he muttered to himself.

Wang Donglin recalled his elementary school experience at the national tournament. One match in particular stood out. He was in a desperate position, completely outnumbered and vulnerable. It looked as if his opponent could easily crush him. But strangely, his opponent made a series of slow moves, giving him a chance to catch his breath.

At that moment, Wang Donglin kept asking himself, why was his opponent so cautious? What was he guarding against? Was there a crucial move he’d missed?

Following this line of thought, after much contemplation, Wang Donglin finally figured out the crucial move and successfully won the match. This was his final victory in that national tournament.

Today’s situation was very similar to that of the past. He had to understand exactly how important he was to the ‘Organization,’ or he would perish without realizing it.

There was one obvious way out—contact the police immediately and surrender. But if the information Lu Tianfeng had given him this morning was correct, this path would ultimately lead to his own death.

The other option was to escape alone. With Judy’s credit cards, he should be able to escape far and wide. But how far would he have to flee? If Judy’s various identities were all prearranged for her by the ‘Organization,’ then even escaping to the ends of the earth would be futile.

The third option was to go back and try to contact Lu Tianfeng, but Wang Donglin wasn’t sure he was still willing to cooperate.

“This is such a difficult situation!” Wang Donglin slammed the steering wheel.

But even so, he couldn’t just sit there and wait for death.

The current situation was like the most complex middle game in chess, a complex web of intertwined forces, with every move affecting the entire system. A single wrong move could lead to a complete loss.

In such a situation, a cautious player would actively seek to simplify and clarify the situation. However, a player at a disadvantage would often choose to take risky moves, further confusing the situation.

Only by creating chaos could one induce the opponent to make a mistake, thus creating an opportunity for a comeback.

Wang Donglin suddenly had an idea and picked up one of Judy’s phones and logged into Weibo.

After Wang Donglin was arrested, Wang Xiaomian took over his daily Weibo account, clearing all previous content and posting a single apology to everyone: “I’m sorry.” This Weibo post, which prohibited comments and reposts, remained isolated on the personal homepage, yet the pageview data below showed nearly 50 million views.

Luckily, Xiaomian hadn’t changed his usual password.

Wang Donglin entered the new Weibo compose screen and quickly typed five words. After a pause, he decisively pressed the publish button.

These five words would spread across the internet in the blink of an eye.

“Come and catch me!”

Posting location: Provincial Highway X25, Hongfeng Gas Station.

Wang Donglin couldn’t help but laugh at the “Sent Successfully” notification.

The cat-and-mouse game was only just beginning to reach its climax.

CONTENT END 90

chapters.title: Chapter 91
chapters.content:
May 31st, 11:40 a.m., in a deserted alley.

Cheng Tuo, wearing a baseball cap with its brim covering half his face, sidled up to a corner. In the dark corner, another figure was already standing.

Zhou Huansheng, with a head full of white hair. “You’re here?” Zhou Huansheng’s voice was calm, yet tinged with an undeniable authority.

“Teacher Zhou, there’s a lot going on at the police station today, and I couldn’t get away…” Cheng Tuo hurriedly explained.

“There’s been a major commotion today!” Zhou Huansheng sighed.

“Yes, Wang Donglin’s escape is giving us a headache…”

Zhou Huansheng waved his hand, interrupting Cheng Tuo. “No, the real commotion is far more serious. Today, we’ve experienced a rare case of time-series disruption.”

“Time-series disruption?” Cheng Tuo’s question wasn’t due to confusion but rather to shock.

As a member of the ‘Organization,’ he knew exactly what time-series disruption meant—

Disrupting the normal operation of an event was a heinous crime.

“On June 2nd, in the normal time flow, the traitors activated a time reversal, forcing time back to May 31st, which was early this morning. Therefore, we are now in an illegal time flow, and the temporal disorder is becoming increasingly severe, with multiple temporal disturbances occurring…”

“What should we do?” Cheng Tuo, not a Perceiver, only then realized the severity of the situation.

“Find the key variable and eliminate it as soon as possible.”

“Is it Wang Donglin?” Cheng Tuo’s face showed a look of difficulty. Now there were thousands of police officers chasing Wang Donglin, but there was still no sign of him. It would be difficult to accomplish anything with his own strength.

“There are two key variables: Wang Donglin and Lu Tianfeng.” Zhou Huansheng paused, then said, “Both must be eradicated.”

“They are very cunning. I’ve been tracking them all day, but I can’t even find a trace of them.” Cheng Tuo chuckled bitterly.

“You can’t do it alone, but the ‘Organization’ is backing you up.” Zhou Huansheng handed Cheng Tuo a briefcase and patted his shoulder. “It contains key clues to tracking down Wang Donglin. Hurry and get to it.”

Cheng Tuo weighed the briefcase; it was heavy, containing at least a hundred pages of information, and he had no idea what it contained.

“I’ll go right away.”

“Remember, everything must be done cleanly and efficiently.” Zhou Huansheng made a chopping gesture. “Absolutely no future troubles can be left.”

“Understood,” Cheng Tuo replied, bowing his head.

Because before the ‘Organization,’ no matter who you are, you have no choice but to bow.

But not everyone bows willingly.

CONTENT END 91

chapters.title: Chapter 92
chapters.content:
June 1st, 3:00 a.m., Suburban Motel.

Lu Tianfeng was half asleep, only to hear occasional crackling sounds.

What was that sound?

The sound of keyboard tapping.

Where am I? What am I doing?

The thought of this question instantly sobered Lu Tianfeng.

“Don’t run!” Lu Tianfeng sat up abruptly in bed.

“Are you okay?” Zhang Zhiqi asked calmly.

Lu Tianfeng rubbed his aching eyes and blinked hard. He saw Zhang Zhiqi sitting cross-legged on the other bed, a laptop on his lap, presumably collecting data overnight.

“Didn’t you say you wanted to sleep until you woke naturally?” Lu Tianfeng teased.

“Indeed, I’ll work when I wake up.” Zhang Zhiqi yawned. “Since you’ve had enough sleep, why don’t I take over?”

Lu Tianfeng noticed that Zhang Zhiqi’s eyes were bloodshot; it looked like he hadn’t slept a single minute.

“Okay, I’ll go get some rest… but first, let me tell you what’s going on.” Lu Tianfeng checked the time; he’d already slept for over four hours.

“Shortly after you fell asleep, a major incident unfolded. Wang Donglin’s Weibo account suddenly updated with a message taunting the police.”

Zhang Zhiqi turned the screen to give Lu Tianfeng a better view.

“Come and catch me!” Lu Tianfeng frowned as he read. This irrational behavior was unlike the Wang Donglin he knew. “This phone must have been immediately tracked by the police.”

“That’s true, but the location was a busy gas station. Wang Donglin’s no fool. Would he have brought his phone with him? At 12:25, the police found the phone on the luggage rack of a long-distance bus, but there was no sign of Wang Donglin. He simply slipped the phone onto the bus while it stopped at the gas station to let passengers use the restroom.”

Lu Tianfeng smiled bitterly. “This guy really copied me precisely!”

“Haha, a great teacher produces a great student!” Zhang Zhiqi quipped.

Wang Donglin’s tactics mirrored the same ones Lu Tianfeng used yesterday morning to mislead the police using an electronic anklet tracking device. It was truly a headache.

Zhang Zhiqi yawned again. “Well, the information is all here. Take your time to read it. I’m getting old and can’t stand it any longer. I need to get some sleep first!”

Lu Tianfeng nodded and dimmed the bedside light. Seeing Zhang Zhiqi seemingly fall asleep as soon as he lay down, he thought of his cousin’s experience and couldn’t help but feel a surge of emotion.

“I should study it carefully…” Lu Tianfeng muttered softly, returning his attention to the screen.

“Come and catch me!”

After the screenshot of the Weibo post was enlarged, looking at the five large black characters and a large exclamation mark, Lu Tianfeng suddenly wondered if there was some important information hidden in these words.

Wang Donglin was a man with a calmness that was a little scary. Why would he deliberately provoke the police?

Unless he had a compelling reason to do so.

However, what else could be hidden in these five short words?

“No, there’s more information…”

Wang Donglin’s Weibo post included geographic information, making it easier for the police to pinpoint his location, increasing the risk of capture. Yet, he still chose to post it this way.

This geographic information is crucial.

Provincial Highway X25, Hongfeng Gas Station.

Lu Tianfeng instinctively moved his mouse around, watching the cursor darting around on the screen.

“If he could just run away, why did he have to leave his location? Could it be that he wanted others to know where he was besides the police?”

But Lu Tianfeng immediately dismissed this idea. No matter where Wang Donglin was hiding, he couldn’t possibly be near this gas station.

“Could it be…”

Zhang Zhiqi’s words echoed in Lu Tianfeng’s ears—a master teacher produces a master student.

Everything Wang Donglin was doing now was a deliberate imitation of Lu Tianfeng.

“He also knows another of my techniques…”

The digital index code table was one of the simplest and most effective encryption techniques.

The location information contained only two numbers: 2 and 5.

Corresponding to the phrase “Come and catch me,” the result was “Come.”

Come? Where to?

Lu Tianfeng felt he was only one step away from the truth. Was there something else he’d overlooked?

“Come, come…”

Lu Tianfeng muttered to himself as he casually typed these two words into the search engine.

Songs, comics, movies… Amidst a sea of ​​unrelated search results, one website caught Lu Tianfeng’s eye.

“Come BBQ,” located on Hualian Road, was less than a kilometer from the D City University campus.

This was probably the area Wang Donglin was most familiar with.

Lu Tianfeng quickly opened the website. It was a food review platform. In addition to restaurant information like address, phone number, average cost per person, and recommended dishes, it also contained numerous customer reviews.

The latest review, posted an hour ago, read:

What a hard-to-find place! I almost got lost! I spent the better part of a day searching!

Thankfully, I finally managed to eat there. The food was fantastic, a truly top-tier local kebab place!

PS: The owner said they open at 11:00 a.m., when there are fewer customers and no lines. I highly recommend coming at this time!

The last characters of the first three lines, when combined, form “Lu Tianfeng.” This couldn’t be a coincidence.

“Wang Donglin, do you want to meet me?” Lu Tianfeng pondered.

Eleven a.m.—that was the time Wang Donglin had specified.

Though he didn’t know why Wang Donglin had the audacity to approach him, Lu Tianfeng believed it was a message only he could decipher.

He hesitated for a moment, then gave up the thought of replying. He forced himself back into bed, closed his eyes, and tried to relax as much as possible.

What he needed most right now was rest, complete rest.

Because his body was beginning to ache inexplicably again.

.

June 1st, 3:30 a.m., Moyun Town Bar Street

After relentlessly inspecting several scenes, Yan Jin returned to the police car, plopped down heavily, and sighed again.

“How’s the situation?” an elderly voice asked from the backseat.

“It’s a mess.” Yan Jin pulled a cigarette from his pocket, glanced at it, and stuffed it back in his pocket. “Old Dai, this case is incredibly difficult, so we need your personal assistance.”

“Captain Yan, you’re being polite. I’m already half-invalid. I just hope I don’t burden everyone during the operation.” Dai Chunhua, a veteran detective from the Fourth Squadron who was semi-retired, was the other individual in the car. He rubbed his thigh and said, “This leg aches every time it’s windy or rainy. It really makes me admit I’m getting old!”

“Old Dai, there are only two of us in this car, so I’ll be frank.” Yan Jin turned and looked at Dai Chunhua seriously. “If it weren’t for your sharp eyes, we never would have caught Wang Donglin.”

Dai Chunhua smiled faintly and said, “The credit goes to everyone. I just contributed a little.”

“Old Dai, when it comes to investigating cases, you will always be my mentor.”

“Okay, let’s talk about the case.”

Yan Jin nodded and said, “Let’s start with Yu Yongsheng’s case. There were no signs of a struggle at the scene. He was stabbed through the heart by a sharp weapon, like a slender dagger, and subsequently died of heavy bleeding. Judging from the angle and depth of the wound, the murderer was at very close range and was between 1.5 and 1.6 meters tall…”

“A woman,” Dai Chunhua said succinctly.

“Why do you say that?”

“Yu Yongsheng is a skilled fighter within the team. Looking across the entire criminal police brigade, few would dare claim a single-handed victory over him. If he was stabbed in the heart without putting up a fight, the killer must have completely overwhelmed him.” Dai Chunhua sighed softly. “For example, the attacker was a delicate woman. Considering the height you just mentioned, I think it’s very likely a woman.”

“Old Dai, you really shouldn’t have retired.” Yan Jin flipped to a page in the file. “Forensic colleagues have confirmed that the murder weapon used in Yu Yongsheng’s assassination was the same dagger found at another crime scene that killed the female bartender, Judy. Based on the current clues, it’s highly likely that Judy was Yu Yongsheng’s killer, but she was killed by her companion for unknown reasons.”

“Her companion was Wang Donglin?” Dai Chunhua squinted, watching the raindrops on the car window.

“Besides Judy’s fingerprints, there’s also Wang Donglin’s on the dagger.”

“Slitting the throat? That doesn’t fit with Wang Donglin’s ‘murder philosophy’…”

“Based on the wound analysis, it seems Judy volunteered to face her own death.” Yan Jin paused. “A woman whose life story is a mystery, whose identity is entirely fabricated, and who is ready to die—does that remind you of anything?”

“Professional killers, mercenaries—they’re definitely not ordinary people. During the operation in Tiedao New Village yesterday morning, a mercenary’s body was also found, right?” Dai Chunhua said, pounding his thigh vigorously. “Do you remember what I said after we successfully arrested Wang Donglin last time?”

Yan Jin said sternly, “Of course I do. You said Wang Donglin’s last crime pattern showed an irrational change. The case isn’t that simple.”

“These mysterious mercenaries have reinforced my suspicions. The connection between Wang Donglin and them… What exactly is the connection? This will be a crucial breakthrough in the case.”

At this moment, Yan Jin suddenly slapped his forehead. “Oh, I remember something puzzling.”

“Oh? Tell me!”

“Lu Tianfeng told Tong Yao that he hijacked the prison van to take Wang Donglin because he wanted to uncover the truth behind Wang Donglin’s case.”

A gleam flashed in Dai Chunhua’s eyes. “Lu Tianfeng also thinks there’s something fishy going on?”

“Yes. What’s strange is that he wasn’t involved in the investigation of Wang Donglin’s case, so why could he so confidently say there was something fishy going on? And the timing of his prison van hijack yesterday morning was so clever, almost like…”

“He predicted the future,” Dai Chunhua expressed Yan Jin’s doubts. Many within the police force were also quite curious about Lu Tianfeng’s hidden “informant,” and there was even a joke circulating that Lu Tianfeng’s true identity was a clairvoyant.

Of course, they all knew Lu Tianfeng’s intelligence definitely wasn’t derived from psychic abilities, which made it all the more terrifying.

“Let’s not get off topic. We must focus on tracking down Wang Donglin.” Dai Chunhua closed his eyes and pressed his fingers against his temples. “Why do you think he posted that inexplicable Weibo?”

“To distract us and escape?”

Dai Chunhua shook his head. “That gas station wasn’t part of our primary search area. Posting another Weibo post there would be a bit superfluous. And I firmly believe Wang Donglin wouldn’t do something meaningless.”

“Yes, I know you’ve been obsessed with those two still-undiscovered ‘souvenirs.'”

“Everything that seems ‘superfluous’ is key to solving the case. The missing ‘souvenirs’ are key, as are Wang Donglin’s Weibo posts.”

Dai Chunhua slowly opened his eyes, his lips moving as he silently recited the five characters.

“Come and catch me… Come and catch me…”

Dai Chunhua snorted coldly, saying in a voice almost audible only to him, “Let me fulfill your wish.”

CONTENT END 92

chapters.title: Chapter 93
chapters.content:
June 1st, 7:00 a.m., Tee Mall, open-air parking lot, on the outskirts of D City.

This large, suburban shopping mall, open 24 hours a day, sat beside the highway. At night, the entire building was ablaze with lights, earning it the nickname “The Great Lighthouse” from nearby residents.

Although it was just daybreak, it was the perfect time for supermarkets to restock their shelves with fresh vegetables and meats. Housewives familiar with the area arrived in groups, keeping time.

In a gray sedan, Wang Donglin stretched and rubbed his lower back, aching from sleeping slumped over in the driver’s seat all night.

After leaving Hongfeng Gas Station in the middle of the night, he drove to the nearest shared car rental station, obtained a new ID, rented a new car, and then drove all the way to Tee Mall, where he spent the entire night in the parking lot. He didn’t dare stay in a hotel, as even an illegal inn would likely be a target for police raids. Sleeping in his car was safer.

Wang Donglin slapped his cheeks to sober up faster. He heard his stomach growling in protest, so he fished for some change in Judy’s bag, jumped out of the car, and ran to the fast food restaurant outside Tee Mall to buy a breakfast sandwich.

Fearing he might be recognized by passersby, he didn’t dare sit down to eat. After buying his breakfast, he hurried back to his car, only taking a large bite of his sandwich after locking the door again.

However, before he could swallow his breakfast, he felt something hard pressing against the back of his head.

“Don’t move!” a deep, cold voice boomed from the back seat.

Wang Donglin’s blood froze instantly. He had no idea who had come and even less understanding of where he had gone wrong. He had clearly locked the car when he went to buy breakfast.

“Put your hands on the steering wheel… If you dare move, your head will explode.”

“Who are you?” Wang Donglin finally managed to utter with difficulty.

“Criminal Police Brigade, Cheng Tuo. Wang Donglin, you’re under arrest.”

“Police?” Wang Donglin’s mind raced. There were so many baffling things about this whole situation, and he had to find a way out quickly.

In this complex situation, there must be a crucial move. If you can figure it out, you win; if you can’t, you lose.

“Click!” The safety on the pistol went off.

“Wait, don’t shoot!” Wang Donglin shuddered and shouted, “We can talk.”

“Haha!” Cheng Tuo sneered. “What can we talk about?”

“Who are you?” Wang Donglin suddenly understood the inconsistency. “I’m a serious criminal. How could the police send only you to arrest me?”

Cheng Tuo took a breath but said nothing. “You must have checked the documents used to rent my car and tracked the phone I used, but these items originally belonged to another woman. The police couldn’t possibly know this information.”

“You’re quite clever.” Cheng Tuo couldn’t help but admire Wang Donglin’s ability to maintain such clarity of thought even with a gun pointed at his head.

“Those fake identities were prepared by the ‘Organization’ in advance, so only someone within the ‘Organization’ could use them to track me.”

“People who are too clever often don’t end well.” Cheng Tuo pressed the gun closer.

Wang Donglin shrugged and smiled. “Officer Cheng, if you were just a lackey of the ‘Organization,’ you should have shot me long ago. Since you didn’t choose to shoot, we should sit down and discuss how we can cooperate.”

“What gives you the right to talk about cooperation?”

“Then do you know why the ‘Organization’ is so determined to eliminate me?”

Cheng Tuo didn’t answer. He wasn’t sure he knew the real reason. After all, when the ‘Organization’ issued a mission, they rarely laid out the full story. They only pursued results, not the process, and were even more reluctant to reveal any information.

Wang Donglin chuckled and continued, “It seems you’re not valued within the ‘Organization’ either!”

“Stop the nonsense and tell me everything you know. Don’t forget, your life is in my hands.”

“Officer Cheng, I wonder if you’re interested in working with me to bring down the ‘Organization’?” Wang Donglin slowly turned, and their eyes met for the first time.

“Just you?”

“I have a partner, your old friend, Lu Tianfeng.”

“What exactly is your relationship?” Cheng Tuo frowned. Although he held the gun, Wang Donglin firmly controlled the negotiation initiative.

Wang Donglin turned his head and looked straight ahead again. “Officer Cheng, I didn’t know you before, and I can’t say I trust you now. If you wish to join us, please earn my trust—at the very least, you shouldn’t point a gun at your allies.”

“We’re not allies now,” Cheng Tuo replied coldly. He couldn’t let Wang Donglin lead him around any longer. “I suggest you come back to the station with me. If you refuse, I’ll shoot you for resisting arrest.”

“And then you can report to the ‘Organization,’ right?” Wang Donglin sighed exaggeratedly, shaking his head. “You’ll regret it, because you have no idea how important I am.”

“Just say what you mean. Don’t be so subtle.” Cheng Tuo was genuinely feeling uneasy. Wang Donglin’s impervious attitude made him uneasy.

“Officer Cheng, if you can be a little patient, we can make it to noon today.” Wang Donglin knew he had a good chance of convincing Cheng Tuo. “As long as you can cover for me and Lu Tianfeng to meet smoothly, I guarantee you’ll get the reward you seek.”

“What reward do I want?”

“Solve the case, get a promotion, rise to prominence, and more importantly, break free from the ‘Organization’s’ control.”

Cheng Tuo still didn’t answer directly, but he subconsciously lifted his gun away from Wang Donglin’s head.

Wang Donglin breathed a sigh of relief and patted his chest gently.

This crucial move had finally been made correctly.

.

June 1st, 7:30 a.m., inside the command vehicle of Wang Donglin’s pursuit team.

Yan Jin and Dai Chunhua, who had been busy all night, were taking advantage of their rare downtime to take a nap, but a phone call interrupted the tranquility within the vehicle.

“I’m Yan Jin; go ahead.”

“Captain Yan, this is Xiao Huang from the technical analysis team at headquarters. We’ve spotted someone who looks like Wang Donglin in the security surveillance footage.”

Yan Jin immediately perked up: “Thank you for your hard work. Please send me the information.”

With the rise of technology, urban security surveillance footage was playing an increasingly important role in the pursuit of fugitives. High-definition video and facial recognition technology were becoming increasingly popular, coupled with increasingly powerful hardware, making AI-powered tracking of fugitives a reality. Three years ago, D City implemented a “Manhunter” system that collected data from 5,000 urban security cameras and automatically analyzed facial features to accurately identify fugitives. After three years of practical experience and system expansion, the system now incorporated data from over 20,000 surveillance cameras and could analyze the features of over a thousand faces per second.

It was this tireless “Manhunter” who, early this morning, captured a suspicious individual outside a self-service car rental shop. By repeatedly replaying and comparing surveillance video captured at a Hongfeng gas station, the technical analysis team confirmed that someone was driving a white sedan from the station to the rental shop, then renting a gray sedan through the self-service machine. The white sedan was parked haphazardly on the roadside. Forensic personnel, after extracting fingerprints from the car, confirmed the driver to be Wang Donglin.

Thus, Wang Donglin was currently on the run in the gray sedan. The relevant license plate information had been uploaded to the database, and the analysis team was diligently searching parking lots and roads throughout the city for the vehicle.

“The search results just came back. That gray car was recorded entering the parking lot of the Tee Mall on the outskirts of the city but not leaving it.” Yan Jin’s tone was tinged with excitement. “It went in around 2:00 a.m. and hasn’t come out yet. He might have been sleeping in the car.”

Dai Chunhua seemed quite calm. “How far are we from the Tee Mall?”

“There aren’t many cars on the road right now. We can get there in five minutes.”

“Captain Yan, I suggest we don’t report Wang Donglin’s whereabouts to the police for now. Let’s handle it directly.”

Yan Jin was stunned, unable to react for a moment. “Old Dai, this is no small matter.”

“To track down Wang Donglin, our police force has mobilized almost the entire city. This deployment can corner him, but the downside is that information shared so quickly greatly increases the chances of leaks,” Dai Chunhua said thoughtfully. “I’m worried there’s a mole within our team.”

Yan Jin thought for a moment and nodded in agreement. After all, Wang Donglin’s location had been pinned down, and the Tee Mall The area surrounding the mall was desolate, and he couldn’t escape without a car.

Yan Jin decided to hold off on reporting the incident and instead gave his squad instructions via the intercom.

“Everyone, head to Tee Mall immediately and block the parking lot entrances and exits. I’m looking for a gray sedan with license plate number DV116. Repeat, DV116. This car must not leave the lot at any cost. Under no circumstances, understand?”

“Roger!”

“Understood!”

Five minutes later, Yan Jin and his men had completely surrounded the target vehicle.

But they were still too late. The car was empty, and as soon as the door opened, a strong, unpleasant odor wafted through. Someone had sprayed bleach all over the cabin, completely obliterating any fingerprint.

Yan Jin looked around and realized this location was a blind spot for surveillance. He estimated that checking the footage wouldn’t reveal anything, but he still sent someone to contact the mall’s security personnel to obtain the surveillance footage for evidence.

Dai Chunhua walked heavily around the car several times, his brow furrowed, his head lowered in silence.

“Old Dai, what did you find?”

“I’m thinking about the bleach.”

“It’s a common crime scene tactic. What’s wrong with that?” Yan Jin asked.
