“We’re pretty sure Wang Donglin drove this car. Why would he need to use bleach to destroy the evidence? Think back to the several cases he’s been involved in since his escape. The scenes weren’t compromised at all.”

Yan Jin was shocked. That’s right, Wang Donglin was blatantly provoking the police. Sprinkling bleach wasn’t his style.

“There was another person in the car, the one who took Wang Donglin away,” Yan Jin said, speculating.

“And someone who’s very familiar with our on-site investigations and acts with extreme caution.”

Although Dai Chunhua didn’t say it explicitly, Yan Jin immediately recalled the veteran detective’s reasoning from just a few minutes ago. Was there really a mole in the police force?

Yan Jin suddenly remembered that he should report the latest situation to his superiors.

CONTENT END 93

chapters.title: Chapter 94
chapters.content:
June 1st, 8:00 a.m., in a motel room.

Chen Nuolan had a long, long dream. In it, she was inside the Feng Teng Gene office building, being relentlessly pursued by a group of masked men. Bullet after bullet grazed her ear, nearly killing her.

But then, Lu Tianfeng appeared. He held a small silver pistol, but it held an endless supply of bullets. He shot his enemies one by one, each a headshot.

“Nuolan, follow me.”

Lu Tianfeng took her hand, warm and strong.

“Feng, there’s no way out.” The two ran to the edge of a building’s rooftop.

“As long as I’m here, there’s a way forward.” Lu Tianfeng put his arm around her waist. “Close your eyes.”

Chen Nuolan closed her eyes, only to hear the whistling wind. Unable to resist, she opened them. Lu Tianfeng was holding her, soaring through the sky.

The masked men didn’t give up. Some sprouted wings from their backs, while others transformed into crows, relentlessly pursuing them.

Black feathers flew toward Chen Nuolan like sharp swords, but just as they were about to pierce her, they froze in midair.

Lu Tianfeng gave her a confident smile.

“Look, time has stopped.”

“But time won’t stop forever!” Chen Nuolan said, with a hint of worry.

“Don’t worry. As long as I’m here, no one can hurt you.” Lu Tianfeng gently kissed her forehead.

But she still felt uneasy, so she squeezed Lu Tianfeng’s hand tightly, as if only the real touch could calm her.

A flash of lightning streaked across the sky, and the sky suddenly turned gloomy and gray.

The black feathers hovering in midair suddenly moved.

“Feng! Be careful!” Chen Nuolan, terrified and sweating profusely, desperately shouted…

Chen Nuolan suddenly jumped out of bed. Someone gently grasped her hand. She looked closely and saw Lu Tianfeng sitting beside her, looking at her with concern.

“Did you have a nightmare?” He gently wiped the sweat from her forehead.

“Feng…” Chen Nuolan didn’t reply and threw herself into Lu Tianfeng’s arms.

The two embraced tightly for a long moment without needing to exchange many words. Only then did Chen Nuolan reluctantly release his hand, blushing as she asked, “Why are you here? Where’s Tong Yao?”

“She and Zhang Zhiqi are in the next room. The police just released new information, and they’re following up on the investigation.”

“What about you?”

“My mission now is to protect you.” Lu Tianfeng patted Chen Nuolan’s head.

Chen Nuolan’s heart warmed, and she remembered Yu Yongsheng, who had died because of her poor decision. She lowered her head in guilt, sobbing and apologizing, “Feng, I’m sorry. Last night, I…”

“It was just an accident. You’re not to blame. Besides, I’ve already figured out a solution.”

“A solution…to the problem?” Chen Nuolan was momentarily stunned.

“People can’t be brought back from the dead, but I can turn back time.” Lu Tianfeng looked Chen Nuolan in the eye and said firmly, “I’m going to find the people who can manipulate time to go back to yesterday and save Yongsheng and the other innocent people who tragically died in this incident!”

“Is this… possible?” Chen Nuolan was stunned.

“Of course it is. If they can turn back time once, they can definitely do it again. The key is to find those people!” Lu Tianfeng gritted his teeth.

“From a scientist’s perspective, turning back time isn’t something that can be done so easily.” Chen Nuolan hesitated, choosing her words. “Achieving time reversal must come at a price.”

“A price?” Lu Tianfeng’s heart sank as he recalled the discomfort he’d felt after drinking the so-called enhancement potion. But he controlled his expression well, not letting any worry or fear show in front of Chen Nuolan.

“Are you feeling any worse for wear?”

“No, I feel more alert after a good night’s sleep,” Lu Tianfeng said with a smile.

“Don’t try to be brave. I’m worried… that potion you mentioned might have side effects.”

“It’s okay. I’ve experienced countless time loops before…”

“Knock, knock, knock—”

Lu Tianfeng was interrupted by a rapid knock on the door, followed by Tong Yao’s voice.

“Boss, we need to evacuate immediately. There are police outside.”

“Okay.” Lu Tianfeng grabbed Chen Nuolan’s hand. “Stay with me.”

.

June 1st, 8:15 a.m., D City Police Department Office Building, Command Center.

The constant flow of negative news early in the morning had left the officers’ faces etched with exhaustion and helplessness. First, the team led by Yan Jin reported that they had spotted Wang Donglin at a Tee Mall on the outskirts of the city, but the police were slow to close in and failed to apprehend him. Meanwhile, the team conducting a blanket search of every hotel also located a guest suspected of being Lu Tianfeng, though they too had a close encounter with the suspect.

“Everyone, stay alert! Don’t get discouraged,” Director Luo said, clapping his hands vigorously as he encouraged everyone. “We’re getting closer and closer to our target. Previously, the search operation had lagged behind the fugitive by several hours, but now the gap has narrowed to less than an hour. It’s rush hour, and all major roads are experiencing varying degrees of traffic congestion. I don’t think Wang Donglin can get far.”

“Director Luo, we’ve deployed additional personnel and set up roadblocks to screen passing vehicles. We’ve also notified all bus and taxi drivers passing near the Tee Mall to be on the lookout for anyone resembling Wang Donglin,” reported Wu Guoqing, who had been sitting in the command center.

“Great. How’s Lu Tianfeng doing?”

“A front desk clerk at a motel provided a tip: someone checked into two double rooms last night, using only two ID cards. When our colleagues arrived, they found both rooms empty. Investigation confirmed that both IDs used to check in were fake. One of the IDs had the name ‘Li Dabao,’ but the photo on it was of Lu Tianfeng.”

Director Luo thought for a moment and said, “Since that’s a motel, where’s the car?”

“After checking the license plate, we found it’s owned by this person.” Wu Guoqing handed Director Luo a file. The cover was the standard D City Police Department cover. He opened the first page and saw “Cancelled” stamped in red.

It was Zhang Zhiqi’s personal file.

Director Luo couldn’t help but frown. “Why is it him? Is he connected to yesterday’s gunfight at Qunxian Building?”

“Yes, the gunfight took place near Zhang Zhiqi’s office.”

“What a troublesome guy! Quick, bring him back and interrogate him.” Director Luo slammed the file back on the table. He knew Zhang Zhiqi well and didn’t need to dig through the files to understand the situation.

To his surprise, Wu Guoqing looked embarrassed and said, “Director Luo, our colleagues have already found the car and Zhang Zhiqi, but…”

“Can’t you get anything useful out of him?”

“Zhang Zhiqi said he only took the girls there to get a room last night, and that they rented two rooms purely to hide their tracks.”

“What a joke! He’s not a celebrity; why would he want to hide his tracks?” Director Luo said with a mixture of anger and amusement.

“We know he’s lying, but we have no evidence. Besides, Zhang Zhiqi was with a girl, Tong Yao.”

Director Luo immediately understood. Lu Tianfeng had quietly relocated, and Zhang Zhiqi and Tong Yao had proactively appeared to attract the police’s attention. If Lu Tianfeng and Zhang Zhiqi had truly orchestrated this scheme, Director Luo wouldn’t have bothered to deal with them. After all, finding Wang Donglin was the priority.

“Okay, don’t waste time investigating Zhang Zhiqi. Have Tong Yao report back immediately!” Director Luo, as if suddenly remembering something, asked, “What’s the situation with Cheng Tuo?”

“Team Cheng has dispersed their forces and is searching the area within a five-kilometer radius centered on Small Stone Bridge. So far, no results have been found.”

Director Luo’s gaze shifted to the large map on the wall. Small Stone Bridge and Tee Mall, two locations where Wang Donglin had been seen, were marked with red flags. The two flags appeared to be relatively close together on the map.

“How strange…” Director Luo muttered to himself, lost in thought.

.

June 1st, 8:40 a.m., Tee Mall, security camera room.

The police had taken full control of the area, accessing footage from all security cameras in the parking lot and at the mall entrance between 1:00 a.m. and 8:00 a.m., searching for any clues about Wang Donglin’s whereabouts.

The time the car entered the parking lot was quickly determined: 2:47 a.m. The security camera at the entrance captured the lower half of the driver’s face. Based on feature analysis, it was virtually certain that the driver was Wang Donglin. However, Wang Donglin later parked his car in a blind spot, preventing the security cameras from fully monitoring the vehicle’s interior.

Wang Donglin appeared again in the video at 7:02 a.m. He got out of the car and went to a fast food restaurant to buy breakfast. Five minutes later, he returned to the car and disappeared completely.

“Old Dai, what do you think?” Yan Jin asked.

“The problem lies in those five minutes.” Dai Chunhua stared at the screen intently.

“Do you think someone contacted him inside the fast food restaurant?” Yan Jin turned to his subordinates and said, “Pull up the surveillance footage from the fast food restaurant and check it carefully.”

Dai Chunhua shook her head slightly. “Captain Yan, go out for a cigarette and relax.”

Yan Jin was a little surprised. He knew that Dai Chunhua had quit smoking several years ago due to health problems, but he still said “yes” calmly. The two of them walked out of the monitoring room and into the corridor.

“What’s going on? Tell me.”

Dai Chunhua sighed. “Captain Yan, this is very complicated!”

“The contact wasn’t inside the fast food restaurant? So they met in the car…” Yan Jin was also a smart man, naturally able to draw inferences from one instance. “We can check if any vehicles deliberately drove into the blind spot after entering the parking lot.”

Dai Chunhua patted Yan Jin on the shoulder. “I’ve noticed. The parking lot was empty in the early morning, but a black commercial vehicle, despite its proximity, drove straight into the blind spot after entering the lot around 5:00 a.m. and didn’t leave until after 7:00 a.m.”

“Did you see the license plate?”

“3R898, does that number sound familiar?”

“This is…”

“I logged into the internal system and checked. It’s one of our police force’s operational vehicles, assigned to Cheng Tuo’s team for this mission.”

Yan Jin’s expression suddenly grew serious. He finally understood why Dai Chunhua had told him this privately. He immediately recalled what Director Luo had said yesterday.

“Lu Tianfeng suspects there’s a mole in the police force.”

Could the traitor be Cheng Tuo?

“Captain Yan, what do you think we should do next?” Dai Chunhua asked.

“Let me think… Something seems off. If Cheng Tuo was going to meet Wang Donglin, then they should have escaped as quickly as possible under cover of darkness. Why did they wait until after seven to reconnect?”

Dai Chunhua nodded repeatedly. “You’re right. Cheng Tuo must have been lurking to ambush Wang Donglin. He took advantage of Wang Donglin’s absence to buy breakfast, sneaked into his car, and subdued him. But he didn’t bring Wang Donglin back to the police station…”

Yan Jin suddenly thought of a terrifying possibility. If Cheng Tuo was the mole, then the details of Wang Donglin’s escort might have been leaked by him. His true intention might be to kill Wang Donglin.

Dai Chunhua bent down and pounded his thighs. “I think there are only two possibilities: first, Cheng Tuo is using Wang Donglin as bait to lure out the mastermind and capture him. Second, Cheng Tuo has ulterior motives for taking Wang Donglin away, and he needs to find a secluded place to silence him.”

“If it’s the former, we can’t act rashly and alert the enemy. But if it’s the latter, we need to stop him immediately.” Yan Jin was caught in a dilemma.

Unexpectedly, Dai Chunhua laughed. “This isn’t that complicated. The simplest approach is to keep an eye on Cheng Tuo’s vehicle. It’s easy enough to find the exact location of a mobile vehicle, isn’t it?” “

Unless conducting a highly classified mission, all police vehicles have GPS enabled. During this large-scale search operation, Cheng Tuo absolutely dared not turn it off, lest he draw unnecessary attention.

“Old Dai, you and I will handle this. Let’s not tell anyone else.”

“As you say.” Dai Chunhua smiled, but a sigh of resignation trailed off.

It was truly painful to doubt a colleague who had shared life and death with you.

CONTENT END 94

chapters.title: Chapter 95
chapters.content:
June 1st, 9:15 a.m., Lucky Tea House, private room.

Crystal shrimp dumplings, steamed siu mai, bean curd and beef balls, radish cake, boat congee… A dazzling array of Cantonese dim sum filled most of the table. Zhang Zhiqi was devouring his meal, while Tong Yao sat off to the side, sulking, not even moving her chopsticks.

“Officer Tong, aren’t you hungry?” Zhang Zhiqi asked, his voice muffled by the fullness of his mouth.

“What did you call me?” Tong Yao replied coldly.

“Officer Tong, is there a problem?” Zhang Zhiqi asked in astonishment.

“You’ve already checked into a hotel with me, and you’re still being so polite?” Tong Yao retorted in annoyance.

Zhang Zhiqi slapped his forehead. He finally understood that Tong Yao was sulking over the nonsense he’d just spouted to deceive the police.

He immediately put down his chopsticks, swallowed his food, and said seriously, “If you’re upset about what I said, I sincerely apologize, but my crude words had a deeper meaning.”

“A deeper meaning? So I need to learn from you?” Tong Yao scoffed.

“I wouldn’t call it learning, but I can certainly share some insights.” Zhang Zhiqi pretended not to hear the hidden meaning and said, “Do you think that information will be relayed to the command center?”

“Of course it will. Then everyone will…”

“Will your colleagues and superiors believe what I say?” Zhang Zhiqi interrupted Tong Yao.

Tong Yao paused, finally beginning to understand Zhang Zhiqi’s meaning.

“Are you saying you said that on purpose?”

“The ultimate lie is knowing I’m lying, yet feeling helpless. The reason I’m exaggerating and making things up is to send a clear message to the command center: Don’t waste your time on me. You won’t gain anything.”

Tong Yao was furious. “Your subtext is so cryptic. How could anyone possibly understand?”

“Don’t worry. Who is the commander-in-chief this time? Director Luo? Wu Guoqing? Whoever it is, they should know me well and understand what I mean.”

“Hmph, you overestimate yourself, don’t you?” Tong Yao was slightly persuaded, her anger subsiding somewhat. But once her anger cooled down, her stomach began to growl in protest.

“Come, have some shrimp dumplings. I’ll formally apologize to you once again.”

“I’ll forgive you for now. Business is more important.” Tong Yao devoured the shrimp dumplings in one gulp, completely disregarding her so-called ladylike image. “Are you planning to go find that guy in the pig mask for the Boss?”

“Yes,” Zhang Zhiqi nodded vigorously.

“But we don’t have any clues. How can we investigate?” Tong Yao asked curiously. She knew they were no ordinary men, efficient and thorough, leaving no traces. Moreover, they were committing the crime on June 2nd in the “future.” She felt it was simply impossible to begin.

However, Zhang Zhiqi was full of confidence. He smiled and said, “Although this is difficult, it’s not difficult for me. Do you know why I chose this place for breakfast?”

“Can we find clues here?” Tong Yao suddenly perked up. Before Zhang Zhiqi could reply, the door to the private room opened. The visitor, dressed in a suit and smiling broadly, was the floor manager of this place.

“Brother Qi, it’s been ages since I’ve seen you here for morning tea! What brings you here today?” the floor manager greeted Zhang Zhiqi with exaggerated enthusiasm.

“Come, let me introduce you. This is Ah’Wei, the manager here and my buddy. This is Tong Yao, my friend and a criminal police officer.”

“So it’s Officer Tong! I was wondering how this beautiful woman looked so impressive and must be someone special.”

Tong Yao forced a smile. She didn’t like this kind of flattery, but she didn’t know what to say.

“Ah’Wei, I’m here today to ask a favor,” Zhang Zhiqi said, putting his arm around Ah’Wei’s shoulder.

“Brother Qi, please tell me. As long as it’s within my power, I’ll go through fire and water for it.”

“Stop talking nonsense. I don’t want you to go through fire and water. Let me ask you a question. If a friend of mine is planning their anniversary, and let’s say he has secretly booked a restaurant to surprise his wife, and I really want to know where he booked it, can I find out?”

Ah’Wei thought for a moment, perhaps processing the question in his mind, before saying, “If I have the person’s name, phone number, and more detailed personal information, I can try.”

“Oh? Tell me, how are you going to find out?”

“Although there are many restaurants in D City, which one is suitable for it… wedding anniversaries are usually celebrated at Western restaurants. Most people, when choosing a Western restaurant, consult online recommendations and opt for new establishments with good reputations or established establishments. There aren’t many restaurants that truly fit this category.

Zhang Zhiqi nodded in agreement, then followed up with a question: “But there are at least a hundred reputable Western restaurants in the city, right?”

“There are definitely a hundred or so. But after all, we’re all in the same business, so we can still find out by asking each other if someone has made a reservation at the restaurant. It just takes a little more time.”

“Ha, you’re quite clever!” Zhang Zhiqi praised.

Tong Yao, watching Zhang Zhiqi and Ah’Wei’s conversation, marveled. She hadn’t expected Zhang Zhiqi to use this method to conduct his research. It was truly effective and efficient. Ah’Wei definitely was the right person to find.

“Actually, there’s an even simpler way,” Ah’Wei said, glancing cautiously at Tong Yao.

Zhang Zhiqi, sensing Ah’Wei’s concerns, immediately said, “I’ve known her for many years. We’re close friends, so you can be absolutely confident.”

Tong Yao internally smiled bitterly, silently grumbling, “We don’t seem that close yet,” but nodded calmly.

Ah’Wei then continued, “If we could just use the police and check his call logs, wouldn’t we know where he called to make the reservation?”

Zhang Zhiqi and Tong Yao glanced at each other simultaneously.

The police… hadn’t Lu Tianfeng always suspected a mole within the force?

If the masked man and the police mole were in cahoots, all these confusing clues would have a logical explanation.

Seeing Zhang Zhiqi remained silent, Ah’Wei offered a tentative question, “Brother Qi, how about you write your friend’s information for me, and I’ll check it out for you?”

“No thanks. I’ve come up with a better idea.” Zhang Zhiqi patted Ah’Wei’s shoulder again. “But it’s definitely not about abusing police resources for personal gain. Don’t get the wrong idea.”

“Of course, of course. Brother Qi is so smart; he’s bound to have a better idea. How could I possibly be spouting nonsense!” Ah’Wei smiled knowingly.

“Please ring my bill first. I’ll enjoy my tea for a while.”

“Thank you, Brother Qi. I’ll give you a 20% discount… no, 40%! Officer Tong, please come back often!” Ah’Wei bowed repeatedly and respectfully left the private room.

After the door to the private room closed again, Tong Yao finally couldn’t help but ask, “What’s your relationship with this guy? He seems a little too enthusiastic.”

“Nothing much. I just saved his whole family.” Zhang Zhiqi took a sip of tea and said calmly, “It’s a long story. We’ll talk about it someday. For now, let’s deal with the problem at hand.”

Was there really a mole within the police force?

Tong Yao suddenly remembered that her phone had been unusually quiet today. She pulled it out, only to find it had automatically shut down due to a dead battery.

Did she forget to charge it last night? Tong Yao reluctantly put the phone away.

.

June 1st, 9:30 a.m., on the city tour bus.

This was one of D City’s unique tourist routes. The bus was a bright red, vintage double-decker bus. The route was a loop, connecting end to end, passing through many popular tourist attractions and core business districts. There were 24 stops in total, and the full circuit took two to three hours. Passengers could get off the bus at any time or stay on until it stopped at night, circling the city.

The most striking feature of this route was its slow pace. While this might seem unacceptable to rushed commuters, it was actually Lu Tianfeng and Chen Nuolan’s greatest strength.

Because their most pressing task right now was to kill time.

The two of them snuggled up together, sitting in the last row of seats on the upper deck of the double-decker bus, looking like a close couple on a road trip.

But their whispers weren’t the sweet nothings you might imagine; they were serious matters.

“The law of conservation of energy determines the very nature of the universe. Whether it’s time looping or time reversing, it’s impossible to ignore this law and allow it to occur at will.”

“I don’t really understand these scientific theories…” Lu Tianfeng smiled wryly. Chen Nuolan was incredibly serious when it came to scientific theories, and he couldn’t argue with her.

“Simply put, no one can control the reversal of time without restriction. If that were possible, wouldn’t the development of human civilization be completely halted? It would be tantamount to easily destroying the entire world!”

Lu Tianfeng looked at the white-haired elderly man on the side of the road and the baby sleeping in the stroller he was holding and wondered: What would it be like if we were trapped in an endless cycle, the elderly man never aging, and the baby never growing up?

“Does controlling time reversal mean destroying the world?”

“Even if someone could manipulate time, it would require an immense amount of energy to maintain the balance of the universe.” Chen Nuolan looked at Lu Tianfeng worriedly and said, “Feng, you can’t travel through time and space again and again to change history. It could very well lead to irreversible and serious consequences.”

Lu Tianfeng’s arm around Chen Nuolan stiffened for a moment. “Are you trying to dissuade me from trying to reverse time again?”

“Yes,” Chen Nuolan whispered, knowing what that answer meant.

“So the girl Wang Donglin murdered was just going to be left like that? And what about Yongsheng…” Lu Tianfeng was a little agitated, barely able to control his voice.

Chen Nuolan, on the other hand, appeared quite calm. “Feng, do you know that those of us engaged in cutting-edge research often come across inventions that could revolutionize human society, even the world? Cars, airplanes, nuclear energy, the internet… many technologies will revolutionize our lives. In a sense, the most advanced scientists are like gods, influencing the fates of hundreds of millions of people with a single gesture.”

“What are you trying to say?”

“My mentor taught me to always remember that we are all human, not gods. Not to rashly change the world just because you think you can.”

Lu Tianfeng’s mouth twitched. “Nuolan, do you wish I didn’t have the ability to travel through time?”

“Yes, I’d rather you were just an ordinary person.”

“But if I didn’t have that ability—” Lu Tianfeng took a deep breath before finishing his sentence, “you’d be dead long ago.”

“What?”

Lu Tianfeng smiled wryly and recounted the events of his first encounter with Chen Nuolan.

If he weren’t someone who could perceive time loops, he wouldn’t have been able to change the course of the Tianma Jewelry Center robbery, and Chen Nuolan would have been killed by a stray bullet during that incident. Upon learning this for the first time, Chen Nuolan was so shocked she was speechless. She had no idea how to handle the news that she should have died years ago.

“So, you still think I shouldn’t try to change history?”

Chen Nuolan was silent for a long time before sighing softly. “If I had to choose, I’d still prefer you to be an ordinary person, even if that meant I’d die.”

“Why?”

“Because I can imagine your pain and loneliness, and I don’t want you to have to endure it.”

Lu Tianfeng was stunned. He hadn’t expected Chen Nuolan to say such a thing.

He gently held her hand and said, “But as long as you’re here, I think it’s all worth it.”

“Feng, you don’t know the consequences of continuing to rewind time…”

Just then, the double-decker bus pulled up at a stop to pick up and drop off passengers. A moment later, a clatter could be heard from the stairs. Four people, wearing sunglasses and tracksuits, who looked like tourists from out of town, ascended the observation deck. After glancing around, they chose seats in the last row.

Lu Tianfeng and Chen Nuolan’s conversation was temporarily interrupted as two of the four new passengers sat in the row in front of them and two to their right. While it was normal for people to sit anywhere on public transportation, it was somewhat unusual for them to choose to sit near a couple when there were clearly plenty of empty seats.

Even stranger was that none of the four had taken off their sunglasses.

Lu Tianfeng suddenly caught a whiff of a peculiar spice from the passenger in front of him, a scent unique to Southeast Asia.

He immediately remembered where he had smelled this scent before.

On the night of June 2nd, which no longer existed, he had smelled the same aroma on the robber leader, Pig-Head.

The sun was still shining brightly outside the window, but Lu Tianfeng felt as cold as if he had fallen into an ice cellar.

At this moment, a man in the front seat slowly turned around and removed his oversized sunglasses, revealing an unremarkable square face.

“Nice to meet you, Officer Lu, but I’d also like to say, ‘It’s nice to see you again.'”

He was indeed Pig-Head.

“Remember what I said? You underestimate us, and I’ll definitely find you.” The man turned his gaze to Chen Nuolan, his lips curled slightly in a malicious sneer. “Hello, Miss Chen.”

Chen Nuolan frowned. She could sense the visitors’ ill intentions, but she couldn’t guess who they were, so she simply remained silent.

“It’s you,” Lu Tianfeng said in just two words, tightening his grip on Chen Nuolan’s hand.

“It’s us,” the man said, proudly pointing at the two companions sitting to Lu Tianfeng’s right. Guns could be vaguely seen hidden beneath their tracksuits, pointed directly at Lu Tianfeng. “By the way, we’re now acquaintances. You can call me ‘Ah’Yong,’ meaning ‘Perpetual.'”

“How did you know I was here?”

“I’m sorry, but I’m asking the questions now, and you answer them.” Ah’Yong grimaced with a fake smile. “Where did you hide Wang Donglin? Hand him over, and I’ll let you both go.”

“I’m sorry, Wang Donglin escaped a long time ago, and I don’t know where he is now,” Lu Tianfeng said coldly.

“Oh? Really?” Ah’Yong shrugged nonchalantly. “It’s okay. Just go get him.”

“You guys should be pretty capable, right? Why do you have to rely on me to find him? Even the entire city’s police force can’t find Wang Donglin; how do you expect me to?”

“You figure it out. I just want the result—trade Wang Donglin for your woman,” Ah’Yong said as he unzipped his sweatshirt, letting Lu Tianfeng see the gun hidden inside, then zipped it back up. “How long do you need? Is half a day enough?”

“You’re asking too much!” Lu Tianfeng gritted his teeth. But how could he possibly handle four people with four guns on his own? Furthermore, he had to consider the safety of Chen Nuolan and the other passengers. There was nothing he could do.

“It seems half a day is enough for you. Bring Wang Donglin to this place before 6 p.m.,” Ah’Yong muttered to himself, pressing a business card into Lu Tianfeng’s hand. He then chuckled at Chen Nuolan, “Miss Chen, please come with us!”

“Can I refuse?” Chen Nuolan asked calmly.

“You don’t have a choice.” Ah’Yong patted the gun hidden within his shirt. “I’m a ruthless person. I kill without blinking an eye. Your boyfriend witnessed it once, and he can confirm I’m not bragging.”

Chen Nuolan’s palms were sweating, and she could feel Lu Tianfeng’s hands growing colder.

“I’ll get you out. Wait for me,” Lu Tianfeng managed to force out the words.

“Yes, I’ll wait for you.” Chen Nuolan, completely oblivious to the number of thugs watching her, leaned forward and kissed Lu Tianfeng hard on the lips.

A kiss filled with strength and courage.

“I’ll wait for you,” Chen Nuolan repeated, then stood up resolutely.

The double-decker bus was steadily slowing down, and a bus stop was not far ahead.

Lu Tianfeng felt his body begin to fall apart again, his head buzzing as if a bug had crawled into it.

CONTENT END 95

chapters.title: Chapter 96
chapters.content:
June 1st, 10:00 a.m., Hualian Road.

A black commercial vehicle was parked in front of Come BBQ, which had not yet opened. The windows were covered with dark film, making it difficult for passersby to see inside.

“Officer Cheng, I need to use the restroom.” Wang Donglin sat in the back seat, his hands handcuffed to the door handles, leaving him no room to move freely.

Cheng Tuo, sitting in the driver’s seat, said without turning around, “There’s no public restroom nearby. Just bear with it.”

“Brother, it’s only ten o’clock, and I have an 11:00 appointment with Lu Tianfeng. How can I bear it…”

Before he finished speaking, Cheng Tuo tossed an empty mineral water bottle onto the backseat.

“Can you handle it yourself? Do you want me to take off your pants for you?”

Wang Donglin’s lips twitched, and he muttered softly, “It’s okay. I can still bear it.”

“That’s all right…” Cheng Tuo’s phone suddenly vibrated. He looked down and saw the same incoming number he hadn’t wanted to see.

“This is Cheng Tuo; go ahead.”

“Is the problem solved?” Zhou Huansheng’s voice on the other end of the line was emotionless.

“Not yet, but it will be soon.” With Wang Donglin nearby, Cheng Tuo spoke carefully.

“Wang Donglin is in your hands?”

“No such thing…”

Zhou Huansheng immediately interrupted Cheng Tuo: “Cheng Tuo, you’re on Hualian Road now, right?”

Cheng Tuo sat up alertly, his hand instinctively reaching for the holster on his waist.

“You’ve missed your last chance to come clean with the ‘Organization,'” Zhou Huansheng said coldly.

At that moment, Cheng Tuo heard the sound of tires screeching from behind him. He reacted with incredible speed, dropping his phone, releasing the parking brake, and stepping on the accelerator. However, before Cheng Tuo could even leave his parking space, a white van pulled up directly to the right, blocking his path.

Without hesitation, Cheng Tuo turned the steering wheel all the way to the left, floored the accelerator, and with the roar of the engine and the clatter of tires, the car barreled onto the sidewalk.

Fortunately, the sidewalk was sparsely populated, leaving Cheng Tuo ample room to dash along for a bit. Then, aiming for a gap in the road, he yanked the steering wheel hard, drifting the car back onto the roadway. This rash of moves, like a series of stunts, left Wang Donglin in the back seat groaning.

“Captain Cheng, can you drive slower? My butt’s about to break apart.”

Cheng Tuo, without even turning, glanced in the rearview mirror. Seeing the white van still in pursuit, he said calmly, “If they stop us, you’ll be in big trouble.”

“What’s that—ouch!” Wang Donglin’s head banged against the car window as Cheng Tuo unexpectedly made another sharp right turn.

The van behind him, though less agile, managed to keep up, though the gap between them grew ever wider. If Cheng Tuo could pull off a few more of these sharp turns, he might be able to escape his pursuers.

“Bang! Bang! Bang!”

The people in the van recklessly opened fire on Cheng Tuo’s car.

“Hold on!” Cheng Tuo shouted, steering the car in an S-shaped pattern like a snake.

“Captain Cheng, your driving skills… are truly impressive.” Wang Donglin bent down, gripping the door handle tightly, a mixture of laughter and tears.

As he spoke, the car suddenly swerved.

“Are these people crazy?” Cheng Tuo saw no sign of giving up. Just as he was about to call for backup, the wail of police sirens reached his ears.

Cheng Tuo couldn’t help but feel wary. This support had arrived too quickly. Either a colleague happened to be on duty nearby, or this was a pre-planned operation.

In the rearview mirror, he could see a blue sedan approaching at breakneck speed, its roof flashing with warning lights. It wasn’t a patrol car on routine duty; it was probably a plainclothes officer from the criminal investigation team.

The white van finally realized the situation was amiss and abruptly turned left at the fork in the road, discontinuing its pursuit of Cheng Tuo. However, the blue sedan following behind it didn’t pursue the fugitive who had been openly firing in the city. Instead, it headed straight for Cheng Tuo’s car.

Clearly, the other party was also targeting Wang Donglin. “Why are you so popular?” Cheng Tuo teased Wang Donglin.

“I don’t know.” Wang Donglin finally sat up straight.

“Let’s get rid of them first.” Cheng Tuo hadn’t finished speaking when he stepped heavily on the accelerator.

.

June 1st, 10:05 a.m., University Town Road.

Just now on Hualian Road, Yan Jin and Dai Chunhua had been observing Cheng Tuo from a distance. The moment the white van appeared, they immediately became alert. When Cheng Tuo forced his way onto the sidewalk, Yan Jin acted decisively.

“Should we call for backup?” Dai Chunhua asked sternly.

“Let’s see what’s going on.” Yan Jin’s car followed the white van closely, his hazard lights activated.

They hadn’t gone far before Cheng Tuo’s black commercial vehicle and the white van parted ways at a fork in the road. Yan Jin hesitated for a brief moment, and Dai Chunhua gave him a timely reminder: “Chase Cheng Tuo and Wang Donglin.”

Yan Jin turned the steering wheel to the right and pushed the accelerator as far as it would go, but he was still getting further and further away from Cheng Tuo’s car.

“Captain Cheng, why is he driving so recklessly?” Yan Jin felt he was losing control of his car, feeling a bit overwhelmed.

“Cheng Tuo is probably the best driver in our police force. Did you know he participated in amateur car races in college?” Dai Chunhua said, clutching the seatbelt tightly, his face pale.

“I really didn’t know that…”

As he spoke, Cheng Tuo’s car suddenly veered off onto a side street. Yan Jin was caught off guard and passed him, forcing him to frantically turn around.

By the time he re-entered the side street, Cheng Tuo’s car had already vanished into the distance.

“Damn it!” Yan Jin slammed the steering wheel furiously.

“Don’t panic. Log in to the intranet and check his car’s location.”

Yan Jin immediately pulled out his phone and expertly logged into the internal system. However, Cheng Tuo’s car had its GPS turned off, leaving only their current location.

“He turned off the GPS.”

“So he’s deliberately trying to avoid the police,” Dai Chunhua pondered. “Captain Yan, should we report this?”

“Something as serious as a street gunfight must be reported!”

“I mean, should we disclose Cheng Tuo’s story?”

Yan Jin was speechless. He was in a dilemma. If he told the truth about Cheng Tuo, his superiors would probably hold them accountable for not reporting and acting without authorization. But if he continued to conceal Cheng Tuo’s secrets, the situation would spiral out of control. Furthermore, he couldn’t tell whether Cheng Tuo was loyal or treacherous. If Wang Donglin escaped with Cheng Tuo’s help, he couldn’t bear the responsibility.

Dai Chunhua seemed to have recovered his breath, and his complexion was back to normal. He slowly said, “Let’s not overthink things. Keep it simple and direct.”

“I have a simple and direct solution—call Captain Cheng.”

“I agree.” The two exchanged glances and nodded knowingly.

But the result disappointed Yan Jin greatly. After dialing Cheng Tuo’s cellphone, he only heard a notification: “The number you dialed is powered off. Please try again later.”

“Powered off…” Yan Jin was only halfway through his words when a strange number suddenly appeared on his phone.

.

June 1st, 10:20 a.m., Hualian Road, near Come BBQ.

Lu Tianfeng, wearing a baseball cap, hurried to Hualian Road and immediately noticed something was amiss. This usually quiet street was now teeming with people. Upon further inquiry, he discovered that a gunfight had just occurred, and the police were currently collecting evidence. The gossipy crowd, who had only heard of gunfights in movies and TV shows, had surrounded the scene in three layers.

“I saw it! Those people were lunatics. They were in a car, firing machine guns into the crowd!” an old man spat excitedly.

“Nonsense! Where are those machine guns? They were using sniper rifles!” another woman sternly retorted.

“That’s not a sniper rifle; that’s a machine gun!” the old man retorted, unconvinced.

Lu Tianfeng felt a mixture of anger and amusement. These two people were clearly talking nonsense, yet they both believed they were right. Perhaps it was just human nature to fall into this kind of self-righteous presumption.

Self-righteousness. Presumption.

These two words suddenly echoed faintly in Lu Tianfeng’s ears. He felt a faint spark of inspiration strike his mind, but when he tried to capture it, it vanished in an instant.

Something felt off, but he couldn’t place it for the moment.

Lu Tianfeng took a deep breath and walked towards the nearby Come BBQ restaurant. The police were all around, greatly reducing the certainty of his encounter with Wang Donglin. However, there was a benefit: the crowd made it easier for them to conceal their whereabouts.

But under these circumstances, would Wang Donglin really dare to show up?

But no matter what, he had to find Wang Donglin; otherwise, Chen Nuolan’s life would be in danger.

Lu Tianfeng instinctively pulled out his phone and opened the “Come BBQ” page on the review platform. He scrolled down and refreshed the comments section.

Under Wang Donglin’s comment, there was a new reply, updated eight minutes ago.

“I’ve been to this place before, and the food isn’t great. It’s not as good as the new kebab place in Huapu Center on the Second Ring Road in University Town! P.S. I know some people will say I’m a scumbag, but I’m definitely not!”

Lu Tianfeng casually checked the electronic map, but there was no place called “Huapu Center” on it. He searched again on a search engine and discovered that the so-called “Huapu Center” was actually a high-rise building under construction. However, due to the developer’s bankruptcy, construction had been suspended, and the property was currently being auctioned off, awaiting the next buyer.

It was impossible for a kebab restaurant to exist in a place like that.

So this must have been the contact information Wang Donglin had left for him.

But there was another thing about this message that caught Lu Tianfeng’s attention: a glaring typo—”托” (tuō) was written as “拓” (tuò). If someone accidentally pressed the wrong key while using a mobile phone input method, “托” (tuō) would usually be mistaken for the commonly used homophones “拖” (tuō) or “脱” (tuō). “拓” (tuò) was a less frequently used character, making it less likely to be mistyped.

If Lu Tianfeng’s reasoning was correct, Wang Donglin had deliberately inserted the character. His immediate reaction to seeing “拓” (tuò) was his boss, Cheng Tuo.

Could it be that Wang Donglin had been controlled by Cheng Tuo? Was this a trap?

However, Lu Tianfeng quickly dismissed this theory. If Cheng Tuo had used Wang Donglin to set up a trap, he would have meticulously checked every message Wang Donglin sent, and there was no way he would have missed such an obvious clue.

It seemed that only one possibility remained, and no matter how incredible it was, it was the truth.

Wang Donglin and Cheng Tuo were together. They had joined forces.

CONTENT END 96

chapters.title: Chapter 97
chapters.content:
June 1st, 10:30 a.m., corner café.

Zhang Zhiqi and Tong Yao sat in a booth in the far corner, a laptop in front of them, its screen displaying a rapidly scrolling pile of data.

Tong Yao glanced at the screen and sighed, “Even I can’t understand what you’re looking at.”

Zhang Zhiqi took a sip of his coffee and said calmly, “It’s normal for an outsider to not understand.”

“I’m not an outsider. I’m one of the best intelligence analysts in the police force,” Tong Yao said, her eyes widening in anger.

“There are always people better than you. I’m the best intelligence analyst in the country, bar none,” Zhang Zhiqi said, gesturing to Tong Yao’s phone charging on the table. “This is the first time I’ve seen someone working in intelligence work whose life’s work tool runs out of battery.”

“This…” Tong Yao was speechless. She still couldn’t figure out what was wrong with her phone. It had been plugged in for a while, but the screen still showed 1% battery and wouldn’t turn on.

“Do you want me to check it out for you?”

“No need to bother you,” Tong Yao flatly refused. “Let’s get down to business.”

“Business? We can’t talk about that until Yan Jin shows up!” Zhang Zhiqi folded his arms and said confidently, “He should be here soon.”

“Are you sure Captain Yan will come?” Tong Yao knew Yan Jin as a meticulous and impartial man. It was hard to imagine Zhang Zhiqi convincing him to come with just a phone call and a few vague words.

“Ninety percent chance. People are always curious. He’ll definitely want to know why I contacted him out of the blue. And I think he’s probably in trouble and needs help.”

Looking at Zhang Zhiqi’s confident and triumphant expression, Tong Yao couldn’t help but sneer. “Haha, you’re too blindly confident. Don’t you know…”

However, Tong Yao swallowed the last half of her words because she had already seen Yan Jin push open the door and enter the coffee shop, followed by Dai Chunhua, who was limping. Zhang Zhiqi waved to Yan Jin naturally, as if greeting an old friend.

“Captain Yan, I’m here.”

“Hello.” Yan Jin stepped forward, glancing at Tong Yao without showing the slightest bit of surprise. Then he said to Zhang Zhiqi, “Are you ‘Hound’ Zhang Zhiqi?”

“Yes.”

“Why did you call me suddenly?”

Zhang Zhiqi smiled faintly and didn’t answer immediately. Instead, he raised his eyebrows at Tong Yao, suggesting, “See, I guessed right, didn’t I?” Tong Yao, feeling both amused and helpless, looked away, pretending not to notice.

“Captain Yan, I want to make a deal with you.”

Yan Jin’s face turned cold, and he said sternly, “Deal? Do you know how dangerous Wang Donglin is? Do you know how many people he killed in less than 24 hours of his escape? If you have information, share it as soon as possible. If not, don’t waste the police’s precious time.”

Zhang Zhiqi tapped the coffee cup in front of him and said, “I don’t have any information, but if you can tell me the firsthand information the police have, perhaps I can help you find Wang Donglin’s whereabouts.”

Yan Jin wondered if there was something wrong with his ears. “Are you trying to tease me? Why are you asking me for confidential police investigation information?”

“Because of my ability! Captain Yan, don’t you want to know why I would reach out to you, and at such a coincidental time?”

Yan Jin and Dai Chunhua exchanged glances. This was the question they had been discussing on the way to the meetup, but they couldn’t figure it out.

Zhang Zhiqi confidently rotated his laptop screen 180 degrees so Yan Jin and Dai Chunhua could see the information displayed.

“This is the data analysis system I developed. The data on this screen contains information about all vehicles involved in the pursuit and investigation of Wang Donglin’s escape, including registered users and real-time location information. All data is updated every ten seconds. Too much data to handle? Exactly, so intelligent noise reduction and data analysis are needed… Judging from your expressions, you two don’t understand what I’m saying, right? Never mind. I’ll just state my conclusion. Of all the vehicles involved in the pursuit of Wang Donglin this morning, only two behaved erratically. Car A was initially tracking and monitoring Car B. Then Car B suddenly accelerated, with Car A following closely behind. Two minutes later, Car B forcibly disconnected from its GPS data. What does this mean?”

The frantic scrolling of data on the screen, coupled with Zhang Zhiqi’s ramblings, stunned Yan Jin and Dai Chunhua. Neither knew what to say, so they could only smile wryly.

This was exactly the reaction Zhang Zhiqi had hoped for, so he tapped a few times on the keyboard, bringing up another window. “You should know that this system isn’t isolated. This is an internal police emergency report. At 10:05 a.m., a shooting occurred on Hualian Road. The time of the incident perfectly matches the sudden acceleration of the two cars in pursuit. Clearly, the occupants of Cars A and B can provide firsthand information from the scene. Looking at the vehicle registration forms, Car A is registered to Yan Jin, and Car B to Cheng Tuo. However, I can’t get through to Captain Cheng, so I can only contact you, Captain Yan.”

Yan Jin had been a police officer for many years, possessing extensive experience and strong case-handling skills, but he had always adhered to traditional investigative procedures. He didn’t care about the technical details of high-tech gadgets and had never seen such a dazzling intelligent analysis system. He even doubted whether Zhang Zhiqi was talking nonsense. As for the older Dai Chunhua, his brows furrowed in confusion.

Yan Jin had to ask Tong Yao, “Is this system he’s created reliable?”

“The power of this system is beyond my knowledge, but theoretically, it works,” Tong Yao replied honestly.

“So, information that seems useless to Captain Yan can become powerful data support for my system. And what might take you hours or even days to find, I can get in just minutes.” Zhang Zhiqi turned the computer screen back to face him. “The choice is yours now. Trust me and share the clues, or let’s part ways.”

“Old Dai, what do you think?” Yan Jin hesitated, so he had to ask Dai Chunhua beside him.

Dai Chunhua’s eyes glazed over. Yan Jin asked again, his voice rising. He finally awoke, sighing, “The world is changing so fast! My old bones are completely useless!”

Although Dai Chunhua didn’t say it directly, it was self-evident that he felt he couldn’t compete with Zhang Zhiqi.

Since that was the case, Yan Jin decided to reveal all the information he had. After all, there’s strength in numbers, and Zhang Zhiqi’s nickname “Hound” was well-deserved.

“Okay, here’s what happened…”

“Dong, dong, dong—”

A short, pleasant melody played; Tong Yao’s phone had finally recovered from its low battery and was ready to start.

But Zhang Zhiqi had snatched up her phone before Tong Yao did. After glancing at the status bar, his usually calm expression suddenly shifted to one of awe.

“Oh no!” Zhang Zhiqi slapped his thigh hard and exclaimed.

.

June 1st, 10:45 a.m., Huapu Center construction site.

According to the original design, this would be a rare integrated commercial and office building in the University Town area. But the developer’s bankruptcy might prevent it from ever being finished.

Lu Tianfeng walked around the wall and noticed that both the front and rear entrances to the construction site were equipped with security booths. However, perhaps due to a lack of funds to pay them, there wasn’t a single guard inside. There were already several gaps in the wall, allowing adults to easily slip through. It seemed this unfinished building might be a haven for the local homeless.

Was it Wang Donglin or Cheng Tuo who chose this meeting place?

He decided not to hesitate and bent down to crawl through the wall. Inside, the ground was muddy and dotted with several chaotic footsteps. This hole appeared to have been used by at least ten persons today.

Lu Tianfeng took a moment to identify the two freshest footprints in the mud. These tracks, unlike the others, led not toward the building itself but to the underground parking lot, likely belonging to Wang Donglin and Cheng Tuo. He followed them until he entered the parking lot.

It was pitch black, completely dark, and the air was filled with the stench of decay characteristic of a sealed space. He wondered what small animal had died there.

There was a shallow layer of water on the ground, likely a mark left by last night’s heavy rain.

Just as Lu Tianfeng hesitated, unsure whether to go further, a flicker of light appeared in the darkness ahead.

Short, long, short, short, short.

This was a special signal in Morse code, meaning “wait.”

Lu Tianfeng strode forward impatiently, no longer having any reservations. No matter who the other person was or what their purpose was in inviting him to meet, he was unconcerned.

Now, his only concern was Chen Nuolan’s safety. After turning a corner in the darkness, he saw light again. Deep within the parking lot, there lay a square patio, a rare spot bathed in sunlight, even covered in lush green grass.

Wang Donglin crouched on a collapsed concrete pillar, his hands handcuffed, but his expression remained relaxed. Seeing Lu Tianfeng appear, he grinned as a greeting. Cheng Tuo, with a sullen expression, stood at the other end of the pillar, staring coldly at Lu Tianfeng. From their positions and the expressions on their faces, it was hard to tell if they were friend or foe.

“Ah’Feng, you’re finally here.” Cheng Tuo’s tone was a bit cold.

“Captain Cheng, why are you here?” Lu Tianfeng resisted the urge to rush forward and slap Wang Donglin, speaking with great effort.

“My mission is to bring you two back to the police station, but I want to give you a chance to explain why you hijacked the prison van.” Cheng Tuo placed his hand on the pistol at his waist. “I don’t want to point a gun at my brother. Don’t force me.”

“That’s a long story…”

“No, it’s very simple.” Wang Donglin laughed sharply, forcing the conversation to stop. “To sum it up, Captain Lu and I are the ones the ‘Organization’ wants to target, while Captain Cheng is the one working for the ‘Organization.'”

“What?” Lu Tianfeng shuddered, his entire body trembling as memories of the past suddenly flooded back into his mind.

While everyone in the police station was speculating about the identity of Lu Tianfeng’s “mysterious informant,” Cheng Tuo never questioned the details, instead giving Lu Tianfeng complete trust and support.

When personnel transfers occurred between departments, it was Cheng Tuo who proactively suggested that the newly recruited Huang Xuanxuan be assigned to Lu Tianfeng’s training program, and Huang Xuanxuan was ultimately confirmed to be a member of the ‘Organization.’

When Lu Tianfeng’s investigation into the Feng Teng Gene case reached a stalemate, it was Cheng Tuo who advised him not to rely solely on informants and to trust his own judgment.

If all this were interpreted as Cheng Tuo already knowing Lu Tianfeng’s abilities, then it made sense.

Cheng Tuo’s expression changed, seemingly in anger, but more like irritation. He shouted, “Shut up!”

“What did I say wrong? Please correct me, Captain Cheng.” Wang Donglin’s smile widened. Lu Tianfeng finally understood: this was Wang Donglin’s true purpose.

He intended to stir up conflict between Lu Tianfeng and Cheng Tuo, then find an opportunity to reap the benefits.

Cheng Tuo took a deep breath and said, “Initially, I was just concerned about Ah’Feng’s informant. Then someone claiming to be from the ‘Organization’ came to me, wanting to negotiate a deal. I thought it was a little ironic. I’m an honest police officer, and they’re a mysterious, illegal ‘Organization.’ Why would they want to deal with me? But they said they wouldn’t let me do anything illegal, yet they would tell me the background of Ah’Feng’s informant. I thought it was fine, so I agreed.”

“Once you agree, there’s no way to back out, right?” It seems Wang Donglin had experienced something similar.

Cheng Tuo paused. “That’s right. I’m just an ordinary person, and I really can’t stand up to the ‘Organization.’ And they kept their word. They didn’t ask me to do anything extreme. They just asked me to reveal details about the cases Ah’Feng was handling.”

Lu Tianfeng smiled bitterly. “Why did they go to so much trouble to monitor me?”

“I don’t know. They don’t trust me. They just tell me some ‘secrets’ from time to time, letting me know how powerful the ‘Organization’ is, so they can put invisible pressure on me.” Cheng Tuo shook his head and sighed. “Who would have thought that superpowers really existed in this world?”

At this moment, Lu Tianfeng noticed that Wang Donglin, who was listening nearby, looked confused and surprised, as if he had heard something he didn’t know.

“Wait.” Lu Tianfeng stopped Cheng Tuo and turned to Wang Donglin. “Wang Donglin, tell me everything you know about the ‘Organization’ first.”

“Why do you have to make me speak first?” Wang Donglin dropped his playful smile.

“Because we’re police officers, and you’re a suspect,” Lu Tianfeng said bluntly.

The word “we” made Cheng Tuo’s eyes light up.

Because Lu Tianfeng had calmly stated his position.

CONTENT END 97

chapters.title: Chapter 98
chapters.content:
Wang Donglin’s Memories (V)

Moli’s body was found three days later, and the police came to visit soon after. Of course, that night’s class reunion was the last time she appeared in public, and I was her ex-boyfriend, having been to the same karaoke bar that night. So naturally, I couldn’t escape the police’s questioning.

But I’m sure I acted quite naturally. I even confessed to the police that I had run into Moli in the karaoke bar that night. We chatted for several minutes, and then I returned home. As for where she went next, I have no idea.

“What did you talk about that night?” The interrogating officer stared at me suspiciously.

I replied calmly, “It was just small talk, rambling. I don’t really remember.”

“What did you think the atmosphere was like?”

“It was awkward, but I tried to be polite. We were together before, and the breakup was a bit unpleasant, so you know.” I spread my hands, expressing my frustration.

“Do you hate her?” The officer bluntly cut to the point without any tact.

“It’s been so many years, I don’t have any feelings anymore!”

In all these years, I hadn’t contacted Moli at all, and I never mentioned her name to my friends. No one in the world knew how I truly felt about her.

The police officer quickly scribbled something in his notebook and asked, “So, after leaving the KTV that night, did you go straight home?”

“Yes, my girlfriend… my fiancée, Wang Xiaomian, can vouch for that. I arrived home at 9:30 p.m.”

“And then what?”

“And then?” I feigned confusion and replied, “Then I stayed home the entire time and didn’t go out again.”

I knew he would confirm the veracity of my testimony with Xiaomian. And though Xiaomian might be shy, she would definitely reveal every detail of our sexual encounter that night to completely clear me of suspicion.

As my fiancée, Xiaomian’s testimony was questionable, but it should be more than enough to withstand the police’s sweeping investigation.

As long as no new evidence emerged and there were no traces of me on the body, I wouldn’t be the focus of the police investigation. I handled the interrogation very well.

Fortunately for society as a whole, criminals with mental fortitude like mine were rare. Most people would crumble under the police’s psychological pressure and confess.

However, the day after my police questioning, an email from a stranger suddenly arrived in my inbox.

“Did you have a good time getting together with your ex-girlfriend?”

I immediately deleted the email and emptied my recycle bin, but my hands were sweating.

Who sent the email?

Five minutes later, I received a second email from the same sender, also with a single sentence.

“It felt good to kill your ex-girlfriend, didn’t it?”

This time, I didn’t even have the courage to delete the email. I sat blankly at my computer, waiting for the third email.

I knew the sender would contact me again.

Five minutes later, this time, the email contained a picture attachment, clearly marking the location where I’d dumped the body. This location was quite a distance from where the body was last found, making it top-secret information unknown even to the police investigators.

And yet, all my secrets were in their possession.

My fingers trembled uncontrollably, and I told myself over and over again not to reply to these emails. This was most likely a trap set by the police to lure me into revealing my true identity.

But if they already knew where I’d dumped the body, why didn’t they just arrest me instead of playing dirty?

I calmed down a bit and realized that the sender couldn’t be the police.

So who could it be?

The fourth email gave me the answer.

“Mr. Wang Donglin, you now have two options: first, ignore these emails, in which case we will send all the evidence to the police in an anonymous letter, and your crimes will be made public. Second, cooperate with us and solve a small problem for us. See the attached document for details. We will give you a week to make a decision. After a week, if we find that the problem we need your help with has not been resolved, we will immediately contact the police.”

The attachment was a large compressed file. I waited anxiously for it to download. When I opened it, I found the detailed profile of a woman, including her resume, family information, academic credentials, and even a large collection of her photos and personal blog posts.

Was she the “problem” that needed to be solved?

I noticed another document in the attachment. It simply read: “This girl should be your type, right? Take her out and hand over the pink keychain she carries to us as proof of mission success. Leave the keychain in locker 139 at the D City University swimming pool within a week. Take the locker key with you, and we’ll find a way to retrieve it. Good luck.”

I gasped. Was the other party really forcing me to kill someone?

I carefully examined the girl’s profile. Her name was Lin Jiarui, 27 years old. She had a master’s degree from a prestigious university and was currently working in drug research and development at a local biomedical research institute. She didn’t seem like someone who would forge deep grudges with others. So who would go to such lengths to kill her?

I waited another ten minutes, but still no new emails arrived. It looked like the other party wouldn’t be giving me any further instructions. So I stood up and paced anxiously around my study. The one-week deadline was incredibly tight. I had no time to properly strategize my action plan. Besides, Xiaomian wasn’t expected to be back home this weekend. I couldn’t just bring my target home and then strike like I had done the last few times.

The more I thought about it, the more anxious I became. I even felt like the police were about to knock on my door.

“Tap, tap, tap—” Then, there was a knock, followed by Xiaomian’s voice. “Honey, would you like some fruit?”

“No, thank you!” I quickly turned off the monitor, fearing Xiaomian would walk in and see my screen.

“Oh, are you busy?”

“Yes, something happened.”

“Then I won’t bother you.” Fortunately, she was a woman who knew her limits.

After Xiaomian’s footsteps faded, I breathed a sigh of relief. My back was already drenched in sweat. To preserve my happy life, I had no choice but to kill Lin Jiarui, who had nothing to do with me.

I spent two days meticulously compiling and studying every bit of information on Lin Jiarui, thoroughly understanding her lifestyle and habits. I knew her favorite colors, foods, clothes, hangouts, and topics of interest. Based on this information, I devised a plan, albeit imperfect, that had a reasonable chance of success.

I decided to take advantage of her Saturday afternoon shopping trip and arrange a chance encounter. I’d then use topics that appealed to her interests to attract her and then try to arrange a dinner date. Of course, I also considered the possibility of the hookup failing. If that happened, I planned to follow her and find an opportunity to assault her. To that end, I even bought a stun gun and a police baton.

However, things went even more smoothly than I’d imagined. Perhaps I have a special attraction to women. When I accidentally bumped into Lin Jiarui in a bourgeois bookstore, she picked up a book I’d dropped and was surprised to discover it was a new release by her favorite author. The glint in her eye confirmed that this attempt was a sure thing. Long unrequited, Lin Jiarui was susceptible to my sweet talk. Two hours after we first met, she agreed to dinner. When she blushed and shyly climbed into the passenger seat of my car, she certainly had no idea its ultimate destination would be her death.

I abandoned my usual cautious method and opted for a more adventurous approach. As we passed a deserted road, I announced that the check engine light was on and I needed to stop and check. Lin Jiarui foolishly followed me out to investigate. Taking advantage of her unpreparedness, I activated the stun gun to its highest setting and rammed it into her waist.

“Ouch!” Her body convulsed violently before collapsing in exhaustion. To be absolutely sure, I placed the stun gun on her neck and activated it again.

Lin Jiarui screamed strangely and completely lost consciousness. I carried her to the back seat and quickly drove to the hotel where I had booked a room under a false name. The hotel had direct access from the underground garage to the guest rooms, and they were recently undergoing a surveillance system upgrade, so many cameras were temporarily unavailable, making it an ideal location for committing a crime.

I supported the unconscious Lin Jiarui, and with much effort, I finally brought her to the room. In the elevator, I passed a couple who looked at me strangely. I held my composure, smiled apologetically, and said, “Sorry, my wife is drunk in broad daylight.”

Perhaps because I appeared so calm, the couple actually believed my nonsense and didn’t suspect me. This made me believe that goddess luck was on my side again today.

As I brought Lin Jiarui into the room and laid her on the bed, she suddenly woke up, but it was too late. In this perfectly soundproofed room, no one would know what I did to her.

She cried and struggled desperately, but ultimately, she was no match for my strength. I pinned her to the bed, and after a few slaps, she surrendered.

“I agree to your request, but you can’t hurt me…” she said tremblingly.

“Any request?” I teased her.

“Yes… yes…”

“Don’t worry, I won’t hurt you. Just go into the bathroom and take a shower,” I whispered, nibbling her ear.

This was probably the cleanest, most thorough shower she’d ever received.

But I had lost all memory of that period.

Half an hour later, I came to myself. Looking at Lin Jiarui, her eyes wide open, sleeping at the bottom of the bathtub, my body inexplicably aroused. Unexpectedly, this forced act of murder brought me a greater sense of satisfaction than ever before.

According to my original plan, I would return home after the murder, wait until midnight when no one was around, and then return to my hotel room and secretly remove the body through the basement garage. But that night, perhaps because I was too nervous, I sweated profusely. On the way home, the air conditioning gave me the first signs of a cold. I returned home groggily, took the cold medicine and warm water that Xiaomian handed me, swallowed the pills in one gulp, and fell asleep, not waking up until noon the next day.

After waking up, I found my cold symptoms were mostly gone. Unfortunately, I couldn’t get back to the hotel to deal with the aftermath. I quickly searched my pockets and luckily remembered to bring the keychain requested in the mysterious email. I figured the hotel staff would discover the body by 2 or 3 p.m. at the latest, and the keychain would become crucial evidence. So I immediately ran to the swimming pool and locked the keychain in locker 139 as instructed. I took the locker key and threw it in the trash.

I had completed all my tasks; the rest was up to fate.

The police knew what happened next. Although the hotel’s surveillance system was under maintenance, some cameras were still functioning. Two days later, you arrested me and brought me to trial. However, no one could have predicted that the results of the psychiatric evaluation would save my life.

But then again, I’d rather be shot than spend my life as a lunatic in a psychiatric hospital.

CONTENT END 98

chapters.title: Chapter 99
chapters.content:
June 1st, 11:15 a.m., Huapu Center construction site, underground parking lot.

Wang Donglin sighed deeply, finally finishing his story. Uncharacteristically, he lowered his head. As he recounted, his tone alternated between calm and indifferent, and then his eyes flashed with utter madness and joy, leaving Lu Tianfeng trembling with fear.

Every time Wang Donglin revealed his demonic face, Lu Tianfeng fought hard to resist the urge to punch him.

“Have you finished?” Lu Tianfeng asked calmly, catching his breath.

“Oh, I let one thing slip. The night after I killed someone, I received my final email. It contained only seven words: ‘Thank you on behalf of the Organization.'”

“And then you deleted it?”

“Yes,” Wang Donglin nodded.

“No, you’re hiding something.” Cheng Tuo, who had been silent the entire time, suddenly interrupted coldly. “Wang Donglin, you just suggested to me that we join forces to fight the ‘Organization,’ but after hearing your story, I don’t know what your basis is for saying that. You don’t even know what the ‘Organization’ is!”

Wang Donglin gave a dry laugh, shrugged, and didn’t answer.

“If you’re just stalling for time…”

“Captain Cheng, I guess Wang Donglin just doesn’t want to reveal his cards so easily.” Lu Tianfeng took a step forward. He was beginning to understand Wang Donglin’s style.

Wang Donglin viewed life as a chess game and everyone as an opponent. Therefore, he always had a backhand in mind, speaking only to the point, leaving room for maneuver.

But Lu Tianfeng was determined to push him into a corner.

“Wang Donglin, you should remember why I told you I wanted to save you.”

Wang Donglin’s mouth twitched. “I remember.”

“If you don’t show some sincerity in cooperating, then let’s go back to the police station. I’ll accept the investigation and punishment from my superiors, and you’ll return to the psychiatric hospital and await the next assassination attempt by the ‘Organization.'”

Wang Donglin looked up and met Lu Tianfeng’s gaze, knowing he meant what he said.

“I… I think I’ve figured out why the ‘Organization’ sent someone to kill me…” he stammered.

“Why?”

“It’s likely they discovered I copied data from a USB drive—the keychain Lin Jiarui carries is actually a mini USB drive.”

“Really?”

“Where’s the data?”

Wang Donglin’s words triggered a furious reaction from Lu Tianfeng and Cheng Tuo. They both wanted to rush forward, pin Wang Donglin down, pry open his mouth, and dig out every last bit of information.

“Captain Lu, you’re right. This is my trump card, and I absolutely cannot play it lightly.” Wang Donglin glanced at Lu Tianfeng, then turned to Cheng Tuo. “Now it’s your turn to show your sincerity.”

“What do you want?” Cheng Tuo demanded sharply.

“Freedom.” Wang Donglin looked up at the bright blue sky above. “I don’t want to go to jail, and I don’t want to go to a psychiatric hospital.”

“You’ve killed so many, and you still want freedom?” Cheng Tuo sarcastically asked.

“If you can’t fulfill my wish, then this is the end. We will all perish together. Your career, your family, your future… everything you have.”

Wang Donglin grinned, his eyes darting between Lu Tianfeng and Cheng Tuo, trying to discern which of the two men was more easily swayed and who could truly be his friend.

Lu Tianfeng glanced at Cheng Tuo, meeting his sharp gaze. In truth, he had a vulnerability unknown to the other two present: Chen Nuolan was still in the hands of the criminals, and he couldn’t just hand Wang Donglin over to the police.

What was Cheng Tuo thinking? Would he break completely with the ‘Organization,’ or would he follow its orders and kill Wang Donglin?

There was a more risky and tempting option. Lu Tianfeng could even choose to “kill” Cheng Tuo right then and there, then exchange Wang Donglin for Chen Nuolan. During the exchange, he could force Ah’Yong to rewind time again, thus completely erasing everything that had happened in the past two days.

This was probably the most ideal outcome.

However, Cheng Tuo had clearly considered everything carefully. He drew his pistol, pointed it steadily at Wang Donglin, and silently adjusted his stance, staying as close to Wang Donglin as possible and away from Lu Tianfeng, eliminating the possibility of Lu Tianfeng rushing forward to grab the gun.

“Wang Donglin, hand over the data copy!”

“What if I refuse?”

“Then you will be shot here for resisting arrest.” Cheng Tuo aimed his gun at Wang Donglin’s crown.

“Captain Lu, is this against the rules?” Wang Donglin deliberately posed the question to Lu Tianfeng.

“Lu Tianfeng is also a fugitive now,” Cheng Tuo answered before Lu Tianfeng could speak.

The implication was that even if Cheng Tuo shot them here, he’d have a strong enough excuse to report to his superiors.

“Captain Cheng…” Lu Tianfeng tried to persuade him, but he didn’t know what to say.

A burst of hearty laughter suddenly came from above the three people’s heads, scaring them so much that they all looked up at the same time.

“Haha, we finally found you!”

Zhang Zhiqi’s face appeared at the edge of the skylight above, followed by Tong Yao.

.

Half an hour ago, in a street corner café.

After looking at Tong Yao’s phone, Zhang Zhiqi’s expression changed. He nervously pulled out a portable toolbox and prepared to dismantle the phone.

“Wait, what are you trying to do?” Tong Yao quickly shielded her phone.

“Your phone has been hacked, and it’s been compromised at the hardware level.”

“What?” Tong Yao’s eyes widened in disbelief. After all, she was the police station’s technical expert, and with Yan Jin and Dai Chunhua present, it would be truly embarrassing if her phone was hacked.

“It’s not your fault; it’s just the enemy’s cunning.” Zhang Zhiqi took advantage of Tong Yao’s daze to remove the back of the phone and remove the battery, and soon the circuit board appeared.

Tong Yao could only silently pray that Zhang Zhiqi could not only disassemble the phone but also put it back together.

“Look, this is the hacker program chip.” Zhang Zhiqi quickly found the problem and picked up a small chip, only a few millimeters long, with tweezers.

“Really?” Tong Yao smiled wryly.

“Someone used this chip to control your phone and even used your account to log into the police intranet and get all the latest information.”

“So impressive?” Yan Jin, confused with his lack of technical knowledge, couldn’t help but exclaim at this.

“Awesome? Just average, I guess. This program must have a fatal bug, causing the process to freeze, going into an infinite loop, and constantly draining the phone’s resources and battery, which is why it’s so revealing. According to our hacker code, resorting to hardware modification is already considered inferior…”

“You’re going through so much trouble. Are you trying to show off your skills?” Tong Yao angrily exposed Zhang Zhiqi’s trick.

“Of course,” Zhang Zhiqi said brazenly. “I’ll research this chip later. Right now, the most important thing is to find Wang Donglin. Captain Yan, stop keeping me in suspense and tell me!”

Yan Jin was at a loss for words. Where had he been keeping things a secret? Wasn’t Zhang Zhiqi just busy fiddling with his phone? But business was important. He quickly and concisely recounted how they’d discovered Cheng Tuo might have controlled Wang Donglin but hadn’t reported it in time, how they’d been monitoring and tracking him, and how they’d unexpectedly encountered a gunfight.

“So, in the end, Cheng Tuo relied on his driving skills to shake you off?”

“Yes,” Yan Jin nodded.

“Even if you missed the intersection and turned back, the delay wouldn’t have been more than twenty seconds. How far could the car have gotten?” Zhang Zhiqi asked, puzzled.

“Because we didn’t request support from headquarters, we couldn’t execute interception measures.” Yan Jin felt a little ashamed, thinking this was a golden opportunity he missed while he hesitated.

“No, you don’t understand me,” Zhang Zhiqi waved his hands. “At the time, Cheng Tuo didn’t know who you were, only that you were police officers. Therefore, when he formulated his escape strategy, he must have assumed that you had requested reinforcements from headquarters.”

Seeing Yan Jin’s expression still blank, Zhang Zhiqi simply pulled up a map of the area near the university town on his computer. Then, with a clattering keyboard, a dot of camera icons appeared on the map.

“Look, this is where Cheng Tuo got away from you, right? If I were him, I’d know running for my life is useless. Every traffic camera would record his escape. So, the better option is to find a secluded spot nearby, try to avoid being captured, and then find another way to escape.”

Yan Jin slapped the table, suddenly realizing, “So he’s still nearby!”

“Write down the license plate number for me. I’ll search the surveillance camera data.”

By this point, Yan Jin was already extremely convinced of Zhang Zhiqi’s abilities and quickly gave him the license plate number. Zhang Zhiqi searched for it and quickly drew a red circle on the map.

“Cheng Tuo’s car only appeared in the surveillance cameras at two intersections, so the area he could have hidden in is easy to deduce: it’s within this red circle.”

“Is that easy to deduce? How did you calculate it?” Tong Yao asked, unable to resist her curiosity.

“Trade secret,” Zhang Zhiqi blinked.

Although Yan Jin was hesitant to mobilize headquarters for a large-scale search due to a lack of evidence, he immediately dispatched all available personnel to the University Town area to conduct a search within the area Zhang Zhiqi had outlined. Meanwhile, Zhang Zhiqi, saying he wanted to help find someone, pulled Tong Yao out. Tong Yao was reluctant. After all, she was a police officer. How could she follow this private investigator around instead of following the main force? Unfortunately, Zhang Zhiqi had dismantled her phone into pieces, and she had to rely on him to put it back together, so she could only follow him silently.

Unexpectedly, as soon as they left the coffee shop, Zhang Zhiqi leaned over and whispered, “We have to find Cheng Tuo and Wang Donglin before Yan Jin and the others do.”

“Do you know where they are?”

“Of course. If all I can do is draw circles on a map, why would I charge so much?” Zhang Zhiqi said proudly. “There’s only one perfect hiding spot within that area. I’m sure Yan Jin and Dai Chunhua will figure it out soon.”

“Where is it?” Tong Yao felt like a clueless elementary school student in front of Zhang Zhiqi.

“This city’s famous unfinished development, Huapu Center.”

.

June 1st, 11:30 a.m., Huapu Center construction site

Three people underground, two above ground, and a delicate and complex situation formed between these five individuals.

Logically, with two active police officers and one suspended at the scene, all three shared the responsibility of apprehending Wang Donglin. However, Lu Tianfeng was preoccupied with Chen Nuolan, Cheng Tuo was in a dilemma, and Tong Yao was completely unaware of what had transpired in the underground parking lot. For a moment, none of the three dared to suggest taking Wang Donglin away.

As for Wang Donglin, handcuffed and unable to move freely, he appeared to be resigned to his fate, at the mercy of his prey. But in reality, the data he had hidden was his most powerful trump card. He was confident that neither Lu Tianfeng nor Cheng Tuo would easily hand him over to anyone else. However, the situation on the chessboard was already very passive; he could only wait for his opponent to make a mistake; he absolutely could not take the initiative.

Zhang Zhiqi, on the other hand, had the least psychological burden. To him, Wang Donglin was nothing more than a 300,000 yuan reward; whoever brought Wang Donglin to the police station would have a chance of collecting the reward. But he didn’t dare speak easily, his mind racing. He had already sensed the problem, knowing that a single misstep would lead to a complete loss.

The biggest problem was Chen Nuolan’s unexplained absence, coupled with Lu Tianfeng’s distraught expression. Zhang Zhiqi suspected something serious had happened.

Zhang Zhiqi already considered Lu Tianfeng a friend, and if a friend was in trouble, he couldn’t just sit back and watch.

The awkward silence lasted for a while, until Cheng Tuo took the initiative to break the deadlock: “Wang Donglin, come with me back to the police station. Tong Yao, you will assist me in escorting the prisoner. All other non-essential personnel may disperse.”

Before Tong Yao could reply, Lu Tianfeng said firmly, “No!”

“Why?” Cheng Tuo’s voice was tinged with anger.

“Because Wang Donglin lied.” Lu Tianfeng extended his hand, pointing directly at Wang Donglin’s nose. “He also concealed some very crucial information. This could kill us all.”

Wang Donglin was stunned for a moment, then gave a wry smile.

Lu Tianfeng was indeed an opponent to be reckoned with. The situation in this chess game was truly unpredictable.

CONTENT END 99

chapters.title: Chapter 100
chapters.content:
June 1st, 12:00 p.m., Unknown Location.

After Chen Nuolan detected a slight scent, the blindfold covering her eyes was taken off. When her vision returned, she was instantly taken aback.

After being forcibly abducted by Ah’Yong and his men, she was quickly blindfolded. It felt like she had been bouncing around in a car, and she had no idea how far she had traveled. She kept wondering where she would end up: an abandoned building, a remote old warehouse, or a pitch-black basement?
