Already, Chen Nuolan had braced herself for the worst. But as she opened her eyes, she was shocked to see that she was in a lavishly furnished and cozy home with gentle light, clean air, and the sound of songbirds resonating outside.

This must be some sort of upscale villa complex outside of D City.

“Miss Chen, welcome.” A middle-aged man in his forties, dressed in a neat suit, stood up from a white leather sofa and extended his hands warmly to Chen Nuolan.

“Hello,” Chen Nuolan replied calmly but did not acknowledge the offered hand.

The middle-aged man, unperturbed by the gesture, naturally withdrew his hand and gestured to Ah’Yong and his group, who had escorted Chen Nuolan. Within seconds, Chen Nuolan and he were the only ones left in the room.

“Ah’Yong and his group are unruly individuals. If they’ve offended you, please forgive me, Miss Chen.” The middle-aged man picked up the purple clay teapot on the table and poured Chen Nuolan a cup of hot tea.

Chen Nuolan’s mouth was genuinely dry, so she took the cup and drank without hesitation. After all, if the other party wanted to kill her, they could have killed her eight or ten times over. The tea was also top-quality, fresh, and fragrant.

“This is good tea,” Chen Nuolan said calmly, setting down the cup.

“Miss Chen, please take a seat. My name is Situ Kang. It’s nice to meet you, and I hope we can become friends.”

Chen Nuolan was puzzled, but she spoke harshly, “Mr. Situ, do you like to use violence to make friends?”

“This is purely a helpless move. If we don’t use some tactics, I’m afraid Miss Chen won’t even pay attention to us!” Situ Kang smiled faintly and spread his hands. “Your boyfriend, Lu Tianfeng, wouldn’t let us get close to you either.”

“No need to beat around the bush. Just tell me. What exactly do you want?”

Situ Kang smiled again. “I have a genetic technology project and would like to invite Miss Chen to be our technical advisor.”

“Sorry, I’m not interested,” Chen Nuolan flatly declined.

“As a scientist, you shouldn’t make hasty decisions!” Situ Kang poured another cup of tea and handed it to Chen Nuolan. “This project is similar to RAN-X!”

Chen Nuolan’s heart trembled, and she almost lost her grip on the cup. RAN-X was Feng Teng Gene’s top secret. Even Chen Nuolan only had a vague understanding of it. How could this man know about it?

Besides, Lu Tianfeng had warned her that she should feign ignorance about everything regarding RAN-X.

“I don’t understand what you’re talking about,” Chen Nuolan replied abruptly, even to herself, feeling overly contrived and unable to conceal her inner panic.

Situ Kang continued on his own: “Three years ago, genetics expert Ray Costa published a bold hypothesis about using genetic technology to enhance human immunity, dubbing it the ‘Costa Hypothesis.’ This paper sparked a wave of discussion within the field, but researchers around the world soon discovered a fatal flaw in the paper, completely disproving the ‘Costa Hypothesis.’ The ideas in the paper were quickly forgotten by the academic community—”

Chen Nuolan became increasingly surprised as she listened. She had studied Ray Costa’s paper and even discussed some of its worthy points with her boss, Luo Tengfeng. But she had never expected Situ Kang to be so well-versed in academic research. He was definitely not just any robber.

“However, there are still some persistent researchers who delve deeply into the various possibilities behind the ‘Costa Hypothesis’ and derive their own new theories. You should know that D City is at the forefront of domestic genetic technology research, and two people in this city have achieved significant breakthroughs in their research on the ‘Costa Hypothesis.'”

Chen Nuolan remained silent, but she had already guessed that one of them was the deceased Luo Tengfeng.

“In addition to Luo Tengfeng, there was another young female researcher, Lin Jiarui, who took a different approach and proposed a modified version of the ‘Costa Hypothesis.’ However, her limited experience in the industry and her influence didn’t attract much attention. But the most terrifying thing is that all of these researchers met tragic deaths: Ray Costa died in a car accident in the United States, Luo Tengfeng was killed in the Feng Teng Gene case, and Lin Jiarui died at the hands of the ‘Souvenir Killer,’ Wang Donglin.”

“Dead?” Chen Nuolan suddenly realized that Lu Tianfeng’s warnings and safeguards were not just illusions.

“Someone is killing the people researching this technology. They don’t want this technology, which could significantly improve human immunity, to be released.” Situ Kang crossed his arms over his chest. “Miss Chen, do you know why they’re doing this?”

Chen Nuolan remained silent, but she knew the unspoken rules of the industry. When a new technology promised to cheaply and safely treat a stubborn disease, it often impacted the profitability of many vested interests, leading to multiple pressures from all sides. Some new technologies were delayed for years or even decades from reaching the public eye, and in the worst-case scenario, they might disappear from the historical stage entirely.

Even so, biotech specialists had never stopped their research and development, believing that one day, a cost-effective treatment would overcome numerous obstacles and successfully save patients from financial hardship.

And Situ Kang’s insinuation that someone was cruelly preventing the release of a new technology through murder was arguably crossing Chen Nuolan’s limit.

But a voice in Chen Nuolan’s heart reminded her that she didn’t know Situ Kang’s background, and his words might not be reliable.

“Since this is such a dangerous job, Mr. Situ, please seek help from someone else. I’m sorry I can’t help you,” Chen Nuolan said coldly.

“My offer is kind, but I hope Miss Chen will reconsider it.” Despite being repeatedly rejected, Situ Kang remained calm and composed. “Or, you can review the project materials before making a decision.”

Chen Nuolan knew this was a dangerous bait, so she didn’t respond.

“However, we still have a small problem.” Situ Kang’s serious expression flashed for the first time. “Lin Jiarui’s research data isn’t in our possession. It’s been hidden by Wang Donglin. Therefore, I eagerly hope Captain Lu can bring us good news as soon as possible.”

.

On June 1st, at noon, on the Ring Road, in a dilapidated van that wobbled slowly as it ran.

Zhang Zhiqi was driving, Lu Tianfeng took the passenger seat, and Cheng Tuo and Tong Yao sat in the back, flanking Wang Donglin, keeping a close eye on the dangerous serial killer.

Half an hour ago, when Lu Tianfeng had shared his shocking theory, everyone was stunned, each with countless questions. However, Zhang Zhiqi remained the calmest, suggesting an immediate relocation, or else Yan Jin and the others would soon find them.

So, keeping a close eye on each other, the five of them left the Huapu Center construction site together. Zhang Zhiqi was resourceful; in just ten minutes, he’d managed to procure a moving van from nowhere. The van was shabby and low-profile, ensuring it wouldn’t attract attention.

“Have we gotten far enough?” Cheng Tuo said, a little impatiently. “Let’s stop out front and have a chat.”

“Captain Cheng, stop here? I’m afraid the police will be here soon…”

“Stop talking nonsense!” Cheng Tuo interrupted Zhang Zhiqi. “Don’t try to act so hard in front of me! Stop right now!”

“Alright.” Zhang Zhiqi stopped arguing and, seeing an open-air parking lot ahead, drove in.

As soon as the car stopped, Cheng Tuo eagerly asked Wang Donglin, “What else are you hiding from us? Tell me!”

“I’ve told you everything I need to. Believe it or not,” Wang Donglin said with a slow and confident pace.

“Ah’Feng, why do you think Wang Donglin is lying?” Cheng Tuo turned to Lu Tianfeng.

Lu Tianfeng stared at Wang Donglin for a moment before speaking, “Because there’s something clearly inexplicable in Wang Donglin’s story.”

“Really?”

“He said the ‘Organization’ only encouraged him to kill through a few emails, and that there was no other contact. But that doesn’t explain why, after escaping, he’d managed to rush to Moyun Town and meet the bartender, Judy, at the bar.”

A flicker of hesitation crossed Wang Donglin’s eyes.

Lu Tianfeng continued, “Apparently, he thought Judy could help him escape, and there was an undisclosed deal between him and the ‘Organization.’ I believe the ‘Organization’ gave him some kind of promise or guarantee.”

Cheng Tuo frowned and asked, “But then Judy was murdered. Based on the clues at the scene, the perpetrator was most likely Wang Donglin.”

Wang Donglin snorted noncommittally.

Lu Tianfeng said, “This means the agreement between Wang Donglin and the ‘Organization’ has been broken. Judy wasn’t Wang Donglin’s savior but his ‘killer.’ The ‘Organization’ intended to silence him.”

“Silence?” Tong Yao exclaimed.

“So, what exactly was the agreement between you and the ‘Organization’?” Lu Tianfeng stared at Wang Donglin, demanding.

Wang Donglin pursed his lips, refusing to speak.

“Since you won’t tell me, let me guess. This promise from the ‘Organization’ was enough to make you willingly take the risk of murder, even choosing a completely unfamiliar environment to commit the crime, ultimately leading to your arrest after the crime was exposed. What kind of promise could have led someone like you, usually calm and rational, to make such an irrational choice?”

“A promise to save his life,” Zhang Zhiqi suddenly interrupted.

“That’s right. The ‘Organization’ told Wang Donglin that if he didn’t cooperate, they would report his crimes, and if the evidence proved irrefutable, he would surely be executed. But if he did cooperate, the ‘Organization’ would find a way to exonerate him. Even if the court sentenced him to death, they could still arrange a prison break to rescue him…”

Tong Yao asked, puzzled, “But why did Wang Donglin trust the ‘Organization’s’ assurances? What if he was imprisoned and the ‘Organization’ didn’t rescue him?”

Lu Tianfeng held up three fingers and said, “There are three reasons: first, someone else has evidence against Wang Donglin, so he had no choice but to accept the ‘Organization’s’ harsh terms; second, if he were reported, he would be doomed, so he might as well take a gamble and bet that the ‘Organization’ would actually send someone to rescue him; and third, he bought himself ‘insurance’ by making a copy of the data the ‘Organization’ wanted. If anything unexpected happened, this data could be used as a bargaining chip.”

Wang Donglin’s expression shifted, as if he was trying hard to control his emotions.

“When the prison van hijacking happened yesterday morning, I noticed that Wang Donglin was very calm at first. He probably thought those mercenaries were sent by the ‘Organization’ to rescue him. But soon, he realized that those people were out to kill him, so he began to doubt the ‘Organization.’ Last night, when he went to Moyun Town to meet Judy, he was wary. Once the situation was not right, he immediately turned against her. The final result was that he killed Judy and continued to escape on his own. At this time, he knew very well that if he was isolated and helpless, he would definitely not be able to escape the double forces of the police and the ‘Organization.’ He’s been searching the internet for a long time, so he posted provocative messages on Weibo and left me a message in code, hoping to collaborate with me.”

At this moment, Cheng Tuo said coldly, “It’s a pity I got there first.”

“Wang Donglin, you only have one option now: confess everything to us—what the real deal was between you and the ‘Organization,’ what promises they made you, and everything else you know. Tell us everything.”

Wang Donglin remained silent, like a mute. The atmosphere in the car suddenly dropped to freezing point.

“Looks like we can’t get anything out of him. We’ll just have to take him back to the police station,” Cheng Tuo said, a little annoyed.

“I want to talk to you privately,” Wang Donglin suddenly said to Lu Tianfeng.

“I won’t allow it,” Cheng Tuo immediately refused.

“Forget it, then. Let’s all wait for death together!” Wang Donglin chuckled coldly, closed his eyes, and leaned back heavily in the seat.

“Captain Cheng…” Lu Tianfeng looked at Cheng Tuo, wanting to say something but stopping himself.

Once the most trusted partner in each other’s eyes, they now understood that their initial “trust” was based only on calculation and chance. Even more troubling for Lu Tianfeng was the question of whether Cheng Tuo, standing before him, truly still stood on the side of the police.

“Captain Cheng, let Captain Lu give it a try!” Tong Yao carefully avoided calling him “Boss” to prevent Cheng Tuo from misunderstanding.

“Let’s try it!” Zhang Zhiqi agreed.

Cheng Tuo pondered for a moment, then slowly nodded. “Let’s give it a try. The three of us will get out of the car, remove the keys, and keep Wang Donglin’s handcuffs out of the way. I’ll stand by and watch from a distance. If there’s any movement inside the car, I’ll shoot immediately.”

“Don’t worry, I’ll keep an eye on him,” Lu Tianfeng said. Cheng Tuo didn’t answer, not sure whether he was reassured or not by Lu Tianfeng. He sighed softly and got out of the car with Tong Yao and Zhang Zhiqi.

Finally, Lu Tianfeng and Wang Donglin were the only ones left in the van.

CONTENT END 100

chapters.title: Chapter 101
chapters.content:
Wang Donglin’s Confession

Yes, you’re smart enough to see the hidden meaning in my story.

With my cautious nature, I wouldn’t just kill someone for a few inexplicable emails. Some people, simply reading newspaper stories like “So-and-so was caught by police after a string of murders,” will arbitrarily assume that killing is easy and that the police are fools.

In reality, it’s incredibly difficult to kill someone without being caught.

So when I received that series of strange emails, I simply deleted them completely and emptied my Recycle Bin, not even wanting to look at them.

However, one email with several picture attachments caught my eye.

Although the pictures were a bit blurry and looked like they’d been taken from a distance, each one was shocking.

Moli and I met at the karaoke bar, left together, and walked side by side through the alley… until we both entered my house, and in the wee hours of the morning, I loaded her body into my car, and finally, there were the photos of me dumping it by the lake. These photos formed a complete and reliable chain of evidence that would definitely convict me.

Why was this so? It seemed the other party knew I was going to kill that night, so they were lying in wait nearby, filming the entire process.

But I only truly resolved to kill Moli after I successfully tricked her into leaving that night. No one, not even me, could have known my plan in advance.

Unless the other person isn’t human but a demon.

Looking at such an email, I was completely devastated. My hands trembled, and I didn’t even have the courage to hit the delete button.

What should I do?

Just then, my phone rang. It was an unfamiliar number. For some reason, I was startled and jumped to my feet. I had a feeling it wasn’t a harassing telemarketing call but a voyeur.

“Hello…”

“Teacher Wang, our photos are pretty good, aren’t they?” The caller used a voice changer, and his tone was strangely distorted.

“Who are you? What do you want?” I screamed uncontrollably.

“It’s simple. I want to make a deal.”

“How much…?” I asked, feeling unsure. I had a feeling the person who had taken these photos was no ordinary person. They might not be after money at all.

“Money? That’s too vulgar! Teacher Wang, if these photos get out, you’ll be dead!”

My legs gave way, and I sat down helplessly. “Whatever you want, I’ll give you…”

“A life for a life—it’s a fair exchange. Don’t hang up; check your email first.”

There was a new email with information about Lin Jiarui.

“You mean I should kill this girl?”

“Yes, killing her will save your own life.”

“Give me some time to prepare…”

“There’s no time. You must kill her within a week, or I’ll hand over all the photos to the police.”

“Wait…” I was filled with despair, a bitter taste in my mouth. “I don’t have time to prepare. If I act rashly like this, I’ll probably be caught by the police.”

“So?”

“Since I can’t escape justice, why would I kill another person and aggravate my crime?” Although I knew I had no right to bargain, I did so anyway.

“Oh, that’s an easy problem to solve. I can guarantee your safety,” the other party said casually.

“Guarantee? On what basis?”

“Then, please remember the following instructions carefully. Every step must be taken with care…”

The mysterious person on the other end of the phone asked me to select the personal belongings of the two victims and bury them in two different locations. You wouldn’t have guessed it, but the media dubbed me the “souvenir killer,” believing I buried a “souvenir” with each murder. But in reality, those “souvenirs” were fabricated afterward. The night I killed Jiang Suyu, she was wearing a black butterfly hairpin. I disposed of it when I dumped the body, but I happened to remember the brand, so I bought a new one and buried it in the park. The other “souvenir” was something I had deliberately saved. When I was dating Moli, I gave her a worthless silver necklace as a token of our love. So, after killing her, I kept her necklace as a memento. Unexpectedly, this impulsive decision ultimately proved to be a huge boon.

They asked me to bury two “souvenirs,” not three or even one. Looking back, I think the main purpose was probably to make the keychain missing from the fourth victim, Lin Jiarui, less conspicuous. But at the time, I didn’t think much of that. I was solely focused on following their instructions, hoping to save my life.

Of course, I considered the possibility of deception, that after I’d killed someone, they wouldn’t care about my life or death. But I wasn’t stupid. I made a copy of the data on Lin Jiarui’s keychain USB drive, figuring that if anything went wrong, I’d confess to the police and hand over the data for investigation.

However, the ‘Organization’ was truly powerful. On my first night in detention, a small note appeared on my bed: Relax, we’ll get you out.

Relax?

We’ll see.

The ‘Organization’ told me I could admit to the murders—I couldn’t deny them, after all—but I wasn’t to answer any questions about the “souvenirs.”

Interestingly, aside from the note that appeared on the first day, the power of the ‘Organization’ seemed to have vanished. I received no further instructions from them. While awaiting trial, I couldn’t sleep every night. The days were filled with endless interrogations, trials, psychiatric evaluations, psychological analyses, and case replays, leaving me exhausted and with a splitting headache.

Sometimes, I even forgot who I was, as if I had just woken from a dream. When I opened my eyes, I saw that the sky was dark and it was already evening.

One day, in my daze, I received news I wasn’t sure whether to see it as good or bad: the psychiatric evaluation results indicated that I would be sent to a psychiatric hospital instead of prison. That same night, a mysterious note appeared by my bed for the second time. It read: “Be prepared to regain your freedom.”

I suspected the ‘Organization’ would take action midway between my transfer from the detention center to the psychiatric hospital, but I didn’t expect you, a ruthless Cheng Yaojin1, to appear midway and snatch me away. At the time, I was in a state of confusion, not knowing whether to laugh or cry. I didn’t dare admit that I was in cahoots with the van hijackers, so I had to follow you on the run. However, as we escaped, I gradually realized that something was amiss.

I only knew someone was trying to get rid of me, but I didn’t know who I could trust. Everyone, including you, Lu Tianfeng, might have ulterior motives. In the end, I chose to escape on my own, traveling to Moyun Town to find Judy, the contact I’d agreed to with the ‘Organization.’ As expected, Judy tried to silence me, so I had no choice but to preemptively eliminate her. After careful consideration, I still believed you were the most suitable partner.

Why?

Because I see that you possessed a certain ability, one that mirrored the ‘Organization’—your ability to disrupt their planned prison van hijacking proved you have the power to stand up to them head-on.

I believed the data I held holds special meaning for you, unlike anyone else, so a deal between us was the most cost-effective. We would each get what we need, and we would maximize our profits.

What do I want now?

As I said earlier, I want freedom. I want to leave this city, even this country. I just want to escape this mess unscathed, regardless of the ‘Organization,’ the police, or the case. I want to flee to a small country in Southeast Asia and start a new life.

Yu Yongsheng? Who? Oh, the man who was relentlessly pursuing me…

I didn’t want to kill him. I just wanted to escape as quickly as possible. In my panic, I ran into Judy, who told me to hide under the eaves while she dealt with the pursuers. I never expected that woman to be so ruthless. In an instant—alas, after witnessing that scene, I no longer trusted anyone from the ‘Organization.’ They are all devils, lunatics, not a single sane person.

Why did I kill someone on the run?

Did I… kill someone?

Yes, the woman in the red car… No, I didn’t want to kill her at all. I just wanted to trick her into taking me to Moyun Town… But in the car, the demon suddenly appeared, and then…

The woman was also at fault. Not only was she not afraid at all, but she also actively threw herself into the demon’s arms. I shouted at her to leave, but she seemed completely oblivious to my words and only laughed even more wildly.

I was powerless, watching the demon push her into the icy river, watching the desperate splash of water rise before finally returning to calm.

Lu Tianfeng, let’s work together. I’ll give you all the data the ‘Organization’ is trying so hard to obtain, and you’ll help me leave D City and flee far away.

To show my sincerity, I can give you the data first. How about that?

You… there’s no reason to refuse, right?

CONTENT END 101

chapters.title: Chapter 102
chapters.content:
June 1st, 12:20 p.m., suburban area, open-air parking lot.

After listening to Wang Donglin’s confession, Lu Tianfeng fell into deep thought.

Not far away, Cheng Tuo and Tong Yao stood on either side, watching the van with vigilant eyes. Zhang Zhiqi had vanished, nowhere to be seen.

“Have you considered, Captain Lu?” Wang Donglin waited impatiently.

“Even if I agreed, we can’t leave,” Lu Tianfeng said, evasively.

Wang Donglin couldn’t help but smile. “You’re kidding! The steering wheel is right in your hands. Just a touch of the accelerator and the car would speed away. How would Cheng Tuo react in time? I don’t believe he would open fire without hesitation.”

“Zhang Zhiqi took the car keys!”

“You know, a car has at least two keys. Before Zhang Zhiqi got out, he put something in the doorway storage rack. What is it?” Wang Donglin winked slyly.

Lu Tianfeng leaned slightly to the side, stretched out his arm, and touched the storage rack. His expression suddenly changed.

“Spare key?”

“Yes, this is the opportunity he created specifically for you.”

Lu Tianfeng glanced at Cheng Tuo and estimated the distance between him and the van: about twenty meters. Once the van started, even if Cheng Tuo immediately drew his gun, aimed, and fired, it would take two or three seconds, not to mention that he might not be able to react immediately.

Just a few seconds, and the van would be gone in a cloud of dust.

This might be his best chance to take Wang Donglin away. Thinking of this, Lu Tianfeng subconsciously clenched the key in his hand.

“Don’t hesitate. This opportunity cannot be missed.” Wang Donglin continued to fan the flames.

Lu Tianfeng’s mouth twitched, but he finally took a deep breath and said, “Hold on tight.”

“It’s okay. I’ve already experienced Cheng Tuo’s driving skills.”

“Then you’re in luck. You can compare mine.” As Lu Tianfeng spoke, he inserted the key in a lightning-fast motion, twisted it, released the parking brake, and stepped on the accelerator, all in one smooth movement.

The minivan was rather old, after all. It paused as it accelerated, and the engine seemed almost to stall. Fortunately, after a brief, strange noise, the vehicle rushed out like a wild horse. Wang Donglin, in the back seat, lost his grip and slammed his head against the car door.

Cheng Tuo’s reaction was indeed incredibly fast, drawing his pistol in less than a second, but at the moment he was about to fire, he hesitated.

In a flash, the van swerved around a corner and sped towards the parking lot exit.

Cheng Tuo ultimately couldn’t pull the trigger. With a long sigh, he lowered his gun and watched Lu Tianfeng drive away.

“Captain Cheng…” Tong Yao stepped forward and whispered.

Cheng Tuo shook his head and was about to say something when Zhang Zhiqi appeared, wearing a Bluetooth headset and a mysterious smile.

“How’s it going?” Cheng Tuo asked Zhang Zhiqi.

“As expected, Wang Donglin confessed everything to Lu Tianfeng, and they’re on their way to retrieve the confidential data.”

“I just hope Ah’Feng truly understands your plan and doesn’t mess around!”

“Don’t worry, he’ll understand.” Zhang Zhiqi patted his chest confidently.

Tong Yao was already stunned by Lu Tianfeng’s sudden and forceful abduction of Wang Donglin. Unexpectedly, Cheng Tuo and Zhang Zhiqi not only ignored it but also spoke in riddles she couldn’t understand, leaving her even more bewildered.

“What are you talking about?” Tong Yao asked.

“It’s Zhang Zhiqi’s plan. Let him explain.” Cheng Tuo raised his chin.

“It’s simple. I simply used your disassembled phone and the spare car key. I placed them both in the storage rack by the door, and deliberately let Wang Donglin notice me putting the key there.”

“Huh?” Tong Yao still didn’t understand.

“Wang Donglin is a suspicious person, always calculating every move. After seeing my actions, he’ll undoubtedly invent all sorts of stories, endlessly speculating on my reasons. Of course, no matter what he thinks, one conclusion is obvious: I’m trying to help him escape.”

Tong Yao finally understood. It turned out that Zhang Zhiqi had set a trap for Wang Donglin to fall into.

“Next, Wang Donglin will do everything he can to incite Lu Tianfeng to drive away and remind him to find the key hidden by the door. In the storage rack, Lu Tianfeng will find not only the spare key but also a disassembled phone, its circuit board exposed and half its casing missing, yet it’s still active.” Zhang Zhiqi pointed to his earpiece; he’d heard every word of the conversation in the car. “Lu Tianfeng still hasn’t hung up, proving he’s cooperating with my plan. We can track their car using the phone location.”

Tong Yao smiled wryly and said, “So you used my phone to spy!”

“Recycling… no, making the most of it, isn’t that great!”

“I’m truly impressed by you,” Tong Yao exclaimed. What truly amazed her wasn’t the trick of using half of the phone for eavesdropping, but the fact that Zhang Zhiqi had managed to convince Cheng Tuo to cooperate with this stunt without her noticing.

Otherwise, with Cheng Tuo’s marksmanship and reflexes, how could he have missed the target in time?

“Let’s get down to business. Where are they going now?” Cheng Tuo asked.

“The destination isn’t far. They’re heading back to University Town, heading to D City University.”

“Could it be that Wang Donglin hid something at home?” Cheng Tuo was puzzled. After Wang Donglin’s arrest, his home had been thoroughly searched by the police, and his computer had been thoroughly inspected by the Technical Forensics Center. If he had hidden any storage device or encrypted directory, it would have been discovered long ago.

.

So, where else could Wang Donglin have hidden the data?

June 1st, 12:40 p.m., D City University, back door.

As soon as the van stopped, Wang Donglin immediately opened the back door and jumped out. He dove into a trash can on the side of the road and vomited.

Lu Tianfeng frowned and said softly, “The bumps are because of the car’s suspension, not my driving skills.”

Wang Donglin bent over, finally recovering his composure. He wiped his lips and forced a smile. “Yes, it’s definitely the car’s fault.”

“You didn’t hide it at home? The police are watching your house.”

“No, how could I dare leave it at home? The data is in the work-study office of the Student Affairs Office, on the hard drive of a public computer.”

“Public computer?” Lu Tianfeng was surprised. He hadn’t expected Wang Donglin to keep something so important on a public computer where it could be discovered at any moment.

Wang Donglin let out a smug look. “Even you wouldn’t have thought of that, would you?”

“Weren’t you worried about the public computers malfunctioning and needing a system reinstall, overwriting the data?”

“I did worry about that, but the solution is simple—I’ve kept a copy on each of the five public computers in the office.”

“What if all the computers need to be upgraded?”

“Don’t I know how much funding the work-study office has? The computers were just upgraded last year, so don’t expect to see another upgrade for another three to five years.”

Lu Tianfeng laughed heartily. Wang Donglin’s solution, though crude and simple, was remarkably effective. The data files on public computers were already disorganized, so even if there were hidden directories and files, no one would care. Furthermore, the police would thoroughly investigate his personal computer, but they couldn’t possibly check every computer in the office.

“So we just walk in brazenly and copy the data?”

“Of course, you’ll also need to know the name and password of the hidden directory… Captain Lu, I’ve demonstrated my sincerity. Now it’s your turn to show some support, right?”

“What do you want?”

“Let me go.” Wang Donglin raised his still-cuffed hands. “Go get the data now, and I’ll disappear. We’ll be even.”

Lu Tianfeng uncuffed Wang Donglin without a word.

“Tell me the name of the hidden directory and the password.”

“On drive D, under the Program Files directory, there’s a hidden folder called ‘QQDAT’. There’s a compressed file inside. The password to decompress it is ‘wdl2018impossible99’.”

“Thank you for coming up with such a complex password.” Lu Tianfeng, out of caution, wrote the password down on his phone’s notepad and handed it to Wang Donglin.

After confirming the password, Wang Donglin rubbed his red wrist and said pitifully, “Captain Lu, this car’s already been exposed. You won’t be driving it again, will you? Can you lend it to me for a while?”

“It’s okay. I didn’t rent this car anyway.” Lu Tianfeng took out the car key and gently tossed it to Wang Donglin.

The moment Wang Donglin reached out to take it, he realized something was wrong.

The car key wasn’t tossed to him, but high over his head and behind him.

The other man took the key steadily.

“Want to borrow the car? Then you should have borrowed it from me!”

Wang Donglin looked back, his face pale.

The car key was in Zhang Zhiqi’s hand, with Cheng Tuo and Tong Yao standing on either side.

He’d been tricked. Wang Donglin tried to force a smile to dispel the fear and despair in his heart, but after several attempts, he couldn’t.

If this were a game of chess, then he’d already been checkmated by his opponent.

.

June 1st, 12:50 p.m., D City University, Student Affairs Office, Work-Study Program Office.

Because it was noon, the office was empty except for a young female student, slumped over her computer desk, asleep. She didn’t even look up when she heard Lu Tianfeng’s footsteps. She must have been used to the constant flow of people coming in and out of the office.

If the people in the ‘Organization’ knew Wang Donglin had hidden their top-secret data in a place like this and had even left a copy on every computer, they’d probably be furious.

Lu Tianfeng found a random chair, sat down, turned on the computer, and quickly found the hidden folder Wang Donglin had mentioned. To be safe, after copying the data, Lu Tianfeng also deleted the hidden folder.

Lu Tianfeng also disposed of the hidden files on the other four public computers one by one. Now, the USB drive he had with him was the only remaining copy of the data.

Lu Tianfeng hid the USB drive and was about to leave when a middle-aged man wearing glasses, who looked like a teacher, pushed open the office door. He was surprised to see Lu Tianfeng’s unfamiliar face.

“Who are you?” the middle-aged man shouted.

“Oh, sorry, wrong door.” Lu Tianfeng had already completed his mission, so he naturally wanted to avoid further trouble and made a random excuse to slip away.

“Wait a minute, this is the Student Affairs Office. How could you have walked into the wrong door?” The middle-aged man grabbed Lu Tianfeng tightly and shouted, “Are you a thief? Someone, come!”

The sleeping female student was awakened by this, and looked up at Lu Tianfeng with a bewildered look.

“Quick, call the police! We’ve caught a thief!”

The female student picked up her phone and began dialing.

Lu Tianfeng groaned inwardly, but if he really asked them to call the police, things would be very difficult.

“Wait, I’m the police. I’m here to carry out my mission,” Lu Tianfeng said quickly.

“Police? I don’t believe it. Where’s your ID?”

“I don’t have any ID, but I’m Lu Tianfeng from the City Criminal Police Brigade. I was on TV a while ago for solving a major case. You can search online; you might even find my photo.”

“Lu Tianfeng?” the middle-aged man repeated his name.

“That’s right, the road, the sky, the peaks…”

“Very good, so you’ve already got what Wang Donglin hid?” A gleam suddenly flashed in the man’s eyes, and a terrifying aura emanated from his body.

Before Lu Tianfeng could react, the female student had already slammed into his back and thrust the stun gun into his waist. A sharp pain shot straight to his forehead.

“You…” Lu Tianfeng’s vision spun, and his body slid uncontrollably, finally landing on the floor. “Who… is it…”

“Thank you for finding the data for us.” The man patted Lu Tianfeng’s shoulder, then searched his pockets, finding the USB drive.

“No…” Lu Tianfeng desperately tried to stand up, reaching out to grab the man’s arm.

Another electric shock hit him from the back of his neck, and his vision went black, and he lost consciousness.

In the last second before he passed out, he thought of Chen Nuolan.

“I’ll wait for you.”

CONTENT END 102

chapters.title: Chapter 103
chapters.content:
June 1st, 1:00 p.m., outside the back gate of D City University.

Wang Donglin, as if drained of all his strength, slumped in the back seat of the van, his expression vacant and silent. Cheng Tuo guarded the door, while Tong Yao and Zhang Zhiqi stood on the other side. The three of them had Wang Donglin firmly under their watch. Now, even if he possessed extraordinary abilities, he wouldn’t be able to escape.

“I’ll go check on Captain Lu,” Zhang Zhiqi said to Tong Yao, his hands in his pockets.

“It’s best not to run around,” Tong Yao objected.

“I’m free anyway.” Zhang Zhiqi raised his hand, waved to Cheng Tuo, and turned to head for the Student Affairs Office. Although he appeared calm and composed, he was actually a little anxious.

Because the current situation was a bit too peaceful.

The police were issuing a citywide warrant for Wang Donglin, and Yan Jin and Dai Chunhua had obtained his exclusive analysis, indicating the search wasn’t far behind. The ‘Organization,’ having failed in their previous hijacking and murder attempts, would undoubtedly continue their pursuit. The gang Lu Tianfeng encountered before time travel was likely not part of the ‘Organization,’ but they too wanted something from Wang Donglin. Finally, Chen Nuolan wasn’t by Lu Tianfeng’s side at the crucial moment, and Lu Tianfeng offered no explanation, suggesting he didn’t want to, or couldn’t, reveal the reason.

Based on various signs, a massive tsunami might be brewing beneath the calm surface of the sea.

Thinking of this, Zhang Zhiqi couldn’t help but quicken his pace.

He soon arrived at the Student Affairs Office.

“Classmate, where is the Work-Study Program Office?” Zhang Zhiqi asked a hurriedly approaching girl.

“Oh? Ah, over there, just around the corner,” the girl replied, seemingly in a hurry, her voice mumbling as she scurried off. “Turn left or right… Ugh, kids these days are so rude.” Zhang Zhiqi shook his head helplessly, glanced at the sign on the wall, and headed towards the work-study office.

However, before he even reached his destination, Zhang Zhiqi sensed something was amiss—puffs of smoke were billowing from behind the closed door at the end of the corridor.

“Fire!” Without a word, Zhang Zhiqi smashed the fire alarm on the wall with his fist, rushed forward with a fire extinguisher, and kicked the office door open.

Thick, pungent smoke mixed with billowing heat rushed towards him, forcing Zhang Zhiqi to step back. Blazing flames filled the office. Such a fierce fire was definitely not an accident; it was likely arson.

“Lu Tianfeng!” Zhang Zhiqi screamed at the top of his lungs, but no one in the fire scene responded.

Zhang Zhiqi gritted his teeth, opened the fire extinguisher, and fiercely sprayed it at the flames in front of him. The fire subsided slightly, and amidst the smoke, a figure lay motionless on the floor.

“Lu Tianfeng!” Zhang Zhiqi called again, but Lu Tianfeng remained motionless, seemingly unconscious.

Seeing the fire was still spreading, Zhang Zhiqi threw away the extinguisher, took a deep breath, and dashed into the flames. Without even a moment to catch his breath, he dragged Lu Tianfeng out.

The flames were all around him, and the scorching heat weighed on him, filling him with despair. Amidst the smoke and flames, Zhang Zhiqi lost his sense of distance and direction. Relying solely on intuition and perseverance, he desperately advanced towards his chosen destination.

A distinct burning sensation pierced his skin, yet Zhang Zhiqi dared not even breathe. If he inhaled the thick smoke, he would have no hope of escaping alive.

Luckily, he hadn’t taken the wrong direction.

Zhang Zhiqi led Lu Tianfeng out of the work-study office. Meanwhile, several enthusiastic students and teachers had arrived, hearing the alarm. Several, armed with fire extinguishers, tried to contain the blaze and prevent it from spreading outside. Two girls helped support Zhang Zhiqi and Lu Tianfeng while they called an ambulance. The scene was in chaos. Zhang Zhiqi breathed in deep gulps of fresh air, observing the crowd intently.

The arsonist likely hadn’t gone far, wanting to confirm with his own eyes whether Lu Tianfeng had perished in the flames. A more ruthless individual might have been able to blend in with the crowd and attack Lu Tianfeng again.

Therefore, Zhang Zhiqi absolutely dared not relax for even a moment. His eagle-like gaze scanned every face in the crowd.

Curiosity, fear, excitement, confusion, uneasiness…

Among this diverse array of faces, there stood one impassive one.

Zhang Zhiqi’s gaze didn’t linger, but he had already secretly memorized that face.

“I’m… fine…” Lu Tianfeng woke up, seemingly fine.

Zhang Zhiqi quickly squatted down and whispered in Lu Tianfeng’s ear, “What’s going on?”

Lu Tianfeng blinked, immediately understanding the situation. Without asking any unnecessary questions, he simply said, “Someone stole the data.”

“Who?”

“A man in his forties, wearing black-framed glasses, with a scholarly air, looking like a teacher, and a woman in her early twenties, dressed like a university student…”

“A white sleeveless shirt, black jeans, shoulder-length hair?” Zhang Zhiqi’s mind suddenly flashed back to the image of the girl he’d asked for directions earlier.

“How… did you know…” Lu Tianfeng was stunned.

“As for that man you mentioned…” Zhang Zhiqi abruptly stood up and tried to find the aloof man, but he was nowhere to be found.

“They haven’t gone far. Chase them!” Zhang Zhiqi pulled Lu Tianfeng up from his sitting position. “Go wash your face first.”

.

June 1st, 1:15 p.m., D City University, Administration Building.

Lu Tianfeng and Zhang Zhiqi straightened their wrinkled clothes in the restroom closest to the scene and scrubbed the soot from their faces. D City University was already a key police surveillance location. After the fire, not only would the firefighters arrive to put out the blaze, but nearby police officers would also undoubtedly arrive to assist with the investigation. If they were to walk around covered in black soot, they’d likely be stopped and questioned.

“Where are we going next?” Lu Tianfeng asked, washing his face with water in his hands.

“To find the two people who stole the data.”

“Where are we going?” Lu Tianfeng studied himself in the mirror, seemingly unable to discern any major problems.

“It’s the same anywhere. As long as there’s free Wi-Fi, just use it.”

“You want to find someone online?” Lu Tianfeng’s disappointment was palpable. “Isn’t that like looking for a needle in a haystack?”

“D City University already has tens of thousands of teachers and students, plus thousands of outsiders visiting every day. How are you supposed to find them without high-tech methods?”

Lu Tianfeng was speechless. He knew Zhang Zhiqi was right, but his mind was in a tangle, and he couldn’t come up with any good ideas.

“Come on.” Zhang Zhiqi pulled Lu Tianfeng out of the bathroom. He didn’t actually use the free Wi-Fi but simply found an empty room, went in, picked up his tablet, and started using it.

Lu Tianfeng leaned in curiously, wanting to see what Zhang Zhiqi was fiddling with. But the screen was filled with a dazzling array of codes and countless images flashing rapidly, making it impossible to make them out clearly.

“Don’t understand?” Zhang Zhiqi asked casually, his eyes fixed on the screen.

“Hmm.”

“That’s right, you don’t understand.”

Lu Tianfeng noticed that the images flashing on the screen all seemed to be ID photos, so he asked, “What’s this for?”

“Logging into D City University’s personnel database and retrieving the ID photos of all faculty, staff, and current students.”

“And then comparing them one by one? How can you be sure those two people are faculty, staff, and students?” Lu Tianfeng found it a bit baffling.

“To answer the first question, there’s no need for a one-by-one comparison. The AI ​​will do most of the work for us,” Zhang Zhiqi said, pointing to the screen.

It turned out that he had entered some facial features, and the system would immediately analyze and filter them, leaving only suitable candidates. For example, after entering “male, height over 1.7 meters,” the system returned over 3,000 candidates. Adding the new condition “wearing glasses” reduced the number of candidates. Then, adding more detailed conditions like “square face, high nose bridge, dark skin,” the number of candidates continued to dwindle.

When only a few dozen candidate photos remained, Zhang Zhiqi switched the image browsing mode to manual, flipping through them one by one. The moment a certain photo appeared on the screen, they both shouted in unison, “That’s him!”

D City University General Affairs Office, Office Assistant, Deng Zixiong.

“Confirm the girl’s identity again!” Lu Tianfeng said.

Zhang Zhiqi immediately took action. Unexpectedly, this time it was a bit more difficult. The system took quite a while, and they tried different facial feature keywords before finally locking onto the girl’s identity.

D City University Department of Philosophy, Senior, Ma Yueyi.

“Now, let me answer your second question: Why do I think they’re from D City University?” After successfully finding his target, Zhang Zhiqi stood up and stretched.

“I’ve figured it out.” Lu Tianfeng stared intently at the ID photo on the screen. “Because they didn’t have much time to prepare, they scrambled to make arrangements after learning I was going to the work-study office. They had to deploy personnel nearby.”

“Yes, they must have tapped Tong Yao’s phone… After removing the hacking chip, they could only eavesdrop by tracking and decoding the phone number. I didn’t expect they actually had that capability.”

“I’m really confused. How could there be so many people connected to the ‘Organization’ in this school…” Lu Tianfeng froze mid-sentence, unable to finish the rest of his sentence.

“What’s wrong?” Zhang Zhiqi asked, puzzled.

Lu Tianfeng remained silent. He recalled many people and events. The mysterious ‘Organization’ was indeed inextricably linked to this university.

In the previous Feng Teng Gene case, individuals implicated at D City University included Zhou Huansheng, who mysteriously disappeared years ago; Luo Tengfeng and Chen Nuolan, who were caught up in the turmoil surrounding RAN technology; and Tan Jiaqiang of the Nifeng Club. In this incident, the serial killer, Wang Donglin, was a member of the university, and his crimes primarily took place on campus. And now, Deng Zixiong and Ma Yueyi had suddenly appeared, stealing the data…

“A terrifying thought suddenly struck me,” Lu Tianfeng said sternly.

“What thought?”

“Could the headquarters of this ‘Organization’ be within this school?”

The usually calm Zhang Zhiqi’s eyes widened in surprise.

Lu Tianfeng continued, “But no matter what, we must find these two individuals.”

Deng Zixiong and Ma Yueyi were their only leads.

Lu Tianfeng was still quickly browsing their files when he suddenly pointed at the screen and asked in surprise, “Huh? Ma Yueyi’s still pursuing a double degree?”

Ma Yueyi was a philosophy student, but she’d chosen a double degree program in psychology. Her second degree thesis was on criminal psychology research, and her thesis advisor was Yuan Chengren, a long-retired professor with only the title of honorary professor.

Lu Tianfeng looked at Deng Zixiong’s profile again and discovered that he, too, had graduated from the Department of Psychology at D City University many years earlier, majoring in educational psychology. He had stayed at D City University directly after graduation, and his thesis advisor back then had also been Yuan Chengren.

The commonality between the two finally surfaced.

“Let’s go find Professor Yuan,” Zhang Zhiqi said simply.

.

June 1st, 1:20 p.m., D City University, outside the back gate.

Fire trucks, police cars, and ambulances rolled onto the campus one after another, sirens blaring. It was clear something was amiss.

Cheng Tuo anxiously checked his watch. Lu Tianfeng had been gone for over half an hour. He should have returned long ago, but he was nowhere to be seen. Even more unsettling was the fact that even Zhang Zhiqi, who had said he’d check on him, hadn’t responded.

“Let’s call them and urge them to come back,” Cheng Tuo said to Tong Yao.

“Captain Cheng, look at my phone…” Tong Yao pointed at the circuit board inside the car. She wondered how Zhang Zhiqi had dialed through it.

“Do you remember their phone numbers?”

Tong Yao shook her head. These days, almost no one bothered to remember long strings of numbers. Lu Tianfeng was using a temporary card, and Zhang Zhiqi and she had only just met. How could she possibly remember their numbers?

“Don’t bother! They probably just took the data and ran off.” Wang Donglin, who had been listless, suddenly perked up and spoke with a playful smile after noticing the new development.

“Stop talking!” Tong Yao glared at Wang Donglin fiercely.

However, Wang Donglin smiled instead and asked, “Then how do you explain their loss of contact? It was just a copy of data. Does that require two people to go together?”

“Shut up!” Tong Yao couldn’t help but feel a little impatient.

Cheng Tuo silently glanced at his watch, then at Tong Yao. “It looks like something serious has happened on campus. The police will soon be conducting a search for suspicious individuals in the surrounding area. If we don’t relocate quickly, we’ll likely be discovered.”

“Then… where should we go?”

“What do you think?” Cheng Tuo unexpectedly addressed Wang Donglin.

Wang Donglin hadn’t anticipated Cheng Tuo’s sudden move. Stunned for a moment, he retorted, “You’re asking me?”

“Yeah, now that you can’t provide any clues or help me get the so-called secret data, what use are you?” Cheng Tuo’s sneer was chilling. “I might as well just send you back to the police station.”

“Captain Cheng, let’s talk it over.” Wang Donglin adjusted his sitting position, his arrogance subdued. “I, I can still help you…”

“Help me with what?” Cheng Tuo asked expressionlessly.

Wang Donglin licked his chapped lips, his eyes rolling as he seemed to be trying to think through how to respond to Cheng Tuo’s question.

“Since there’s nothing more to say, let’s go.” Cheng Tuo didn’t give Wang Donglin much time to think. Without a word, he started the van and prepared to leave.

“Wait! I… I just remembered something very important!”

“Tell me!” Cheng Tuo said as he released the parking brake.

“I suspect someone from the ‘Organization’ is hiding inside the school!” Wang Donglin said impatiently. “He might live upstairs!”

“Why do you say that?” Cheng Tuo and Tong Yao were skeptical.

“Did you hear the conversation between Lu Tianfeng and me just now? Someone secretly filmed me committing the murder, and I’ve analyzed the angles of the photos. Several of them could only have been taken from the unit above me.”

“Upstairs? Do you know which unit?”

Wang Donglin lived in an older faculty dormitory building, only eight stories high, so checking every single one wouldn’t take too long.

Wang Donglin smiled wryly and said, “For something so important, of course I’ve put a lot of effort into investigating. Based on the angles and height of the photos, my primary suspect is Mr. Yuan Chengren, who lives in Unit 501 on the fifth floor of the building next door.”

“Yuan Chengren?” Tong Yao thought the name sounded familiar, but she couldn’t place it. “A retired professor of psychology from D City University, a leading figure in domestic criminal psychology. I think only he could do something like this.”

Tong Yao finally remembered: “Oh my god! This Teacher Yuan… is Zhang Zhiqi’s former teacher!”

Zhang Zhiqi had stopped by Yuan Chengren last night. What exactly did they talk about? If Yuan Chengren truly had ties to the ‘Organization,’ could Zhang Zhiqi still be trusted? Why had he chosen to go find Lu Tianfeng? What exactly happened on campus?

Tong Yao was devastated. She forced herself to close her eyes and took a deep breath before she calmed down.

“What should we do now?”

Tong Yao and Cheng Tuo looked at each other. They wanted to enter the school to investigate, but they couldn’t bring the wanted criminal Wang Donglin with them. However, if they were left alone to guard Wang Donglin, they didn’t trust each other. After all, both of them were in a somewhat awkward position, not fully following police protocol.

Naturally, Wang Donglin was aware of the sensitivity of the situation, but he said nothing and laughed to himself. He was aware that the hints he gave would trouble Cheng Tuo and Tong Yao. The location of the data and Lu Tianfeng’s safety would be their concerns, so they couldn’t wait there indefinitely. Any hasty decision is likely to result in mistakes.

So Wang Donglin simply had to wait for the situation to develop further.

“I’d better log in to the system.” To conceal his whereabouts, Cheng Tuo had previously disconnected his phone’s network connection, but now he had no choice but to access the internal police system to check for the latest information.

The moment he opened the interface, a red, bold emergency message appeared: “A fire has occurred at D City University. Suspected arsonist may be involved in the Wang Donglin case. All units requested to provide nearby reinforcements.”

“There’s a fire on campus. The location of the fire… is the Student Affairs Office’s Work-Study Program Office.”

“Are there any casualties?” Tong Yao asked anxiously.

“No casualties have been reported so far.”

“Captain Cheng, I’d better go check it out,” Tong Yao volunteered. Although she worried Cheng Tuo might have ulterior motives, she was even more concerned about the situation with Lu Tianfeng and Zhang Zhiqi.

“Aren’t you afraid that Wang Donglin and I might strike some kind of private deal?” Cheng Tuo bluntly stated.

“I trust you.”

“What if you trust the wrong person?”

“Then I’ll go to the ends of the earth to bring you and Wang Donglin to justice,” Tong Yao said earnestly.

Cheng Tuo smiled. “Don’t worry, I know exactly who I am.”

Hearing this, Wang Donglin, who was sitting nearby, suddenly curled his lips. He knew that this was his best and last chance to escape.

CONTENT END 103

chapters.title: Chapter 104
chapters.content:
June 1st, 1:30 p.m., D City University, Faculty Dormitory area.

Yuan Chengren’s home.

After knocking on the door with no response, the lock clicked and then snapped open from outside.

Lu Tianfeng and Zhang Zhiqi cautiously pushed the door open.

“Teacher Yuan?” Zhang Zhiqi called inside, but silence reigned.

“Look for clues.” Lu Tianfeng had an uneasy feeling; he felt Yuan Chengren might have already taken action.

Yuan Chengren’s room was simply furnished, the furniture plain. The only decorations were the walls covered with honorary awards, certificates, and photos of events. Above the cabinets stood a row of glittering trophies—these were the most memorable moments of his life.

“Nothing special,” Zhang Zhiqi said, checking the bedroom. The quilt was neatly folded, and the clothes in the closet were equally tidy; nothing seemed out of place.

“What’s in the drawers?” Lu Tianfeng asked.

“The drawer is locked, so let’s not force it open. Teacher Yuan might just have gone for a walk…”

“Two people just tried to kill me, and they were both Yuan Chengren’s students. Is this just a coincidence?” Lu Tianfeng demanded.

Zhang Zhiqi said nothing, sighed, turned his head to the side, and looked out the window.

Lu Tianfeng was about to move forward to pick the lock when Zhang Zhiqi suddenly nudged him with his elbow and pointed out the window: “Look over there.”

“What are you looking at?”

“That’s Wang Donglin’s yard, right? From this angle, you can just see what’s going on under the parking shed.”

Lu Tianfeng looked over and saw that it was indeed the case.

“So the person who took the photos and threatened Wang Donglin was Yuan Chengren?”

Zhang Zhiqi slowly shook his head: “It’s hard to say…”

Just then, the two heard the sound of a key unlocking the door outside.

“Don’t panic; let me do the talking.” Lu Tianfeng stepped forward, just in time to meet Yuan Chengren entering the house. Yuan Chengren was so frightened by the thought of someone in the house that he dropped the shopping bag to the floor, sending eggplants, carrots, and apples tumbling across the floor.

“Zhang Zhiqi?” Yuan Chengren recognized the student standing behind the stranger, his expression calming slightly, but he still asked in confusion, “What exactly happened?”

“I’m Lu Tianfeng from the City Criminal Police Brigade. There’s a case right now that requires your assistance, Professor Yuan…”

“Stop!” Yuan Chengren raised his right hand, making a stop gesture. “The police needing my assistance is different from you trespassing on someone’s property, right? Is that how police work these days?”

“I’m sorry, it’s an emergency…”

“What’s an emergency? Do you have a search warrant?”

Yuan Chengren slumped down on the sofa, not even bothering to pick up the fruits and vegetables on the floor. Fortunately, Zhang Zhiqi was quick-witted and quickly scooped up the items into his shopping bag, handing it to Yuan Chengren.

“Teacher Yuan, don’t be angry. My friend is just a little peculiar…”

Yuan Chengren rolled his eyes at Zhang Zhiqi and said nothing.

Lu Tianfeng steeled himself and said, “Professor Yuan, an arson occurred at your school half an hour ago. Both suspects were former students of yours, so we’d like to ask you a few questions.”

“Arson? My students?” Yuan Chengren sneered. “I’ve been teaching for over thirty years, and I’ve taught at least seven or eight thousand students. If one of them actually broke the law, can they really blame me?”

Lu Tianfeng stood there, feeling a little awkward. Yuan Chengren’s anger didn’t seem like an act. Could it be that he had no connection to the ‘Organization’?

“Teacher Yuan…”

“Zhang Zhiqi, it’s okay for others not to respect their teachers, but don’t you?”

“Yes, yes, you’re right.” Zhang Zhiqi admitted his mistake, bowing his head in a rare moment of apology.

“Hurry up and leave! If you don’t, I’ll call your superiors. Has Han Guangrong retired? Hasn’t Luo Yongping been promoted to director?” Yuan Chengren’s face flushed as he unceremoniously recited the full names of the two directors.

“Well… excuse me…” Lu Tianfeng and Zhang Zhiqi, feeling somewhat dejected after their unsuccessful trip, were about to depart.

However, at that moment, someone knocked three times on the open door.

“Knock, knock, knock—”

Tong Yao stood outside, holding a black USB drive.

“Professor Yuan, how did you manage to put this thing in the mailbox downstairs? Thieves are so savvy these days; hiding things in mailboxes won’t fool them anymore.”

Tong Yao smiled faintly and reached out as if to hand the USB drive to Yuan Chengren, but Yuan Chengren didn’t take it.

After all, the USB drive belonged to Lu Tianfeng.

The suddenness of the incident caught Lu Tianfeng and Zhang Zhiqi off guard. Yuan Chengren’s face seemed to be frosted, cold, but also less angry than before.

“Teacher Yuan, this is…” Zhang Zhiqi struggled to utter the words. In his mind, Yuan Chengren was not only his teacher but also his hero.

“I won’t say anything,” Yuan Chengren said slowly, his words remarkably clear.

“I was just downstairs when I saw Yuan Chengren take this USB drive out of his shopping bag and put it in the mailbox.” Tong Yao handed the USB drive to Lu Tianfeng. “Boss, is this yours?”

“Yes,” Lu Tianfeng nodded, accepting the recovered data.

Yuan Chengren looked coldly at the three people in the room, silent.

“Tong Yao, please take Teacher Yuan back to the police station and ask him to cooperate with our investigation. Zhang Zhiqi, come with me to research what exactly this data is.”

“Wait!” Unexpectedly, Tong Yao and Zhang Zhiqi reacted strongly, shouting in unison.

Lu Tianfeng was stunned. “What’s going on?”

Zhang Zhiqi spoke first, “You’re just going to let Tong Yao take Teacher Yuan back alone? Isn’t that a bit dangerous?”

He winked at Lu Tianfeng repeatedly as he spoke, and Lu Tianfeng finally remembered his earlier deduction: if the ‘Organization’ headquarters was indeed on campus, perhaps their people were lying in ambush nearby, lurking.

Tong Yao had originally wanted to remind Lu Tianfeng that Zhang Zhiqi was also Yuan Chengren’s student and that she couldn’t trust him completely, but she hadn’t expected him to be so concerned about her safety, leaving her unsure whether to voice her concerns.

“Then let’s go together.” Lu Tianfeng understood and nodded.

“Who said I’m going back with you?” However, Yuan Chengren was not prepared to cooperate. “I refuse. If you try to take me away by force, expect to suffer.”

After that, Yuan Chengren sat firmly on the sofa, his arms folded over his chest, with an air of unwavering determination.

Lu Tianfeng realized that Yuan Chengren was stalling for time, and the enemy might arrive sooner than expected.

Zhang Zhiqi was equally helpless. He stared at the row of glittering golden trophies on the cabinet, especially the most prominent one, the “Crime Fighting Pioneer” honorary trophy awarded by the Provincial Public Security Department, and felt a deep sense of irony.

“Knock, knock, knock—”

There was someone outside the door.

Yuan Chengren remained seated, but the corners of his mouth curled up involuntarily.

Lu Tianfeng gestured to Tong Yao, signaling her to check on the situation. Tong Yao nodded, quickly walked to the door, and asked loudly, “Who is it?”

“Hello, courier. Is this Mr. Yuan Chengren’s home?” the male voice replied.

“Yes, but I can’t open the door right now. Can you leave the package outside?”

The courier persisted, “Excuse me, is Mr. Yuan home? He needs to sign for this package in person.”

Tong Yao cast a questioning look at Lu Tianfeng. Lu Tianfeng glanced at Yuan Chengren and decided to let Tong Yao open the door.

“Be careful.”

The door opened, revealing a courier in an orange uniform and a sports cap, holding a heavy cardboard box.

“Can you sign for me?” Tong Yao asked.

“If Mr. Yuan isn’t available, I can sign for him, but please show your ID,” the courier said, peeking into the room and spotting Yuan Chengren sitting on the sofa.

At the same moment, Lu Tianfeng also saw the courier’s face clearly.

He was Ah’Yong, the man who had kidnapped Chen Nuolan!

When Yuan Chengren saw Ah’Yong, his expression froze for a moment. Perhaps he had expected someone else to appear outside the door.

“Don’t let him in!” Lu Tianfeng shouted, but he was still a step too late.

Ah’Yong hurled the cardboard box at Tong Yao. Seeing the heavy weight and the powerful force of the box, Tong Yao could only dodge. Ah’Yong kicked the wooden door open, pulled a pistol from his waist, and aimed it at Yuan Chengren, who was reclined on the sofa.

Lu Tianfeng reacted incredibly quickly, rushing forward and tackling Yuan Chengren to the ground.

“Puff—puff—” The silenced pistol left two clear bullet holes in the sofa.

Ah’Yong rushed into the room, ready to continue chasing the fallen Yuan Chengren, but Tong Yao had already rushed out from the side and launched a sweeping kick at Ah’Yong’s knees. Unexpectedly, Ah’Yong’s boxing and kicking skills were also impressive. Not only did he nimbly dodge Tong Yao’s attack, but he even seized the opportunity to counterattack, kicking her in the waist.

Tong Yao, tears streaming down her face, retreated three steps, half-realizing Ah’Yong’s gun was aimed at her. She quickly dodged to the side.

But Ah’Yong didn’t fire. Out of the corner of his eye, he saw a dark shadow hurtling toward him and hurriedly dodged. With a clang, the honorary trophy, flung by Zhang Zhiqi, slammed against the wall, its base instantly breaking in two.

Ah’Yong fired a shot in Zhang Zhiqi’s direction, forcing him to tumble and evade the attack. However, realizing he was outnumbered, he didn’t recklessly continue firing. Instead, he leaned against the door, adopted a defensive stance, and turned his gun back toward Yuan Chengren and Lu Tianfeng.

“Hand over the thing, and I’ll spare your life.” Ah’Yong forced a smile. “Officer Lu, you know I always keep my word.”

“What is it?”

“The data hidden by Wang Donglin.”

Lu Tianfeng suddenly realized that Ah’Yong and his boss were both after the data. It seemed their real purpose in demanding Lu Tianfeng hand over Wang Donglin was to track down the data. Unexpectedly, Lu Tianfeng had taken the data directly, saving them a lot of trouble.

What exactly was this data? Was it that important?

“I’ll give you the data in exchange for releasing Chen Nuolan.”

“No problem,” Ah’Yong replied without hesitation.

“I need to deal face-to-face to ensure Chen Nuolan’s safety.” As he spoke, Lu Tianfeng had already picked up the teapot filled with warm water from the table and held up a USB drive in his other hand. “Just a reminder, this antique USB drive isn’t waterproof. If it falls into the teapot, it’ll be ruined.”

Ah’Yong’s eyes widened. “You dare?”

“Why wouldn’t I? I’m telling you, there’s no backup of this data.”

Ah’Yong thought for a moment and sneered, “Chen Nuolan has only one life, and there’s no backup.”

Now it was Lu Tianfeng’s turn to remain silent.

As the two of them exchanged sharp words, Tong Yao and Zhang Zhiqi exchanged silent glances, their minds swirling with questions.

Who was this man? Why did Lu Tianfeng seem to know him? Where had Chen Nuolan gone?

But the situation was so complex, there was no chance for them to ask. Seeing Lu Tianfeng’s silence, Ah’Yong knew he had the upper hand psychologically, so he softened his tone.

“Officer Lu, this data is of no use to you at all, so why are you clinging to it?”

Yes, they fought tooth and nail for this data, yet they don’t even know what it actually was. How ironic!

Lu Tianfeng’s heart began to waver.

Ah’Yong, feeling certain of victory, relaxed even more. With his gun raised in his right hand, he took two steps toward Lu Tianfeng and held out his left hand: “Hand it over.”

Lu Tianfeng’s eyelids twitched constantly. He knew that no matter what choice he made, he would likely regret it.

At this critical moment, something unexpected happened.

“Tap, tap—” A series of rapid sounds echoed outside the door.

Ah’Yong, who had been standing in the living room with the air of a victor, suddenly froze. Several flowers of blood bloomed on his chest, and the bright red spread rapidly.

“You…”

The arrogant Ah’Yong uttered only this word before closing his eyes and falling forward, his body tumbling to the ground. Several terrifying black holes appeared on his back, blood oozing continuously.

The front door was riddled with bullet holes. Someone outside was firing wildly through the door with a submachine gun, and Ah’Yong’s position bore the brunt of the attack, taking multiple hits.

Almost instantly, Yuan Chengren, who had been motionless, suddenly lunged forward and bit Lu Tianfeng’s left wrist, where he was holding the USB drive. Lu Tianfeng cried out in pain, his grip unconsciously loosening, and the USB drive fell squarely into the teapot.

Lu Tianfeng instantly realized that Ah’Yong and his men were after the data, while Yuan Chengren only wanted to destroy it.

“Retreat to the room!” Lu Tianfeng quickly poured out all the water from the teapot and retrieved the USB drive.

In fact, before Lu Tianfeng gave the order, Tong Yao and Zhang Zhiqi had already spontaneously moved toward the bedroom. Yuan Chengren, taking advantage of Lu Tianfeng’s efforts to rescue the USB drive, fled to the door with agility rarely seen in an elderly man.

Lu Tianfeng knew he couldn’t bother with Yuan Chengren anymore, so he immediately dodged into the bedroom and locked the door behind him.

“Escape from the balcony!” Zhang Zhiqi shouted.

All three knew the enemy’s firepower was fierce; it was likely the same group that had planned to hijack the prison van yesterday morning. They couldn’t engage them head-on and had to flee as quickly as possible.

Luckily, Yuan Chengren’s balcony didn’t have a metal security screen, and it was less than a meter away from the neighbor’s balcony, making it easy to climb over.

“Tong Yao, you go first. Take this.” Lu Tianfeng pressed the wet USB drive into Tong Yao’s hands.

Tong Yao was stunned for a moment but said nothing. After taking the USB drive, she kicked off with her feet and lightly jumped onto the balcony of the next house. Zhang Zhiqi followed closely behind. Although his landing was not as graceful as Tong Yao’s, he also stood firmly.

“That USB drive is waterproof,” Zhang Zhiqi said to Tong Yao quickly.

“Huh?” Tong Yao finally understood. Lu Tianfeng’s earlier negotiations with the gunman had been nothing but a bluff. She admired Lu Tianfeng’s ability to remain calm and set up a trap in a life-or-death situation and was also amazed by Zhang Zhiqi’s ability to see through Lu Tianfeng’s scheme in a split second.

Instantly, Lu Tianfeng leaped forward, but the pursuers were already behind him.

“Hurry!”

The three men ducked and rushed into the family’s bedroom. Fortunately, no one was inside, or they would have been terrified. Although the room was adjacent to Yuan Chengren’s balcony, the hallway outside was disconnected. Lu Tianfeng and the others ran down the stairs, not daring to look back. They knew that once they left the building and reached the street, they would encounter the police officers who were stalking Wang Donglin’s home.

No matter how brazen the enemy was, they wouldn’t dare engage in a firefight with the police in broad daylight. Furthermore, due to the previous fire, the number of police deployed on campus was ten times greater than usual.

“Run!”

Lu Tianfeng had only one thought at the moment.

They had exited the dim corridor and returned to the sunlight, and there was no sound of pursuing footsteps or the crackle of bullets behind them.

Lu Tianfeng recognized the car ahead; last night, when they had visited Wang Xiaomian, they had distracted the police inside and were able to sneak into Wang Donglin’s home.

But surprisingly, the car was now empty. The officers who had been on surveillance were nowhere to be seen, most likely having gone to the fire scene to provide reinforcements.

“Get in the car!” Lu Tianfeng checked the door; it was unlocked.

“They’re not chasing us,” Zhang Zhiqi said as he jumped into the passenger seat and fastened his seatbelt.

“Yuan Chengren might have thought the data was truly destroyed. If that were the case, he would prioritize his own safety and flee immediately,” Lu Tianfeng said.

Tong Yao patted her chest. “Then we’re incredibly lucky.”

But Lu Tianfeng’s expression didn’t betray a trace of relief. “There’s another possibility. When the criminals opened fire through the wooden door, they had no idea where Yuan Chengren was, yet they continued firing recklessly. Perhaps it’s because Yuan Chengren’s life or death didn’t matter to them.”

Zhang Zhiqi remained silent. His gaze was drawn to the three men not far away, and he nudged Lu Tianfeng with his elbow.

The three men were all wearing matching tracksuits. They walked with their heads bowed, their collars raised high, obscuring most of their faces, making it difficult to see their faces. Notably, their steps were almost synchronized: firm and powerful. Their positions and movements centered around the car, forming a subtle encirclement. As they drew closer, Zhang Zhiqi could even make out the outlines of submachine guns hidden beneath their tracksuits.

It was the deliberate illusion of calm a predator creates before swooping down on its prey.

Lu Tianfeng and Tong Yao also noticed their aggressors almost simultaneously, but they were too close. If they chose to escape now, they would likely become targets.

They remained in the car, watching helplessly as the enemy approached. One of them had already unzipped his tracksuit, revealing the black handle of his gun.

At noon, sunlight filtered through the shade of the trees onto the school road. A few unaware students rode their bicycles, chatting and laughing with each other as they passed the ruthless criminals.

Seeing the passing students, Lu Tianfeng became even more afraid to get out of the car. He sighed, thinking, even if he himself would be shot in the car, he would never let these unarmed young people get hurt.

Tong Yao and Zhang Zhiqi exchanged glances, each sensing the resignation in the other’s eyes.

It seemed they had no choice but to accept their fate.

The three men walked to within two meters of the car before simultaneously pulling submachine guns from their coats. The black muzzles were ready to spew deadly bullets from three different directions. Meanwhile, the three men inside the car held nothing that could be called a weapon.

The outcome would be decided in the next second.

Unexpectedly, at that moment, the situation suddenly changed.

A boy who had just passed by on a bicycle suddenly jumped off, raised his bicycle with both hands, and slammed it into the back of one of the gunmen, knocking him to the ground. The other two gunmen immediately turned their guns around, but they were still a step too slow. Seven or eight people rushed out from both sides, quickly disarmed them, and handcuffed them.

“A very standard arrest move! They’re police!” Zhang Zhiqi exclaimed excitedly.

At this moment, Lu Tianfeng finally spotted Yan Jin, the operation commander, hiding behind a large tree, and Dai Chunhua, sitting on a bench beneath the tree, reading a newspaper.

CONTENT END 104

chapters.title: Chapter 105
chapters.content:
June 1st, 2:00 p.m., D City University, Faculty Dormitory area.

Several police cars flashed their lights, and dozens of uniformed officers cordoned off the scene. Forensic technicians had already gone to Yuan Chengren’s home to collect evidence, and a search warrant had been issued for Yuan Chengren, Deng Zixiong, and Ma Yueyi.

Lu Tianfeng sat in one of the police cars, asking Tong Yao to tend to the arm wound she had sustained during their escape. Yan Jin and Cheng Tuo were also in the car. In the back seat sat Wang Donglin, his face hidden by his coat.

“It’s finally over,” Cheng Tuo said to Lu Tianfeng with a long sigh of relief.

Lu Tianfeng hesitated. He still had many questions, but he couldn’t bring them up in front of Yan Jin. Yan Jin, on the other hand, asked directly, “Captain Cheng, thanks to the timely clues you provided, we were able to apprehend the criminals. But I don’t understand why you didn’t report Wang Donglin immediately after capturing him. Why did you also conceal the information about Yuan Chengren’s involvement in the case at D City University? Thankfully, Wang Donglin didn’t escape. If something had happened, who would have taken responsibility?”

Cheng Tuo patted Yan Jin’s shoulder. “Don’t worry, I’ll write the report. Captain Yan, you’ve done an excellent job this time. Even if our superiors hold us accountable, I’ll take responsibility.”

“This isn’t even about assigning responsibility…” Yan Jin had a vague feeling that Cheng Tuo was hiding something from him, but the primary mission—capturing Wang Donglin—had already been accomplished, and he didn’t want to create any more complications at this point.

“You also need to think carefully about how to report this to your superiors,” Cheng Tuo said, addressing Lu Tianfeng again.

Lu Tianfeng glanced at Wang Donglin in the backseat. Knowing he couldn’t escape the law, Wang Donglin’s expression was surprisingly calm, and his gaze back at Lu Tianfeng was extremely complex.

Wang Donglin didn’t seem to have conceded defeat. No, not only had he not, but he seemed to still harbor hope, even looking at Lu Tianfeng with the pity of a victor.

Lu Tianfeng suddenly understood. Wang Donglin no longer had anything to lose. No matter how much he lost, he would only remain where he was. But he was different.

He could lose his job, his beloved, everything at any moment…

“Take Wang Donglin back to the police station first. I have something else to do.”

“Wait a moment.” Yan Jin grabbed Lu Tianfeng, who was about to get out of the car. “Where are you going? You’re also involved in the case. You can’t just leave.”

“Captain Yan, my girlfriend’s life is in danger. I need to save her.”

“Then I’ll send someone to go with you.”

“No, that would alert the enemy.” Lu Tianfeng shook his head. If Ah’Yong could track them here, then the boss behind the scenes was likely aware of the situation.

He touched the USB drive that Tong Yao had just returned to him. The data inside was crucial evidence in the case. If Yan Jin understood the whole story, he would definitely not agree to let him use the data in exchange for Chen Nuolan.

“I have to go alone.”

“Captain Lu, this is against the rules!”

“Captain Yan, if everything had to be done according to the rules, we might not have caught this guy yet,” Cheng Tuo interrupted, pointing at Wang Donglin.

Yan Jin looked at Lu Tianfeng, a flicker of hesitation in his eyes. Normally, he should have taken Lu Tianfeng back to the police station for a thorough interrogation, but he also knew that Lu Tianfeng was not one to play by the rules.

Lu Tianfeng leaned forward, leaning close to Yan Jin’s ear, and said in a voice only he could hear, “Let me go. Only I can uncover the truth in the Wang Donglin case.”

Yan Jin’s pupils suddenly dilated.

“Yes, I believe you have a hunch too. The truth isn’t that simple.”

.

June 1st, 2:30 p.m., Unknown Location.

Chen Nuolan sat alone in a luxurious room, with plenty of food and drinks and a large collection of books and magazines to ensure she wouldn’t get bored. The door was locked from the outside, leaving her unable to leave. She had no idea where Situ Kang had gone, and he hadn’t been seen since.

She irritably tossed the travel magazine back onto the table. At the same moment, the sound of a lock opening could be heard from outside.

Situ Kang pushed the door open and walked in. He wasn’t accompanied by any of his men, his expression a little stiff.

“Miss Chen, did you have a good rest?”

“Mr. Situ, please speak frankly.” Chen Nuolan sensed something was amiss.

Situ Kang sat down and gestured for Chen Nuolan to do the same. He slowly poured a cup of tea before saying, “I have good news and bad news. Which one would you like to hear first?”

“Bad news, I prefer to leave hope for the end.”

“The bad news is that the people I sent to support Lu Tianfeng were completely wiped out. I don’t know what happened.” Situ Kang’s tone was calm, not at all like someone suffering a heavy loss.

Chen Nuolan was startled, terrifying images flashing through her mind, but she remained calm and asked, “What’s the good news?”

“The good news is that Lu Tianfeng is on his way to us. I sincerely hope he’s successfully completed his mission.”

“Is he coming?”

“Yes, but if he comes empty-handed, our deal won’t be completed.” Situ Kang downed his tea in one gulp. “That would be a lose-lose situation.”

“What if he can’t meet your demands? Will you kill me?”

“Killing is just a useless way to vent my anger, and I never do meaningless things.” Situ Kang smiled, but there was a coldness in his smile.

“Then what is meaningful?” Chen Nuolan’s eyes rolled as he came up with the answer. “You can turn back time again, right?”

“In short, yes.” As Situ Kang spoke these words, his entire demeanor subtly changed, taking on a sense of superiority that looked down upon the world.

“So you’ll force Lu Tianfeng to risk his life for you again and again until you achieve your goal?”

“Unfortunately, Lu Tianfeng’s current abilities are limited. He can only reverse time once. If he does it again, he’ll likely die.”

“What did you say?” Chen Nuolan’s mouth dropped open in surprise.

“That’s a long story. Reversing time comes at a price…”

Chen Nuolan recalled the plan Lu Tianfeng had shared with her: to return to yesterday and save the innocent people who died in this time reversal, including his close friend Yu Yongsheng.

Last night, he’d almost given up, but it was precisely because he felt he could still try to salvage everything that he had the confidence and courage to keep going.

If he were told now that it was impossible to reverse time again, would he still be able to hold on?

“Lu Tianfeng has experienced time loops many times before, so why do you say he doesn’t have this ability?”

“Because time reversal lasting several days and time reversal lasting 24 hours are two completely different concepts.” Situ Kang picked up the travel magazine Chen Nuolan had been reading and flipped to a page. “Look, this is the world’s most luxurious cruise ship, capable of safely crossing the Pacific. So, can a small boat in the park do the same?”

“No.” Chen Nuolan began to understand.
