“According to the laws of time fluctuations, a single-day cycle is a natural phenomenon, like ocean waves, while a time reversal lasting several days is a man-made giant vortex. Although Lu Tianfeng is a Perceiver, he has no professional training. Being able to withstand a three-day time reversal is already quite remarkable.”

Chen Nuolan keenly grasped the key point in Situ Kang’s words: “Can this be professionally trained?”

“Any ability can be strengthened through practice.” Situ Kang glanced at his phone and said, “Let’s talk later. Your superhero boyfriend will be here in about five minutes.”

“How do you know his whereabouts so well?” Chen Nuolan found Situ Kang truly unfathomable.

“Because one of my men gave him a business card with a microchip embedded inside. It has GPS.” Situ Kang showed his phone screen. “With technology becoming increasingly advanced, privacy has become virtually nonexistent. Speaking of which, as a scientist, Miss Chen should be most aware of the earth-shattering changes that technological development has brought to human society, right?”

“If high technology is abused by bad people, it would be truly terrifying,” Chen Nuolan said, adding a double meaning.

Situ Kang chuckled instead of getting angry. “Who has the final say on whether a technology is being abused or not? For example, nuclear weapons are now unanimously opposed by the world, but why did everyone cheer when the atomic bomb ended World War II? Furthermore, Miss Chen’s current research in biotechnology and gene therapy is often called a ‘privilege of the rich.’ Many of the latest drugs and research findings are simply unaffordable to ordinary people. So, can your work be defined as abusing scientific resources and serving the wealthy?”

Chen Nuolan knew Situ Kang was talking nonsense, but for a moment, she couldn’t think of a way to refute his point, so she turned away angrily.

“Alright, let’s go greet Officer Lu together.”

“Together?”

“Yes, guess what’s outside the door?” Situ Kang winked at Chen Nuolan vigorously.

Chen Nuolan shook her head. She didn’t want to guess. She only knew that the world outside this door was fraught with danger.

.

June 1st, 2:40 p.m., Suburban District, East Mud Hall.

Although this place name carried a somewhat eerie aura, it was actually the former site of the D City Cement Factory. In response to the national call for industrial upgrading and transformation, the factory first reduced production, then ceased operations, and became reliant on rented warehouses. Ultimately, unable to sustain itself, it was forced to disband, leaving behind this vast expanse of factory buildings and a mountain of foreign debt.

A few years ago, a company whose origins remain shrouded in mystery but claimed to have strong capital acquired the cement factory site, hung up the “East Mud Hall” sign, and heavily advertised in the media, claiming to transform the abandoned factory into a “cultural and creative industrial park.” This overwhelming publicity gave East Mud Hall a brief surge of popularity, but it quickly faded into obscurity due to the failure of its management, and the boastful company was forced to pack up and leave.

Today, East Mud Hall has long been abandoned, with “Danger Keep Out” signs plastered on most of the buildings, but even without them, no one would approach.

Lu Tianfeng glanced at the address on the business card, reaffirming his position. He strolled along the cracked cement path until he reached the deepest part of the factory complex. Unexpectedly, amidst the rubble, he discovered a small, brightly decorated building, utterly out of place and eerie.

Lu Tianfeng strode briskly toward the strange structure. As he reached the bottom floor, the mahogany door slowly opened. A well-dressed middle-aged man stood before him, smiling at him.

Behind the middle-aged man stood two muscular young men holding Chen Nuolan, one on each side. Chen Nuolan appeared composed.

“Nuolan! Are you okay?” Lu Tianfeng couldn’t help but yell.

Chen Nuolan finally lost her composure, her eyes suddenly reddening. “I’m fine.”

“My name is Situ Kang. It’s our first meeting. Officer Lu, please give me your guidance.” Situ Kang extended his right hand towards Lu Tianfeng, seemingly wanting to shake hands with him, but at the same time also stopping him from moving forward.

“Are you Ah’Yong’s boss?” Lu Tianfeng stopped and stared at Situ Kang.

“Ah’Yong was my subordinate.” Situ Kang’s mouth twitched at the mention of his name.

“He’s dead.”

“I know. I hope his sacrifice was worthwhile.” Situ Kang looked Lu Tianfeng up and down. “Where’s Wang Donglin?”

“He’s been taken away by the police, but here’s what you want.” Lu Tianfeng pulled a USB drive from his pocket and held it high so Situ Kang could see it clearly.

Situ Kang’s eyes suddenly lit up with excitement. “Excellent, Officer Lu, you really haven’t let me down!”

“But I have one condition—”

“Come in and talk.” Situ Kang waved his hand, heading back inside. Chen Nuolan was also escorted back.

Lu Tianfeng had no choice but to follow them in. Inside, he saw the exquisite decor and amenities, completely different from the dilapidated factory outside.

There was a long sofa in the living room. Situ Kang sat down and invited Chen Nuolan to sit next to him. Then he waved to Lu Tianfeng, “Come, show it to me.”

Lu Tianfeng looked around. They were all Situ Kang’s men, several of whom appeared to be carrying weapons.

“Let her go first.”

“Don’t be so impatient. I’ve just formally invited Miss Chen to serve as my scientific advisor.” Situ Kang turned and smiled at Chen Nuolan. “So, I’ll need her help interpreting the information there.”

Lu Tianfeng stared at Chen Nuolan in astonishment. Chen Nuolan shook her head gently, and he immediately understood that she had been coerced.

However, Lu Tianfeng had no other choice. He tossed the USB drive to Situ Kang and said, “I hope you won’t break your promise.”

“I won’t…” Situ Kang inserted the USB drive into the computer, his attention completely focused on the screen. “It’s indeed Lin Jiarui’s research data. Excellent!”

Chen Nuolan, unable to suppress her curiosity, glanced over and was immediately captivated by the content. Lin Jiarui’s research direction actually shared some similarities with her previous project at Feng Teng Gene, but Lin Jiarui had taken a different approach, proposing some new ideas and providing corresponding basic experimental data.

If this wild idea were confirmed, it would be a major breakthrough in gene therapy. Even more exciting, some of the experimental data was already supporting further research.

“Miss Chen, is this data valuable?”

“Yes,” Chen Nuolan replied readily, “but it will take more time to study.”

“Excellent, then let’s share this achievement with the world,” Situ Kang said, typing away at his keyboard.

Chen Nuolan was stunned to see Situ Kang share this priceless data, acquired at the cost of human lives, completely free of charge on major genetic technology discussion websites, forums, and all related information distribution areas!

In just a few seconds, a core secret of a brand-new technology that could change the future of genetic technology became a freely accessible resource for everyone.

“Why make this data public?” Chen Nuolan was stunned. She had assumed Situ Kang was profiting from it, but she hadn’t expected the situation to unfold in this way.

“The more people participate in the research, the greater the chance of success. I only hope this technology can be truly realized, not profited from. Isn’t that great?” Situ Kang laughed heartily.

Lu Tianfeng finally spoke: “I understand. You’re targeting the ‘Organization.'”

The ‘Organization’ tried every possible means to destroy the data, but Situ Kang was determined to do the opposite. He even shared the data online as soon as he got it. This way, even if the ‘Organization’ had all the power, it wouldn’t be able to completely delete the data that had spread throughout the internet.

“Yes, as the saying goes, the enemy of my enemy is my friend. Would you consider a long-term partnership with me?”

“Partnership?”

“Yes, I can tell you the secrets of the ‘Organization,’ and then we can join forces to fight it,” Situ Kang said confidently.

Although Lu Tianfeng was extremely averse to any involvement with the man before him, the offer was so tempting that the words of refusal were on the tip of his tongue, but he couldn’t utter them.

When Situ Kang saw through Lu Tianfeng’s inner struggles, his face lit up with a determined expression.

“Someone told me something similar before, and then he died.”

“Don’t worry, I’m not going to die that easily,” Situ Kang said calmly, not angry at all.

Lu Tianfeng glanced at Chen Nuolan, who happened to be looking back at him.

—I just want to test the true nature of the ‘Organization.’

—No matter what choice you make, I will support you.

The two exchanged silent glances, and then Lu Tianfeng spoke word by word, “Tell me, what exactly is the ‘Organization’?

CONTENT END 105

chapters.title: Chapter 106
chapters.content:
Situ Kang’s Story

Exactly how many years the ‘Organization’ has existed is something no one can truly say. They actually have an official name: the “Heavenly Time Society.” Their members’ sole mission is to maintain the progress of human society by manipulating the flow of time.

Let’s provide an example since this could be too abstract. For instance, the original historical process states that the atomic bomb was built during World War II but was never used. Until Nazi Germany came back to life and Europe was thrown into another war, the Japanese army obstinately resisted on the battlefield in East Asia, postponing the conflict for more than a year.

At this point, the “Heavenly Time Society” took action. They turned back time to the moment when the US military decided whether to use the atomic bomb. Then, they sent people to subtly alter history, reducing Hiroshima and Nagasaki to ruins, thus ushering in peace for humanity prematurely. There were many similar incidents. The US-Soviet Cold War once escalated into World War III, unrest in Central Asia triggered nuclear war, and AIDS once became a terrifying global epidemic, claiming hundreds of millions of lives.

However, none of these stories ever occurred within the current realm of human understanding because history only preserved a final version, and the authors of this final version were none other than members of the “Heavenly Time Society.”

You should now realize the actual significance of the “Heavenly Time Society.” In other words, they are more significant than any other institution in human history. The concentration of such power to decide the fate of humanity in the hands of such a small number of people is astounding.

Does the Heavenly Time Society always make the right decisions? How much destruction will human society endure if they make the incorrect choice? Or, more profoundly, is the history that the Heavenly Time Society has shaped the present day necessarily the best possible state of human civilization? Did they make a mistake already?

Yet the world remains completely in the dark, completely unaware that the fate of the world is being manipulated by the Heavenly Time Society.

The likelihood of becoming a “Perceiver,” or someone who can see the “small vortexes” in time—time loops that happen five times a day—is extremely low among regular people. According to statistics, there is a very slim chance of becoming a Perceiver—roughly one in a million. While some persons perceive time loops for the first time in their adult years, others are Perceivers from birth.

Over 90% of Perceivers suffer mental breakdowns, suicide, or are treated as insane due to this special ability. This is especially true for adolescents under 18, who, due to their immaturity, have an unnatural mortality rate as high as 99%.

Perceivers who manage to live a normal life in human society are highly skilled in all areas, including intelligence, emotional intelligence, and self-control. They know how to conceal their identities and even leverage this ability to their advantage in social activities—Officer Lu is a prime example.

The “Heavenly Time Society” also has the vital responsibility of covertly growing and expanding their staff. They carefully gather data about every Perceiver in their vicinity, keep tabs on their lives, and choose the best applicants for hiring. Members’ perception and management of the time flow will progressively improve through a variety of training and reinforcement techniques. The most exceptional of them will have the chance to become “Interveners,” with the ability to sense and activate the time reversal.

Within the Heavenly Time Society, the number of Interveners is rigorously regulated. There are only seven people with this capability, and only three of them are officially authorized Interveners. The others, who are not allowed to use their skills at will, are only stand-ins. The organization’s directives must be rigorously followed by all three of the official interveners as they use their powers. Any unlawful attempt to change time is a grave crime that carries a death sentence.

However, underworld forces exist everywhere there are people. The Heavenly Time Society cannot break the laws of history, even though it has the power to affect the whole path of human history. Members of the group are getting younger and more exposed to contemporary views as time goes on. Internal regulations that stretch back centuries are getting progressively out of date, yet any attempt to update them will unavoidably encounter fierce opposition.

The Heavenly Time Society has experienced an unparalleled crisis in recent years. Scientists are now able to explore the enigmatic field of human gene editing thanks to the quick development of genetic technology. Even though the researchers themselves are totally ignorant of it, their research findings have already had the power to affect the likelihood that humans would develop time flow perception. However, the foundation of the Heavenly Time Society’s power and control over human history will eventually be overturned when someone combines the capacity to sense time flow with gene editing technology.

Imagine if it were possible to turn even regular people into Perceivers through technology, and if the likelihood of a Perceiver arising was one in a hundred rather than one in a million. Would so many people still be under the power of the Heavenly Time Society? As a result, the Heavenly Time Society is compelled to take extreme action, killing researchers whose work has already revealed Perceivers’ secrets. But technological progress cannot be reversed. damaging a project and killing one person today, only to discover someone else working on a related project the next day. The issue won’t be resolved by this.

This has led to divisions within the Heavenly Time Society. Some ask, why must human society develop according to the Heavenly Time Society’s rules? Why resort to murder to maintain the organization’s normal operations? Does the Heavenly Time Society’s criteria for interfering in the course of history need to change?

At one point, I was one of the four substitute Interveners for the Heavenly Time Society. But I detest power struggles above all. The organization has seen a growth in factions in recent years, with several factions constantly plotting for control while producing little substantive work.

I was sick of Heavenly Time Society and wanted to get out. But the organization never provided the idea of “quitting.” To apply to leave would be to betray the organization and gain a traitor’s reputation.

Defectors in the heyday of the Heavenly Time Society would have been doomed to die. However, a lot has changed. They were so consumed by internal conflict that they didn’t have time to care about me and were afraid of my capacity to control time. They chose not to engage in a full-on battle with me, so they ignored me and released me.

After leaving the Heavenly Time Society, I realized how vast the world is. Human society has countless possibilities for development. Why do we choose the path we consider “good” and force everyone to follow it? Even if we possess the power to alter the flow of time, do we have to change the world? Can’t we just live normal lives?

I thought a lot and ultimately decided to change the world. No, I should say I hope the world returns to its original state, allowing human society to develop freely. Even if this means more wars and disasters, that’s the choice people make.

The first thing I did was make money, using my abilities to make a fortune. Stocks, futures, bonds, gambling—any speculative avenues—were my best bets for making money.

In just two years, I amassed a considerable amount of capital. Then I recruited people, developed connections, and step by step built my own business empire.

I discovered that with money, many problems can be easily solved. I used to worry that the Heavenly Time Society would come after me, but as my influence grew, the Heavenly Time Society shunned me. How could I even harbor any urge for revenge?

I’ve also put a lot of effort into finding modern genetic experts over the last two years to see whether any of them have created Perceiver-related technology. If so, I planned look for ways to safeguard their work. The Heavenly Time Society is still very strong, unfortunately. Luo Tengfeng was eliminated, and soon after Lin Jiarui was also killed. My only option, given my delay in action, is to figure out how to get the data that Lin Jiarui left behind.

Officer Lu, I’m very grateful for finding the data for me. Miss Chen, I also hope you’ll join us in researching ways to unlock the potential of human Perceivers. But even if you’re reluctant, that’s fine. I believe that after today, the entire field of genetic research will experience a major upheaval. With so many researchers, someone will surely succeed.

Perhaps, what’s happening in this small house marks the beginning of a new world for humanity.

How fortunate we are to witness this moment!

T/N: Whew! That’s a loooot of information to process.

CONTENT END 106

chapters.title: Chapter 107
chapters.content:
June 1st, 3:10 p.m., East Mud Hall, small Western-style building.

Situ Kang finally concluded his passionate speech and looked at Lu Tianfeng expectantly.

“What have you considered, Officer Lu?”

Lu Tianfeng rested his chin on his hand and pondered, “In short, Mr. Situ, you possess both powerful time manipulation abilities and immense wealth and influence, correct?”

“Indeed, I also care deeply about the lives of ordinary people and hope to restore freedom to all of humanity,” Situ Kang declared brazenly.

“In the movies, that’s a line only crazy villains would say.”

“But I’m not crazy, nor am I a villain.”

“Then can you turn back time again, returning to May 31st?” Lu Tianfeng asked.

Situ Kang was stunned for a moment, then raised his head and burst into laughter. “Officer Lu, are you kidding? I finally achieved my goal. How could I possibly start over again? Turning back time would come at a tremendous cost…”

At this point, Situ Kang stopped talking, clearly unwilling to reveal any more secrets. Lu Tianfeng’s face darkened, and he snorted coldly.

“Besides, I’ve already explained to Miss Chen that your abilities as a Perceiver are limited. This time, you gained the ability to sense time reversal thanks to the enhancer we provided, but your body hasn’t caught up yet. If you were to experience another reversal, you might die.”

“So, will I still be able to sense time reversal in the future? Or will I be limited to perceiving time cycles within a single day like before?”

“I can’t answer that question. It’s true that some people have permanently enhanced their perception abilities by drinking enhancers, but others have died after drinking them.” Situ Kang suddenly laughed, a chilling sound. “Since you’re not dead, there’s still a chance you can permanently gain the ability to sense time reversal.”

“I see,” Lu Tianfeng said calmly, showing no particular emotion.

He had already prepared himself mentally. Chen Nuolan was right; turning back time wouldn’t come without a price, and he’d already experienced the physical pain firsthand.

Even if he could travel through time, he would still encounter many unavoidable situations.

“Well, I have one last question.” Lu Tianfeng straightened up, suddenly seeming taller. This was the first time he’d revealed his true aura and edge since entering the room.

“Wang Donglin is one of your pawns, right?”

Situ Kang’s face changed, his heart pounding. He realized he had underestimated Lu Tianfeng.

The policeman had finally seen through everything.

T/N: Yes. It’s this short. This is all of part 8. Maybe so we could absorb the previous chapter’s information overflow?

CONTENT END 107

chapters.title: Chapter 108
chapters.content:
Lu Tianfeng’s Analysis

Wang Donglin was truly an unfathomable man. Until the very last moment, when he seemed to have exhausted all his cards, he still concealed his true secret.

Yuan Chengren, a member of the Heavenly Time Society, saw through Wang Donglin’s criminal activities and used them to blackmail him, forcing him to kill Lin Jiarui and seize the experimental data. These were all facts. However, as I listened to Wang Donglin’s confession, a question lingered in my mind. Whether he was reported or arrested for his rash actions, his murder would have been exposed anyway. Why would Wang Donglin so obediently obey Yuan Chengren’s orders?

Common sense suggests that there was likely an exchange of “benefits.” However, according to Wang Donglin, the Heavenly Time Society offered him no tangible benefits. Given Wang Donglin’s cautious personality and meticulous approach, how could he have agreed to such a sure-win deal? I began to suspect a hidden agenda.

My initial hypothesis was that Yuan Chengren, using his status as a criminal psychology expert, was shielding Wang Donglin, teaching him how to perfectly impersonate a schizophrenic. Furthermore, he could leverage his authority to influence the results of the D City University Criminal Psychology Laboratory’s diagnosis.

However, this theory still leaves several inexplicable flaws. First, why did the other two psychiatric evaluation agencies reach the same conclusion? Is Yuan Chengren’s influence that significant? Second, assuming the Heavenly Time Society mobilized its vast resources to protect Wang Donglin, the question becomes, why did they go to such great lengths? Wang Donglin possessed nothing powerful enough to threaten them; the leverage in this deal was unequal. Third, during negotiations, Wang Donglin repeatedly pleaded with me to release him and grant him freedom. Why did he think he could escape the police’s tight net?

In the end, this idea was rejected because Wang Donglin willingly exposed Yuan Chengren in a desperate attempt, accusing him of coercing and intimidating him into killing Lin Jiarui. If Wang Donglin and Yuan Chengren were really on the same page, he wouldn’t have given the police Yuan Chengren’s name, thereby allowing their connection to be known.

However, Wang Donglin’s choice to sacrifice Yuan Chengren as part of his survival strategy proves that Yuan Chengren and the Heavenly Time Society weren’t the true agents behind his exoneration. So, who else could strike a deal with Wang Donglin? What exactly does Wang Donglin possess that makes them so eager?

Mr. Situ, you’ve answered these questions I’ve never fully grasped. Wang Donglin’s most valuable asset is, of course, Lin Jiarui’s data. In his confession, he just made a passing reference to the reason he backed up the data, which is a little confusing. However, all would make sense if someone had given him an offer to purchase this data.

My guess is that your deal went something like this: Wang Donglin was upset by Yuan Chengren’s threats, and you, the Heavenly Time Society’s sworn enemy, noticed Yuan Chengren’s actions and suspected they might be related to the research data, so you decided to bribe Wang Donglin.

Wang Donglin wouldn’t trust you easily. He might demand a payment or a guarantee that he won’t receive the death penalty if apprehended by the police. Since you have money, any problem you can solve now won’t be a problem for you. So, you spent a fortune, likely using both coercion and bribery to deal with the examiners at three different institutions, fabricating results that would allow Wang Donglin to avoid imprisonment.

According to your plan, you might have kidnapped Wang Donglin from a psychiatric hospital, where security was relatively lax. However, the members of the Heavenly Time Society were also on the alert. They saw through your plan, hijacked Wang Donglin’s prison van, and killed him. Only then did you become aware of the Heavenly Time Society’s actions, but it was too late. To avert defeat, you immediately sent Ah’Yong to set a trap to threaten me, forcing me to time reverse back to May 31st to save Wang Donglin’s life.

This explains why Wang Donglin wasn’t initially surprised by the prison van hijacking, only realizing something was amiss when he realized the other party was actually trying to kill him. After a series of twists and turns, I was ultimately able to rescue him. But Wang Donglin later made a mistake, because he had actually struck some kind of agreement with both you and the Heavenly Time Society. He decided to go to Moyun Town to locate the bartender, Judy, because he was unable to distinguish between those attempting to save him and those attempting to murder him in the midst of the chaos.

Wary Wang Donglin soon realized that Judy intended to kill him and that the Heavenly Time Society had already considered him as a pawn. However, this didn’t mean he had complete trust in me. Frightened, he decided to contact me, believing that as a police officer, I would never harm him.

Thus, Wang Donglin obtained the hidden data through me, hoping to complete the deal and regain his freedom. However, a series of unforeseen events left him in the hands of the police, making it impossible for him to escape through his tricks.

When the situation reached this point, he decisively abandoned his escape plan and reconfigured his status as a “schizophrenic.” This guaranteed his survival, which would then offer hope.

Yes, I mean, Wang Donglin had always been playing the role of a “split personality,” but in reality, his two “personalities” were merely fabrications to avoid prosecution. From the beginning to the end, he possessed only one personality: a narrow-minded, cold-blooded, and cruel man who would do anything to achieve his goals, calculating everything to the utmost.

To perfectly portray his role, he even deliberately killed a completely innocent woman while on the run, because only such an unconscionable crime would justify his psychiatric evaluation’s conclusion of “insanity and loss of self-control.”

Wang Donglin is a real demon, and you are the one who let him go so he could carry out his crimes. Like him, you disrespect other people’s lives and violate their dignity in order to fulfill your claimed objectives. You can either support Wang Donglin’s killings or leave him when he is no longer needed. Although Ah’Yong was supposedly your confidant, you could discard him entirely as long as you could obtain the data.

If I agree to cooperate with you, who knows when you’ll stab me in the back due to a conflict of interest?

You are indeed the enemy of my enemy, but you will never be my friend. Because I’m a police officer, I won’t let any criminal go, within my power, like Wang Donglin, whose hands are already stained with blood.

I’m sorry, but I have to remove your chess piece from the board now.

CONTENT END 108

chapters.title: Chapter 109
chapters.content:
June 1st, 3:25 p.m., East Mud Hall, Small Western-style Building.

“Excellent, very good, very good!”

As soon as Lu Tianfeng finished speaking, Situ Kang burst into applause. He cheered and clapped his hands vigorously. “Officer Lu, with just these scattered clues, you’ve almost pieced together the entire truth. Your clarity of thought and rigorous logic are astonishing. As far as I know, there’s only one minor flaw in your reasoning.”

“What flaw?”

“The Wang Donglin case has garnered widespread public attention. If someone wants to falsify his mental health evaluation report, it’s not something I can solve with just money!”

Situ Kang let out an inexplicable laugh, which disgusted Lu Tianfeng.

“You mean… Wang Donglin is indeed mentally ill?”

“I’m not sure if Wang Donglin has a split personality, but if he’s been acting all along, then he’s really relying on his solid acting skills to get away with it.” Situ Kang sat back on the sofa and poured himself a cup of tea. “You’ve pretty much guessed the rest, so I won’t say anything more.”

“So you admit to a deal with Wang Donglin?”

Situ Kang leaned back in the sofa, smiling. “He said he had some data to sell me, and I was interested, so he quoted a price. That’s all. Officer Lu, is this deal illegal?”

Lu Tianfeng knew that as long as Situ Kang insisted he didn’t know Wang Donglin’s data was from an illegal source, he could easily evade legal action. Another possible charge against Situ Kang was accusing him of orchestrating the abduction of Chen Nuolan, but now that the key suspect, Ah’Yong, was dead, the case was hopelessly inconclusive.

As for the story of Situ Kang manipulating time, orchestrating the hostage situation on June 2nd and forcing Lu Tianfeng to hijack the prison van, it was pure nonsense.

In Lu Tianfeng’s eyes, despite Situ Kang’s numerous crimes, there was no evidence of his crimes. It could even be said that in this present time, he was just an ordinary, law-abiding businessman.

Lu Tianfeng recalled Zhang Zhiqi’s description of his cousin’s tragic past. If someone committed crimes only in a “non-existent” time, were they a good person or a bad person? Since the law couldn’t punish these people, could they just continue their crimes with impunity?

Thinking of this, Lu Tianfeng subconsciously clenched his fists.

Situ Kang noticed this subtle gesture, but he simply shrugged and said calmly, “You feel dissatisfied and that this is unfair, right? We’re not ordinary people, so why should we be bound by rules made by ordinary people?”

“Because there are many ordinary people in this world, we absolutely cannot break the rules at will.”

Situ Kang sighed, clearly disagreeing with Lu Tianfeng’s point, but he didn’t dwell on the issue. Instead, he stood up and said abruptly, “I have some things to take care of. I’ll take my leave now.”

Situ Kang gestured to his subordinates behind him and was about to leave when Lu Tianfeng extended his hand, blocking his way. Situ Kang’s two bodyguards immediately drew their pistols, pointing them at Lu Tianfeng and Chen Nuolan, respectively, but Situ Kang simply smiled and waved them down.

“Perhaps we’ll have a chance to work together again in the future. Let’s talk it over. Officer Lu, do you have any questions?” Situ Kang smiled triumphantly.

“I hope Wang Donglin receives the punishment he deserves.”

“This is a police officer’s job. I can’t help!” Situ Kang spread his hands.

“You two had a deal. You can help me prove that Wang Donglin killed Lin Jiarui in order to sell the data for a high price. This would qualify his crime as a premeditated murder and robbery, rather than an unconscious act driven by his alter ego.”

“Why should I get involved in this mess?”

“Because Wang Donglin is no longer of any use to you. But if you give up on him, I can temporarily renounce our enmity.”

Situ Kang showed an amused expression. “So, while we can’t be friends, we don’t have to be enemies?”

“I’ll let bygones be bygones, but if you do it again, I won’t let you off the hook.”

“What a shame! I find it difficult to stay true to my duties.” Situ Kang rolled his eyes. “But you’re right about one thing: Wang Donglin is no longer a chess piece. If you can properly dispose of him for me, it would be a win-win situation for both of us.”

“It’s a deal.” Lu Tianfeng nodded.

“Police-civilian cooperation ensures long-term peace and stability.” Situ Kang pulled a cell phone from his pocket and handed it to Lu Tianfeng. “I found this on the street. See if it’s useful!”

Lu Tianfeng took the phone expressionlessly. He knew the game had reached a draw at this point. But deep down, his greatest wish was to defeat Situ Kang.

Because who knew what crazy things this man would do in the future?

“Let’s go,” Lu Tianfeng said gently, taking Chen Nuolan’s hand.

Chen Nuolan nodded, stood on tiptoe, oblivious to the surroundings, and kissed Lu Tianfeng on the cheek.

“No matter what you do, I will always support you.”

CONTENT END 109

chapters.title: Chapter 110
chapters.content:
June 1st, 8:00 p.m., D City Police Station, Interrogation Room.

Wang Donglin sat upright in his chair. No matter who asked him any question, he remained silent, staring intently at the interrogator with a sinister sneer.

“This guy is truly insane,” every officer involved in the interrogation agreed.

But when Lu Tianfeng entered the interrogation room, carrying a transparent evidence bag, Wang Donglin’s expression suddenly changed. He saw a cellphone inside.

Although he didn’t know whose phone it was, he faintly recognized a sense of danger.

“I found it,” Lu Tianfeng blurted out without a second thought.

“What?”

“The buyer’s phone.”

“What buyer?” Wang Donglin’s expression remained calm, but the corner of his mouth twitched imperceptibly.

“That man named Ah’Yong gave you a substantial deposit, right? Why would he turn his back on you after failing to close the deal?”

“I have no idea what you’re talking about.” Wang Donglin instinctively reached for the disposable paper cup in front of him, only to discover it was already empty. Lu Tianfeng scrolled through the evidence bag, checking the text messages on the phone. “Times have truly advanced. Black market transactions now use electronic currency, globally exchangeable, and with confidential sources. But I regret to inform you that if we only had access to your electronic currency account, we wouldn’t be able to find out who transferred the money to you. But if we had access to the accounts of both parties involved in the transaction, we’d have irrefutable proof.”

Wang Donglin crumpled the paper cup in his hand.

“You killed Lin Jiarui for money, right? Here are not only the electronic currency transfer records but also the complete chat logs.”

“No! Lu Tianfeng, I told you, I was forced to kill because someone from the ‘Organization’ threatened me.” Wang Donglin stood up anxiously.

“Where’s the evidence?” Lu Tianfeng smiled. This was the first time in his conversations with Wang Donglin that he’d truly smiled out of joy.

Because Lu Tianfeng was absolutely certain that Wang Donglin had destroyed all the evidence long ago, he gloated over his nearly perfect crime. He had planned every step carefully, taking every factor into account. He even reached secret agreements with both the Heavenly Time Society and Situ Kang, demanding they guarantee his survival. He even added a third layer of security, feigning a split personality to deceive professional psychiatric evaluation agencies.

His destruction of all other evidence had, in turn, made the very evidence Lu Tianfeng had produced the most crucial and decisive evidence.

“Your evidence is isolated and perjured; it has no legal validity…” Wang Donglin flushed and stammered incoherently.

“It’s okay. Give us some time, and the complete chain of evidence will emerge. This is enough to prove that your murder of Lin Jiarui was completely premeditated. It has nothing to do with schizophrenia or anything like that.”

Wang Donglin slumped back into his chair, his expression relatively calm. Aside from the involuntary twitch at the corner of his mouth, there was nothing unusual.

He had finally lost his last line of defense, but he didn’t want to give up. He couldn’t.

If he gave up here, he would lose everything, including his life.

“I won’t say anything,” he finally said through gritted teeth.

“You don’t need to say anything. I’ll investigate.” Lu Tianfeng casually withdrew the evidence bag. “I’m not here to interrogate you, but—”

Lu Tianfeng suddenly lowered his voice, leaned forward, and spoke in Wang Donglin’s ear, in a voice only he could hear.

“I just want you to experience the taste of failure.”

Wang Donglin’s stomach turned sour. Yes, this was the taste of failure.

He seemed to be back to the night his father had perished in the fire and his mother had confronted him. He could hear Moli’s ruthless sneer at him.

From that day on, he was a complete loser.

The mask he had worn for so many years was finally ruthlessly torn off by Lu Tianfeng.

“I lost…” he said woodenly.

Lu Tianfeng seemed not to hear him and left the interrogation room without a glance.

Before closing the door, he whispered, “The net of heaven is vast and wide, and nothing can escape it.”

As the door closed, Wang Donglin slumped in his chair, not even having the strength to sit up straight.

CONTENT END 110

chapters.title: Chapter 111
chapters.content:
June 1st, 8:30 p.m., rooftop of the D City Police Department office building.

Under the dim light, a small red dot flickered.

A lone man smoked a cigarette.

Another, smaller, female figure also appeared on the rooftop.

“So you’re a smoker too?” Tong Yao said to Zhang Zhiqi, somewhat surprised. She had never seen him smoke in the past two days.

“I’m not a heavy smoker, actually, but strangely enough, I felt the urge to smoke the moment I arrived on this rooftop.” Zhang Zhiqi put out his less than half-smoked cigarette.

“Is this considered an occupational hazard?” Tong Yao knew, of course, that the rooftop served as the building’s smoking area. “Or, deep down, do you still miss your days as a police officer?”

Zhang Zhiqi chuckled. “Forget it. Being a private investigator is more liberating and offers more solutions.”

“Hmph, aren’t you still relying on information from the police’s internal system? I’ll find a way to shut you down later.”

“Officer Tong, don’t be so ruthless. Leave me a way out. I can still help you solve cases in the future. Best of both worlds.”

Tong Yao gazed at the twinkling night lights in the distance and said with emotion, “I really have to thank you this time. Without your help, we might not have been able to capture Wang Donglin so easily.”

“You’re welcome. It’s only natural having taken money for a job… By the way, are you sure you can get the reward offered by your police for me?”

“I’ll do my best.”

“If it doesn’t work out, that’s fine. Just keep my business in the loop.” Zhang Zhiqi actually offered Tong Yao a way out, which rather left her a little confused.

“Why are you suddenly listless? That’s not like you.”

“Because the circumstances of this case are incredibly complicated. Although Wang Donglin has been apprehended, it’s not over yet,” Zhang Zhiqi sighed. “Not to mention, it involves things like time loops, time reversals, and rewriting history… How can a mere mortal like me face all that? The subject is completely beyond my scope!”

Tong Yao couldn’t help but burst out laughing. “Haha, you’re clearly the country’s top information technology expert, bar none. How can you be considered a mere mortal?”

“Well… Officer Tong, you’re too kind.”

“Besides, you’re not facing this alone.” Tong Yao looked into the distance and said slowly, “Don’t you still have us?”

“Us…” Zhang Zhiqi felt a lump in his throat. He suddenly remembered his days as a criminal police officer, how his brothers had watched over each other and fought side by side.

In fact, he had always missed that warm and reassuring feeling.

Just like now.

CONTENT END 111

chapters.title: Chapter 112
chapters.content:
June 1st, 9:00 p.m., D City Police Department Office Building, Canteen.

Cheng Tuo sat in a corner of the canteen, a cup of warm soy milk in hand, looking lost in thought, his lips barely touching the liquid.

“Captain Cheng,” Lu Tianfeng, also holding a similar cup, took the seat across from Cheng Tuo.

“Ah’Feng, thank you for your hard work these past two days.”

“Thank you, too. Go home and rest early tonight.”

“Okay.”

Lu Tianfeng felt a wave of inexplicable sadness. He hadn’t imagined that they, who had been through thick and thin together, would end up sitting here exchanging meaningless pleasantries, their true questions unspoken.

Perhaps Cheng Tuo also felt the conversation was too awkward. He took a long swig of soy milk and said, “Ah’Feng, please believe me. Although I’ve had contact with people from the ‘Organization,’ I’ve absolutely never done anything against humanity, let alone you.”

“I believe you.” Perhaps worried his tone was too understated, Lu Tianfeng emphasized again, “I completely believe you. I really do.”

“At first, I was just curious about your informant. I didn’t expect it to be such a quagmire. Once you step into it, it’s not so easy to escape unscathed.” Cheng Tuo lowered his head and let out a long sigh. “By the way, guess who in the ‘Organization’ is my street guy?”

“Who is it?” Lu Tianfeng had a hunch; it would be a familiar name.

“Professor Zhou Huansheng of the Department of Biology at D City University was declared missing seven years ago, and his whereabouts remain unknown,” Cheng Tuo said, tapping his cup. “That’s one of the reasons I’ve been in contact with them. I wanted to know what happened to Zhou Huansheng and where he’s been hiding all these years. Even more bizarre is that the Zhou Huansheng I see now looks younger than the photo in the archives, but that photo was likely taken ten years ago.”

Even with a certain mental preparation, Lu Tianfeng was still secretly surprised.

Was the power of the “Heavenly Time Society” really as exaggerated as Situ Kang claimed? If they could hide Zhou Huansheng for seven years, then the current hunt for Yuan Chengren and the others would likely be fruitless.

“What kind of enemies are we facing?” Lu Tianfeng said with deep emotion.

“Don’t worry. Tong Yao, I, and the entire police department will have your back.”

Lu Tianfeng couldn’t help but smile bitterly. “Captain Cheng, first find a way to explain this incident to Director Luo. I might not be a police officer tomorrow.”

CONTENT END 112

chapters.title: Chapter 113
chapters.content:
June 1st, 10 p.m., a small dock on the outskirts of D City.

Yuan Chengren finished reading the message on his phone, his right hand trembling.

“Teacher Yuan, what’s wrong?” asked Ma Yueyi, poking her head out of the cabin of a fishing boat.

Deng Zixiong, sitting at the stern of the fishing boat with a serious expression, also asked, “Has the contact person not arrived yet?”

Yuan Chengren sighed, looking up at the sky. “This is insane! Situ Kang actually shared Lin Jiarui’s experimental data and related materials with the world. Right now, I estimate that over a hundred different teams and institutions are studying that data like they were a treasure.”

“So our mission… was a complete failure.” Ma Yueyi shuddered. Although she was relatively new within the Heavenly Time Society, she was well aware of the punishment faced by members who failed their missions.

“We’re doomed now. The Organization has definitely abandoned us.”

“Abandoned? No, they’re not just abandoning us; they’re taking our lives.” Yuan Chengren handed the phone to the other two. “Did you see that?”

The screen displayed a shocking line of text:

“End your own life. No blame will be placed for past mistakes. If you disobey orders, you will be killed.”

“What era is this? Still spouting these pretentious lines? How contrived!” Ma Yueyi pouted, her expression disdainful.

“Teacher Yuan, it’s all a dead end anyway. Instead of just sitting there and waiting to die, why not fight to the death?” Deng Zixiong said viciously.

“What do you mean by fighting to the death?” Yuan Chengren asked.

“Let’s go find Situ Kang and join him to fight those old fogies!”

“Okay!” Ma Yueyi agreed immediately.

Yuan Chengren simply closed his eyes and said nothing.

CONTENT END 113

chapters.title: Chapter 114
chapters.content:
June 1st, 11:50 p.m.

Chen Nuolan stood up at her desk and rubbed her tired eyes. Although Lu Tianfeng had told her to get some rest as soon as she got home, she tossed and turned in bed, unable to fall asleep. So she simply got up and delved into Lin Jiarui’s experimental data. Naturally, the more she read, the more alert and excited she became.

Following this line of thought, gene therapy research could truly take a major step forward!

Thinking of this, Chen Nuolan immediately set to work. While rummaging through boxes and drawers for information, she pulled out a piece of scratch paper and quickly designed the experimental plan she was contemplating to try next. Only after filling several A4 pages did she suddenly come to her senses and remember that she was currently unemployed and didn’t even have access to a proper laboratory.

She immediately began revising her resume, adding her Feng Teng Gene experience to her previous template, and almost submitted it. However, before sending the email, she decided she should wait for Lu Tianfeng to get home and discuss it with him.

Chen Nuolan glanced at the clock; it was almost midnight.

“Are you back?” She pulled out her phone and typed the message, then thought for a moment before deleting it.

Just then, the sound of the door unlocking could be heard.

Chen Nuolan ran over, just in time to meet Lu Tianfeng as he entered.

“Feng…” She hugged him.

“What’s wrong?”

“I suddenly miss you so much.”

I’m so afraid of losing you. That was what Chen Nuolan really wanted to say.

“Nuolan, didn’t I tell you I’d definitely go home today?” Lu Tianfeng patted Chen Nuolan’s head. “Because tomorrow, June 2nd, is the anniversary of our first meeting!”

Chen Nuolan rested her head against Lu Tianfeng’s chest and whispered softly, “For you, it’s like returning to this day all over again, right?”

“Yes,” Lu Tianfeng replied, and the atmosphere suddenly grew a little heavy.

“Last June 2nd, we experienced a life-and-death separation, right?”

“But this time, we won’t be separated again,” Lu Tianfeng said solemnly, holding her face.

“I know, but… some people who should have been alive are now dead…” Chen Nuolan’s eyes welled up.

She thought not only of Yu Yongsheng but also of a girl she had never met before, whom she had only read about in the news, murdered by Wang Donglin.

Perhaps there were even more people she didn’t know about who had gone from life to death in this shift in the time flow. Of course, there were also those who had gone from death to life. For example, herself and Wang Donglin.

Chen Nuolan suddenly felt that this feeling of survival, gained by altering the flow of time, wasn’t a good one. She felt like a thief, stealing lives that belonged to others.

“Don’t overthink it, okay?” Lu Tianfeng, seeing through Chen Nuolan’s concerns, offered no more words of comfort. Instead, he quietly and tightly embraced her.

There would still be many difficulties and obstacles ahead, but he was confident he could face them with her.

The clock finally struck twelve.

A new day had arrived. A new beginning, and also a new ending.

“Nuolan, I love you.”

The answer he received was a long, passionate kiss.

No matter what, as long as we were together, we couldn’t give up easily.

CONTENT END 114
